Field Meaning hostModId Host mod id for this session options LEGACY or STRICT policy used by prepare sources Ordered source descriptors definitions Selected definitions allDefinitions All parsed definitions, including lower-priority candidates registerFiles Located registration content paths reloadFiles Located and preflighted reload paths indexFiles Located index manifest paths claims Deduplicated claims declared by selected definitions diagnostics Immutable diagnostic snapshot from prepare dependencies Normalized owner dependency map reservedSymbols Host-reserved configuration symbols

Each definition is wrapped in a LocatedDefinition<T>:

Field Meaning key Handler type domain and identity; required non-null in STRICT handler Handler that parsed and applies this value definition Typed result from parse source SourceDescriptor carrying sourceId, rootId, rank, and namespaces sourceOrder Effective priority order for this session (from rank for platform sources) logicalPath Content file path jsonPointer Location inside the content file declarationOrder Session-wide discovery sequence number

registerFiles, reloadFiles, and indexFiles are public read-only lists that hosts can inspect or persist to record the exact files consumed.

docs.title: Identity Selection
docs.text: Definitions are grouped by (typeName, identity). Anonymous definitions have key == null.

docs.title: NON_REGISTRATION or LEGACY
docs.text:
Unless the handler declares HandlerCapability.OVERLAY, only the candidate with the highest priority is selected per key:

sourceOrder
  → declarationOrder

Higher sourceOrder wins; within the same source, later parsed definitions win. Because logicalPath sorting governs parse order, definitions in lexicographically later paths within the same source receive higher declarationOrder values. Handlers declaring HandlerCapability.OVERLAY retain all candidates sharing an identity so they can merge or overlay them.

docs.title: STRICT REGISTRY_CLAIMS
docs.text:
In STRICT mode, definitions whose handler declares REGISTRY_CLAIMS (and not NON_REGISTRATION) retain all candidates sharing a DefinitionKey. Claim validation must then prove they do not collide on a final registry key:

  • Same (registry, id) key -> CLAIM_CONFLICT, entire batch rejected;
  • Same DefinitionKey with distinct final registry keys -> allowed by the current implementation;
  • Any selected claim matching a host-reserved key -> CLAIM_CONFLICT.

This catches cases where two distinct JSON IDs resolve to the same block or item key. A source cannot bypass conflict checks merely by using distinct definition identities that claim the same block id.

Note that STRICT runs validate on all retained candidates sharing a registration identity. Even a lower-priority candidate whose final claim differs from a higher-priority one will block the build if it fails validation; registration types do not follow the "pick winner first, validate winner only" rule used by configuration types.

docs.title: Anonymous Definitions
docs.text:
• LEGACY: all selected without deduplication;
  • STRICT: emits MISSING_IDENTITY and rejects the build (REJECTED).

docs.title: LEGACY vs. STRICT
docs.text:
Behavior LEGACY STRICT JSON decoding Gson lenient mode Strict UTF-8 + StrictResourceJson; duplicate keys, comments, trailing commas, etc. block apply Parse failure Records error; continues applying other definitions Blocks the entire batch before apply Unknown top-level field Warning Error Missing identity Allowed Error Handler capabilities Not checked Requires STRICT_PREFLIGHT, strictValidationImplemented(), and exactly one identity role validate Not invoked Invoked on all selected definitions Parent cycles Warning Error Claim collection Invoked Invoked Claim conflict Intra-data conflict is warning; reserved-host conflict is error, yet build continues Rejects entire batch before apply Unknown owner dependency Warning Error Duplicate source root / rank Error, yet build continues Error, rejects entire batch

"Duplicate source root" refers to duplicate (sourceId, rootId); distinct rootIds under the same sourceId are valid. Duplicate rank values likewise record INVALID_SOURCE: STRICT rejects before apply, while LEGACY may continue.

Built-in registration handlers follow these identity paths:

Legacy JsonTreeBuilder:               minecraft:foo -> <hostModId>:foo
Pipeline LEGACY DefinitionKey/apply:  minecraft:foo -> <hostModId>:foo
Pipeline STRICT DefinitionKey/apply:  minecraft:foo -> minecraft:foo

Thus BuildOptions.LEGACY uses lenient JSON, skips STRICT validate, and preserves the historical identity rewrite; built-in handlers also catch single-entry apply exceptions in non-strict contexts and continue, though custom apply throws still yield FAILED. A bare foo maps to the host namespace in LEGACY; in STRICT, resolveIdentity yields <hostModId>:foo, and validate then rejects it with INVALID_IDENTITY.

Built-in block and item claims read the final ID from DefinitionKey, so minecraft:foo stays aligned across DefinitionKey, claims, and apply in STRICT, while LEGACY consistently applies the historical rewrite across all three.

In LEGACY mode, BuildResult can still return APPLIED while carrying ERROR diagnostics. APPLIED indicates that apply ran to completion, not that inputs were clean. Strict verification must check both !prepared.hasBlockingDiagnostics() and result.successful().

Owners present in the dependencies map that have no corresponding source descriptor do not raise an error on their own, although any dependencies they declare are still checked against known source owners. Hosts should ensure the dependencies map contains only expected owners so typos do not silently go unnoticed.

docs.title: Boundary Between prepare and build
docs.text:
prepare can be called repeatedly, producing fresh declaration orders, selected definitions, and diagnostics. build can also be called multiple times on the same PreparedContent, though each invocation constructs a fresh root and re-runs apply and finalizers; hosts should normally build once per prepared session.

PreparedContent checks only that hostModId matches the pipeline; do not pass an older PreparedContent to a new pipeline whose handler list, finalizers, target, or reserved keys have changed, because definitions retain handler references from the pipeline that prepared them.

PreparedContent holds no open ContentSource streams. Standard handlers finish parsing JSON during prepare, so providers can close SnapshotContentSource immediately afterward to release the underlying snapshot. Custom definitions that defer source reads must document and manage that lifecycle explicitly.

Building with zero definitions is valid. A source with no indexes, an explicit empty on_register array, or an assets/data-only pack yields zero selected definitions; provided no blocking diagnostics exist, build creates an empty JsonRegistryGroup, runs finalizers, and returns APPLIED. Hosts can handle "assets-only pack + zero Java registry entries" uniformly without synthesizing placeholder definitions.

docs.title: build Execution
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as build
    participant T as RegistrationTarget
    participant O as RegBuildContext
    participant H as handler
    participant F as finalizer

    B->>B: strict + blocking? → REJECTED
    B->>O: create JsonRegistryGroup
    B->>T: createContext(host, root, options)
    B->>B: stableApplyOrder(definitions)
    loop every selected definition
        B->>O: withCurrentDefinition
        B->>H: apply(def, O)
    end
    loop finalizers in order
        B->>F: afterBuild(O, prepared)
    end
    B-->>B: APPLIED

Blocking diagnostics in STRICT mode are checked by:

prepared.hasBlockingDiagnostics()

Only Severity.ERROR is blocking; warnings never prevent build.

Apply ordering:

  1. TypeHandler.getPhase();
  2. Pipeline handler registration order;
  3. sourceOrder;
  4. logicalPath;
  5. jsonPointer;
  6. declarationOrder;
  7. Topological order from parentDefinition.

If context creation throws, sorting throws, any apply throws, or any finalizer throws, build halts further steps and returns FAILED.

Commit semantics for BuildResult:

Status rootGroup() Caller Action REJECTED null Do not apply or mount onto the registration tree APPLIED Newly built root group Mount after confirming no host-level failures FAILED Newly created, possibly incomplete root group Do not mount by default unless partial side effects are proven safe

Both successful() and applied() return status == Status.APPLIED. Neither returns true on FAILED.

docs.title: Failures and Rollback
docs.text:
build does not attempt to undo already-executed Reg.setParent, withProperty, factory side effects, or finalizer writes.

Therefore:

  • REJECTED occurs before apply, leaving no pipeline apply side effects;
  • FAILED may have built a partial registration tree;
  • When a finalizer fails, all selected definitions have already applied and earlier finalizers may have run side effects;
  • Because a newly created JsonRegistryGroup has usually not yet entered Minecraft's registry events, a host can discard an incomplete rootGroup, though it cannot automatically erase process-wide cache writes made by custom handlers.

Handler apply implementations should keep visible mutations scoped to the active context and root group so the host can safely discard the root on FAILED.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text:
BuildDiagnostic:

record BuildDiagnostic(
        Severity severity,
        Stage stage,
        Code code,
        String sourceId,
        String ownerId,
        String logicalPath,
        String jsonPointer,
        String handler,
        String message,
        String suggestion
)

Stages (Stage):

SOURCE
MANIFEST
PARSE
SELECTION
VALIDATION
CLAIMS
APPLY
FINALIZE

SELECTION is reserved in Stage; current selection failures typically emit under PARSE (identity errors) or VALIDATION (capability errors).

Primary diagnostic codes (Code):

Stage Codes SOURCE INVALID_SOURCE, UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY, SOURCE_FILE_MISSING, SOURCE_READ_FAILED MANIFEST MANIFEST_INVALID, MANIFEST_EMPTY, INVALID_PATH PARSE CONTENT_INVALID, UNKNOWN_TYPE, PARSE_FAILED, IDENTITY_FAILED, MISSING_IDENTITY VALIDATION HANDLER_NOT_STRICT_READY, INVALID_IDENTITY, UNKNOWN_FACTORY, UNKNOWN_REGISTRY_GROUP, MISSING_REFERENCE, REFERENCE_NOT_DECLARED, REFERENCE_AMBIGUOUS, GROUP_CYCLE, VALIDATION_FAILED CLAIMS CLAIM_FAILED, CLAIM_CONFLICT APPLY APPLY_FAILED FINALIZE FINALIZER_FAILED

Logical paths and JSON Pointers are constructed by appending the handler's relative pointer onto the definition pointer. Custom handlers should pass relative pointers such as "/field".

severity has only WARNING and ERROR. LEGACY does not automatically downgrade every error diagnostic to WARNING; several structural errors remain ERROR in both modes, though LEGACY builds do not check diagnostics to block apply. In STRICT, the pipeline's addIssue helper promotes issues to ERROR.

BuildDiagnostic entries are not automatically forwarded into Diagnostics, and /kasuga_data does not display new-pipeline results on its own. Providers must emit them via logs, commands, SavedData, or a host-specific report.

In a BuildDiagnostic, sourceId identifies the concrete platform source, ownerId identifies the dependency/authorization unit, and logicalPath is the path inside the root. Raw parcelId is not a standard field on BuildDiagnostic; train-pack hosts should recover parcel identity from their frozen (sourceId, rootId) mapping when building user reports rather than assuming ownerId equals a parcel or pack ID.

docs.title: Reserved Registry Claims
docs.text:
Existing deferred registry entries in a host's Reg tree can be snapshot into reserved keys:

Set<RegistryClaim.RegistryKey> reserved =
        RegistryClaimSnapshot.collect(hostRegistryRoot);

Pass reserved into the pipeline constructor so STRICT mode rejects any data definition whose claim collides with it.

RegistryClaimSnapshot.collect:

  • Performs a BFS over getChildren() starting from root, skipping any RegistryGroup whose dispatchWhen predicate returns false along with its subtree;
  • Collects MinecraftDeferRegistryReg nodes;
  • Extracts keys via getRegistryKey() and resolveId();
  • Does not check whether the deferred value has already entered Minecraft's registry.

The snapshot therefore reflects registration intentions under the current dispatch predicates. Callers should ensure host code registrations are already attached to root and all ID mappings are configured before collecting.

docs.title: Finalizers
docs.text:
BuildFinalizer finalizer = (context, content) -> {
    // all selected definitions have been applied
    return Map.copyOf(crossDefinitionResult);
};

Finalizers are suited for:

  • Creating derived registrations once all groups, styles, and primary entries exist;
  • Running one-shot cross-type summary validation;
  • Producing a session-scoped management object.

Finalizers are not suited for:

  • Mutating PreparedContent;
  • Re-applying overridden definitions;
  • Assuming automatic rollback on failure;
  • Running non-idempotently across repeated build invocations.

BuildResult.finalizerResults holds return values from finalizers that succeeded; when a finalizer throws, its result is not added and subsequent finalizers do not run.

Finalizers sit at the session boundary after all selected apply calls finish and before the root group attaches to the host tree. Use them for one-off derived registrations or whole-session summaries, not per-definition member registration that can happen inside each definition's apply. Businesses with zero definitions (e.g., zero bogeys) should allow finalizers to produce an empty/no-op derived result cleanly.

docs.title: Process-Wide Finalizer Hooks
docs.text:
DataDrivenBuildHooks allows extensions to register finalizers outside the host provider:

DataDrivenBuildHooks.registerFinalizer(
        "example",
        (context, content) -> content.claims().size()
);

List<BuildFinalizer> finalizers =
        DataDrivenBuildHooks.finalizersFor("example");

Hooks are bucketed by hostModId in thread-safe lists and have no unregister API. Initialization code must guard against registering the same finalizer repeatedly on reloads or repeated calls.

The pipeline itself does not automatically query DataDrivenBuildHooks; the provider or host must fetch finalizersFor(hostModId) and pass them to the pipeline constructor.

docs.title: RegistrationTarget
docs.text:
Default target:

RegistrationTarget.standard()

Custom target example:

RegistrationTarget target = (host, root, options) ->
        new MyRegBuildContext(host, root, options.isStrict(), hostServices);

The target must return a RegBuildContext. If createContext throws due to unavailable services or resources, build wraps the exception as APPLY_FAILED and returns FAILED with no definitions applied.

This wraps context creation only; adhering to the host/root contract inside the custom context remains the target implementation's responsibility.

docs.title: Host Provider
docs.text:
DataDrivenRegistrationProvider is the per-mod takeover point:

@FunctionalInterface
public interface DataDrivenRegistrationProvider {
    JsonRegistryGroup build(String hostModId);
}

Installation:

public final class ExamplePacks {
    private static DataDrivenRegistrationProviders.Attachment attachment;

    public static void install(PipelineServices services) {
        attachment = DataDrivenRegistrationProviders.install(
                ExampleMod.MOD_ID,
                hostModId -> buildRoot(hostModId, services)
        );
    }

    private static JsonRegistryGroup buildRoot(
            String hostModId,
            PipelineServices services
    ) {
        List<ContentSource> sources = services.openFixedSources();
        PreparedContent prepared;
        try {
            prepared = services.pipeline().prepare(
                    sources,
                    BuildOptions.STRICT,
                    services.dependencies()
            );
        } finally {
            services.closeSources(sources);
        }

        BuildResult result = services.pipeline().build(prepared);
        services.report(result.diagnostics());
        if (!result.successful()) {
            return null;
        }
        services.commitRegisteredRoots(result, prepared);
        return result.rootGroup();
    }
}

This example assumes openFixedSources() opens independent SnapshotContentSource instances via FixedResourceSource.capture(). Real hosts should retain and close the Attachment for test isolation or explicit teardown. Calling install a second time for the same host without closing the prior attachment throws IllegalStateException; Attachment.close() removes only its own registration instance.

Providers must be installed before JsonTreeIntegration's registration callback executes. Returning null mounts no JSON root; exceptions thrown by a provider propagate directly out of the registration callback.

docs.title: JsonTreeIntegration Dispatch Compatibility
docs.text:
On each mod registration dispatch:

DataDrivenRegistrationProvider provider =
        DataDrivenRegistrationProviders.find(modId).orElse(null);

if (provider != null) {
    JsonRegistryGroup root = provider.build(modId);
    if (root != null) modRegistry.addChild(root);
    return;
}

try {
    JsonRegistryGroup root = JsonTreeBuilder.buildForMod(modId);
    if (root != null) modRegistry.addChild(root);
} catch (Exception failure) {
    LOGGER.error("Failed to load JSON registrations for mod '{}'", modId, failure);
}

The try/catch in JsonTreeIntegration wraps only the buildForMod fallback. The provider branch must handle its own exceptions and diagnostics.

Because the standard pipeline copies parsed definitions into PreparedContent, a provider may close its sources immediately after prepare. If custom definitions defer reading from sources, the provider and handler must coordinate closure timing; build is unaware of source lifetimes. Resource pack publication should likewise wait until successful(), pack rejection closure, and dependency checks complete so rejected roots never leak into the Approved resource stack.

docs.title: Legacy JsonTreeBuilder
docs.text:
When no provider is installed:

  • JsonTreeBuilder locates the mod file via ModList;
  • Scans data/<mod>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/ inside the mod JAR;
  • Parses in index filename, manifest array, and content array order;
  • Deduplicates with DuplicateIdResolver (last-wins) before apply;
  • Uses global handlers from TypeHandlerRegistry;
  • Uses two-argument resolveIdentity(modId, definition) legacy identity rules, including the minecraft: to host namespace compatibility rewrite;
  • Uses Gson tolerant parsing without the new pipeline's strict JSON, claims, or finalizer support;
  • Records exceptions during apply into the mod's loading-error bucket;
  • Returns a single-source JsonRegistryGroup.

The legacy entry point suits single-mod JARs that need no cross-source claim preflight. It does not provide:

  • Multi-owner dependency declarations;
  • Strict source priority;
  • Enforcement of validate and claims;
  • Full preflight against reserved registry claims;
  • Custom provider sources or finalizers.

Even after migrating to the new pipeline, JsonTreeBuilder.parseIndexManifest, resolveIndexManifests, and parseContentBody remain useful as pure-JVM schema test helpers.

docs.title: Recommended Host Flow
docs.text:
1. Install the provider early during mod construction;
  2. Collect existing code registrations to build reserved claims;
  3. Capture ResourceSnapshots from the host's frozen roots and wrap main/parcel/shared views with ContentSourceFactory.snapshot(...);
  4. Assign globally unique ranks to every (sourceId, rootId) and order sources by rank;
  5. Declare direct owner dependencies;
  6. Run STRICT prepare;
  7. Write diagnostics to the host report;
  8. Do not call build or mount a root when blocking errors exist;
  9. Commit only APPLIED roots after build;
  10. Publish the corresponding ApprovedResourcePacks / MC pack layers only after the final approved root set is settled;
  11. Persist BuildResult, source/root ordering, manifest paths, and claims for startup consistency checks across restarts.

docs.title: Factories, Registry Groups, and Host Integration
docs.text: TypeHandler interprets JSON structure, while FactoryRegistry turns type and params into Reg nodes. Registry groups provide property inheritance, RegistryGroup handles runtime dispatch, and the host projects the same fixed ResourceSnapshot into both registration ContentSource views and MC Approved pack layers.

docs.title: FactoryRegistry
docs.text:
FactoryRegistry lives in core and is shared by data-driven and host mods:

FactoryRegistry.register("panel_block", factory, true);
FactoryRegistry.registerItem("manual_item", itemFactory);
FactoryRegistry.registerBlockEntity("panel_be", blockEntityFactory);
FactoryRegistry.registerGeneric("custom_type", genericFactory);

Source: FactoryRegistry.java.

Category Registration Query Block register(type, factory[, createsBlockItem]) get, contains, createsBlockItem Item registerItem getItemFactory, containsItem Block entity registerBlockEntity getBlockEntityFactory, containsBlockEntity, getBlockEntityTypes Generic registerGeneric getGeneric, containsGeneric

Each table is a process-wide ConcurrentHashMap. Registering the same type again silently replaces the old factory, and there is no namespace isolation. Prefix custom type names with your mod id, and register factories during @Context bean initialization before the first prepare. Calls such as register and registerBlockEntity are independent rather than transactional; failing partway through leaves earlier types registered.

Factory params is an open JSON object:

Reg<?, Block> create(String id, @Nullable JsonObject params);
Reg<?, Item> create(String id, @Nullable JsonObject params);
Reg<?, ?> create(
        String id,
        Supplier<Block[]> validBlocks,
        @Nullable JsonObject params
);

Each factory defines its own parameter keys. STRICT mode checks whether a factory exists and implements a given Java capability interface, but cannot validate private params schemas inside individual factories.

FactoryRegistry has no production unregister or reload API. Replacing a factory dynamically immediately affects subsequent validate and apply calls, so all factory registration should finish before startup builds and must never depend on resource pack state during /reload.

docs.title: Block Factories and Default Block Items
docs.text:
Data-driven blocks commonly create both a block and a block item:

@SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
private static <T extends Block> Reg<?, Block> blockWithItem(
        String id,
        Function<BlockBehaviour.Properties, T> blockSupplier
) {
    return (Reg<?, Block>) (Reg<?, ?>)
            BlockReg.of(id, blockSupplier).withDefaultBlockItem(id);
}

FactoryRegistry.register(
        "panel_block",
        (id, params) -> blockWithItem(id, PanelBlock::new),
        true
);

The third boolean argument records a factory capability flag rather than reflecting over the returned Reg:

  • true: built-in BlockTypeHandler.claims also claims minecraft:item with the same id as the block;
  • false: claims the block only;
  • Re-registering the same type with false clears the previously recorded item capability.

If a factory calls withDefaultBlockItem yet registers with false (or omits the flag), STRICT mode misses that item claim. Conversely, passing true when no block item is created causes claims to diverge from the actual registration tree.

The built-in BlockTypeHandler derivation covers only the convention where a block item shares the block's id. If a factory creates a different item id via withBlockItem, or creates multiple items, write a dedicated handler to declare exact claims—the boolean flag alone cannot express those relationships.

docs.title: Derived Claims
docs.text:
BlockTypeHandler.claims emits:

minecraft:block / <effective block id>
plus when createsBlockItem is true:
minecraft:item / <effective block id>

ItemTypeHandler emits only:

minecraft:item / <effective item id>

BlockEntityTypeHandler derives:

minecraft:block_entity_type / <block namespace>:<block path>_be

If a factory also registers creative tabs, menus, entities, or fluids as child entries, built-in handlers cannot see those children. Implement a dedicated TypeHandler or provide host-level reserved/derived claim tracking when full coverage is required.

RegTypeHandler.claims reads the final id from the active DefinitionKey, keeping block and item claims aligned with the STRICT or LEGACY apply identity rules: explicit minecraft: stays minecraft: in STRICT and rewrites to the host namespace in LEGACY.

docs.title: Factories with State Properties
docs.text:
Blocks declaring state_properties require a factory implementing StatefulBlockFactory:

FactoryRegistry.register(
        "stateful_panel",
        (StatefulBlockFactory) (id, params, states) ->
                blockWithItem(id, properties ->
                        StatePropertyContext.construct(
                                states,
                                () -> new StatefulPanelBlock(properties)
                        )),
        true
);

The block class must:

  1. Add JSON properties in createBlockStateDefinition;
  2. Apply JSON default values via StatePropertyContext.applyDefaults;
  3. Forward StateProperty hooks if change listeners or synchronization are needed.

See Block-State Properties for the complete API.

docs.title: Built-in Factories
docs.text:
Built-in factories in the current source tree:

  • data_driven_block: plain stateful block factory. JsonTreeBuilder.ensureHandlersRegistered() calls DataDrivenBlockFactory.registerIfAbsent() to register it; new pipelines that skip that initialization entry must register it explicitly.
  • fsm_block: FSM block factory in modelling, registered with createsBlockItem = true.
  • fsm_be: FSM block entity factory reading state_machine, model, and model_name.
  • contentTesting fixtures such as simple_block, simple_item, and test_be, which are not shipped for downstream consumption.

fsm_block and fsm_be are registered by FsmBlockEntityFactories.registerBuiltin(). Production code does not invoke that initializer automatically; tests and game tests call it explicitly. Any host using those two types in a real registration flow must invoke it before prepare. Third-party mods should register their own factories and never depend on contentTesting types as a stable API.

docs.title: RegistryGroup Property Inheritance
docs.text:
Reg.applyProperties executes parent-first:

JSON root
  → parent registry_group
  → child registry_group
  → concrete block/item

Child groups therefore override parent groups, and concrete blocks or items override groups. The parent chain in RegistryGroupHandler governs property inheritance, independently of the runtime predicate on RegistryGroup.dispatchWhen.

Creative tab (tab) resolution follows a separate rule:

  1. If the block or item declares its own tab, use that value;
  2. Otherwise, check the tab stored directly on its referenced registry_group;
  3. To inherit a tab, declare it explicitly on the group referenced by the content entry rather than expecting parent group tabs to cascade automatically.

docs.title: RegistryGroup Dispatch
docs.text:
Registry root = new Registry("example");

RegistryGroup coreRuntime = new RegistryGroup().setParent(root);
RegistryGroup coreData = new RegistryGroup()
        .dispatchWhen(state::isCorePackEnabled)
        .setParent(root);

// runtime code registrations
new RuntimeOnlyReg().setParent(coreRuntime);

// JSON and optional code registrations owned by the pack
new PackOnlyReg().setParent(coreData);

dispatchWhen stores a BooleanSupplier evaluated on every RegistryGroup.dispatchRegister:

if (predicate.getAsBoolean()) {
    super.dispatchRegister(context);
}

When the predicate returns false:

  • The group's own register does not run;
  • None of its child nodes execute;
  • The subtree remains attached in the in-memory registration tree;
  • The predicate may flip to true later, and subsequent dispatches traverse the subtree normally.

Calling dispatchWhen again replaces the previous predicate rather than composing them.

Dispatch predicates never delete nodes or alter parent/child links. Because RegistryClaimSnapshot.collect skips groups whose predicate returns false along with their subtrees, disabled code registrations do not claim reserved slots; once the predicate returns true, later snapshots include them again.

Runtime exceptions thrown by a predicate abort that dispatch pass, so predicates should remain simple and side-effect-free.

docs.title: JsonRegistryGroup
docs.text:
DataDrivenBuildPipeline creates:

new JsonRegistryGroup(hostModId + ":json_root")

and installs the default namespace mapping on it:

root.withProperty(
        ResourceLocation.class,
        location -> ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(
                hostModId,
                location.getPath()
        )
);

In LEGACY mode, RegTypeHandler attaches a per-registration mapping only when the explicit namespace is not minecraft, so minecraft:path continues to resolve under the host namespace. In STRICT mode, any explicit namespace (including minecraft) installs its own mapping so the final id matches EffectiveId.of. This behavior is governed by RegBuildContext.isStrict().

JsonRegistryGroup supports setParent and dispatchWhen just like any RegistryGroup; hosts adjusting it between DataDrivenBuildPipeline.build returning and attaching it to the mod root should keep their lifecycle and predicated-group policy explicit.

docs.title: Combining Built-in and Custom Handlers
docs.text:
The new pipeline takes an explicit handler list. To reuse the library's built-in types:

JsonTreeBuilder.ensureHandlersRegistered();

List<TypeHandler<?>> handlers = new ArrayList<>();
handlers.addAll(TypeHandlerRegistry.all());
handlers.add(new PanelModeHandler());

DataDrivenBuildPipeline pipeline = new DataDrivenBuildPipeline(
        ExampleMod.MOD_ID,
        handlers,
        finalizers
);

Because TypeHandlerRegistry is process-wide, multiple mods registering custom types under the same name would overwrite one another. Production extensions are safer passing custom handler instances directly into the host's pipeline list with source-prefixed type names.

docs.title: Coexistence of Code and Data Registrations
docs.text:
Registry modRegistry = new Registry("example");
RegistryGroup runtime = new RegistryGroup().setParent(modRegistry);
RegistryGroup data = new RegistryGroup()
        .dispatchWhen(packState::dataEnabled)
        .setParent(modRegistry);

jsonRoot.setParent(data);

Recommended boundaries:

  • Place Java classes, shared gameplay logic, and fixed infrastructure in runtime;
  • Place pack-togglable default entries and pack-snapshot-dependent code registrations in data;
  • Ensure registry groups, JSON handlers, and factories are registered before build;
  • Include in reserved claims only code entries that could actually collide with JSON entries;
  • Never rebuild Java registry groups during /reload asset refreshes.

docs.title: Resource Packs and ResourceManager
docs.text:
Fixed sources, registration views, Reg, and Minecraft resource packs form four distinct layers:

Layer Role ResourceSnapshot Fixes actual bytes, URIs, revisions, and root identity from startup sources ContentSource Reads manifests and JSON from a single concrete snapshot/root Reg tree Creates Java/Minecraft registry entries during registry events Resource pack Provides assets, data, models, textures, language files, and reload JSON during resource reloads

A host typically coordinates all four:

  1. Pin each pack/root as an independent snapshot with non-shared close lifetimes, then expose it to DataDrivenBuildPipeline via ContentSourceFactory.snapshot(...);
  2. Construct MappedPackResources / Approved pack layers from the same root set and ranks during pack discovery;
  3. Ensure valid pack.mcmeta, assets/, and data/ layouts;
  4. Keep MC pack priority consistent with ResourceSourceDescriptor.rank override semantics;
  5. Ship resource packs even for Java-only registered blocks/items so models, textures, and translations are not missing.

ApprovedResourcePacks.register(id, sources, routing) retains the provided ResourceSource list and calls source.capture() on each AddPackFindersEvent discovery. Production code should pass FixedResourceSource instances; passing live directory or archive sources causes discovery to re-read changing install directories. Each source/root yields a separate MappedPackResources layer opening files via snapshot leases rather than flattening multiple layers into one "last-winner directory".

MappedPackResources projects only pack.mcmeta, pack.png, assets/, and data/, synthesizing runtime metadata for the active PackType when pack.mcmeta is omitted. ApprovedResourcePacks orders pack generation by rank, while final per-file resolution still follows Minecraft's active ResourceManager.

ResourceSystem wraps client and server native ResourceManager instances in ScopedResourceManager. ReloadOrchestrator registers as a listener via ScopedResourceManagerConsumer and executes:

reload(scopedResourceManager.getResourceManager());

Reload therefore reads from Minecraft's active pack stack:

  • Higher-priority resource/data packs override lower-priority files at the same namespace and path;
  • Disabled packs are absent from ResourceManager;
  • getResourceStack resolves active pack-stack files (with ManagedReloadAllowlist filtering authorized layers for managed packs);
  • /reload updates state machines and clip buckets, never block or item registries.

Both the registration view and MC pack projection should reference the same frozen snapshot/root. Because MappedPackResources bridges captured bytes directly, v2 needs no second authoritative materialized cache directory on disk; any optional persistent cache a host builds must act strictly as an acceleration copy for capture, never a second source of truth read separately by registration and resource discovery.

rank defines platform-layer order, but ResourceSystem does not decide which packs are enabled in business terms. The host must derive both the registration source list and the Approved pack list from the same frozen selection, and must not publish a user pack into the resource stack if registration rejects it.

docs.title: Startup Consistency
docs.text:
Consider persisting the following in reports or SavedData:

  • Enabled pack IDs and versions;
  • Concrete (sourceId, rootId) list and global ranks;
  • Manifest logical paths;
  • Prepared claims;
  • Build status;
  • Key diagnostic codes.

If a world restarts with a different enabled pack set, previously saved registry entries may be missing, causing old block or item data in the world to be lost or fall back. Hosts should compare historical snapshots against the new snapshot before server start and reject incompatible worlds. KasugaLib's data-driven layer supplies the build and claim data; the host defines world compatibility policy.

docs.title: Troubleshooting and Migration
docs.text: Data-driven failures typically fall into four layers: whether files reached the source, whether manifests are valid, whether handlers and schemas match, and whether final claims conflict. Narrowing by layer is far faster than debugging "nothing loaded".

docs.title: Identify Which Registration Entry Point Ran
docs.text:
Symptom Diagnosis Logs contain host-recorded PreparedContent, BuildResult, or diagnostic codes Host provider + multi-source pipeline Logs contain Loaded N JSON entries ... for mod Legacy JsonTreeBuilder Neither appears No index, provider not installed, mod did not dispatch registration, or zero content

The pipeline itself does not enforce a fixed startup log line; confirm whether the new pipeline is active by checking provider registration and structured BuildDiagnostic outputs rather than relying on a single log message.

For the legacy entry point, check for:

No data-driven index directory for mod '<id>'
Loaded ... JSON entries ... for mod '<id>'
Failed to load JSON registrations for mod '<id>'

For the new pipeline, inspect what the host recorded from:

PreparedContent.sources()
PreparedContent.registerFiles()
PreparedContent.reloadFiles()
PreparedContent.definitions()
PreparedContent.claims()
PreparedContent.diagnostics()

PreparedContent is the authoritative snapshot of startup state. When "the file clearly exists on disk but did not load", inspect the sources and logical paths recorded there instead of assuming resource pack paths match.

If partial definitions from a source already parsed before enumeration or reading throws, prepare retains the earlier results and appends SOURCE_READ_FAILED. STRICT rejects the whole batch; LEGACY may proceed to apply, so the presence of some definitions does not mean the entire source loaded cleanly.

docs.title: Zero Definitions Loaded
docs.text:
Check in order:

  1. SourceDescriptor.namespaces includes the namespace in data/<ns>;
  2. SnapshotContentSource.declaredIndexes includes the actual manifest paths, or a standard source places manifests directly under data/<ns>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/;
  3. Manifests declare on_register rather than the removed sources field;
  4. Content paths are relative to data/<ns>/;
  5. Content files actually exist inside the same source/root snapshot;
  6. Neither the ContentSource, FixedResourceSource, nor underlying ResourceSnapshot was closed/retired early;
  7. The provider was installed before the first registration dispatch.

The new pipeline permits sources with zero manifests, so "0 definitions" is not inherently an error; confirm assets/data-only packs via registerFiles().isEmpty() and host expectations.

For main/parcel train packs, also verify:

  • main and every parcel have distinct rootId values;
  • rootId contains no colons;
  • Ranks across all packs and roots are globally unique;
  • Each parcel declares only its own indexes, and main does not accidentally sweep in undeclared parcel indexes;
  • Registration and Approved pack projection read from the same frozen roots.

docs.title: INVALID_SOURCE
docs.text:
INVALID_SOURCE covers more than a duplicate sourceId. In v2, it checks:

Duplicate (sourceId, rootId)
Duplicate global rank

Having main, parcel-m1, and parcel-m2 under the same sourceId is valid as long as rootId distinguishes them. Every root must also carry a unique rank rather than restarting from 0 per pack.

docs.title: MANIFEST_INVALID
docs.text:
Check item by item:

  • Only on_register and on_reload are allowed at top level;
  • Values must be JSON arrays of strings;
  • At least one domain must be declared (empty arrays are legal);
  • Every path must be relative, slash-separated, and end with .json;
  • No path may appear in both domains.

Manifest diagnostics are always ERROR. LEGACY builds may proceed anyway, but a result carrying MANIFEST_INVALID must never be treated as healthy.

STRICT also rejects duplicate JSON keys, comments, trailing commas, extra top-level documents, malformed UTF-8, nesting deeper than 64 levels, and documents exceeding 100,000 nodes. Regenerate invalid files as standard JSON rather than relying on Gson's lenient parser.

docs.title: SOURCE_FILE_MISSING
docs.text:
Manifest paths are anchored at data/<ns>/:

manifest: "content/blocks.json"
physical: data/example/content/blocks.json

Writing "data/example/content/blocks.json" causes the loader to look up data/example/data/example/content/blocks.json.

Also check path casing and allowed characters. Registration ContentSource allows broader JVM/filesystem filenames, whereas runtime reload must construct a ResourceLocation ([a-z0-9/._-]); DataDrivenBuildPipeline's reload preflight does not check ResourceLocation character rules for you.

docs.title: UNKNOWN_TYPE
docs.text:
The registration phase and reload phase use separate handler sets:

Content Correct Manifest Domain Correct Top-Level Key Blocks / items / groups on_register blocks, items, registry_groups Block entity on_register Embedded blocks[].block_entity State machine on_reload or state_machines/ glob state_machines Animation clip on_reload animation_clips

Common mistakes:

  • Writing block_entities as a top-level field;
  • Running prepare before reload handlers are installed;
  • Listing registration files under on_reload;
  • Listing reload files under on_register.

docs.title: UNKNOWN_FACTORY
docs.text:
The type value is not registered in FactoryRegistry:

FactoryRegistry.contains(type)
FactoryRegistry.containsItem(type)
FactoryRegistry.containsBlockEntity(type)

Ensure factory beans initialize before the first prepare. Never rely on contentTesting factories as release APIs in production.

data_driven_block is registered on demand only when JsonTreeBuilder.ensureHandlersRegistered() runs; fsm_block and fsm_be require the host to call FsmBlockEntityFactories.registerBuiltin(). Handler lists on the new pipeline and FactoryRegistry are initialized independently.

docs.title: UNKNOWN_REGISTRY_GROUP
docs.text:
Group references match verbatim by raw string:

{"registry_group": "example:panels"}

must match:

{"id": "example:panels"}

panels and example:panels do not match. If the group belongs to another owner, an explicit owner dependency is also required.

docs.title: REFERENCE_NOT_DECLARED
docs.text:
The referenced definition exists in the session, but the current owner cannot see it:

Map.of("addon_owner", Set.of("core_owner"))

Dependencies are direct only. If A references C while A depends only on B and B depends on C, validation still fails; A must declare C directly.

docs.title: MISSING_REFERENCE
docs.text:
No definition with that DefinitionKey exists anywhere in the session. Check:

  • Whether the handler type domain matches;
  • Whether the identity carries a namespace or underwent EffectiveId;
  • Whether the referenced definition failed during parse and never entered the directory;
  • Whether a registry id was passed where a configuration identity was expected.

docs.title: INVALID_IDENTITY
docs.text:
Built-in blocks and items require an explicit namespace in STRICT mode:

"id": "example:panel"

Do not write:

"id": "panel"

The legacy JsonTreeBuilder rewrites bare IDs into the host namespace, whereas strict external packs require full IDs for preflight, reporting, and cross-source diagnostics. Note that the two identity paths treat minecraft: differently:

JsonTreeBuilder: minecraft:panel -> <hostModId>:panel
STRICT:          minecraft:panel -> minecraft:panel

A STRICT pack writing minecraft: genuinely claims the vanilla namespace. For bare panel, resolveIdentity temporarily produces <hostModId>:panel, and validate then rejects it with INVALID_IDENTITY. DataDrivenBuildPipeline selects the identity rule via BuildOptions; new packs should use STRICT and trace anomalies along resolveIdentity -> validate -> apply -> claims.

Built-in block and item claims read the final ID from DefinitionKey. Explicit minecraft:panel keeps minecraft:panel across DefinitionKey, claims, and apply in STRICT, whereas LEGACY maps all three to the host namespace.

Embedded block entities have no id of their own. Their validation inspects _parent_block injected by extractEmbedded, so the host block's id must likewise be an explicit namespace:path.

docs.title: CLAIM_CONFLICT
docs.text:
Two definitions—or a definition and a host code registration—compete for the same final registry key:

(minecraft:block, example:panel)
(minecraft:item, example:panel)

Check:

  • Whether two sources wrote different JSON IDs that resolved to the same key after namespace mapping;
  • Whether a block factory declared createsBlockItem = true;
  • Whether a standalone item shares an id with an auto-generated block item;
  • Whether the host's reserved snapshot includes all existing code registrations;
  • Whether an external source should have been excluded via disabled packs.

LEGACY may record only a warning and continue into unsafe Minecraft registry behavior. Production multi-source setups should always use STRICT.

docs.title: HANDLER_NOT_STRICT_READY
docs.text:
A handler is missing:

HandlerCapability.STRICT_PREFLIGHT

or strictValidationImplemented() returning true, or does not declare exactly one of:

HandlerCapability.NON_REGISTRATION
HandlerCapability.REGISTRY_CLAIMS

It can also indicate duplicate typeName() values in the pipeline's handler list.

docs.title: GROUP_CYCLE
docs.text: Two or more registry_groups.parent edges form a cycle. Break one parent link or extract an acyclic shared parent group.

docs.title: VALIDATION_FAILED
docs.text: A handler's validate method threw an unexpected RuntimeException. Expected content problems should be reported through ValidationContext.error/warning; only programming or invariant errors belong under VALIDATION_FAILED. Check whether validate attempted to access an uninitialized global service.

docs.title: APPLY_FAILED
docs.text:
Even after prepare passes, a factory or apply can still fail. Common causes:

  • A factory depends on an unregistered deferred holder;
  • A group id is missing from apply metadata;
  • Type casting failure;
  • Factory parameters fail object construction invariants;
  • Host services are unavailable during context creation.

Failures may occur after some definitions have already applied. Hosts should not mount a FAILED root unless partial side effects are explicitly proven safe.

If context creation fails, no definition has applied; if sorting, definition apply, or a finalizer fails, partial side effects may already exist. BuildResult.Status and finalizerResults describe execution progress only and cannot roll back process-wide caches.

docs.title: FINALIZER_FAILED
docs.text: All selected definitions applied, and a finalizer failed afterward. Fix the finalizer or make it diagnosable and idempotent. BuildResult.finalizerResults contains only the values returned before the failure.

docs.title: Provider Appears Inactive
docs.text:
Check:

  • install uses the exact modRegistry.getModId() string;
  • install runs before the registration callback executes;
  • No test or earlier instance left an active Attachment on the same hostModId;
  • The provider's source build did not return null;
  • The provider did not throw an exception;
  • The returned root is mounted only when result.successful().

If a provider returns null, JsonTreeIntegration does not fall back to the legacy JAR scan; the provider has already taken ownership of that host.

docs.title: Reload Content Does Not Update
docs.text:
Check on_reload:

  • Whether the pack is actually enabled in the active pack stack during /reload;
  • Whether the handler's typeName() is registered in ReloadHandlerRegistry;
  • Whether the pack provides that exact logical path;
  • Whether Decoded.errors() is non-empty;
  • Whether a later-loaded file overrode the identity via last-wins;
  • Whether a script-bucket entry is shadowing the resource entry.

state_machines files omitted from manifests can still be discovered via directory glob (for unmanaged packs), whereas animation_clips must be listed under on_reload.

docs.title: Java Content Registered, but Models or Translations Missing
docs.text:
Reg handles Java registries only. Provide:

assets/<ns>/blockstates/<block>.json
assets/<ns>/models/block/<block>.json
assets/<ns>/models/item/<item>.json
assets/<ns>/textures/...
assets/<ns>/lang/en_us.json

and ensure the resource pack reaches the client's ResourceManager.

docs.title: Data Pack Override Order Diverges from Source Order
docs.text:
Platform rank governs data-driven prepare/build order and ApprovedResourcePacks layer generation, while Minecraft's ResourceManager still determines runtime resource selection. Derive all of the following from a single frozen selection:

  • main/parcel/shared ContentSource ordering;
  • PackResources registration and ranking;
  • Recorded active packs;
  • Client and server consistency.

If registration and resource projection independently re-scan the install directory, re-assign ranks, or use different disabled sets, you can end up with "Java registration succeeded but models are missing" or "assets from a rejected pack remain visible". Compare the (sourceId, rootId, rank) lists on both sides first.

docs.title: Existing World Missing Blocks or Items After Restart
docs.text: Once the registered set changes, IDs saved inside existing worlds may no longer exist. KasugaLib provides prepared claims and build results, while world compatibility policy belongs to the host. Compare the historical pack set and claims before loading a world and refuse startup when entries are missing or replaced.

docs.title: Registration
docs.text:
• DataDrivenBuildPipeline: structured BuildDiagnostics residing strictly on PreparedContent and BuildResult;
  • Legacy entry point: JsonTreeBuilder.getLoadingErrors(modId) / Diagnostics.errors(modId);
  • In-game command: /kasuga_data errors [mod].

docs.title: Reload
docs.text:
• Logs carrying handler, file, and namespace context;
  • Diagnostics.Domain.RELOAD_DATA;
  • /kasuga_data errors [namespace] displays both registration errors and reload entries for that namespace.

Build diagnostics from the new pipeline are not forwarded automatically into Diagnostics. Providers should emit them to host reports, logs, or custom outlets.

Runtime reload manifest parsing reuses the legacy manifest parser, so manifest schema errors land in the legacy per-mod compatibility error bucket, whereas file decode, unknown top-level keys, and register failures land in RELOAD_DATA. RELOAD_DATA clears on every cycle, while the per-mod compatibility bucket is not cleared by the reload cycle. Command permission level is 2.

Suggested triage order by code:

Code Check First INVALID_SOURCE Duplicate (sourceId, rootId) or duplicate global rank (also recorded as ERROR in LEGACY) UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY Misspelled dependency owner, or missing source for that owner MANIFEST_INVALID / MANIFEST_EMPTY Top-level fields, array types, dual-domain listing, at least one domain declared INVALID_PATH / SOURCE_FILE_MISSING Relative to data/<ns>/, .json suffix, traversal segments, actual file presence SOURCE_READ_FAILED Missing file, mid-capture mutation or limit exceeded, closed ZIP/directory handle UNKNOWN_TYPE Registration vs. reload file in the wrong manifest domain, or handler not installed PARSE_FAILED / CONTENT_INVALID Element codec, required fields, array shape, strict property validation MISSING_IDENTITY / INVALID_IDENTITY resolveIdentity output and explicit namespace on built-in handlers HANDLER_NOT_STRICT_READY Duplicate type names, or missing STRICT_PREFLIGHT, strictValidationImplemented(), or unique role CLAIM_FAILED / CLAIM_CONFLICT Unreported handler claims, final (registry, id) collision, reserved snapshot APPLY_FAILED / FINALIZER_FAILED Factory initialization, context services, partial side effects already executed

docs.title: 1. Standardize Indexes
docs.text:
Migrate from the legacy flat layout to:

data/<ns>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/

Rename sources to on_register and move reload content to on_reload, keeping all paths relative to data/<ns>/.

Typical migration:

Old: data/example/kasugalib/blocks.json
New: data/example/kasuga_lib/data_driven/main.json
     data/example/kasuga_content/blocks.json

{
  "on_register": ["kasuga_content/blocks.json"],
  "on_reload": ["animation_clips/wheels.json"]
}

state_machines/ can still rely on directory glob discovery (in unmanaged packs), while animation_clips/ must be listed explicitly under on_reload. The legacy kasugalib/ directory is no longer read.

docs.title: 2. Choose an Entry Point
docs.text: Requirement Entry Point Single mod JAR, no multi-source overrides, no strict claims Legacy JsonTreeBuilder Multiple built-in or external packs, dependencies, strict conflict checks, finalizers Provider + DataDrivenBuildPipeline

docs.title: 3. Design Sources and Owners
docs.text: Assign stable sourceId, ownerId, namespaces, and globally unique rank per pack, and stable rootIds for each main, parcel, or shared root without passing colon-containing business parcel IDs as rootId. Keep "which ZIP a file came from" (sourceId) distinct from "which dependency unit owns it" (ownerId).

docs.title: 4. Declare Dependencies
docs.text: Convert actual cross-owner references into the dependencies map. Dependencies are never inferred from content paths, namespaces, or source order.

docs.title: 5. Make Handlers STRICT-Ready
docs.text:
• Registration types: declare STRICT_PREFLIGHT + REGISTRY_CLAIMS;
  • Configuration types: declare STRICT_PREFLIGHT + NON_REGISTRATION;
  • Override strictValidationImplemented() to return true;
  • Implement side-effect-free validate;
  • Declare every final registry entry in claims;
  • Implement deterministic parentDefinition.

Install handlers and factories explicitly before the first prepare. Call JsonTreeBuilder.ensureHandlersRegistered() to reuse built-in registration handlers and data_driven_block, call FsmBlockEntityFactories.registerBuiltin() if using FSM factories, and register custom handlers and factories directly in your pipeline and FactoryRegistry.

docs.title: 6. Collect Reserved Claims
docs.text:
Collect host code registrations before build:

Set<RegistryClaim.RegistryKey> reserved =
        RegistryClaimSnapshot.collect(hostRoot);

or supply an equivalent complete set of reserved registry keys.

docs.title: 7. Wire the Provider
docs.text:
Install the provider before registration dispatch. Inside the provider:

  • Open fixed sources;
  • Run STRICT prepare;
  • Record diagnostics;
  • Run build only when no blocking errors exist;
  • Mount only APPLIED roots;
  • Persist source order, claims, and status.

docs.title: 8. Wire Resource Packs
docs.text: Build Approved pack layers from the same fixed root set with matching source/root ranks. Publish resources only after strict preflight, rejected-pack closure, and build succeed—never add all packs to the resource stack before the provider finishes its checks.

docs.title: 9. Verify
docs.text:
Recommended verification layers:

  • JsonTreeBuilder.parseContentBody / parseIndexManifest: pure schema rules;
  • DataDrivenBuildPipelineTest-style fixtures: multi-source, strict mode, claims;
  • JUnit suites for data-driven and core;
  • FML / game tests: real registry events;
  • Dedicated server: startup with no client dependencies;
  • Client: models, textures, language files, and /reload;
  • Existing world: registry-set changes and history guard.

Common commands:

./gradlew :modules:data-driven:test :modules:core:test --console=plain
./gradlew :modules:modelling:modelUnitTest --console=plain

docs.title: Current Documentation Boundaries and Implementation Gaps
docs.text:
The following behaviors are verified in source code, without framework-level automated enforcement:

  1. DataDrivenBuildPipeline's reload preflight does not run globDirectories() discovery, so state machine files omitted from manifests are discovered only by the runtime orchestrator.
  2. FactoryRegistry, legacy TypeHandlerRegistry, and ReloadHandlerRegistry are process-wide global tables with last-registration-wins overwrite and no production unregister API.
  3. DataDrivenRegistrationProviders allows one provider per host with no layered composition.
  4. DataDrivenBuildHooks has no unregister API; repeated initialization can register duplicate finalizers.
  5. Claim registry names are plain strings with no centralized registry-key validation.
  6. build has no transactional rollback; FAILED may leave context or finalizer side effects behind.
  7. BuildDiagnostic.Stage.SELECTION is declared on the enum, while the current pipeline does not emit diagnostics directly under that stage.
  8. Legacy Directory/ZIP ContentSource adapters fix file lists or hold open handles rather than process-wide frozen bytes; use FixedResourceSource + ResourceSnapshot whenever registration, discovery, and reload must share frozen input.
  9. The library does not register resource or data packs automatically; pack discovery, physical path support, and override ordering are host-implemented.
  10. The built-in block handler derives only the same-id block item claim; other child registry entries created by custom factories require dedicated handlers or host claim tracking.
  11. World save compatibility policies, pack history, and missing-pack rejection logic belong to the host.
  12. ValidationContext.find(key) delegates to findAllVisible(key) and returns a definition only when exactly one visible candidate exists, while canReference(key) checks whether at least one visible candidate exists; handlers needing custom selection across multiple visible candidates should inspect findAllVisible(key) directly.
  13. The new pipeline does not auto-install TypeHandlers or factories. Reusing built-ins requires calling JsonTreeBuilder.ensureHandlersRegistered(), and FSM factories require the host to call FsmBlockEntityFactories.registerBuiltin().
  14. Source preparation exceptions are isolated per source rather than transactional; paths, candidates, and definitions already parsed before the failure remain in that prepare session.
  15. Pipeline reload preflight does not construct ResourceLocation instances, so runtime reload can still reject a preflighted on_reload path for uppercase letters or illegal characters.
  16. Runtime reload manifest parsing reuses the legacy per-mod error bucket; RELOAD_DATA covers only diagnostics raised directly by ReloadOrchestrator and reload handlers.
  17. Unused keys in the dependencies map that match no source owner do not emit a standalone diagnostic.
  18. SnapshotContentSource.declaredIndexes filters only indexes(), neither pruning readable files nor validating index paths; the host must validate declared entry paths and parcel mappings itself.
  19. DataDrivenBuildPipeline's BuildDiagnostic has no parcelId field; hosts must enrich train-pack reports from their frozen (sourceId, rootId) mapping.
  20. If a registration provider does not share a commit boundary with Approved pack discovery, rejected sources can enter the MC resource stack prematurely; publication must happen after final registration selection.
  21. DataDrivenBuildPipeline and the built-in handlers' DefinitionKey, claims, and apply share either LEGACY or STRICT identity rules selected via BuildOptions.

These boundaries do not prevent single-source compatibility or controlled host integrations, but before cross-repository release it should be clear which host layer owns each item—especially items 13–16, which directly explain cases where configuration looks valid yet handlers/factories are missing at runtime or diagnostics land in a different outlet.

docs.title: Proxy: An Adapter Between Minecraft Elements and Animation
docs.text:
Proxy here is not a network proxy. It describes how one live Minecraft element, such as a block entity or a Create bogey, acquires controllers, animation targets, visual resources, and a lifecycle. The Proxy Kernel separates host events from animation state so block entities, Create devices, and external hosts can share the same model and animation abstractions without each host creating its own clock or scheduling path.

flowchart LR
    subgraph Host["Minecraft / Create Host"]
        E[MC Element]
        A[Host Adapter]
    end

    subgraph Kernel["render-core Proxy Kernel"]
        D[ProxyDefinition]
        S[ProxySession]
        C[ManagedAnimationScope]
        T[Target / Publication]
    end

    subgraph Visual["Models and Rendering"]
        M[ModelInstance]
        R[Renderer]
    end

    E -->|tick / frame / lifecycle| A
    D -->|definition + token| S
    A -->|typed input| S
    S -->|single advance| C
    C -->|same revision| T
    T -->|render port| M
    M --> R
    S -.->|post-commit writeback| A

docs.title: The Problem It Solves
docs.text:
A Minecraft element usually owns three kinds of state:

  1. Host state such as a block entity's selected gear, a Create bogey's wheel angle, or a train frame input;
  2. Animation state such as an FSM, playback time, an input snapshot, and the current revision;
  3. Visual state such as a model instance, bones, rigid parts, visibility, and resource rebuilds.

Advancing these states independently causes repeated ticks, logical writeback during rendering, different parts observing different result generations, and animation state loss during resource reload. The Proxy Kernel fixes the boundary:

  • A host submits observations and lifecycle events;
  • One element instance has one ProxySession;
  • One session owns exactly one ManagedAnimationScope;
  • A controller advances exactly once per logical step, and targets read committed output;
  • A visual manages resources and render frames without advancing logical time;
  • Writeback occurs only after the scope commits.

docs.title: System Layers and Data Flow
docs.text:
Layer Responsibility Main types Minecraft/host adapter Converts block, Create, or external-host events into typed calls ProxyTickers, ProxySessionHost, host adapters Registration and ownership Stores shared definitions and permits at most one session per element and token ProxyDefinition, ProxyRuntime, ProxyAttachToken Instance coordination Connects input, controller, scope, writeback, and visuals ProxyComposition, ProxySession Animation core Fixed-step time, input snapshots, controllers, and target publications ManagedAnimationScope, TargetBinding, TargetPublication Visual Writes published results to models, parts, and render-frame inputs ProxyVisualPort, AnimationRenderPort, ModelInstance

There is one normal logical path:

host tick
  → observe and freeze input
  → prepare controller
  → scope.advance(...)
  → publish targets from the same generation
  → visual maintenance
  → read controller output
  → write back to the host

A render frame uses a separate path:

host frame
  → session.publishFrame(frame)
  → visualPort.publishFrame(frame)
  → target/model sampling
  → renderer

publishFrame() does not increase the revision and does not advance the root timeline. It may change an interpolation phase, root transform, or frame-domain motion, but it must not produce events, consume triggers, or resample logical animation sources.

docs.title: Element and Adapter
docs.text: An element is the actual host represented by the proxy, such as FanBlockEntity, Create's ContraptionBogey, or a ContentTesting block entity. The adapter converts the host API into stable typed inputs, commands, and frame inputs. The kernel does not read Minecraft-specific state and does not branch on concrete host classes at runtime.

docs.title: Definition, Template, and Runtime
docs.text:
ProxyDefinition is an immutable registration entry containing a stable ProxyKey and a ProxyTemplate that creates a composition. Definitions are reused across instances and never store a particular element's gear, session, or model instance.

ProxyRuntime is the explicit registry and attach authority. It ensures that an attach token is consumed only once and that an element has at most one live session. ProxyAttachToken identifies one attachment attempt, so a stale callback cannot mutate a newer session.

BlockEntityProxyDefinitions maps a BlockEntityType to a definition. This lets the generic ProxyTickers find the right template when the host first ticks.

docs.title: Composition
docs.text:
ProxyComposition<T, I, O, C, F> declares the indivisible runtime parts of one device:

  • I: input captured during one logical observation;
  • O: host output produced after commit;
  • C: host command;
  • F: render-frame input;
  • typed input, controller, writeback, command, and visual ports;
  • the scope's LogicalStepPolicy and a set of TargetBindings.

Keeping these parts in one value prevents a session from pairing a machine from device A with visual resources from device B. A composition is still instance-scoped and must not store state shared across elements.

docs.title: Session
docs.text:
ProxySession owns one element instance at runtime. It serializes tick, frame, and lifecycle calls, creates the sole ManagedAnimationScope, registers targets, and gives the scope's AnimationRenderPort to the visual.

A session reports whether a logical step committed. ProxyTickOutcome.advanced means at least one logical substep committed. A later writeback or visual failure can also set aborted = true; the already committed logical step must not be reported as if it never happened.

docs.title: Scope, Controller, and Target
docs.text:
ManagedAnimationScope owns logical time. A controller prepares input and is evaluated once by the scope; it never advances a second clock. Targets consume the committed batch and do not read state machines, playback, or animation sources directly.

All targets in one batch share a revision. Root transforms, poses, and rigid parts therefore describe the same logical generation instead of sampling at different times.

docs.title: What a Port Is
docs.text:
A port is a role-specific interface. It is neither a network port nor necessarily a cross-thread message queue. A port exposes one capability so a session can depend on a narrow contract rather than a Minecraft block, FSM, or Flywheel implementation.

Port Input Output or side effect Invariant ProxyInputPort<T, I> Element One immutable observation Read once per step and keep frozen ProxyControllerPort<I, O> Frozen input RuntimeController and post-commit output Preparation does not advance time; evaluate once ProxyWritebackPort<T, O> Committed output Host state Runs only after commit and may expose rollback ProxyCommandPort<T, C> Queued command Controller/machine state Applied before the next logical step ProxyVisualPort<T, F> Scope render port and frame input Models, resources, visibility No logical clock and no second scope

Ports exist to keep invalid dependencies out. A visual cannot obtain the full scope, and a target cannot obtain a state machine. Tests can replace real Minecraft or graphics dependencies with fake ports.

docs.title: Tick and Frame
docs.text:
Path Time semantics Advances revision Typical content tick(gameTime, deltaSeconds) Game tick commits one or more fixed logical steps Yes, once per committed substep Input, FSM, commands, logical root transforms publishFrame(frame) Presentation sampling for the current render frame No Interpolation alpha, frame root, visibility maintenance

Game ticks and render frames are separate timelines. A Minecraft adapter maps partialTick into RenderSampleContext.interpolationAlpha; it must not advance an animation source again.

docs.title: Session Lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> NEW
    NEW --> ACTIVE: attach / activate
    ACTIVE --> SUSPENDED: hide / freeze
    SUSPENDED --> ACTIVE: resume
    ACTIVE --> RESOURCE_WAIT: resource unavailable
    SUSPENDED --> RESOURCE_WAIT: resource unavailable
    RESOURCE_WAIT --> ACTIVE: rebind and resume
    RESOURCE_WAIT --> SUSPENDED: rebind while paused
    ACTIVE --> CLOSED: destroy
    SUSPENDED --> CLOSED: destroy
    RESOURCE_WAIT --> CLOSED: destroy
    CLOSED --> [*]

The code exposes these resumable states:

  • SUSPENDED: the element is hidden, frozen, or temporarily not consumed; resources remain and the same session resumes later;
  • RESOURCE_WAIT: a model or visual is not ready; animation and controller state remain, and a successful rebind() reconstructs the visual;
  • CLOSED: a terminal, idempotent release of the scope, targets, controller binding, and visual. A later element creates a new session.

A normal first host tick attaches and activates the session. suspend() is not close(); use it for temporary hide or freeze behavior.

docs.title: Registration, Automatic Attachment, and Ownership
docs.text:
The standard block-entity flow has two distinct moments:

  1. During content registration, BlockEntityProxyDefinitions.register(type, id, template) declares the definition;
  2. On the first element tick, ProxyTickers.forBlockEntity(type) finds the definition by type and creates a session with the host's stable attach token.

Definitions are shared; sessions are private to elements. The token rejects consumed or stale attachments, so an old visual callback cannot control a newer session after reload or rebuild.

External hosts do not always have a BlockEntityType. Create's train bogey path, for example, uses CreateBogeyProxyAdapter to register a temporary definition directly with ProxyRuntime, attach explicitly, and forward destroy/hide/show events to close(), suspend(), and resume().

docs.title: Commit, Writeback, and Failure Recovery
docs.text:
A logical step follows a strict order:

commands → input → controller preparation → scope advance
         → same-batch publications → controller output → writeback

Triggers are not consumed before the scope commits. A failed controller or command application rolls back reversible state and leaves commands retryable. Writeback runs after commit. If writeback or visual maintenance fails, ProxyTickOutcome records both the committed step and the failure.

If visual replacement fails, the session enters RESOURCE_WAIT, preserving the old visual where possible. A later successful rebind() reuses the original scope, so animation revision does not restart merely because resources were rebuilt.

docs.title: Current Production Integrations
docs.text:
Scenario Integration Location FSM block/fan Register a type, then let ProxyTickers attach on the first tick FanProxyComposition, FanBlockEntity, FanBlock Placed Create bogey Block entity implements ProxySessionHost and uses the type catalog ExampleBogeyProxyComposition Create train bogey External-host adapter owns and attaches a session directly CreateBogeyProxyAdapter, ProxyBogeyVisual

These paths share the same invariants: one element, one session, one scope; one logical advance; render frames change presentation only.

docs.title: Current Boundaries
docs.text:
• Multiplexer runtime variant selection remains owned by the external host;
  • Some train-bogey machine synchronization still uses the legacy ElementProxy.push path;
  • Real Flywheel, portal, Iris/Sodium, resource-reload, and dedicated-server acceptance remain;
  • Normal block content should use BlockEntityProxyDefinitions + ProxyTickers; direct external attachment is for hosts without a Minecraft BlockEntityType lifecycle.

See the Proxy integration guide for concrete signatures, host skeletons, and troubleshooting.

docs.text:
The aggregate :modules:library mod registers the following NeoForge metadata at runtime:

Field Value Notes modId kasuga_lib Runtime mod ID (KasugaLib.MODID) displayName KasugaLib Next Display name group lib.kasuga Gradle mod_group_id version 1.0.0 Current mod_version; downstream range kasuga_lib_version_range = [1.0.0,) Archive name kasuga-library-1.0.0-all.jar Root build.gradle sets archivesName = "kasuga-${project.name}"; shadowJar adds classifier all

docs.text: In the current repository (modules/library/build.gradle and sibling publishing blocks), only a local file-system Maven repository (file://${project.projectDir}/repo) is declared; no public remote Maven repository URL is configured for lib.kasuga:*. Within the workspace, downstream mods (such as KuaYue) consume KasugaLibNext via Gradle composite builds (includeBuild) with dependency substitution.

:modules:old is an archived UI prototype directory and is not wired as a runtime dependency.

docs.title: Composite Build Setup (Recommended)
docs.text:
In your mod's settings.gradle, include the KasugaLibNext workspace and its Gradle plugin build (matching KuaYue/settings.gradle):

pluginManagement {
    repositories {
        gradlePluginPortal()
    }
}

includeBuild("../KasugaLibNext") {
    dependencySubstitution {
        substitute module("lib.kasuga:kasuga_lib") using project(':modules:library')
        substitute module("lib.kasuga:inject") using project(':modules:inject')
        substitute module("lib.kasuga:generator") using project(':modules:generator')
        substitute module("lib.kasuga:resource-compiler") using project(':modules:resource-compiler')
        substitute module("lib.kasuga:formula") using project(':modules:formula')
    }
}

includeBuild("../KasugaLibNext/modules/gradle-plugin")

In your mod's build.gradle, request Bundling.SHADOWED so Gradle resolves :modules:library's shadowJar (-all) artifact rather than the unshaded JAR:

dependencies {
    implementation("lib.kasuga:kasuga_lib:1.0.0") {
        attributes {
            attribute(Bundling.BUNDLING_ATTRIBUTE, objects.named(Bundling, Bundling.SHADOWED))
        }
        transitive = false
    }
}

If your mod also creates its own ModApplicationContext with @Context, @Configurable, or @BeanOnlyIn beans, add lib.kasuga:inject and Micronaut 4.9.10:

dependencies {
    implementation("lib.kasuga:inject:1.0.0") {
        transitive = false
    }
    implementation("io.micronaut:micronaut-inject:4.9.10") {
        exclude group: 'org.slf4j', module: 'slf4j-api'
    }
    additionalRuntimeClasspath("io.micronaut:micronaut-inject:4.9.10") {
        exclude group: 'org.slf4j', module: 'slf4j-api'
    }
    additionalRuntimeClasspath("io.micronaut:micronaut-aop:4.9.10") {
        exclude group: 'org.slf4j', module: 'slf4j-api'
    }
    annotationProcessor 'io.micronaut:micronaut-inject-java:4.9.10'
}
