docs.title: shadowJar Embedding vs. External Runtime Dependencies
docs.text:
The Gradle build explicitly separates embedded libraries from external dependencies:

  1. Aggregate distribution modules/library (shadowJar -all):
  2. Aggregates core, modelling, iris-compat, render-core, render-opengl, create, data-driven, scripting, inject, utils, shader, and formula into one NeoForge mod JAR (mod_id=kasuga_lib).
  3. Uses MicronautServiceShadowTransformer and Shadow relocations to relocate io.micronaut, jakarta.inject, jakarta.annotation, and lib.kasuga.inject under lib.kasuga.vendors.*.
  4. Embeds de.javagl:jgltf-model:2.0.4, de.javagl:jgltf-impl-v2:2.0.4, caliko-1.3.8.jar, and com.google.zxing:core:3.5.3 (modules/core's -all JAR also embeds org.jgrapht:jgrapht-core:1.5.2).
  5. Note: These Maven dependencies (Micronaut, jgltf, ZXing, JGraphT, etc.) do not have separate upstream LICENSE/NOTICE text files checked into the repository; any authorized distribution of shaded -all artifacts must preserve META-INF/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md and META-INF/licenses/ and verify the upstream terms of those Maven libraries.
  6. Explicitly excluded or optional external components:
  7. Iris and Sodium: modules/modelling/build.gradle explicitly excludes libs:iris:.* and libs:sodium:.* from shadowJar; runtime integration goes through modules/iris-compat.
  8. Sable / Aeronautics, Create, CC:Tweaked, LDLib2, LDLib2 Compose, ModernUI: Supplied by the user mod environment or optional adapter mods; not embedded in kasuga-library.
  9. Javet V8 natives (external/slp/javet): The adapter declares the Java javet:5.0.1 dependency (and httpclient:4.5.13), while platform V8 shared libraries are fetched at runtime by JavetDownloader into <gameDir>/native-libraries/javet/ rather than bundled inside the mod JAR.
  10. GraalJS (modules/shader-graal): Declared as standard Maven dependencies (polyglot, js-language, truffle-runtime), not shaded into kasuga-library.
  11. JPMS module-layer split-package constraint:
  12. Under ModDevGradle / FML's JPMS module layer, two JARs on the runtime module path cannot export the same Java packages. Downstream mods consuming kasuga-library's shadowed -all JAR alongside kasuga-inject must exclude standalone lib.kasuga:utils from runtime classpaths to avoid startup ResolutionException (see the KuaYue setup in Consumers).

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text: This page summarizes verified limitations, platform-specific constraints, and compatibility boundaries observed in the source code, build scripts, and verification docs.

docs.title: Graphics Backends and Legacy Modules
docs.text:
• Only OpenGL and the Minecraft Blaze3D host adapter are implemented: modules/render-core defines graphics-API-neutral contracts, while concrete rendering implementations currently exist only in modules/render-opengl and modules/modelling. Vulkan and Metal backends are not implemented; the leftover modules/render-metal directory on disk is neither included in settings.gradle nor tracked in Git.
  • Legacy modelling UI prototype does not compile: modules/old preserves historical prototype sources behind -PkasugaIncludeOld=true using Gradle's base plugin for source browsing only; it references retired registration APIs and is excluded from default builds.

docs.title: macOS and Platform Caveats
docs.text:
• macOS TBO upload path: Because Apple OpenGL drivers incur heavy validation penalties after mapped/subdata updates on texture buffer objects, modules/render-opengl uses MacTboUploadDevice (macos-tbo-orphan, re-allocating storage via glBufferData on every upload) while keeping fenced mapping for VBOs.
  • macOS depth precision and main-thread flag: ksglib_main.fsh documents 1-ULP fixed-function depth rounding and water-layer ordering sensitivity on macOS; standalone LWJGL tasks (renderGlTest, renderPreview, renderBench) require -XstartOnFirstThread on macOS.
  • Desktop display requirement for hidden mode: runClientHeadless defaults to hidden (hidden GLFW window) on macOS and Windows and still requires a desktop display session; only Linux supports display-free egl (EGL_PLATFORM=surfaceless) via the patched GLFW 3.4 Null platform.

docs.title: Iris, Sodium, and Shader-Pack Compatibility
docs.text:
• Bytecode ABI gating and graceful fallback: IrisCameraMixinPlugin and CompatCapability in modules/iris-compat inspect Iris/Sodium signatures at startup. If an installed Iris/Sodium build fails ABI checks, Kasuga logs a warning and shows a fallback toast (kasuga_lib.iris.models.unavailable.message / kasuga_lib.oit.fallback.iris), degrading to non-shader rendering or sorted translucency rather than crashing.
  • Weighted-Blended OIT (WBOIT) scope:
  • Runs at AFTER_TRANSLUCENT_BLOCKS and composites KasugaLib BLEND layers over the already rendered scene; it does not merge vanilla water or shader-pack translucent fragments into the same OIT equation.
  • With an active Iris shader pack, Kasuga cannot inject its depth weight into unmodified shader-pack fragment shaders, so it uses unit-weight WBOIT (subject to Iris's entities_translucent ~0.1 alpha test), resolves only the main color buffer, and falls back to far-to-near sorted translucency when float targets or Iris world framebuffers are unavailable. Shader packs relying on extra custom gbuffer channels for translucent surfaces may require pack-specific integration.
  • Sequential multi-camera rendering: Multi-camera world views render sequentially on a single OpenGL context (concurrent multi-threaded camera drawing is unsupported). Extra camera views omit HUD/GUI, first-person hand, and glowing outlines.
  • Weather filters and shader packs: WeatherFilters automatically falls back from GPU top-down depth filtering to CPU column-height filtering when an Iris shader pack is active (Managed Effects and Post-Processing). Sky Volumetric Clouds and World-Space Lights are not validated across arbitrary third-party shader-pack custom gbuffers.

docs.title: World-Space Lights, Volumetric Clouds, and Particle Fluids
docs.text:
• Screen-depth WorldLights boundaries (World-Space Lights):
  • Runs at POST_PROCESS priority 700/701, reconstructing normals from adjacent scene depth and approximating albedo from scene color. No shadow maps, offscreen occlusion queries, indirect bounce, or separate lighting on transparent geometry without depth/normals; walls do not cast dynamic shadows behind them.
  • Does not alter Minecraft block light levels or mob spawning.
  • Volumetric scattering integrates 48 steps per spherical volume and sums overlapping optical depth/scattering without full inter-volume multiple scattering.
  • Volumetric clouds (Sky Volumetric Clouds): No long-range inter-cloud shadowing, ground cloud shadows, or full weather simulation; dimensions without vanilla cloud layers render no sky clouds. HIGH quality is substantially heavier inside cloud layers than the default BALANCED preset.
  • Particle fluid grids (Managed Effects and Post-Processing): StableFluidGrid3D (GasSmokePreset / LiquidFlowPreset) is a real-time visual approximation without free surfaces, surface tension, droplet merging, conservative FLIP/PIC, or two-way forces back onto entities, pistons, or vanilla fluid blocks.

docs.title: Physics, Ragdolls, Model Formats, and Collisions
docs.text:
• Box3D native build and feature boundaries (PMX and glTF Ragdoll Configuration):
  • When cmake is absent from PATH, Gradle skips building kasuga_box3d and excludes box3d-tagged tests.
  • Box3D provides no fluid-volume/buoyancy API; legacy JSON fields (simulation.solver_iterations, max_angular_speed, limit_stiffness, sleeping.delay_seconds) are accepted for compatibility only and do not alter Box3D solving. PMX 6-DOF joints tighten 3-axis translation to fixed anchors.
  • PMX 2.1 per-vertex soft-body data is parsed only and not wired into Box3D solving or vertex writeback.
  • glTF ragdolls require an adjacent .gltf.json manifest with an explicit ragdoll profile; humanoid body topologies are not auto-guessed without a profile.
  • Outfits and animated collisions:
  • Wardrobe assembly (Wardrobe Benchmarks) does not perform automatic body fitting or cross-skeleton retargeting; arbitrary mismatched outfits are not guaranteed to be clip-free.
  • Server-side datapack collision loading (ServerCollisionModels) automatically supports .bbmodel and standalone .gltf/.glb; other model formats require programmatic wrapping via ServerCollisionModels.Asset (Model Collision and LOD).

docs.title: Offscreen Output, Headless Client, and World UI
docs.text:
• No built-in fixed-timestep offline video encoder: MinecraftFrameOutputs delivers in-process OpenGL OutputFrame / FBO textures on the render thread while game ticks keep running; consumers handle readback, encoding, or IPC (Offscreen Output and Multi-Camera Rendering, MC Final Frame Offscreen Output).
  • Linux EGL and multi-window restriction: Linux egl mode requires the patched GLFW 3.4 Null-platform library (scripts/build-headless-glfw.sh) and a desktop-GL-capable EGL driver; stock GLFW is not equivalent. Multi-window (MinecraftFrameWindows) is unsupported in Linux Null/EGL mode and fails explicitly.
  • World-space UI raycasting and IME (World UI and Free-Cursor Input): Plane intersection neither checks block occlusion nor runs texture alpha tests; default max hit distance is 5 blocks. Automated headless smokes do not cover OS IME candidate windows.
  • Blueprint display bounds (Blueprint and Nestable World Display): BlueprintImporters caps inputs at 64 MiB NBT, 131,072 blocks, and 4096 blocks per axis; built-in decoders cover vanilla/Create structures, Litematic v5–v7, and Sponge .schem v2–v3 (not legacy numeric-ID .schematic files).

docs.title: Scripting and Java Shader DSL
docs.text:
• Javet native download requirement (JavetDownloader.java): kasuga_lib_javet throws on Android; if the host platform V8 library is not pre-staged in <gameDir>/native-libraries/javet/, first launch requires network access to Maven mirrors or manual placement of the native file.
  • Java Shader DSL typed IR gaps (Java Shader DSL Reference): The typed API omits user-defined functions, struct uniforms, struct stage inputs/outputs, non-float uniform arrays, arbitrary swizzles, discard, derivatives, and advanced texture sampling; those currently require @DelicateShaderApi raw GLSL escape hatches or resource shaders.

docs.title: Data-Driven v2 and Packaging Boundaries
docs.text:
• v2 build pipeline boundaries (Troubleshooting and Migration):
  • DataDrivenBuildPipeline reload preflight does not scan globDirectories() (such as unlisted state_machines/ files) and does not construct ResourceLocation, so uppercase or illegal path characters in on_reload can still fail at runtime /reload.
  • build() has no transactional rollback on FAILED; DataDrivenRegistrationProviders allows one provider per host; FactoryRegistry and DataDrivenBuildHooks have no unregister API.
  • World-save compatibility, pack-history guards, and physical pack discovery belong to the host mod rather than KasugaLib.
  • Create / Sable and JPMS conflicts:
  • SableSceneHosts targets Sable 2.0.6 / Aeronautics 1.3.2 (Companion 1.6.0), does not cover Valkyrien Skies or dedicated-server smoke testing, and ContraptionLod syncs within 512 blocks without force-loading chunks.
  • Downstream NeoForge mods pulling kasuga-library (-all) alongside kasuga-inject must exclude standalone lib.kasuga:utils from runtime classpaths to avoid JPMS ResolutionException at startup.

docs.title: Migration Guide
docs.text: This page summarizes breaking changes and migration paths across KasugaLibNext data-driven registration, module packaging, rendering backends, and physics/model subsystems.

docs.title: 1. Data-Driven: Migrating from v1 (JsonTreeBuilder) to v2 (DataDrivenBuildPipeline)
docs.text:
The legacy flat directory layout and single-source registration flow have been superseded by the v2 multi-source strict pipeline (see Troubleshooting and Migration and Data-Driven Registration for detailed checklists):

Area Legacy Pattern (Deprecated / Restricted) Current v2 Pattern Index manifest path data/<modid>/kasugalib/*.json (legacy directory is no longer read) data/<namespace>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/<name>.json Manifest top-level keys "sources": [...] "on_register": [...] (registration phase) and "on_reload": [...] (reload phase), relative to data/<namespace>/, disjoint Reload discovery Single manifest or implicit scanning state_machines/ retains directory glob discovery; animation_clips/ must be listed explicitly in "on_reload" Registration entry Default single-source JsonTreeBuilder scan Install a host provider via DataDrivenRegistrationProviders.install(modId, ...) backed by DataDrivenBuildPipeline (BuildOptions.STRICT recommended) Definition identities Bare id or minecraft:id remapped to host mod ID STRICT mode requires explicit "namespace:path" (bare IDs trigger INVALID_IDENTITY; minecraft: targets the literal vanilla namespace) Handler & factory setup Relied on implicit static loading Explicitly call JsonTreeBuilder.ensureHandlersRegistered() and FsmBlockEntityFactories.registerBuiltin() before first prepare; custom TypeHandlers declare STRICT_PREFLIGHT and exactly one role (REGISTRY_CLAIMS or NON_REGISTRATION) Claim conflicts Relied on late registry exceptions Collect code registrations beforehand via RegistryClaimSnapshot.collect(hostRoot) and gate publishing on BuildResult / BuildDiagnostic

Single-JAR mods with no multi-pack overrides or strict preflight requirements can still use JsonTreeBuilder, but must still adopt the new kasuga_lib/data_driven/ layout and on_register/on_reload keys.

docs.title: 2. Module Layout, Packaging, and Build Migrations
docs.text:
Recent cleanups on master introduced the following structural and classloading rules:

  • Unique per-subproject JAR names (root build.gradle):
  • Every subproject uses base { archivesName = "kasuga-${project.name}" }; do not override subproject archive names to kasuga_lib, which causes ModDev JPMS module layers to merge unrelated jars and trigger NoClassDefFoundError.
  • Single package owner for lib.kasuga.utils:
  • modules/library's shadowJar (-all) bundles modules/utils and relocates io.micronaut, jakarta.*, and lib.kasuga.inject under lib.kasuga.vendors.*.
  • Downstream NeoForge mods depending on both lib.kasuga:kasuga_lib (Bundling.SHADOWED) and lib.kasuga:inject must exclude standalone lib.kasuga:utils from runtime classpaths to avoid JPMS ResolutionException at startup (see the KuaYue configuration in Consumers).
  • Iris compatibility isolated to :modules:iris-compat (c39864f4):
  • Iris/Sodium mixins (WorldViewIris*), IrisVertexBuffer, and CameraIrisSession moved out of modules/modelling into modules/iris-compat (kasuga_lib_iris.mixins.json, IrisCameraMixinPlugin, IrisRenderingIntegration), while legacy IrisConstants in modules/modelling was deleted and replaced by IrisModelFormats, IrisRenderingIntegration, and IrisWorldFramebuffer.
  • modelling retains only IrisIntegration and CompatCapability probing; distribution artifacts include iris-compat classes while excluding libs:iris and libs:sodium.
  • Legacy modelling UI moved to opt-in :modules:old (293ac7b5):
  • modules/modelling/old moved to modules/old and is omitted by default; pass -PkasugaIncludeOld=true only to inspect historical prototype sources.
  • Global Lombok (050cf87d):
  • Root build.gradle applies org.projectlombok:lombok:1.18.42 globally to every Java subproject's source sets.
  • Render core / OpenGL backend split (Rendering Backend Integration Reference):
  • Graphics-API-neutral UML model, scheduling, UploadRing, and FrameOutputRouter live in modules/render-core; OpenGL classes (GpuUploadRing, MacTboUploadDevice, FrameTexture, FramePreviewWindow) live in modules/render-opengl. New graphics backends depend only on render-core.

docs.title: 3. Model, Physics, and Coordinate Migrations
docs.text:
• Unified dynamics & Box3D physics (PMX and glTF Ragdoll Configuration):
  • Physics, IK, and diamond closures live under Skeleton.getDynamics().
  • Vendored Box3D C17 (kasuga_box3d) replaced the legacy fluid-force experiments: legacy simulation.solver_iterations, max_angular_speed, limit_stiffness, and sleeping.delay_seconds remain readable in JSON for compatibility only without altering Box3D solving; prefer swing/twist limits (max_swing_degrees, min_twist_degrees, max_twist_degrees) over legacy rotation_min_degrees / rotation_max_degrees.
  • Floating origin for large coordinates:
  • Avoid storing far-away world translations inside float Transform / Matrix4f values. Use MinecraftRagdollDeployments.Request with double Vector3d worldOrigin, *World(...) ragdoll interaction APIs, and SceneModels.Entry.position(Vec3) (Blueprint and Nestable World Display).
  • Proxy blocks and Blockbench loader boundaries (Modelling Module):
  • Prefer generic proxy_model / proxy_model_be data-driven factories with ProxyComposition / ScopedPlaybackCommandApplier over custom block/BE boilerplate.
  • Keep .bbmodel pixel-UV normalization and intrinsic Z→Y→X Euler ordering isolated inside KsgBbModelLoader; never inject pixel UV normalization or Bedrock sign flips into shared FlatModelData.

docs.title: 4. Scoped Resource Platform and VFS
docs.text:
• For assets shared across registration, resource packs, and scripts, migrate ad-hoc file reads to ResourceSystem, ResourceSources, ResourceSnapshot, and VirtualFileSystem (VfsPath, MountTableVfs, VfsPackResourcesBridge) so registration and runtime pack layers share frozen snapshots (Unified Resource Platform, VFS).
  • When binding lifecycle events, use ResourceEvent.HOST_BOOTSTRAP (host_bootstrap); earlier drafts occasionally referred to bootstrap, which is not a valid enum value.

docs.text:
In addition to KuaYue, the KasugaLibNext repository itself hosts downstream-style adapter mods and test fixtures exercising the public contracts:

  • external/uip/ldlib, external/uip/ldlib-compose, external/uip/modernui: Separate NeoForge adapter mods consuming modules/library for world UI canvases and model previews.
  • external/slp/javet: Separate mod (kasuga_lib_javet) extending modules/scripting with the Javet V8 engine on top of kasuga_lib.

Downstream projects built on KasugaLibNext that wish to be listed here can submit a PR or issue against master in KasugaLibGroup/KasugaLibNext with their repository URL and version compatibility notes.

docs.title: Wardrobe Example Verification Record and Performance Baseline
This Implementation and Verification (2026-10-08)
docs.text:
This change provides real-model examples of texture swapping, clothing model swapping and a vanilla MC held weapon, with every outfit wearing the user-supplied No. 13 hair. The public data consists of the generic Model, Skeleton, material instances and the assembly interface.

Change Effect WardrobeExample Connects user assets to the existing Reader and demonstrates material frame switching, model replacement, cache reuse and holding a sword at the right wrist KsgPmxLoader Atlas texture IDs are derived as a SHA-256 over the archive, the PMX entry and the texture entry, fixing texture mix-ups between identically named assets across archives KsgPmxTextureIdentityTest Covers different archives, different models/textures, Unicode names and old string-hash collisions Iris vertex upload and MC render stack Explicitly fills in intermediate UVs, tangents and entity attributes, supports worker threads and partial updates, and restores the PoseStack in a finally block when rendering fails Shader smoke entry point Optional real shader pack, verifying the active Iris pipeline; by default it only outputs pass/fail logs, with no screenshots and no performance sampling ModelAssemblyProbe Adds RibbonDress short-sleeve/long-sleeve benchmarks with hair, recording the JVM PID, Java version and heap limit Local asset preparation script Turns extracted assets into a local resource pack, can append the enable setting and keeps the other resource packs Performance summary script Validates the reports of three separate JVMs and outputs Markdown only, generating no HTML and no extra summary JSON Gradle and API documentation Adds the opt-in example/automated acceptance properties, the run steps and the performance explanation

The scope of this commit is the source, tests, scripts and API Markdown documentation listed above. Models, textures, resource packs, saves, screenshots, HTML, raw JSON reports, logs and build artifacts are not committed.

The verification environment was macOS / aarch64, Apple M3 Max, Java 21.0.3, Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.203. The client loaded Iris 1.8.12 / Sodium 0.6.13. Earlier screenshots and performance observations used the disabled configuration; separately, the six-stage smoke check with an enabled shader pack was run through with BSL 8.2.04. The verification scope is limited to that environment and that shader pack.

Verification Result renderingReleaseCheck passed modelUnitTest 811 cases, 0 failures, 0 errors, 3 conditionally skipped renderGlTest 13 groups passed; the 21,259 vertices of the real matching base body/long dress passed a CPU/GPU skinning comparison Local PMX probe three JVMs each loaded all 92 PMX files successfully, 0 load failures Real client example with hair WARDROBE_EXAMPLE_PASS, 180 frames, 61 vanilla item submissions BSL 8.2.04 shader path WARDROBE_SHADER_SMOKE_PASS, all six stages completed, actually entering IrisRenderingPipeline with no fallback to no-shader

The client verified, in order, the original colorway, the Rose colorway, the long-sleeve model, switching back to short sleeves, holding the MC sword and wrist rotation. Texture switching keeps the same Model; after a model switch, switching back to short sleeves returns the same assembly Model from the first time, and the build counter does not increase. A new session builds two assembly models in total. Here the switch-back is served by the outfit registry reusing an already-resolved result, so the underlying assembly cache shows hits 0 and builds 2, and registry reuse is not miscounted as an underlying cache hit.

docs.title: Local Performance Results (2026-10-08)
docs.text:
Three separate JavaExec JVMs were run, with PIDs 73993, 74024 and 74050, in the measurement order uncached-first, cached-first, uncached-first. The Java runtime was 21.0.3+10-LTS and the maximum heap was configured to 4 GiB each time.

The results below are the median of the per-JVM batch-mean p50 values. Uncached assembly includes the common geometry/skeleton assembly work; the two warm-cache columns measure, respectively, rebuilding a request and then querying the cache, and reusing an existing request and only querying the cache. File parsing, texture decoding, GPU skinning and drawing are not counted in these CPU assembly metrics.

Case Vertices Bones Uncached assembly (ms) Rebuild request + warm cache (µs) Existing request, cache query (µs) Ayuchan matching base body + long dress 21,259 316 70.168 7.400 0.263 Base body + RibbonDress short sleeves + No. 13 hair 21,397 263 60.738 3.015 0.041 Base body + RibbonDress long sleeves + No. 13 hair 22,069 263 63.751 2.286 0.040 Base body + 1 real small garment 8,806 181 34.303 4.105 0.063 Base body + 10 duplicate small garments 12,955 694 41.089 20.289 0.093 Base body + 100 duplicate small garments 54,445 5,824 125.227 131.003 0.730

The 100-copy stress case repeats the same 461-vertex small garment and shares only the bind-compatible bones; the remaining bones are named independently. This result does not mean that 100 different garments have been fitted to the base body, and cannot be converted into a game FPS gain. The p50 of batch means is not a per-call latency distribution, and a cache query for an existing request is not a whole swap operation.

The following single-call CPU durations were also recorded in the real client; they have no warm-up statistics:

Actual operation Single-call CPU observation (ms) Switching short sleeves to the Rose texture 0.087 Replacing with the long-sleeve model (including instance and backend mount) 289.673 Switching back to the cached short-sleeve model (including instance and backend mount) 171.290 Switching short sleeves back to the Blue texture, two observations 0.073 / 0.014

The CPU assembly cache avoids re-assembling the same geometry and skeleton, but a new ModelInstance and new backend render resources are still created. The cache in this pass did not remove that part of the cost of a whole swap operation; the single-call figures in the table above are also not GPU or whole-frame durations.

docs.title: Current Fitting and Verification Boundaries
docs.text:
RibbonDress and this base body bind their same-named bones at different positions, so the clothing and hair keep their own separate bind skeletons. This example enables no physics and runs no full-body animation; automatic body fitting and skeleton retargeting are not implemented, so it cannot be taken as a guarantee that any garment will have no interpenetration. The Ayuchan matching long dress comparison uses strictly compatible shared bones.

The held item uses a real right-wrist Anchor and the vanilla ItemRenderer, and does not modify the player's inventory. What this client pass actually accepted is the Diamond Sword; the Iron Pickaxe is another option the example provides. The humanoid armor layer for worn armor, other shader packs and other operating systems were not accepted in this example. The BSL path only verifies that it runs; do not read it as a new image-quality acceptance or performance measurement.

The interactive commands and the standalone preview window entry point are provided; the client measurements above use automated headless Free Camera output, and are not to be read as re-verifying standalone window operation in this pass.

docs.title: Smoke Verification With a Shader Pack Enabled
docs.text:
Use an existing local shader pack, for example BSL 8.2.04; relative paths resolve from the repository root.

./gradlew :modules:modelling:runClientHeadless \
  -PkasugaClientDirectory=/tmp/kasuga-wardrobe-client \
  -PkasugaQuickPlayWorld=wardrobe \
  -PkasugaWardrobeShaderSmoke=true \
  -PkasugaWardrobeShaderPack=/absolute/path/to/BSL_v8.2.04.zip

kasugaWardrobeShaderSmoke=true starts the same six-stage example with hair automatically and does not need kasugaWardrobeDemo to be enabled as well. During the real model and item render stages it checks that the current Iris pack is non-empty, that a shader pack is in use, and that the actual pipeline is IrisRenderingPipeline; only when all stages finish and pass the GL checks is WARDROBE_SHADER_SMOKE_PASS recorded. Failure records WARDROBE_SHADER_SMOKE_FAIL, and a successful Gradle exit is not taken as shader acceptance success.

By default this mode reads no pixels, saves no images/JSON and records no operation durations; it cannot be combined with kasugaWardrobeCapture. It uses only the camera's own shader session and does not set BSL as the main view shader pack. To see the actual result, add -PkasugaWardrobeShaderPreview=true, which saves one debug/wardrobe-example/shader-preview.png during the sword stage only and still samples no performance. The image is for local viewing and is not committed.

On this machine the BSL 8.2.04 path completed all six stages, with Iris OIT enabled normally and no model upload failure, matrix stack exception or no-shader fallback. Because the user asked to see the result, one extra sword frame was captured; the original no-shader screenshots and performance report were not overwritten. This verification confirms that the run path is clear; it does not prove that other shader packs, other platforms or final image quality all pass.

docs.title: Performance Showcase
docs.text:
Run modelAssemblyProbe three times as separate JavaExec JVMs, alternating uncached-first, cached-first, uncached-first, with a different report path each time. Besides the matching long dress and 1/10/100 duplicate small garments, the probe also measures this example's base body, RibbonDress short sleeves/long sleeves and hair assembly. When it finishes, run:

python3 scripts/summarize-wardrobe-example.py \
  --capture /tmp/kasuga-wardrobe-client/debug/wardrobe-example \
  /tmp/wardrobe-bench-1.json /tmp/wardrobe-bench-2.json /tmp/wardrobe-bench-3.json

It writes only summary.md in the same directory; --output /path/to/report.md specifies a Markdown path. The summary file depends on no images, HTML or extra summary JSON. The table shows the median of the per-JVM batch-mean p50 values and separates uncached assembly, rebuilding a request then querying the warm cache, and querying the warm cache for an existing request. Input parsing, texture decoding, GPU skinning and drawing are not counted in these CPU assembly metrics. The 100-copy stress case repeats the same real small garment and cannot be read as 100 different garments that have been fitted.

The operations entries in the client report are CPU observations of a few actual operations; a model switch includes instance and backend mounting and must not be mixed with the warm-up benchmarks above or with GPU/whole-frame performance. Performance numbers should be taken from the report actually generated on your own machine.

This is the verification record and performance baseline page. For the recipe covering asset preparation, interactive runs and automated screenshot acceptance, see the real-asset wardrobe swap example.

docs.title: Anchor and Minecraft equipment attachment
docs.text: For the principles see model subsystems. The core Anchor depends only on the generic skeleton and Transform, and the Minecraft item integration lives in lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.api.McModelEquipment.

docs.title: Two kinds of attachment
docs.text: Objects that move as a whole, such as tools, weapons, hats and accessories, use an Anchor. Clothing that needs several bones of the arm, leg or body to deform together uses Model Assembly and keeps its own skeleton, morph and secondary motion. Outfit management can use logical slots uniformly, but clothing geometry is still bound by skin weights; a single anchor does not automatically retarget a clothing skeleton or fit the body. Assembly remaps and preserves the source Anchors; body names are kept, and part names get a part prefix.

docs.title: Defining and reading an Anchor
docs.text:
Skeleton skeleton = model.getSkeleton();
skeleton.defineAnchor("right_grip", skeleton.getBoneMap().get("right_hand"),
        new Transform().translate(0, 0.05f, 0));
skeleton.defineAnchor("left_grip", skeleton.getBoneMap().get("left_hand"), new Transform());
skeleton.defineAnchor("head", skeleton.getBoneMap().get("head"), new Transform());

Skeleton.defineAnchor(String name, Bone bone, Transform localOffset) returns an Anchor, converting the bone-local offset into the model bind space with weight 1 for that bone, and copies the offset. The name must be non-empty and unique, and bone must belong to that Skeleton. Define anchors during resource construction, before instances are created and assembly caches are built; after modifying a shared resource you have to update the revision/invalidate the cache. The original Anchor(name, BoneBinding, Transform authoredBindPose, AnchorData) still supports linear weighting over several bones.

Evaluation uses currentBone * inverseBind * authoredAnchor, consistent with the production skinning path.

Interface Purpose ModelInstance.anchorTransform(String name) The old float world transform; returns null when the Anchor is missing SkeletonInstance.anchorTransformRelative(String name, Vector3d origin) Transform relative to the given double origin, suited to camera-space rendering ModelInstance.attachToAnchor(String name, AnchorModule.Attachment callback) Publishes the transform after the final tick pose; passes null when it cannot be resolved ModelInstance.detachFromAnchor(String name, AnchorModule.Attachment callback) Unbinds using the original callback object McModelHandle.attachToAnchor / detachFromAnchor(String, BiConsumer<String, Transform>) MC handle adapter; unbinds using the original receiver object

The same callback can be attached to several Anchors, and duplicate bindings to the same Anchor are merged; unbinding inside the callback is allowed. Old callback interfaces are released after the model is unmounted, reloaded or switched, and are reconfigured for the new instance through onInstanceChanged. Precision-sensitive rendering uses the relative interface, subtracting the origin in double first and then converting to float; there is no need to obtain a float world position first.

docs.title: Dummy model groups
docs.text:
DummyModelInstance owns a private rig with one identity root and no vertices, meshes, materials or textures. Its asset returns false from Model.isRenderable(): backends skip it before creating a render context, and direct MC GPU instance construction skips the bone TBO as well. Anchors can be created and moved at runtime.

DummyModelInstance group = McDummyModels.create(); // Automatic client frame updates; no resource ID or backend mount.
group.defineAnchor("left", new Transform().translate(-1, 0, 0));
group.defineAnchor("right", new Transform().translate(1, 0, 0));

// Both handles have already mounted successfully.
var left = group.attach("left", leftHandle.instance());
var right = group.attach("right", rightHandle.instance(), new Transform().scale(.5f, .5f, .5f));
group.getSkeletonInstance().transformRoot(new Transform().translate(10, 64, 10).rotate(0, 45, 0, true));
group.setAnchorTransform("right", new Transform().translate(2, 0, 0));
left.setOffset(new Transform().rotate(0, 90, 0, true));

left.close();  // Detach and keep the child's last world pose.
group.close(); // Host removal/world unload: unregister and detach remaining children.

Child roots use parent root * anchor local transform * child local offset; internal child animation is preserved. Children can themselves be dummies. The automatic runtime evaluates ancestor groups first, independently of visibility. Offsets are copied and several children may share an anchor. Cycles, multiple parents and children with an existing root driver or scope-owned animation render port are rejected. Floating-origin composition retains the double origin.

Use Attachment.close() or group.detach(child) to unbind. Closing a child also removes its attachment. Closing a parent does not close children; callers close nested groups separately. After a child's resource reload, its retired instance detaches; use McModelHandle.onInstanceChanged to attach the replacement instance.

For manual/non-Minecraft hosts, construct new DummyModelInstance() and evaluate ancestors before children with evaluateFrame(partialTick, deltaSeconds), or use tick(deltaSeconds) for procedural updates while the host owns animation time. All mutations and cleanup run on the instance's owning thread.

docs.title: McModelEquipment
docs.text:
McModelEquipment equipment = new McModelEquipment(handle, () -> entity)
        .bindHands("right_grip", "left_grip")
        .bindHeadItem("head", new Transform());

// Use a camera-relative world PoseStack after the final pose of the model's current frame has been evaluated.
int count = equipment.render(poseStack, bufferSource, camera.getPosition(), packedLight, packedOverlay);

equipment.unbind(EquipmentSlot.OFFHAND);
equipment.close();

bindHands reads the entity's current main/off hand ItemStack and, following the entity's dominant hand, selects the physical hand anchor and the THIRD_PERSON_LEFT_HAND / THIRD_PERSON_RIGHT_HAND display transform. You can pass two Transforms, for the left and right hands, to adjust the tool's hold position, rotation and scale; they are copied on binding. bindHeadItem uses the HEAD display context, suited to head-worn items such as pumpkins. The vanilla item renderer handles the item model, display context, color and enchantment effects, using the passed lighting and overlay.

equipment.bind(EquipmentSlot.MAINHAND, "right_grip", () -> weapon,
        ItemDisplayContext.THIRD_PERSON_RIGHT_HAND, false, localOffset);

equipment.bind(EquipmentSlot.CHEST, "torso", () -> entity.getItemBySlot(EquipmentSlot.CHEST),
        ItemDisplayContext.FIXED, false, localOffset, context -> {
            customArmorRenderer.render(context);
        });

bind(EquipmentSlot, String anchor, Supplier<ItemStack>, ItemDisplayContext, boolean leftHand, Transform offset) uses the vanilla ItemRenderer; an additional Renderer parameter can integrate custom equipment, armor layers or other display objects. The Context of Renderer.render(Context) contains slot, stack, displayContext, leftHand, entity, poseStack, buffers, level, light, overlay, seed. The ItemStack is borrowed for this frame and is not modified by the attach adapter. Humanoid armor layer/skinning adaptation for fitted armor such as chestplates and leggings is provided by a custom renderer or an assembly entry point; the vanilla item renderer itself does not turn an item icon into fitted armor.

A new binding on a slot replaces the old one; an empty ItemStack, a missing Anchor, or an unmounted/invisible model is skipped. A name binding queries the current instance on every render, so after a resource reload and a swap it automatically uses the new Skeleton; it does not keep an old ModelInstance. close releases the bindings and the entity supplier, and does not close the model, the item renderer or the buffers.

Calls run on the render thread, and the PoseStack must be in camera-relative world space, without duplicating the entity translation. The attach adapter pushes/pops the matrix of each item and restores the PoseStack even when rendering throws; it does not advance tick, animation or physics time. Finish the shared animation/IK/physics pose evaluation first, then draw the model and the equipment, to avoid advancing the simulation repeatedly across camera views.

docs.title: Verification entry
docs.text:
./gradlew :modules:modelling:modelUnitTest
./gradlew :modules:modelling:runClientHeadless -PkasugaClientDirectory=/absolute/path/to/isolated-client -PkasugaQuickPlayWorld=fixture -PkasugaTestAnchorEquipment=true

The success marker is ANCHOR_EQUIPMENT_SMOKE_PASS, and the report is in debug/anchor-equipment.json. The client test uses a geometry-free neutral skeleton and a vanilla sword, pickaxe and pumpkin to verify drawing, dominant-hand switching and anchor motion; it does not display the user's base body.

docs.title: Built-in Effects, Water Simulation, and Spatial Audio Reference
docs.text: This document covers the built-in black-hole post-processing pipeline, shallow-water free-surface simulation and optical rendering, positional spatial audio, and the /kasuga_effects diagnostics and shader-parameter interface in modules/modelling and modules/render-core. For general managed effects and post-processing graphs, see Managed Effects and Post-Processing.

docs.title: 1. Black-Hole Gravitational Lensing Post-Processing (BlackHoleEffect / BlackHoleEffects)
docs.text:
Package: lib.kasuga.rendering.effect.builtin.blackhole (initialized on client startup by BlackHoleEffects.initialize(RenderPipelineRegistrar) inside Constants.onRegisterRenderPipelines).

  • Pipeline registration: registers the Java Shader DSL-generated fullscreen shader kasuga_lib:black_hole (BlackHoleShaderProvider) and priority-1000 PostProcessGraph kasuga_lib:black_hole_graph with a screen-scale, depth-enabled, LINEAR-filtered managed target (kasuga_lib:black_hole_scene). Graph prepare projects active black holes into the current camera view and skips both copy and composite passes when none are visible.
  • Capacity and ordering: BlackHoleEffects.MAX_VISIBLE_BLACK_HOLES = 8. Visible black holes are sorted by projected screen radius descending (ties broken by ID) and truncated to at most 8 entries, packing 16 floats per hole into the HoleData uniform array.
  • Exposed parameters (BlackHoleShaderProvider): LensingScale (default 1.0, range [0, 3]), DiskBrightness (default 1.0, range [0, 4]), and ChromaticScale (default 1.0, range [0, 3]), editable live via /kasuga_effects (Parameters) or /kasuga_effects parameter ....

docs.title: BlackHoleEffect Parameters and Defaults
docs.text:
Immutable record constructed with BlackHoleEffect.builder(ResourceLocation id, Vec3 position) or toBuilder():

Field Default Constraints / Notes eventHorizonRadius 1.0f > 0, event horizon radius in world units influenceRadius 4.0f >= 1.0f, multiplier relative to eventHorizonRadius distortionStrength 0.7f >= 0 accretionRadius 1.65f >= 1.0f, accretion-ring center relative to eventHorizonRadius accretionWidth 0.28f > 0, accretion-ring half-width relative to eventHorizonRadius glowStrength 1.3f >= 0 chromaticAberration 0.025f >= 0, RGB separation relative to eventHorizonRadius rotationSpeed 1.0f Finite angular speed multiplier glowColor (1.0f, 0.32f, 0.06f) BlackHoleEffect.Color(red, green, blue), each component >= 0 depthTest true Whether scene depth occludes the effect accretionDiskTilt 1.0f (0, 1], screen-space minor/major axis ratio (1 face-on, near 0 edge-on)

docs.title: BlackHoleEffects Lifecycle and Commands
docs.text:
• BlackHoleEffects.put(effect): adds or replaces an entry by effect.id().
  • BlackHoleEffects.register(effect): returns an owned BlackHoleEffects.Registration (id(), effect(), update(BlackHoleEffect), close()), where closing an older token cannot remove a newer replacement with the same ID.
  • BlackHoleEffects.remove(id), clear(), size(), snapshot(), shader(). All entries are automatically cleared on level change in ClientTickEvent.Post.
  • Development-client commands (BlackHoleDemo in contentTesting, AUTO_SPAWN = false):
Command Behavior /kasuga_black_hole demo Spawns a single black hole ahead of the player camera /kasuga_black_hole orbit Starts a three-body orbiting black-hole demo /kasuga_black_hole massive Spawns a large tilted accretion-disk black hole /kasuga_black_hole clear Removes the demo black holes /kasuga_black_hole status Prints BlackHoleEffects.shader() readiness, generation, active count, and demo mode

docs.title: CPU Shallow-Water Solver and Optics (modules/render-core)
docs.text:
Package: lib.kasuga.rendering.water, single-owner-thread with zero graphics or host dependencies:

  • ShallowWaterGrid(int size, float cellSize, float restDepth): solves conserved depth and horizontal momenta (h, hu, hv) on a flat bed with a 2D Rusanov finite-volume update (size in 8..512, positive finite cellSize and restDepth, GRAVITY = 9.81f, periodic boundaries, adaptive CFL substeps via step(float seconds) for [0, 1], damping exp(-0.16 * dt)).
  • Core methods: displace(x, z, radius, amount) (volume-conserving depression with surrounding positive ring), impulse(x, z, radius, vx, vz), shift(cellsX, cellsZ) (shifts the moving simulation window while preserving existing world-space waves and filling new edges at restDepth), height(x, z), velocityX(x, z), velocityZ(x, z), cellDepth(x, z), extent(), volume(), minimumDepth(), maximumDeviation(), isFinite(), and reset(). This depth-averaged model does not represent overturning waves or spray.
  • WaterOptics(absorptionRed, absorptionGreen, absorptionBlue, scatterRed, scatterGreen, scatterBlue, shorelineFoam): absorption coefficients in [0, 20], scattering and foam in [0, 1]; built-in presets WaterOptics.DEFAULT and WaterOptics.CLEAR_COAST.

docs.title: Client Water Post-Processing Pipeline (modules/modelling)
docs.text:
Package: lib.kasuga.rendering.effect.builtin.water (WaterEffects.initialize registers resource shader kasuga_lib:water/clear_surface and priority-800 PostProcessGraph kasuga_lib:water/graph):

  • WaterEffects.open(ClientLevel level, double centerX, float bedY, double centerZ, int resolution, float cellSize, float depth): opens the active WaterSurface for level (at most one active surface per ClientLevel; requires WaterEffects.ready()). ClientTickEvent.Post steps active surfaces at 0.05f seconds while unpaused and closes surfaces when switching levels; removing the last surface releases managed targets via PostProcessTargetPool.
  • WaterSurface (AutoCloseable) chainable configuration:
  • followPlayer(boolean) / playerInteraction(boolean) (default true; generates foot ripples, imparts mild water velocity coupling, and shifts the ShallowWaterGrid window when the player moves more than 8 cells from center).
  • renderEnabled(boolean) (default true; hides the optical surface while preserving simulation state).
  • optics(WaterOptics) and terrainHeight(DoubleBinaryOperator) (supplies walkable bed elevation in world coordinates; defaults to flat bedY).
  • interact(Vec3 position, Vec3 velocity, float radius, float displacement): injects local displacement and horizontal momentum within ±0.45 * extent().
  • Encodes (cellDepth - restDepth + 0.25) * 2 as 16-bit RG bytes in a DynamicTexture (HeightSampler) for depth-tested refraction, Beer-Lambert absorption, and Fresnel sky reflection.
  • contentTesting provides /kasuga_cobalt_blue [stop] and /ksglib demo cobalt_blue [stop] (requires a private singleplayer world, ready water shaders, Box3D native physics, and generated assets/kasuga_demo/cobalt_blue/track.json audio assets).

docs.title: 3. Scene Tracks and Spatial Audio (SceneTrack / SpatialAudio)
docs.text:
Package: lib.kasuga.audio (Dist.CLIENT only):

  • SceneTrack(String title, String artist, String album, float durationSeconds, ResourceLocation sound, ResourceLocation audioFile):
  • SceneTrack.load(ResourceLocation metadata) reads JSON metadata (title, artist, album, duration_seconds, sound, audio_file) from the client ResourceManager.
  • available() verifies both BuiltInRegistries.SOUND_EVENT.containsKey(sound) and the presence of audioFile.
  • playAt(Vec3 position, float gain) starts a positional SoundSource.RECORDS voice via SpatialAudio.play(...) (throws IllegalStateException if available() is false).
  • SpatialAudio:
  • SpatialAudio.play(SoundEvent sound, SoundSource category, Vec3 position, float gain) validates finite position and gain > 0, returning an owned SpatialAudio.Voice (AbstractTickableSoundInstance, AutoCloseable, relative = false, looping = false, Attenuation.LINEAR). Streaming and mono spatialization are governed by the registered Ogg resource.
  • SpatialAudio.activeCount() returns active voices; ClientTickEvent.Post closes voices on level change or once stopped.
  • SpatialAudio.Voice exposes seconds(), isPlaying(), failedToStart() (ticks > 60 && !observedPlaying), position(), spatial() (!relative), and close().

docs.title: 4. Effect Diagnostics, Parameter Editor, and /kasuga_effects CLI
docs.text:
Package: lib.kasuga.rendering.effect.debug (client commands registered in Constants.onRegisterClientCommands):

  • Client command tree /kasuga_effects:
  • /kasuga_effects: opens the non-pausing EffectDiagnosticsScreen ("Kasuga Effect Inspector", refreshes every 10 ticks).
  • /kasuga_effects preload: calls RenderShaderRegistry.preloadPending() to queue pending shaders for preloading.
  • /kasuga_effects workers <count>: calls ShaderPreparationScheduler.configureWorkers(count) (0 selects automatic worker count).
  • ShaderParameterCommands subcommands:
    • /kasuga_effects parameter list <shader>
    • /kasuga_effects parameter set <shader> <name> <values...> (booleans accept true/false; vector/color/matrix components are space- or comma-separated)
    • /kasuga_effects parameter reset <shader> <name>
  • EffectDiagnosticsScreen: tabs Effects (owner, pipeline ID, type, active/visible count, render time), Shaders (source kind, state, preload policy/priority, origin, generation, queue wait, prepare/compile times, exposed parameter count, errors, and worker/budget summary), and Pipelines (owner, stage/phase, priority, primitive mode, buffer size, cached variants), with Parameters (opens ShaderParameterScreen), Preload pending, and Done buttons.
  • ShaderParameterScreen: non-pausing schema-driven editor listing every registered shader with exposed parameters (< Prev / Next > cycling, Reset / Reset all, boolean toggles, and per-component sliders labeled Value, XYZW, RGBA, or Mij). Edits mutate RenderShaderHandle.parameters() immediately for the next draw without recompiling and are persisted asynchronously by ShaderParameterPersistence to config/kasuga_lib/shader-parameters.json.

docs.title: Camera Control and Animation Tracks
docs.text:
Interfaces, configuration, and call reference. For the mechanics see camera-animation.md.

The camera handles returned by MinecraftCameras.create(...) and MinecraftFrameWindows.createCamera(...) are Free Cameras, and they support position, rotation, optical zoom, and keyframe playback. For the three camera types and entity following see Player / Free / Fixed Camera. All control operations run on the render thread.

docs.title: Direct control
docs.text:
camera.moveTo(x, y, z);                 // world coordinates, absolute position
camera.moveBy(dx, dy, dz);              // world coordinates, incremental move
camera.rotateTo(yaw, pitch, roll);       // degrees, follows the Minecraft camera convention
camera.rotateBy(dYaw, dPitch, dRoll);    // incremental rotation
camera.setVerticalFov(60);              // vertical FOV, must be within (0, 180) degrees
camera.zoom(2);                        // magnifies the projection 2x
WorldCameraView pose = camera.pose();   // pose for the current tick

Direct control starts from the pose of the current animation tick, keeps the components it does not modify and the output size, then replaces the pose with a fixed one and stops the original animation. Use MinecraftCameras.createFixed(...) when you need to follow an entity; its FOV/projection control preserves the target binding. Free can still use updatePose(Supplier<WorldCameraView>) to describe a custom pose provider; replacing the provider clears the animation. WorldCameraView also provides the same immutable transform methods, so you can compose providers yourself.

Camera zoom changes the projection; it does not scale the world or the output resolution. The factor m satisfies tan(newFov / 2) = tan(baseFov / 2) / m: greater than 1 magnifies, less than 1 shrinks. At the numerical extremes the FOV stays inside the representable (0, 180) degree range.

docs.title: Animation tracks
docs.text:
var start = camera.pose();
var clip = CameraAnimationClip.builder(Id.parse("example:camera_pan"), 3f)
        .move(0, start.x(), start.y(), start.z(), Easing.easeInOutCubic())
        .move(3, start.x() + 10, start.y() + 2, start.z(), null)
        .rotate(0, start.yaw(), start.pitch(), start.roll(), Easing.easeInOutSine())
        .rotate(3, start.yaw() + 90, 15, 0, null)
        .zoom(0, 1, Easing.easeInOutCubic())
        .zoom(3, 2, null)
        .build();
camera.animation().play(clip, false);

Each track independently drives one component of x / y / z / yaw / pitch / roll / zoom. move and rotate are convenience methods that add keyframes for three tracks at once; to change only one component use builder.keyframe(Channel.YAW, time, value, easing). Position and angle values are absolute; zoom is relative to the FOV the provider supplies for the frame, is re-evaluated every frame, and does not accumulate magnification. Missing tracks keep the provider's values, and a window camera still updates its output size with the framebuffer/DPI.

Time is in seconds. Tracks are sorted and copied automatically; duplicate times, duplicate components, times beyond the clip duration, empty tracks, and illegal values are rejected at construction time. Outside the first and last keyframes the endpoint value is held. Easing reuses the model's Easing and applies to the segment after the keyframe. Rotation interpolates unwrapped angle values, so 0 → 720 performs two full turns; to cross the 360 degree boundary, for example, use 350 → 370. When a back/elastic easing drives zoom to zero or below, it is clamped to a tiny positive value so the projection stays valid.

camera.animation().pause();        // pauses the animation; the camera keeps outputting frames
camera.animation().seek(1.5f);     // jumps immediately and clears the old interpolation interval
camera.animation().setSpeed(2f);   // double speed; 0 freezes the clock
camera.animation().resume();
camera.animation().isPlaying();
camera.animation().currentTime();  // monotonic clock even while looping
camera.animation().stop();         // removes the tracks and restores the original pose provider

After a non-looping playback ends, the end pose is kept; replay with play, or seek(0) and then resume(). During standalone playback, camera.pause() pauses both frame output and the camera's own clock advance, and camera.resume() restores them. When following a shared timeline, camera.pause() pauses only that camera's output while other targets keep playing; to pause the whole scene use timeline.pause(). A closed or failed camera rejects further control, including animation controller references saved earlier.

Minecraft advances the clock automatically once per game tick (20 Hz), and does not advance it while the world is paused; each frame interpolates by the game's partial tick. OwnedCamera / CameraAnimationPlayer in render-core can be used standalone: the host calls tick(dt) and samplePose(partialTick) / sample(partialTick). Sampling for rendering does not itself advance the clock.

docs.title: Integration with existing model animation
docs.text:
AnimationPlayer<T> and the camera adapter use ScopedPlayerPosePlayback and ScopedCameraPosePlayback respectively; each owns a private ManagedAnimationScope. They share the Scope, Playback and result-target contracts rather than a public compatibility class. AnimationSampler<T> outputs the model Pose, while CameraClipSampler outputs a CameraPose that has not been applied to the world. Animation sources are sampled only during logical publication; render sampling interpolates the committed generation. The original model play(sampler, data, loop) and JSON are kept. Named clips and static poses now all use ModelPosing; the glTF-specific driver has been migrated to that public entry point.

The existing AnimationClip gains an optional cameras, so one clip can contain model bones, morphs, materials, and multiple named camera tracks. For example, the following JSON moves the model's root and the scene camera in sync:

{
  "id": "example:scene",
  "duration_seconds": 2,
  "bones": [{"bone": "root", "keyframes": [
    {"time": 0, "transform": {"translate": [0, 0, 0]}},
    {"time": 2, "transform": {"translate": [2, 0, 0]}}
  ]}],
  "cameras": [{"camera": "main_shot", "tracks": [
    {"channel": "x", "keyframes": [
      {"time": 0, "value": 100}, {"time": 2, "value": 102}
    ]},
    {"channel": "zoom", "keyframes": [
      {"time": 0, "value": 1}, {"time": 2, "value": 1.5}
    ]}
  ]}]
}

After reading it as scene through AnimationClip.CODEC, bind the targets to the same timeline:

var timeline = new AnimationTimeline();
var modelPlayer = new AnimationPlayer<AnimationClip>(modelInstance);
ModelPoseBinding.install(modelInstance, modelPlayer);
modelPlayer.follow(ClipSampler.INSTANCE, scene, timeline);
camera.animation().follow(scene, "main_shot", timeline);
timeline.play(scene.durationSeconds(), true);
var driver = MinecraftAnimationTimelines.drive(timeline);

timeline.pause();
timeline.seek(1f);
timeline.setSpeed(2f);
timeline.resume();

// Release the driver registration and the target bindings when the scene ends.
driver.close();
modelPlayer.stop();
camera.animation().stop();
timeline.stop();

follow only binds and samples; it does not restart the timeline and does not advance it on its own. Neither the model's existing animate calls nor the camera's automatic tick advance the shared clock a second time. MinecraftAnimationTimelines.drive advances it once per game tick and stops while the world is paused; registering the same timeline twice raises an error. A pure Java host can skip that registration and call timeline.tick(dt) once per tick itself. The control thread hands the clock to the render thread through an immutable volatile snapshot.

The camera's animation().pause/seek/setSpeed/resume and the model player's controls of the same names act on the timeline they are bound to, so when the clock is shared they also control the other targets. stop(), direct control, and closing a camera release only that target; the external timeline keeps working. A model reload/rebind only swaps the output target and keeps the shared clock progress.

The logical camera name (such as main_shot) is independent of the output view ID, so the same track can be bound to multiple camera tracks. You can also bind a standalone CameraAnimationClip and existing model samplers such as glTF/VMD to the same timeline. Clips of different lengths hold their endpoint within the shared period according to their own length, and looping happens uniformly at the timeline's duration.

An existing model player can also act as the clock owner while playing standalone:

modelPlayer.play(ClipSampler.INSTANCE, scene, true);
camera.animation().follow(scene, "main_shot", modelPlayer.timeline());

Here the model host's tick drives the clock and the camera only follows; that clock can no longer be registered with MinecraftAnimationTimelines or have timeline.tick called on it directly. The model's stop/play stops the old owned clock; use an external shared timeline when you need to manage the scene lifecycle independently.

The model pose outlet of ClipSampler / FSM still applies only model channels; camera channels are applied through explicit target bindings. The current shared timeline does not take over the FSM's layer weights or state switching.

docs.title: Continuous velocity and acceleration
docs.text: Java tracks can use Easing.quinticHermite(v0, v1, a0, a1) to prescribe normalized endpoint velocity and acceleration. For duration dt and value delta dv, pass velocity * dt / dv and acceleration * dt * dt / dv; handle zero deltas as constant segments. Sharing physical knot derivatives across adjacent segments keeps motion continuous. Arguments must be finite; the curve may overshoot. Four zero derivatives produce quintic smoothstep. The current codec does not persist this parameterized easing, so do not rely on a JSON round trip preserving it. See the Nebula demo for tracks following a shared player clock.

docs.title: JSON
docs.text:
Read and written through CameraAnimationClip.CODEC; it uses the same easing names as model animation.

{
  "id": "example:camera_pan",
  "duration_seconds": 3,
  "tracks": [
    {"channel": "yaw", "keyframes": [
      {"time": 0, "value": 0, "easing": "ease_in_out_cubic"},
      {"time": 3, "value": 90}
    ]},
    {"channel": "zoom", "keyframes": [
      {"time": 0, "value": 1},
      {"time": 3, "value": 2}
    ]}
  ]
}

Unit tests use ./gradlew :modules:modelling:modelUnitTest --offline. Run the real camera track smoke test with a copied test world:

./gradlew :modules:modelling:runClientHeadless \
  -PkasugaClientDirectory=build/camera-animation-smoke \
  -PkasugaQuickPlayWorld=world-view-test -PkasugaTestCameraAnimation=true --offline

The test directory must already contain saves/world-view-test. On success it prints CAMERA_ANIMATION_SMOKE_PASS and writes the result to debug/camera-animation.json in that client directory.

docs.title: Player / Free / Fixed Camera
docs.text: The generic data lives in lib.kasuga.rendering.output.camera, and the Minecraft integration in lib.kasuga.rendering.output.mc. For the mechanics see Multi-camera and output. All creation, control, and close operations run on the render thread.

docs.title: Types and creation
docs.text:
CameraType Pose and configuration source Control PLAYER Native player camera, first/third person, current FOV/roll, resources, and shaders Native player controls; the handle manages the output lifecycle FREE Standalone world position, rotation, FOV, size, and CameraRenderSettings Direct control, a provider, or animation tracks FIXED Interpolated target position/orientation and offsets; standalone projection and CameraRenderSettings Target following, offsets, orientation mode, and projection control

FIXED is a follow camera bound to a target. For a stationary camera view, use a FREE with a fixed pose. type() is independent of the READY / PAUSED / FAILED / CLOSED lifecycle of CameraState.

CameraHandle player = MinecraftCameras.createPlayer(frame -> consume(frame));
CameraHandle free = MinecraftCameras.createFree("example:free",
        new WorldCameraView(0, 80, 0, 90, 20, 0, 60, 1280, 720),
        CameraRenderSettings.defaults(), frame -> consume(frame));
CameraHandle fixed = MinecraftCameras.createFixed("example:follow", entity,
        new CameraProjection(60, 1280, 720),
        CameraRenderSettings.defaults(), frame -> consume(frame));

createFree accepts either a WorldCameraView or a Supplier<WorldCameraView>, each with a default overload that omits the settings. The original MinecraftCameras.create(...) is kept as a compatibility entry point for Free Camera.

The createFixed signatures are as follows; all of them return CameraHandle:

createFixed(String viewId, Entity entity, CameraProjection projection,
            CameraRenderSettings settings, Consumer<OutputFrame<FrameTexture>> consumer)
createFixed(String viewId, Supplier<? extends Entity> entity, CameraProjection projection,
            CameraRenderSettings settings, Consumer<OutputFrame<FrameTexture>> consumer)
createFixed(String viewId, CameraTarget target, CameraProjection projection,
            CameraRenderSettings settings, Consumer<OutputFrame<FrameTexture>> consumer)
createFixed(String viewId, CameraTarget target, CameraProjection projection,
            CameraFollowSettings follow, CameraRenderSettings settings,
            Consumer<OutputFrame<FrameTexture>> consumer)

A Free/Fixed view ID must be non-empty and unique, and must not be minecraft:main. Player uses minecraft:main, and only one Player handle with a lifecycle is allowed; multiple consumers share the main frame through MinecraftFrameOutputs.open(MIRROR, ...). Player output includes the native world, hands, post-processing, and HUD/GUI, and does not render the world again. Pausing/closing only cancels this handle's subscription; the player's main window and other main-frame consumers keep running. Free/Fixed outputs the world frame.

docs.title: Follow data and entity integration
docs.text:
CameraTarget target = MinecraftCameraTargets.entity(() -> Minecraft.getInstance().player);
fixed.follow(target); // switches the target, keeping the projection and offsets
fixed.updateFollowSettings(new CameraFollowSettings(
        0, 2, 4,       // world-coordinate offset, not rotated with the entity orientation
        0, 10, 0,      // yaw / pitch / roll, in degrees
        true));        // follow the orientation; the angle fields act as additional offsets
fixed.setVerticalFov(55);
fixed.zoom(2);
fixed.setProjection(new CameraProjection(50, 1920, 1080));

CameraTarget is the generic functional interface CameraTarget.Pose sample(float partialTick); Pose(double x, double y, double z, float yaw, float pitch, float roll) contains no Entity or model format type. A custom host can bind any object. The Minecraft adapter uses the entity's interpolated eye position and look direction by default. Passing an entity object keeps that object bound; passing a supplier can pick up a new object after a respawn or dimension change.

In the default CameraFollowSettings.defaults(), all offsets are 0 and followRotation=true. When set to false, the position is still followed, and yaw/pitch/roll act as an absolute orientation in the world. FOV, zoom, projection, and render configuration updates all preserve the target binding. This interface has no automatic wall avoidance or collision push-out logic.

A target that returns null is temporarily unavailable. When the entity is null, has been removed, or does not belong to the current source world, the Minecraft adapter skips that view, pauses its chunk subscriptions, and keeps the handle and output; it resumes automatically once the target becomes available. While waiting, CameraState stays READY and that view's frame counter does not increase; pose() throws IllegalStateException and does not fail the handle. FOV/projection can also be set before the target first appears. A runtime exception thrown by the target fails the camera and releases its resources.

followTarget() returns Optional<CameraTarget>; followSettings() returns the current immutable configuration. Calling a follow write or followSettings() on Player/Free throws UnsupportedOperationException. Fixed does not accept updatePose / moveTo / moveBy / rotateTo / rotateBy / animation(); control it through the follow configuration.

docs.title: Free control and render configuration
docs.text:
For the Free position, rotation, and animation interfaces see Camera animation. Player does not accept standalone pose, projection, follow, animation, and render configuration writes; the corresponding operations throw UnsupportedOperationException.

free.setProjection(new CameraProjection(65, 1280, 720));
CameraRenderSettings settings = free.renderSettings().orElseThrow();
free.updateRenderSettings(new CameraRenderSettings(12,
        CameraRenderSettings.Quality.FANCY,
        CameraRenderSettings.Shader.pack(shaderPack)));

renderSettings() returns empty for Player and the current configuration for Minecraft Free/Fixed. updateRenderSettings rebuilds that camera view's renderer/assets/Iris session on the next render frame where the target is available, preserving pose/follow, animation, view ID, and output subscription. The current frame and its callback keep using the old session configuration, so requesting an update from a callback is safe. The same configuration is not rebuilt; while rendering is paused the change takes effect later. A shader pack requires Iris, and an initialization failure follows the camera failure/release contract. For the fields and resource-pack rules see Multi-camera configuration.

CameraProjection requires a vertical FOV within (0, 180) degrees and positive integer width and height, and provides from(view), withVerticalFov, zoom, and apply(view). Modifying the projection of a Free camera stops its own animation; updating the render configuration does not stop the animation. A window-owned Free Camera uses the actual framebuffer/DPI size.

WorldCameraView.forward(Vector3f out), inverseView(Matrix4f out) and projection(float near, float far, Matrix4f out) write and return a shared direction, camera-to-world matrix and OpenGL perspective matrix. Direction follows Minecraft yaw/pitch; the inverse view includes roll. Projection uses the view's FOV and aspect ratio and requires finite 0 < near < far. For local scenes, construct the view in the same local frame before converting coordinates to float. The Nebula demo shares these matrices between OBJ rasterization and volume rays.

docs.title: Host extension and lifecycle
docs.text:
A pure Java host uses CameraSource.Player(ViewProvider), CameraSource.Free(Supplier<WorldCameraView>), or CameraSource.Fixed(CameraTarget, CameraProjection, CameraFollowSettings) to create the generic data, and hands it to OwnedCamera(String viewId, CameraSource source, Producer producer, Output output, Runnable checkThread, Runnable onClosed). The original constructor that takes a pose supplier still creates a Free Camera. Player's ViewProvider.sample(float partialTick) provides the native camera snapshot; the host implements the actual output producer.

sampleAvailablePose(partialTick) returns an Optional, letting the host skip rendering when a fixed target is unavailable; samplePose(partialTick) requires a pose for this frame. Only Free advances the animation tick; target sampling does not advance simulation time. Producer.renderSettings/updateRenderSettings are the host configuration extension points. Pausing, failure, closing, and resource ownership follow Multi-camera lifecycle.

docs.title: Verification entry
docs.text:
./gradlew :modules:modelling:modelUnitTest
./gradlew :modules:modelling:runClientHeadless -PkasugaClientDirectory=/absolute/path/to/isolated-client -PkasugaQuickPlayWorld=camera-types -PkasugaTestCameraTypes=true

Prepare a copy of the test world in the isolated directory. The client success marker is CAMERA_TYPES_SMOKE_PASS, and the report is at debug/camera-types.json; it covers native main-output sharing and pausing, Free projection, entity interpolation, target recovery, session rebuild after a configuration change from a callback, real world textures, and GL error checks. The JVM tests cover type control boundaries, double precision, offsets/orientation, projection preserving the target, and release on failure.

docs.title: Configuration Options
docs.text:
This page catalogs all configuration mechanisms and options verified in the KasugaLibNext codebase, covering NeoForge ModConfigSpec (registered via Micronaut Configurable beans), JSON/TOML runtime configuration files, and JVM system properties / environment variables.

Note: There is no CoreConfig class in modules/core. Core rendering configuration lives in ClientRenderingRegistry, while other subsystems expose their settings through module-owned Configurable beans, JSON persistence files, or JVM properties.

docs.title: 1. NeoForge ModConfigSpec and the Configurable SPI
docs.text:
During the DI startup phase (see Lifecycle and Initialization Order), ModApplicationContext.init(ApplicationContext, IEventBus, ModContainer) invokes lib.kasuga.inject.auto_configure.Configurable.configure(context, modEventBus, modContainer) right after context.start():

  1. Collects all active beans implementing Configurable via context.getBeansOfType(Configurable.class) (respecting @BeanOnlyIn, @CreateModBeans, and other Micronaut conditions).
  2. Allocates one ModConfigSpec.Builder for each ModConfig.Type (CLIENT, SERVER, COMMON, STARTUP).
  3. Calls onConfigure(ModConfig.Type, ModConfigSpec.Builder) on every bean, which dispatches to configureClient, configureServer, configureCommon, or configureStartup.
  4. Calls modContainer.registerConfig(type, spec) for every built IConfigSpec that is non-empty (!spec.isEmpty()).

docs.title: 1.1 CLIENT Options (Physical Client Only)
docs.text:
Registered by @BeanOnlyIn.Client beans and active only on the physical client:

Config Class (FQCN) TOML Key Type Default / Constraint Description lib.kasuga.registration.beans.rendering.ClientRenderingRegistry ignore_block_entity_renderer boolean false When true, skips BlockEntityRenderer registration through ClientRenderingRegistry.registerBlockEntityRenderer(...) and logs a WARN lib.kasuga.rendering.effect.builtin.weather.WeatherFilterConfig enable_weather_filter boolean true Enables 3D world-space weather occlusion for indoor entity/scene spaces (rain, snow, splashes, and muffled rain audio) lib.kasuga.rendering.effect.builtin.weather.WeatherFilterConfig included_entity_types List<String> [] (entries validated via ResourceLocation.tryParse) Optional entity type IDs that also occlude rain and snow (e.g., "minecraft:boat") lib.kasuga.rendering.effect.builtin.weather.WeatherFilterConfig excluded_entity_types List<String> [] (entries validated via ResourceLocation.tryParse) Entity type IDs excluded from automatic weather occlusion (e.g., "create:carriage_contraption")

Outside a bootstrapped Micronaut / FML config environment (such as plain JVM unit tests), WeatherFilterConfig safely falls back to defaults (isWeatherFilterEnabled() returns true; included/excluded ID sets are empty).

docs.title: 1.2 SERVER Options (Dedicated Server Only)
docs.text: Config Class (FQCN) TOML Key Type Default Description lib.kasuga.scripting.ScriptingServerApplication ignore_scripting_errors boolean false Annotated with @BeanOnlyIn.DedicatedServer. When ServerResourceReloadFinishEvent detects missing script engines: logs WARN if true, or throws RuntimeException if false. Note: non-empty packageSystem.getEngineErrors() still throws RuntimeException

docs.title: 1.3 COMMON Options (CreateConfig)
docs.text:
lib.kasuga.create.CreateConfig is annotated with @Context and @CreateModBeans (active only when ModList.get().isLoaded("create")). Several defaults delegate to KasugaLibCreateApi:

TOML Key Type Default / Range Static Accessor (CreateConfig) Description enable_multi_bogey_carriage boolean KasugaLibCreateApi.getMultiBogeyCarriageDefault() (initially false) isMultiBogeyCarriageEnabled() Allows train carriages to be assembled with more than two bogeys; when false, assembly, persistence, sync, and rendering use the vanilla two-bogey path enable_carriage_y_offset boolean KasugaLibCreateApi.getCarriageYOffsetDefault() (initially false) isCarriageYOffestEnabled() Allows carriages to have vertical (Y-axis) offsets max_bogey_offset double 1.0D ([0.0D, Double.MAX_VALUE]) maxBogeyOffset() Maximum lateral offset (in blocks) an interior bogey may shift from its carriage-local position on curves max_carriage_y_offset double 0.5D ([0.0D, Double.MAX_VALUE]) maxCarriageYOffset() Maximum vertical distance (in blocks) a carriage body may offset from its bogeys in either direction derailed_on_bogey_offset_overflow boolean KasugaLibCreateApi.getDerailedOnBogeyOffsetDefault() (initially false) derailedOnBogeyOffsetEnabled() Whether a train derails when bogeys reach their maximum offsets enable_contraption_lod boolean true isContraptionLodEnabled() Sends distant LOD render meshes for active Create contraptions enable_contraption_weather_filter boolean KasugaLibCreateApi.getContraptionWeatherFilterDefault() (initially true) isContraptionWeatherFilterEnabled() Automatically occludes rain and snow inside Create contraptions (e.g., trains) enable_sable_weather_filter boolean true isSableWeatherFilterEnabled() Automatically occludes rain and snow inside Sable / Aeronautics physics sublevels

docs.title: Downstream Default Overrides (KasugaLibCreateApi)
docs.text:
Dependent mods can override the generated defaults for four COMMON keys during mod construction (before configs load) via lib.kasuga.create.KasugaLibCreateApi. Explicit entries in the user's TOML config file still take priority:

  • KasugaLibCreateApi.setMultiBogeyCarriageDefault(boolean)
  • KasugaLibCreateApi.setCarriageYOffsetDefault(boolean)
  • KasugaLibCreateApi.setDerailedOnBogeyOffsetDefault(boolean)
  • KasugaLibCreateApi.setContraptionWeatherFilterDefault(boolean)

No bean currently implements configureStartup(ModConfigSpec.Builder), so the STARTUP spec remains empty and is not registered.

docs.text:
Low-level rendering, physics, and headless client controls read JVM -D properties and environment variables:
