docs.title: ItemModelRenderers / ItemModelRenderer
docs.text:
The item-side entry of the model system: maps an Item to a pipeline model and provides a BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer (BEWLR) so the GUI, hand and dropped items use this project's renderer.

Package: lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.api.item Source: modules/modelling/src/main/java/lib/kasuga/rendering/models/mc/api/item/

Integration steps and JSON forms: Content Integration: Block and Item Model Resources.

docs.title: ItemModelRenderers
docs.text:
A static registry plus a shared extension. Writes happen during client setup, reads on the render thread.

Method Signature Notes register static void register(Item item, ResourceLocation model, @Nullable String modelName) Binds an item to a model. modelName is MMD-only; pass null otherwise. Last write wins. register static void register(Item item, ResourceLocation model, @Nullable String modelName, float guiScale) Same as above with a GUI display-size multiplier composed with the standard 0.625; it must be finite and positive. binding static @Nullable Binding binding(Item item) The binding, or null when the item is not registered. items static Set<Item> items() Currently registered items (read-only, for diagnostics). clientExtensions static IClientItemExtensions clientExtensions() The shared extension to pass to RegisterClientExtensionsEvent#registerItem. renderer static ItemModelRenderer renderer() The shared BEWLR, created on first use. 
public record Binding(ResourceLocation model, @Nullable String modelName, float guiScale) {}

The two-argument constructor remains compatible and defaults guiScale to 1.0. Scaling affects only ItemDisplayContext.GUI; hand, ground and world block rendering keep their existing sizes.

docs.title: ItemModelRenderer
docs.text:
extends BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer. renderByItem behaviour:

Condition Behaviour the item is not registered in ItemModelRenderers returns immediately, draws nothing the model is not published yet returns for this frame, retries next frame, no log spam PipelineRegistry.backend() is null (not a client runtime) returns otherwise resolves the item's ModelInstance, marks it schedule-visible, draws three passes via MCBackend.renderInstance

Details:

  • Instance identity: kasuga_lib:item/<namespace>/<path>, one per Item, not per ItemStack.
  • Scheduling: the instance stays VANILLA_RENDERER; it is widened to ALWAYS for the draw and restored afterwards. This keeps the world pass from drawing it at the origin.
  • Sampling: the sample mark is released on every draw, so GUI + hand + ground draws in the same frame each sample with the current partialTick.
  • Transform: ItemRenderer already applied translate(-0.5) (vanilla [0,1] model space); the BEWLR cancels it with translate(0.5) and then applies the block/block.json display table (see guide section 5).
  • GUI nudge: private static final float GUI_DOWN_SHIFT = -0.5f; negative is down (GUI Y is flipped), in the model space before the 0.625 scale, roughly 5 px at GUI scale 1.
  • Lifecycle: instances live for the client's lifetime; there is no per-item destruction path. McModelHandle.mount() self-heals them after a resource reload.

docs.title: Interface with MCBackend
docs.text:
Method Notes boolean MCBackend#renderInstance(ModelInstance model, MCBackendContext context) Draws a single instance outside the world pass using the caller's PoseStack; returns whether the instance was found.

The caller builds the MCBackendContext: with camera and frustum null the distance/frustum gates are skipped, the poseStack belongs to the caller, and modelViewMatrix/projectionMatrix come from RenderSystem.

docs.title: Failures and diagnostics
docs.text: Symptom Where Meaning Item invisible no log the item model is not builtin/entity, or registerItem was never called Model appears late [KasugaModelPipelines] bound ... the resource just got published; normal lazy binding Item permanently invisible no log check whether ItemModelRenderers.binding(item) is null

docs.title: LDLib2 Compose Integration
docs.text:
Compose is an optional extension published independently upstream. This project uses ldlib2-compose-1.21.1:21.0.0.1:all and LDLib2 2.2.44, while the adapter module develops and runs on NeoForge 21.1.238. Both Kotlin and the Compose compiler are 2.1.20, and the runtime is embedded in the upstream all JAR. Dependencies and third-party integration code live in external/uip/ldlib-compose; ordinary LDLib2 calls remain in external/uip/ldlib, and the shared library does not depend on Compose.

Compose handles declarative UI construction and state recomposition. The demo still uses StylesheetManager.MODERN, so controls look similar to ordinary LDLib2 pages; the title LDLib2 Compose / 世界双端 UI identifies this demo.

docs.title: Client-Local World Panels
docs.text:
Create world panels on the client render thread after entering a world. transform maps GUI pixels to absolute world coordinates, following the same rules as LdElement.

val panel = ComposeWorldUi.attach(Constants.UI_BACKEND, 360, 300, transform) {
    Box(layout = { width(320.px); height(260.px) }) {
        Text("Compose / 模型预览")
        ModelPreview(
            ResourceLocation.parse("kasuga_lib:models/gltf/maribel.glb"),
            layout = { width(280.px); height(220.px) },
        )
    }
}
// Close on the client when the panel owner removes it; leaving the world also cleans it up.
panel.close()

ModelPreview can also be placed inside an ordinary composeModularUI(...). The resource location and optional modelName follow model_loader. yaw and pitch are in radians, and zoom is positive; changing these parameters via Compose state rotates or zooms the preview. The node factory creates the preview only once so recomposition does not repeatedly allocate GPU resources; the old preview is released when the resource key changes or a conditional branch removes the node.

docs.title: Client-Server UI: Fixed Registration, Client Recomposition
docs.text:
You must follow the upstream server-driven UI rules. UISyncManager assigns numeric IDs in registration order, while composition runs only on the client. Calling registration APIs such as bindDataSource, setOnServerClick, or addServerEventListener inside a composable causes the IDs on the two sides to drift out of sync.

The counter below constructs one synchronized value and one message host in the same order on both sides. The client sends only user intent, and the server determines the result.

class CounterMenu : PlayerUIMenuType.PlayerUIHolder {
    private var count = 0
    private val mirror = mutableStateOf(0)

    override fun createUI(player: Player): ModularUI {
        val root = UIElement().layout { it.width(220f).height(100f) }
        val host = ComposeElement {
            val server = rememberServerMessenger()
            Box {
                Text("Server count: ${mirror.value}")
                Button(onClick = { server.send("increment") }, text = "+")
            }
        }
        root.addChild(BindableValue<Int>().bind(
            DataBindingBuilder.intValS2C { count }
                .onRemoteSyncReceived { mirror.value = it }
                .build(player.level().isClientSide)
        ))
        if (!player.level().isClientSide) {
            host.onMessage("increment") { count = (count + 1).coerceAtMost(100) }
        }
        root.addChild(host)
        return ModularUI.of(UI.of(root, StylesheetManager.MODERN), player)
    }
}

Dynamic lists likewise carry the entire model in a single synchronized value and build controls using key(row.id). The demo uses CompoundTag to transfer each row ID, Chinese title, and acknowledgment count; removal validates argument types, and addition caps the row count. Do not register per-row bindings or RPCs. Message handlers are registered on the outer ComposeElement constructed in createUI; that host must be added on both sides.

Register the factory on both sides with PlayerUIMenuType.register(id) { CounterMenu() }, and open it on the server with PlayerUIMenuType.openUI(player, id). Player ownership, validity, and server lifecycle of the menu object follow the normal LDLib2 path.

docs.title: Moving a Real Client-Server Menu into World Space
docs.text:
Once the standard open-menu packet completes and the client's ModularUIContainerScreen has initialized, call on the render thread:

var host = LdMenuElement.attach(Constants.UI_BACKEND, menu, 400, 360, transform);
Constants.UI_BACKEND.openPointer();
// When finished, close the world panel and the menu still held by the current player.
host.close();

This transfers the existing widget tree while retaining player.containerMenu and the upstream synchronization channel, without creating a separate client-authoritative copy. After the original screen is removed, Compose recomposes when the world host initializes. The host supplies client synchronization ticking, while the server continues syncing through the normal menu flow. LDLib2's UISurface receives the actual canvas dimensions and borrowed FBO so clipping and visual layers do not mistakenly use the main window dimensions.

A player can have only one active synchronized menu at a time. Opening a new menu, closing the menu from the server, or leaving the world cleans up the old host; calling close() on an old host does not close a menu opened later. The application holder remains responsible for server-side permission checks and isStillValid validation. Multiple client-only panels may coexist; use ComposeWorldUi.attach for those instead of hijacking the menu channel to fake client-server synchronization.

See the adapter module documentation for development demos, automated checks, two-client commands, and verification boundaries.

docs.title: Library Packaging, Shade Relocation, and Multiversion Structure Reference
docs.text:
This reference documents the root build conventions and packaging modules (:modules:library, :modules:annotations, :modules:multiversion, and GAMELIBRARY subprojects), including Shadow relocation rules, neoforge.mods.toml metadata assembly, and dependency version baselines.

For the Gradle plugins themselves see Gradle Plugins, Codegen, and Resource Compiler Reference; for the companion scripting mod :external:slp:javet see Scripting and Javet Runtime Reference.

docs.title: Monorepo Build Conventions
docs.text:
Root settings.gradle registers includeBuild './modules/gradle-plugin' and 23 include subprojects (22 unconditional, plus :modules:old only when -PkasugaIncludeOld=true). Root build.gradle applies three global rules:

  1. Java 21 toolchain: java.toolchain.languageVersion = JavaLanguageVersion.of(21) (options.encoding = 'UTF-8' is configured per subproject on JavaCompile / Javadoc tasks rather than in root build.gradle).
  2. Unique archive names (JPMS safety): every subproject with base receives archivesName = "kasuga-${project.name}". ModDevGradle derives the runtime JPMS module name from each JAR filename, so subprojects must never share mod_id (kasuga_lib) as their archive name.
  3. Global Lombok injection: every SourceSet automatically adds org.projectlombok:lombok:${lombok_version} (1.18.42 in gradle.properties) to compileOnly and annotationProcessor.

docs.text:
shadowJar sets archiveClassifier.set('all') (producing kasuga-library-1.0.0-all.jar), reading configurations = [project.configurations.shadowLibrary] plus from(sourceSets.main.output) and the 8 merged subproject outputs appended by useModProject.

Explicit shadowLibrary inclusions:

  • Internal modules: :modules:inject, :modules:utils, :modules:shader, :modules:formula
  • Third-party libraries:
  • de.javagl:jgltf-model:2.0.4 and de.javagl:jgltf-impl-v2:2.0.4
  • modules/render-core/libs/caliko-1.3.8.jar (while processResources copies caliko-LICENSE.txt into META-INF/licenses/)
  • com.google.zxing:core:3.5.3

Shadow configuration details:

  • mergeServiceFiles(): merges META-INF/services/ descriptors.
  • transform(MicronautServiceShadowTransformer) {}: rewrites META-INF/micronaut/** entries to match package relocations.
  • Package relocations (preventing clashes with user environments or other Micronaut/Jakarta mods):
  • io.micronaut -> lib.kasuga.vendors.io.micronaut
  • jakarta.inject -> lib.kasuga.vendors.jakarta.inject
  • jakarta.annotation -> lib.kasuga.vendors.jakarta.annotation

For compilation and ModDev runs, library/build.gradle also declares implementation / additionalRuntimeClasspath / compileOnly dependencies on Micronaut 4.9.10 (excluding org.slf4j:slf4j-api), Create 6.0.11-346 (transitive = false), Ponder 1.0.92+mc1.21.1, Flywheel API/Runtime 1.0.7, Registrate MC1.21-1.3.0+67, and CC:Tweaked 1.116.1.

docs.title: Lifecycle and Initialization Order
docs.text: This page documents the startup, Micronaut DI bootstrap, RegistrationStage dispatch order, client and shader initialization, capability boundary between the registration phase and the reload phase, and shutdown cleanup in KasugaLibNext.

docs.title: 1. Startup Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["Class load KasugaLib: ModApplicationContext.create()"] --> B["KasugaLib constructor: ModApplicationContext.init()"]
    B --> B1["Register modEventBus / forgeEventBus / modContainer singletons"]
    B1 --> B2["context.start(): instantiate @Context beans & @PostConstruct"]
    B2 --> B3["Configurable.configure(): register NeoForge ModConfigSpec"]
    B3 --> C["Post KasugaLibStartupEvent on modEventBus"]
    C --> D["RegistrationStage sequence (Mod Event Bus)"]
    D --> E["FMLClientSetupEvent / Reload Listeners / Shader Registration"]
    E --> F["ServerStartingEvent / Resource Reload (/reload and F3 + T)"]
    F --> G["ServerStoppingEvent / GameShuttingDownEvent Cleanup"]

docs.title: 2. Micronaut DI Bootstrap and @Context Startup Order
2.1 KasugaLib and ModApplicationContext
docs.text:
In the mod entry class lib.kasuga.KasugaLib (@Mod("kasuga_lib")):

  1. Static initialization: ModApplicationContext.create(KasugaLib.class) builds the Micronaut ApplicationContext. In development (!FMLLoader.isProduction()), it wraps classloaders with CombinedClassLoader(modMainClass.getClassLoader(), ApplicationContext.class.getClassLoader()) so bean definitions across classpath entries are discoverable.
  2. KasugaLib(IEventBus, ModContainer) constructor:
  3. Calls ModApplicationContext.init(context, modEventBus, modContainer):
    1. Registers named singletons: IEventBus ("modEventBus" and "forgeEventBus") and ModContainer ("modContainer").
    2. Calls context.start(), instantiating all active @Context beans that pass @BeanOnlyIn, @CreateModBeans, and related Micronaut conditions, and running their @PostConstruct hooks.
    3. Calls Configurable.configure(context, modEventBus, modContainer) to register every non-empty NeoForge ModConfigSpec.
  4. Posts new KasugaLibStartupEvent() via ModLoader.postEvent(...). Dependent mods can call KasugaLib.afterRunning(modEventBus, hook) to listen for KasugaLibStartupEvent (or run immediately if the context is already running). For example, KasugaLibJavet waits for both KasugaLibStartupEvent and native V8 library initialization before registering its ScriptEngineType and BuiltinModuleRegistry factories.

docs.title: 2.2 Core @Context Bean @PostConstruct Wiring
docs.text:
During context.start(), @Context beans wire the registration and reload subsystems:

  • Common and client registry activation:
  • KasugaLibApplication (lib.kasuga): owns the root REGISTRY = KasugaLibRegistry.getRegistryOf("kasuga_lib") and calls REGISTRY.register(modEventBus) in @PostConstruct, registering Side.COMMON on RegisterContextRegistry.
  • KasugaLibClientApplication (@BeanOnlyIn.Client): calls KasugaLibApplication.REGISTRY.registerClient(modEventBus), registering Side.CLIENT.
  • Stage dispatchers:
  • DefaultRegisterContextDispatchers: hooks NewRegistryEvent, RegisterEvent (EventPriority.HIGHEST), RegisterPayloadHandlersEvent, RegisterCapabilitiesEvent, and BuildCreativeModeTabContentsEvent onto Side.COMMON.
  • DefaultClientRegisterContextDispatchers (@BeanOnlyIn.Client): hooks RegisterMenuScreensEvent, RegisterClientExtensionsEvent, and ModelEvent.BakingCompleted onto Side.CLIENT.
  • Data-driven and Create wiring:
  • JsonTreeIntegration: subscribes to RegisterContextRegistry.Side.COMMON so every configured mod Registry queries DataDrivenRegistrationProviders.find(modId) first and falls back to JsonTreeBuilder.buildForMod(modId), attaching the resulting JsonRegistryGroup as a child of modRegistry.
  • CreateRegistrationDispatcher (@CreateModBeans): calls registerBefore(Side.COMMON, RegistrationStage.REGISTER_EVENT, ...) so Create track and bogey entries are prepared and committed before any standard Reg handles RegisterEvent.
  • ClientCreateRegistrationBridge (@CreateModBeans, @BeanOnlyIn.Client): attaches itself to Registry under CreateClientBridge.class on Side.CLIENT (on dedicated servers, CreateClientBridge.noop() is used instead).
  • Reload and factory registration:
  • FsmReloadHandlerRegistrar registers FsmReloadHandler before FsmClipsReloadHandler in ReloadHandlerRegistry.
  • ProxyModelBlockFactories registers built-in proxy_model and proxy_model_be factories in FactoryRegistry.
  • ResourceSystem attaches listeners on modEventBus and forgeEventBus; ReloadOrchestrator and ScriptingApplication (injecting ScriptingSystem) register themselves via ResourceSystem.registerConsumer(...).

docs.title: 3. RegistrationStage Order and Event Mapping
docs.text:
lib.kasuga.registration.stages.RegistrationStage<T> defines reference-identity tokens for registration phases. Each root Registry (Reg tree) dispatches RegisterContext<T> recursively down its child tree:

Order Stage Token Payload Type Dispatcher Side Underlying NeoForge Event / Trigger Notes 1 RegistrationStage.NEW_REGISTRY NewRegistryEvent COMMON NewRegistryEvent Registers custom MC registries (RegistryReg, DeviceRegistries, DocumentComponentRegistries) 2 CreateRegistrationStages.PREPARE CreateRegistrationEvent COMMON registerBefore(COMMON, REGISTER_EVENT, ...) Guards once-only idempotent preparation via CreateRegistrationState (NEW → PREPARING → COMMITTED / FAILED); validates then commits actions in fixed Phase order: TRACK_MATERIAL → BOGEY_SIZE → BOGEY_BLOCK → BOGEY_STYLE 3 RegistrationStage.REGISTER_EVENT RegisterStageContext COMMON RegisterEvent (EventPriority.HIGHEST) Populates vanilla/custom registries (blocks, items, block entities, entities, fluids, menus, sounds, data components) 4 RegistrationStage.REGISTER_CAPABILITIES CapabilityRegistration COMMON RegisterCapabilitiesEvent Registers NeoForge capabilities for block entities or entities 5 RegistrationStage.PAYLOAD_REGISTRATION PayloadRegistrationStage COMMON RegisterPayloadHandlersEvent Registers network payloads via memoized getRegistrar(version) 6 RegistrationStage.CREATIVE_TAB_CONTENT_REGISTRATION CreativeTabContentRegistration COMMON BuildCreativeModeTabContentsEvent Populates creative tabs 7 RegistrationStage.MENU_SCREEN_BINDING MenuScreenBindingStage CLIENT RegisterMenuScreensEvent Binds MenuType to client Screen factories 8 RegistrationStage.REGISTER_CLIENT_EXTENSIONS FluidClientExtensionsStage CLIENT RegisterClientExtensionsEvent Dispatched via registry.dispatchRegister(...) (does not run beforeDispatchFunctions) 9 RegistrationStage.BAKING_COMPLETE BakingCompleteStage CLIENT ModelEvent.BakingCompleted Registers BlockEntityRenderer, EntityRenderer, and DocumentComponentRenderer — RegistrationStage.COMMON_SETUP RegisterStageContext — Not dispatched Declared on RegistrationStage, but DefaultRegisterContextDispatchers does not currently bind it to any NeoForge event (an unused FMLCommonSetupStageContext payload class also exists)

docs.title: 4. Client Setup, Model, and Shader Initialization
docs.text:
Client mod-bus events in lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.Constants and ResourceSystem proceed as follows:

  1. FMLClientSetupEvent:
  2. Constants.onClientSetup: applies -Dkasuga.shaderPreparationWorkers and prestarts workers (ShaderPreparationScheduler), initializes ShaderParameterPersistence (<configDir>/kasuga_lib/shader-parameters.json), creates UIBackend, and posts RegisterRenderPipelinesEvent(CLIENT_RENDER_PIPELINES) once so integrations can register client-lifetime pipelines, effects, post-process graphs, and generated shaders via event.registrar(owner).
  3. ResourceSystem.onClientSetup: wraps Minecraft.getInstance().getResourceManager() in a client ScopedResourceManager, registers it with ReloadableResourceManager, and notifies ScopedResourceManagerConsumers (ReloadOrchestrator, ScriptingSystem).
  4. RegisterClientReloadListenersEvent:
  5. Registers ModelParticleRuntime.invalidateTextures(), calls IrisCompat.onStart(), constructs CombinedTextureManager, calls PipelineRegistry.registerBuiltins(basic) and PipelineRegistry.registerDefaultRoutes(router), and registers KasugaModelManager.
  6. RegisterShadersEvent:
  7. Registers core UML shaders (ksglib_main, ksglib_global_batch, and optional ksglib_oit_composite; failure on ksglib_oit_composite logs a WARN and falls back to sorted translucent rendering).
  8. Calls RenderShaderRegistry.registerShaders(event): ShaderPreloadPolicy.EAGER shaders await source preparation and compile synchronously; ShaderPreloadPolicy.DEFERRED shaders are rescheduled into ShaderPreloadScheduler for frame-budgeted compilation.
  9. RegisterRenderBuffersEvent and RegisterNamedRenderTypesEvent:
  10. Registers model RenderTypes (OPAQUE / CUTOUT / TRANSLUCENT, global batching, Iris compat, and OIT passes) and RenderTypeGroups.

docs.title: 5. Registration Phase vs. Reload Phase Capability Boundary
docs.text:
KasugaLibNext separates the two phases (see How data-driven registration works and Unified Resource Platform and Script Tickets):

Aspect Registration Phase Reload Phase Trigger Mod startup through RegisterEvent (once per process) ServerStartingEvent, /reload, client startup, and F3 + T Source Mod JAR (JsonTreeBuilder) or host-composed ContentSources (DataDrivenBuildPipeline) Resource/data pack stack (ResourceManager) or ResourceSource snapshots (pack-stack overrides apply) Index Domain on_register inside data/<ns>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/*.json on_reload in the same manifests, plus ReloadHandler.globDirectories() (e.g., state_machines/) Supported Objects Registry-frozen objects (Block, Item, BlockEntityType, RegistryGroup, etc.) FSM definitions, animation clips, models/textures, shader sources/parameters, script packages (ScriptRuntime / ManagedScriptEntryPoint) Validation & Error Policy DataDrivenBuildPipeline supports BuildOptions.STRICT: separates side-effect-free prepare() (parsing, validation, RegistryClaim) from build() (applies by PHASE_GROUPS → PHASE_CONTENT → PHASE_EMBEDDED and runs BuildFinalizers) ReloadOrchestrator isolates errors per participant: clears Diagnostics.Domain.RELOAD_DATA, then runs clearBucket() → decode() → DuplicateIdResolver → register() → afterReload() without aborting pack reload Atomic Publication Objects are committed to MC registries during RegisterEvent KasugaModelManager prepares models and PBR bakes asynchronously, then swaps atomically on the game thread via ModelPublicationCoordinator / McModelAssemblies.publishResourceGeneration; ResourceCoordinator follows prepare-then-publish per monotonic generation and retires the previous ResourceGeneration

docs.title: 6. World Runtime and Shutdown Sequence
docs.text:
• Server world lifecycle:
  • ServerStartingEvent: ResourceSystem creates and attaches a server-scoped ScopedResourceManager.
  • ServerStartedEvent: Saved.Impl<T> binds the active MinecraftServer (calling Saved.get() before this throws IllegalStateException).
  • /reload (MinecraftServer.reloadResources): MinecraftServerMixin invokes ResourceSystem.onServerReloading(server) and posts ServerResourceReloadFinishEvent (ScriptingServerApplication checks missing engines here).
  • ServerStoppingEvent: Saved.Impl<T> unloads its MinecraftServer and dimension cache; ResourceSystem notifies consumers (onResourceManagerRemoved, shutting down server ScriptRuntime) and closes server-managed closeables and ResourceCoordinator scopes.
  • Client world change and shutdown:
  • Level switch / disconnect (ClientTickEvent.Post / MinecraftWorldViews.worldChanged()): MinecraftModelRuntime releases active drags and clears particle/light world state; ClientEffectRuntime clears live effects and PostProcessTargetPool; MinecraftWorldViews releases offscreen render targets and CameraIrisSessions while keeping subscriptions.
  • GameShuttingDownEvent: invokes ResourceSystem.close() while the client OpenGL context is still valid, closing client/server consumers, managed scopes, and unifiedVfs (never joining script threads so shutdown cannot stall on a hung engine).

docs.title: Minecraft Model Components v1
docs.text:
The Blockbench editing and preview plugin is maintained in the standalone repository KasugaLib-BlockBenchPlugin; the data format and game-side loading behavior described here remain maintained in KasugaLibNext.

Adds a kasuga_lib object to existing model JSON files. This object does not replace the base model structure: native geometry, textures, hierarchy, display transforms, animations, and related data are still emitted verbatim by the original codecs. Removing kasuga_lib leaves the exact same base model; ordinary readers do not need to understand these components to load static geometry. Specific tools using strict validators that reject unknown fields need to be verified separately for acceptance.

Model Field location Bone source .bbmodel Root kasuga_lib Native outliner groups Java block/item JSON Root kasuga_lib Extension bones; base elements unchanged Bedrock geometry JSON Each minecraft:geometry[i].kasuga_lib Native bones + empty control bones from the extension 
{
  "elements": [],
  "textures": {},
  "kasuga_lib": {
    "version": 1,
    "bones": [],
    "bindings": [],
    "emitters": []
  }
}

The example above shows placement only; complete editable projects, Java/Bedrock examples, and the JSON Schema live in examples/model-components/. Unknown fields inside the extension are preserved by the plugin. When the extension is absent, the legacy model loading path is used; unknown versions are preserved verbatim and blocked from editing in the plugin, and the game loader raises a version error.

docs.title: Bones and References
docs.text:
Each bone entry contains id (a stable project-local identifier; Blockbench uses UUIDs), name (the native bone name for this export), parent (parent ID or null), pivot (absolute rest pivot), and components. References are resolved by ID; during game loading they map to the Bone instances created for that load and are not cached across models. Names and IDs must be unique, and parent chains must be acyclic. Renaming a bone keeps references pointing to the original UUID.

All three extension targets use Blockbench coordinates: lengths in pixels, angles in degrees, and +Y up. The game entry converts pixels to 1/16 blocks and angles to radians. Bedrock native pivots negate X in the existing Bedrock loader; extension data is already in Blockbench coordinates and is not negated again. Rigid-body and particle-emitter position values are local offsets relative to their bound bone, and rotation values are local ZYX Euler angles. Java groups provide translation pivots only; native cube rotations continue to be expressed via elements[].rotation.

Java bindings map zero-based indices of the finally exported elements to bone IDs: {"element":0,"bone":"arm-id"}; null or an omitted binding follows the synthetic root. The mapping is generated in the codec's actual outliner traversal order rather than guessing by name, position, or Cube.all order. When inheriting a parent model's elements, its extension can be inherited; if a child model defines its own elements, the parent extension's index mappings are not inherited.

docs.title: Inverse Kinematics (IK)
docs.text:
IK is placed under components.ik on the effector bone:

{
  "target": "target-id",
  "links": [
    {"bone": "upper-id"},
    {"bone": "lower-id", "min": [-90, -45, -30], "max": [90, 45, 30]}
  ],
  "iterations": 32,
  "tolerance": 0.01,
  "max_step": 45
}

links are ordered from base to tip and must be contiguous ancestors of the effector bone, excluding the effector itself. The target must lie outside the driven chain and may be a group without geometry. Tolerance is in pixels; min and max are XYZ rotation delta limits in degrees relative to the animated pose. Evaluation follows the game's order: animation → IK → physics → attachments. The editor uses CCD while the game uses its existing solver, so exact pose-for-pose parity is not guaranteed near singular poses.

docs.title: Diamond Closure and Active Inputs
docs.text:
Optional top-level diamonds close the endpoints of two IK branches onto a shared pin:

"diamonds": [
  {"id": "valve-gear", "first": "branch-a-tip-id", "second": "branch-b-tip-id",
   "iterations": 64, "tolerance": 0.01}
]

first and second are effector bone IDs that define components.ik. Each branch may belong to at most one closure, and the two branches must be distinct. iterations is 1–256, and tolerance is 0.000001–16 pixels. In the plugin's IK sidebar, expand "Advanced Settings" ("高级设置") and click "Diamond Closure Constraints…" ("菱形闭环约束…") to select branches and modify or remove closures, with Undo/Redo support. The midpoint of the two branch targets serves as the initial closure point, then the two fixed-length branches are solved alternately.

Crank rotation angles, slider strokes, and combination-lever cutoff positions may first be written actively by animations or a logic-side PoseDriver. IK then adjusts the permitted rotational degrees of freedom while preserving those active translations; do not simultaneously write rotation tracks to passive connecting rods. Setting both min and max of a pivot link to [0,0,0] locks its animated pose so only subsequent links rotate. Combination-lever position can come from an acceleration controller as an independent input instead of being back-solved from the closure.

The private QJ demo uses qj.running numeric keyframes: a 2-second wheel cycle, a cutoff input varying independently over 8 seconds, two diamond closures, and main-rod IK. Formulas in the original project are sampled into numeric tracks in the editor before export; the current game .bbmodel loader does not evaluate Molang formulas. Endpoints and visible geometry of this model must be compared through external fixtures; generic CCD and the game solver still do not guarantee element-by-element parity for arbitrary linkages.

docs.title: Rigid Bodies and Joints
docs.text:
At most one components.physics per bone:

{
  "shape": "capsule", "mode": "rotation",
  "size": [1, 4, 1], "position": [0, 4, 0], "rotation": [0, 0, 0],
  "mass": 1, "linear_damping": 0.2, "angular_damping": 0.2,
  "friction": 0.5, "restitution": 0,
  "collision_group": 0, "non_collision_mask": 0,
  "parent_body": "parent-bone-id",
  "joint": {"rotation_min": [-45, -45, -45], "rotation_max": [45, 45, 45], "rotation_spring": [0, 0, 0]},
  "stiffness": 80, "gravity": [0, -156.8, 0]
}

shape is sphere, box, or capsule: spheres take size.x as radius, boxes take half-extents along all three axes, and capsules take size.x as radius and size.y as cylinder length (total height y + 2x). mode is kinematic (follows animation), dynamic (writes back position and rotation), or rotation (writes back rotation only). The game uses the existing SkeletonDynamics/Box3D integration; parent_body specifies the connected parent rigid body, anchored at this bone's pivot. Joints use the spherical cone/twist approximation supported by the current backend and do not claim full 6-DOF limits.

stiffness and per-bone gravity apply only to Blockbench spring previews, with gravity in pixels/s². They are meant for inspecting secondary bone inertia and damping; exact collision and parent-joint response are governed by the game runtime, where gravity comes from the active physics scene settings.

docs.title: Lights
docs.text:
Blockbench's "Kasuga: Place Light" ("Kasuga：放置光源") action creates a native Locator. Lights are stored in an optional lights array at the same level as emitters:

"lights": [{
  "id": "lamp-id", "name": "lamp", "bone": "tail-id",
  "position": [0, 16, 0], "rotation": [0, 0, 0],
  "type": "area", "enabled": true, "color": "#55aaff",
  "intensity": 12, "range": 256, "width": 32, "height": 16,
  "two_sided": false, "density": 0.08, "anisotropy": 0
}]

Types are point, area, and volumetric. Colors are sRGB HEX and are converted to linear RGB on load. Optional temperature accepts 1000–40000 K; when present it overrides color, and deleting that field restores the HEX color. position is relative to the bound bone, and rotation uses local ZYX degrees; an area light at zero rotation faces +Z with its rectangular surface in the XY plane. range, width, and height are in pixels (16 = 1 block). Medium density is per block, and anisotropy ranges from -0.9 to 0.9.

Model instances automatically install the light module, sample bone transforms after the existing post-physics attachment update, and reuse WorldLights. Lights follow the model's root position and bone animation; unloading, resource reload, destruction, and world changes clean up their effect handles. Legacy models without lights keep their existing path. See World-Space Lights for surface lighting and volumetric range, occlusion, and limitations.

docs.title: Particle Emitters
docs.text:
Particle emitters are zero-volume native Locators in the outliner that move with their parent bone and produce no triangles on export. Parameters are stored in the extension's emitters array:

{
  "id": "emitter-id", "name": "exhaust", "bone": "tail-id",
  "position": [0, 8, 0], "rotation": [0, 0, 90],
  "enabled": true, "rate": 30, "max_particles": 256, "space": "world",
  "particle": {
    "texture": "minecraft:particle/flame",
    "lifetime": 1, "speed": 8, "spread": 15,
    "size": 1, "color": "#ff8844", "gravity": [0, -4, 0]
  }
}

bone may be null to indicate model root space. Emission points along the locator's local +Y, spread is the emission cone half-angle, speed and acceleration are in pixels/s and pixels/s², and lifetime is in seconds. world particles move independently after emission with acceleration in model world space; local particle coordinates and acceleration follow the emitter. Both the editor and the game use the specified color and texture ID; the game runtime updates on a fixed step and cleans up on model instance destruction, resource reload, and world changes.

Each emitter allows at most 4096 particles and an emission rate of at most 10000/s; fixed-step simulation caps catch-up when resuming from background stalls to prevent emitting a long backlog of particles at once. Saving, exporting, Undo, switching projects, and unloading all stop preview playback and release temporary resources; preview transforms are never written back into the model's authored bone rotations.

docs.title: Minecraft outfit resources and instance switching API
docs.text: For generic geometry/skeleton assembly see Model Assembly. This page only describes Minecraft's resource lookup, publication and handle integration; Model and its generic subsystems have no model format allowlist.

docs.title: Resource pack definitions
docs.text:
Files live in assets/<namespace>/model_assemblies/<path>.json, and the definition ID is <namespace>:<path>. For example assets/example/model_assemblies/winter.json corresponds to example:winter. Source models still have to be preloaded through the existing model_proxy configuration, see model loading.

{
  "body": {
    "id": "body",
    "model": "example:models/character.bbmodel",
    "regions": { "torso": [0, 1, 2] },
    "hide_regions": ["torso"]
  },
  "parts": [
    {
      "id": "shirt",
      "model": "example:models/shirt.glb",
      "bone_mappings": { "shirt_root": "root" }
    },
    {
      "id": "coat",
      "model": "example:models/coat.mmd.zip",
      "model_name": "coat",
      "include_dynamics": true
    }
  ],
  "bind_tolerance": 0.0001
}
Field Default/Requirement body Required part object; id defaults to body parts Optional part array, order preserved; each item's id is required and must not repeat model Required resource location per part; routing reuses the registered model pipeline model_name Optional internal model name, for Readers that need an internal entry lookup bone_mappings Object from source bone name to output bone name, default {}; the body cannot have aliases regions Object from region name to source face index array, default {} hide_regions Array of hidden region names, default []; an unknown name is an error hide_meshes Array of additional hidden face indices, default []; indices must be integers match_body_bones boolean, default true include_dynamics boolean, default true bind_tolerance Finite positive number, default 1e-4

Definitions are read during the resource preparation phase; after textures are ready they are published on the game thread. Invalid JSON makes that preparation fail, and a partial outfit definition is not published. When sources are missing the definition can still be registered, but mount returns false and it retries on the next tick. Validations that depend on the actual model, such as bind matrices and hidden face ranges, run after the full sources are ready. The body and the clothing must already be in the same bind space; this is not an automatic body-fitting interface.

docs.title: McModelHandle
docs.text:
Package: lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.api.

McModelHandle handle = McModelHandle.ofAssembly(
        ResourceLocation.parse("example:winter"), instanceId, entity.position());
if (handle.mount()) {
    handle.scheduleVanillaRenderer();
    handle.markRenderedThisFrame();
}

boolean switched = handle.switchAssembly(ResourceLocation.parse("example:summer"));
Method Behavior static McModelHandle ofAssembly(ResourceLocation id, ResourceLocation instanceId, @Nullable Vec3 pos) Uses the global assembly service; may be created before the resource is published boolean switchAssembly(ResourceLocation id) Swaps using the global service; returns false when the service or the source is not ready boolean switchAssembly(McModelAssemblies service, ResourceLocation id) Explicit service, suited to custom pipelines McModelHandle onInstanceChanged(BiConsumer<ModelInstance, ModelInstance> callback) Called after the new instance has finished restoring its basic state; can install custom drivers/physics; null clears the callback

A swap first resolves the full sources, gets the cached model and mounts the new instance, then releases the handle's old instance. When a source is not ready, the current outfit is left unchanged; a bind/callback exception cleans up the new instance and is thrown to the caller, keeping the old instance. The callback runs before the generic driver migration, and a new driver set there takes precedence; external side effects of the callback itself are the caller's responsibility.

Position, rotation, scale and the double floating origin, the visibility mode, the distance limit and the ambient multiplier are preserved. Bone local inputs under compatible names, morph activation values, IK switches and persistent targets are copied to the new instance. Temporary per-frame IK targets, physics simulation results, custom tick-loop modules and anchor callbacks are not copied; reconfigure them in the callback. Manual material frames that need per-part remapping are handled in the callback as well.

The generic ModelPosing, AnimationPlayer and compatibility-path FsmPoseDriver implement RebindablePoseDriver. New FSM hosts use FsmPoseEvaluator + ManagedAnimationScope + ModelPoseTarget; FsmPoseDriver is retained only for existing callers that rely on render-thread formula resampling. A named ModelPosing refreshes its data from the new Model's clip library and keeps the original timeline, playback time, speed and paused state; a missing clip restores an empty pose. An external shared clock is not restarted, and other targets following that player's own clock keep the same clock. The rebind of a plain AnimationPlayer/FSM migrates into the target; when its external clip data needs updating, hook that in the callback. A custom driver implements the same interface or is created in the callback.

Replacing or removing a source model, or reloading outfit resources, takes down the instances that borrowed the old resources. The handle keeps the basic state, and a later mount() re-resolves and mounts automatically; outfit definitions in the registry are kept while a source is temporarily missing. destroy() reclaims the current instance and its publication subscriptions, and releases the pending restoration state held by the handle. The instanceId of a global Actor should be managed uniquely by the host; the same service should not let two handles manage the same outfit/instanceId at the same time.

docs.title: Programmatic registration and custom services
docs.text:
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.loaders.assembly.ModelAssemblyDefinition;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.api.McModelAssemblies;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.registry.PipelineRegistry;

var definition = ModelAssemblyDefinition.builder("body",
        new McModelAssemblies.Reference(bodyLocation))
        .part("shirt", new McModelAssemblies.Reference(shirtLocation),
                part -> part.mapBone("shirt_root", "root"))
        .build();
var service = PipelineRegistry.assemblies(); // null before the client's built-in pipeline is initialized
if (service != null) service.register(outfitId, definition);

PipelineRegistry.ASSEMBLY has the value assembly; its pipeline has no format Reader and accepts derived generic Models. A plain of(modelLoc, ...) still routes by file extension; outfit definitions use ofAssembly and do not need a faked file extension.

The complete McModelAssemblies interface:

new McModelAssemblies(
    ModelPipeLine<ResourceLocation, ResourceLocation> output,
    Function<McModelAssemblies.Reference, McModelAssemblies.PublishedSource> sources,
    ModelAssemblyCache cache);

new McModelAssemblies.Reference(ResourceLocation model);
new McModelAssemblies.Reference(ResourceLocation model, @Nullable String modelName);
new McModelAssemblies.PublishedSource(
    ModelPipeLine<ResourceLocation, ResourceLocation> pipeline, ResourceLocation key);

void register(ResourceLocation id, ModelAssemblyDefinition<McModelAssemblies.Reference> definition);
boolean unregister(ResourceLocation id);
void replaceResourceDefinitions(Map<ResourceLocation, ModelAssemblyDefinition<McModelAssemblies.Reference>> next);
Map<ResourceLocation, ModelAssemblyDefinition<McModelAssemblies.Reference>> definitions();
@Nullable ModelAssembly resolve(ResourceLocation id);
@Nullable ModelInstance createAndBind(ResourceLocation id, ResourceLocation instanceId, @Nullable Transform root);
McModelHandle handle(ResourceLocation id, ResourceLocation instanceId);
ModelPipeLine<ResourceLocation, ResourceLocation> pipeline();
ModelAssemblyCache.Stats cacheStats();
void close();

A programmatic definition takes precedence over a resource-pack definition of the same name and is kept across resource reloads. unregister removes the programmatic override and reclaims that definition's instances; if a resource-pack definition exists it is restored, and the return value says whether a programmatic definition was removed. replaceResourceDefinitions applies a fully resolved resource snapshot and cleans up derived models and the assembly cache. close is idempotent and reclaims derived instances, cache references and source publication subscriptions; after closing, calling the resolve/register interfaces is an error. Service operations and model publication/render mounting must run serially on the game thread; the independent synchronization semantics of the base cache are still as described in the generic API.

The default source adapter reuses KasugaModelPipelines.publishedSource(Reference); while a resource reload is in progress it does not resolve resources of the old publication generation. A custom source function can integrate any published Model pipeline, without restricting its format.

docs.title: Generic resource definitions and publication lifecycle
docs.text:
The following interfaces are in render-core and do not depend on Minecraft:

static <K> ModelAssemblyDefinition.Builder<K> ModelAssemblyDefinition.builder(String bodyId, K source);
static <K> ModelAssemblyDefinition.Builder<K> ModelAssemblyDefinition.builder(
        String bodyId, K source, Consumer<ModelAssemblyDefinition.PartBuilder> configure);
ModelAssemblyDefinition.Builder<K> part(String id, K source);
ModelAssemblyDefinition.Builder<K> part(String id, K source, Consumer<ModelAssemblyDefinition.PartBuilder> configure);
ModelAssemblyDefinition.Builder<K> bindTolerance(float tolerance);
ModelAssemblyDefinition<K> build();
@Nullable ModelAssembly.Request ModelAssemblyDefinition.resolve(Function<? super K, ModelAssembly.Source> sources);

PartBuilder provides mapBone(String,String), matchBodyBones(boolean), includeDynamics(boolean), hideMeshes(int...), region(String,int...) and hideRegions(String...). This resource definition's hideRegions is resolved at call time, so define a region before hiding it. A definition can be constructed directly as ModelAssemblyDefinition(List<Part<K>>, float); the parameters of a nested Part<K> are, in order, id, source, Map<String,String> boneMappings, Set<Integer> hiddenMeshes, matchBodyBones, includeDynamics. Any K can be supplied by the host; resolving with a missing source returns null and produces no partial geometry.

new ModelAssemblyRegistry<K, I>(Function<? super K, ModelAssembly.Source> sources, ModelAssemblyCache cache);
void register(I id, ModelAssemblyDefinition<K> definition);
ModelAssemblyDefinition<K> definition(I id);
Map<I, ModelAssemblyDefinition<K>> definitions();
boolean remove(I id);
@Nullable ModelAssembly resolve(I id);
Set<I> invalidate(Model source);
void clearResolved();
ModelAssemblyCache.Stats cacheStats();

The registry keeps resource definitions and the latest complete results, and returned collection views are read-only; call invalidate when a source is updated, and it returns the definition IDs that depend on that old Model, which the host should use to take down the derived instances. A temporarily missing source produces no partial result.

ModelPipeLine adds:

Method Behavior Model getModel(K key) null when not published long modelRevision(K key) Current published version; 0 when absent K modelKeyOf(ModelInstance instance) Looks up the registered key, null when unregistered; the key is kept after binding for constant-time checks AutoCloseable onModelChanged(Consumer<ModelChange<K>> listener) game thread notification, running before the old instance is closed; closing the subscription unregisters PublishedBuilder<K, I, B>.build() A derived pipeline without a SourceManager/Loader; still needs a bridge and backend

ModelChange<K> is key, previous, current, revision, and current is null on deletion. A listener exception does not skip other listeners or the old-instance reclamation; the errors are aggregated and thrown after cleanup completes. Instances are registered by resource key, and different keys sharing the same Model do not reclaim each other; createInstance with the same key/instanceId is idempotent. Calling prepareModel on a publication-only pipeline is an error; the old build methods of SourceManager/Loader pipelines still require a Reader.

Models are managed by ModelPublicationCoordinator.global(). Each ModelPublicationBatch<K> is an independent publisher: publish(prepared) replaces its complete contribution across pipelines, put(pipeline, models) merges keys, remove(pipeline, key) removes an owned key, and close() releases all owned keys. Two publishers cannot use the same key in the same pipeline, even for the same Model; conflicts and preparation failures leave the current generation unchanged. The former publishModels, replaceModels, removeModel, and loadModel methods are removed: use prepareModel and submit its result through a publisher. Reusing the same Model reference does not retire instances.

Models and revisions across pipelines switch in one atomic generation. Pin a generation for consistent multi-read queries:

try (var snapshot = ModelPublicationCoordinator.global().pin()) {
    Model model = snapshot.getModel(pipeline, key);
    long revision = snapshot.modelRevision(pipeline, key);
}

Pins retain Model references and revisions only, not instances or GPU resources. Close pins promptly, and do not race concurrent reads against mutations of Model or its contents. Separate pipeline queries can span generations. Publication, instance and listener operations must run serially on one game thread; reentrant publication from notifications or cleanup is rejected. Listener or cleanup errors are aggregated in PublicationCommittedException: the reported generation is already active, not rolled back. Atomic model generations do not include texture atlases, PMX lookup tables or glTF manifests, which retain independent loading and lifecycle semantics.

docs.title: Driver and input migration
docs.text:
interface RebindablePoseDriver extends PoseDriver { void rebind(ModelInstance fresh); }
void ModelPosing.rebind(ModelInstance fresh);
ModelInstance ModelPosing.model();
void AnimationPlayer<T>.rebind(ModelInstance fresh, AnimationSampler<T> sampler, T data);
void SkeletonInstance.copyPoseInputsTo(SkeletonInstance target);
void MorphInstance<Id>.copyInputsTo(MorphInstance<Id> target);

Skeleton migration copies only named local transforms, IK switches and persistent targets; the root transform and floating origin are migrated separately by the host. Morph migration copies the activation value/factor corresponding to the identity, and does not copy result caches or source structure objects. Names that do not exist on the target are ignored. AnimationPlayer.rebind(fresh, sampler, data) replaces clip data and the target model while retaining the current Scope clock. Standalone and externally shared playback continue to follow their respective clock-ownership rules. These control operations must run serially with tick, and the render sample consumes the existing snapshot mechanism.

docs.title: Pipeline types and publication ownership
docs.text:
ModelPipeLine<K, I> exposes model keys and instance keys. Source/texture types are captured by the loader closure, and backend renderables by private mount adapters. Loader-free pipelines use new ModelPipeLine.PublishedBuilder<K, I, Renderable>()...build() without source/texture placeholders. The loader Builder retains its construction-only types.

The default publication domain is ModelPublicationCoordinator.global(). For an isolated domain, pass the same coordinator to withPublicationCoordinator and new ModelPublicationBatch<K>(coordinator). A domain's owning thread may call releaseThread() between transactions before a replacement thread adopts it; other threads cannot steal ownership. Preparation registration/closing before first use does not bind the domain.

Preparation only removes staged models and has a pass limit derived from the staged entry count. Preparation.beforeNotifications(owner, action) deduplicates transaction-local commit effects by owner identity; those effects run after generation publication and before all model listeners. Aborted preparations do not run them. Assembly cache invalidation uses this phase, independently of cross-pipeline notification order.

docs.title: 3D Model Block Dimensions Interface Design
docs.text: Status: Implemented Target: KasugaLibNext master Related implementation: KuaYue PR #14

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Block dimensions are exposed only by BlockModelSource, without extending the generic MinecraftModelSource. Models without block-grid semantics—such as UML, glTF, and MMD—should not receive this capability.

docs.title: Public Interface
docs.text:
public record BlockDimensions(int length, int width, int height)

public Optional<BlockDimensions> dimensions()
Output Axis Calculation length X maxBlockX - minBlockX + 1 width Z maxBlockZ - minBlockZ + 1 height Y maxBlockY - minBlockY + 1
  • Returns the tight bounding dimensions of the outermost non-air blocks.
  • Interior gaps are included in the span; outer air is excluded.
  • Returns block-grid counts, not block-entity counts.
  • An empty source returns Optional.empty().
  • Source origin, camera, display transforms, and layer explosion do not affect the result.
  • Declared file dimensions are not included in this interface.

Dimensions are computed by scanning block positions once during BlockModelSource construction and cached. Querying does not build a snapshot, touch the GPU, or require the render thread.

docs.title: PR #14 Integration
docs.text:
var size = source.dimensions()
        .orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalStateException("Blueprint has no blocks"));
float scale = (float) (FIT_EXTENT / size.longestAxis());

test_ss8 has length, width, and height 18 x 5 x 4, with longest axis 18, and should use 0.07 / 18 as its scale.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Single block, sparse blocks, translated coordinates, empty model, and non-positive dimensions;
  • Client preview smoke logs dimensions for real BlockModelSource instances and verifies the fluid fixture;
  • Scene unit tests, contentTesting compilation, Create downstream compilation, and git diff --check.

docs.title: UB-mode Self-Check
docs.text:
• First Make it Work: minimal interface is BlockModelSource.dimensions().
  • Subtract Before You Add: no generic source capability, preview forwarding, wrapper adaptation, or composite scene calculation was added.
  • Foundational Thinking: lock down X/Y/Z mapping and tight non-air extents first.
  • Boundary Discipline: compute once at the source construction boundary and cache.
  • Test Behavior: unit tests cover dimension semantics; client smoke covers public method wiring.

docs.title: Minecraft structures and Create model previews
docs.text:
lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.scene.MinecraftModelSource is the common display contract for Minecraft content and Kasuga models. Pass a source to GuiModelPreview, then use ModelPreviewWidget, LDLib2's ModelPreviewElement, or a UIBackend world panel. Contents are drawn to an independent transparent depth canvas and are never placed in the game world.

Construct, sample, render and close sources on the Minecraft render thread. setView and setLayers publish immutable display parameters and may be called by UI threads.

var mc = Minecraft.getInstance();
var source = MinecraftModelSources.structure(mc.level,
        ResourceLocation.parse("minecraft:end_city/base_floor"));
var preview = new GuiModelPreview(source);
var bounds = source.snapshot(LayerLayout.ASSEMBLED, 0).bounds();
mc.setScreen(new MinecraftModelPreviewScreen(Component.literal("End City"), preview,
        (int) Math.floor(bounds.minY()), (int) Math.ceil(bounds.maxY()) - 1));

The viewer provides left-drag rotation, middle-drag pan, wheel zoom, R to reset the view, cumulative layers, isolated slices, showing all layers, and an explosion slider. View gestures start inside the canvas and remain captured until release; gestures started on controls stay with those controls. It closes its preview on removal. Other widget owners must call close() themselves. Changing worlds also releases previews that have been rendered there. A short left click inspects a block's name, registry ID and source coordinates; dragging rotates.

Source Factory Bundled vanilla building / single-player data pack MinecraftModelSources.structure(level, ResourceLocation) Compressed structure-block NBT MinecraftModelSources.structure(level, Path) Loaded template MinecraftModelSources.structure(level, StructureTemplate) Litematica / Forgematica .litematic v5–v7 MinecraftModelSources.litematic(level, Path) Loaded client region MinecraftModelSources.capture(level, minimum, maximum) External projection data MinecraftModelSources.blocks(level, List<StructureBlockInfo>) Create machine region CreateModelSources.machine(level, minimum, maximum) Create contraption entity CreateModelSources.contraption(AbstractContraptionEntity) Attached Create contraption CreateModelSources.contraption(Contraption) uses Create's own entity backlink Create schematic item / template CreateModelSources.schematic(level, ItemStack or StructureTemplate) Local Create structure NBT CreateModelSources.schematic(level, Path)

Block-backed sources can report tight non-air block dimensions. length maps to X, width to Z and height to Y; all three are block-grid counts:

var size = source.dimensions().orElseThrow();
int length = size.length();
int width = size.width();
int height = size.height();

BlockModelSource.dimensions() is computed and cached when the source is constructed. Camera and display transforms, as well as layer explosion spacing, do not affect it. Empty sources return Optional.empty(). The result describes the outermost non-air blocks rather than a file's declared size.

Create factories live in the optional modules/create, in lib.kasuga.create.client.model. The common modelling module does not link Create classes. Assembled structures reuse ContraptionRenderInfo and SchematicRenderer; actors use MovementBehaviour.renderInContraption. Layered geometry and block entities use native renderers, with actors following their block's layer. Private virtual levels select ordinary renderers independently of the game world's Flywheel instances.

Litematic import retains multiple regions, signed sizes, continuously packed palette indices and block-entity NBT. Old Minecraft data uses the structure DataFixer; newer data and missing mod blocks are rejected explicitly. Import factories throw on failure. Draw failures return false and set preview.failure().

preview.setView(-.55f, .25f, 1, .1f, -.05f); // Radians, zoom, right 10% / up 5% of the viewport
preview.setView(-.55f, .25f, 1);            // Three-argument overload resets pan
preview.setLayers(LayerLayout.ASSEMBLED.range(0, 5));
preview.setLayers(LayerLayout.ASSEMBLED.range(5, 5));
preview.setLayers(LayerLayout.ASSEMBLED.separation(1.25));
preview.setLayers(LayerLayout.ASSEMBLED.axis(LayerLayout.Axis.X).separation(.75));
preview.setLayers(LayerLayout.ASSEMBLED);

Coordinates are source-local Minecraft blocks, with Y as the default layer axis. Missing layers retain their spacing. Hiding a layer changes neither remaining offsets nor the full framing bounds. Limits are 131072 blocks, 4096 layers, 4096 blocks per axis, and 64 MiB of decoded NBT. Sources do not tick block entities, play sounds, send packets or change live entity poses. Model appearance/connected textures always use the full original neighbor context; isolated layers filter cut-face visibility while retaining stored block states. Create's cached schematic renderer has a separate 1048576-cell volume bound; the actual block count limit remains unchanged.

Static block/fluid geometry is cached per assembled model or axis/layer. View changes and explosion spacing update matrices; block entities, actors, contraption rotation and animated textures remain live. Transparent quads retain the shared sort. New layouts build once; reload rebuilds geometry and close/world changes release it. Assembled Create schematics retain native live directional shading. Custom LayeredModelSource subclasses can opt into cached planning with an immutable geometryKey(); replace the key when geometry changes. The default null preserves live per-frame planning.

var combined = MinecraftModelSources.compose(
        new MinecraftModelSources.Placement(structure, new Matrix4f()),
        new MinecraftModelSources.Placement(
                MinecraftModelSources.model(() -> alreadyLoadedKasugaModel),
                new Matrix4f().translate(2, 1, 0).scale(.5f)));
var preview = new GuiModelPreview(combined);

Compositions own their children; do not share one source between owners. UML assets remain borrowed, while the preview owns a private instance and GPU state. Third-party adapters can extend LayeredModelSource and implement renderSlice using their own renderer.

preview.setFrameProcessor(input -> {
    runMyPostProcess(input.color(), input.depthTexture(), myTarget);
    return new FrameTexture(myTarget.frameBufferId, myTarget.getColorTextureId(),
            myTarget.width, myTarget.height);
});

The callback runs on the render thread and can use FullscreenPassRenderer or an existing shader. It owns its output target, which must match input dimensions. Do not sample and write the same attachment. currentFrame() is borrowed until the next render, resize or close. Legacy resource/Supplier constructors retain renderbuffer depth compatibility; the source constructor provides a sampleable depth texture.

var scene = SceneModels.open(mc.level);
scene.add(source, new Vec3(10, 70, 10))
        .layers(LayerLayout.ASSEMBLED.separation(.5))
        .transform(new Matrix4f().rotateY(.4f).scale(.75f));
// scene.close() releases sources and registration; changing worlds also closes it.

SceneModels draws before shared world post-processing. Use a separate source for another owner. To follow a Create contraption, use scene.add(source, CreateSceneHosts.contraption(entity)); see Scenes and UI on moving structures for shared model/UI placement. Positions are world coordinates: the model stays fixed as players walk around it. Entry.position moves it, transform sets local rotation/scale, and visible(false) hides it. Use the render thread. Development examples live in test.kasuga.modelling.demo.preview and test.kasuga.create.demo.preview. /kasuga_model_preview opens the UI/world selector; /kasuga_create_gallery opens the floating Create rig with creative flight, and /kasuga_create_gallery stop restores the original player state. See the gallery example.

preview.pick(u, v) takes top-left viewport fractions and inspects the latest displayed snapshot. scene.pick(from, to, partialTick) takes a world-space ray. Hits contain the source BlockState, original block position, displayed hit location and source face. Native outline shapes follow layer, explosion, composition and scene transforms. UML sources without block metadata return no hit. ModelBlockInfo.draw(...) draws the reusable inspection card. Aim and left click in the gallery to display the block information for five seconds without breaking blocks. Press I for transparent world inspection controls: cumulative layers, single slices, all layers, explosion spacing, whole-model scale and reset. Close with Done or Esc to keep flying around the model with its current layout retained. The Rig / Windmill button switches to a real windmill assembled and ticked by Create's native bearing. Its ControlledContraptionEntity keeps driving rotation in assembled, isolated-layer and exploded modes; the display adapter reads the entity without ticking or changing it. With -PkasugaPreviewSchematic=..., click Inspect beside the factory entry for the same world inspection panel, or use /kasuga_create_gallery factory or the panel's Factory button. The factory retains layers, explosion, scale, reset, I to reopen controls and block information.

./gradlew :modules:modelling:modelUnitTest --tests 'lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.scene.*'
./gradlew :modules:modelling:test --tests 'lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.scene.SchematicImportTest'
./gradlew :modules:create:compileJava :modules:create:compileContentTestingJava
./gradlew :modules:modelling:runClientHeadless -PkasugaTestMinecraftPreview=true \
  -PkasugaClientDirectory=/absolute/path/to/isolated-client -PkasugaQuickPlayWorld=fixture
./gradlew :modules:create:runClientHeadless -PkasugaTestMinecraftPreview=true \
  -PkasugaClientDirectory=/absolute/path/to/isolated-create-client -PkasugaQuickPlayWorld=fixture

Client acceptance reads actual RGBA, drives layer/explosion controls and rotation/pan/zoom/reset gestures, and checks transparency, sampleable depth, post-processing, resizing and immediate attachment retirement. Fixtures include the bundled End City, negative-size litematic, section-boundary fluids, and optional Create schematics/drill actors. Inspect ksg_debug/minecraft-preview/report.json in the isolated game directory. Compilation and import tests do not establish pixel or interaction correctness.

For a visible client that stays open for manual testing:

./gradlew :modules:create:runClient -PkasugaMinecraftPreviewInteractive=true \
  -PkasugaClientDirectory=/absolute/path/to/isolated-create-client -PkasugaQuickPlayWorld=fixture

The source selector opens once after the world loads. Esc returns from a preview to the selector, then back to the game. This development-only contentTesting mode has no automatic input, source switching, timeout or exit.

docs.title: PMX and glTF Ragdoll Configuration
docs.text:
Interface, configuration, and call reference. For the concepts see mmd-ragdoll.md.

Physics definitions, IK, and diamond closure now all hang under Skeleton.getDynamics(). For extending the Reader/Builder and for the Caliko integration see skeleton-dynamics.md. SkeletonRagdoll keeps its historical API name; at runtime it only reads the generic skeleton definitions.

SkeletonRagdoll has two construction paths:

  • enablePhysics() uses every rigid body in the PMX file, so it also includes secondary-motion rigid bodies such as skirts and hair.
  • enablePhysics(profile) works for PMX or glTF and uses the profile's bodies to generate stable humanoid capsules and semantic masses; a PMX profile can keep unregistered author-made rigid body chains such as skirts, hair, and accessories through include_secondary_bodies as well. Inertia is generated by Box3D from the shape and the mass. glTF is not allowed to guess a human structure automatically without a profile.

Physics solving is done by the vendored Box3D C17 engine. RigidBodyWorld, SimBody, GenericRigidBody, and BallJoint in uml/dynamic/physics/core only handle Java object mapping, fixed steps, lifecycle, and state synchronization; SkeletonRagdoll is the PMX/skeleton adapter. Any code can create a world directly:

docs.title: Large-coordinate precision
docs.text:
When SkeletonRagdoll is enabled, the model root's world translation is moved out of the float bone matrices and stored as a separate double worldOrigin. Bone evaluation, Box3D rigid bodies, joints, and the cached block collisions all use local coordinates near that origin; at render time worldOrigin - cameraPosition is computed in double first, and only then written into the float pose matrix.

Body.position() and RayHit.point() are simulation-local coordinates; use ragdoll.worldPosition(body) when you need a world position. Double world coordinates such as a camera's or an entity's should enter the physics world through raycastWorld(...), beginDragWorld(...), updateDragTargetWorld(...), addStaticBoxColliderWorld(...), or worldToSimulation(...).

The MinecraftRagdollDeployments.Request constructor that takes a Vector3d worldOrigin preserves the fractional part of the deployment position; the old constructor is still compatible, but it can only inherit the float precision already present in the original Transform.

var crate = GenericRigidBody.box(new Vector3f(0.5f), 8f).at(2f, 5f, 1f);
var world = new RigidBodyWorld(List.of(crate), List.of(),
        RigidBodyWorld.DEFAULT_SUBSTEP_COUNT);
world.addGroundPlane(0f, 0.8f, 0f);
world.step(dt, RigidBodyWorld.KinematicDriver.none());

docs.title: Official implementation: physics blocks
docs.text:
The client-side service MinecraftBlockPhysics turns a Minecraft block's real VoxelShape into a compound Box3D rigid body (MinecraftBlockRigidBody): mass comes from block hardness and friction from slipperiness, it is drawn visually with the vanilla block renderer, terrain collision reuses the ragdoll's incremental block environment, and it interacts with the local player through a kinematic AABB proxy. For the full API and the client/server boundary see physics.md. Command entry points:

  • /kasuga_physics block [1-32]: spawns a physics block in front of the view.
  • /kasuga_physics status / clear: show or clear every physics block.

The cap is MAX_PROPS = 256; blocks that fall out of the bottom of the world are reclaimed automatically, and a dimension change clears everything.

docs.title: Debug commands
docs.text:
• /kasuga_ragdoll deploy: deploys a ragdoll with the built-in demo model on the ground in front of the player.
  • /kasuga_ragdoll deploy <model resource location>: reads the model manifest and deploys any published glTF that declares a ragdoll.
  • /kasuga_ragdoll list, remove all: list and undeploy deployments.

Lifecycle: a dimension change or leaving the world cleans up every deployment and releases mouse dragging; block-collision-environment invalidation notices are forwarded to nearby environments in real time by core's ClientBlockUpdateHooks (the ClientLevel#sendBlockUpdated mixin), and the periodic refresh is only a fallback.

docs.title: Native Box3D backend
docs.text:
• Box3D is pinned to the official main commit 336263320469e5e9febfe18697ab562488f7e97a, with the source in modules/modelling/src/main/native/box3d; for the license see modules/modelling/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
  • CMake statically links Box3D into the kasuga_box3d JNI library; Gradle puts the current platform's artifacts in native/<os>-<arch>/, and the runtime extracts and loads them from the jar. CI builds and tests on Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64, and macOS ARM64 separately, then merges them into the kasuga-modelling-universal universal jar.
  • Box3D owns integration, broad phase, narrow phase, contact, CCD, sleeping, and joint solving; Java contains no fallback solver.
  • PMX spheres, boxes, and capsules map directly to Box3D shapes. PMX six-axis joints map to spherical joints; the rotation range is approximated as cone/twist, and the three-axis translation range is currently tightened to a fixed anchor.
  • Minecraft block collision boxes map to Box3D static hulls created and destroyed incrementally. An infinite plane is approximated by a large static thin box placed along its normal.
  • Box3D has no fluid volume/buoyancy interface, so the old in-house fluid force model has been removed; a Minecraft fluid change still triggers a refresh of the adjacent collision cache, but applies no buoyancy or flow drag.

On the Minecraft side, MinecraftRagdollConfig.load(resourceManager, location) reads a configuration from the resource pack, after which you call config.attach(instance, levelSupplier). The built-in example is at assets/kasuga_lib/ragdolls/test_mmd.json, and a resource pack can override it or provide a new resource location. The built-in rendering demo now uses TDA Bunny Miku 2.0.pmx from test3.mmd.zip, whose body rigid body mapping is at assets/kasuga_lib/ragdolls/tda_bunny_miku.json. Rigid body indices are not reusable across different PMX files.

Model size is controlled by the .mmd.json next to the archive. For example test2.mmd.zip corresponds to test2.mmd.json:

{
  "encoding": "gbk",
  "model_scale": 0.1
}

model_scale can be a uniform scale number or [x, y, z]. When it is omitted, the legacy-compatible 1/12 is still used. The scale is applied uniformly to vertices, bones, rigid body shapes, and joint positions, so render and collision sizes stay consistent.

glTF uses the adjacent .gltf.json model manifest. For example character.glb corresponds to character.gltf.json:

{
  "model_scale": 1.3,
  "ragdoll": "example:ragdolls/character.json"
}

The manifest is the only automatic association entry point: the loader takes the model scale from it and the deployer takes the ragdoll profile from it; Java code never hardcodes selection logic on maribel, renko, or any bone name. A glTF without a ragdoll field still renders and plays animations normally, but a generic ragdoll deployment fails explicitly.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
• bodies: the body rigid body topology. In PMX, rigid_body and parent are PMX rigid body indices; in a glTF profile they are glTF node indices of the model that owns the manifest; the root node omits parent. The MMD adapter first walks the real bone tree to find the nearest registered physics ancestor; only when it finds no physics ancestor does it use parent to bridge separated PMX branches (for example the "upper body" and "lower body" branches that both sit under "waist").
  • include_secondary_bodies: PMX only, default false. When enabled, author-made rigid bodies and their joints that are not replaced by bodies and do not conflict with the main body bones enter the physics world as well, which suits the common bone-driven skirts and hair. It is not the same as PMX 2.1 per-vertex soft-body. Under a hybrid profile, secondary-motion bones keep the animated translation and write back only the physics rotation, so that hair strands and skirt bones are not stretched by the different reference frame of the main body capsules. An attachment point on the main body drives the secondary-motion chains one-way through a kinematic proxy that moves with the main body, using a separate 16-layer collision namespace, which stops a large number of secondary-motion rigid bodies from dragging the main body backward or bouncing off the generated capsules. The built-in TDA example uses 8 Box3D substeps; per-vertex soft-body currently only reads the format and is not yet connected to Box3D solving or vertex writeback.
  • role: pelvis, spine, chest, neck, head, shoulder, upper_arm, lower_arm, hand, upper_leg, lower_leg, foot, or toe.
  • Top-level limits: swing/twist limits can be declared per role instead of repeating them on every body; fields on the body itself take precedence.
  • The humanoid profile uses swing/twist limits by default: max_swing_degrees controls the cone swing, and min_twist_degrees / max_twist_degrees control the twist along the bone axis. limit_stiffness is a legacy profile compatibility field; Box3D manages the limit correction strength itself. The three angle fields must be provided together. When they are omitted, the humanoid defaults for the role apply.
  • rotation_min_degrees / rotation_max_degrees: the legacy three-axis Euler box limit compatibility path; they must appear together and cannot be mixed with the swing/twist fields.
  • simulation.hertz: the fixed world step frequency; a variable frame length is never used to solve directly.
  • simulation.update_mode: render_frame is advanced by an independent runtime and no longer depends on the model actually being drawn by the backend; manual is advanced by the caller through MinecraftRagdollRuntime.step(instance, dt) or instance.simulatePhysics(dt).
  • simulation.substeps: the number of solver substeps per fixed world step. For long multi-segment secondary-motion chains such as long hair and skirts, 8 is recommended; the built-in TDA configuration uses that value.
  • simulation.solver_iterations: legacy configuration compatibility field; Box3D does not expose this iteration count, so it is currently only validated and does not change the solve.
  • simulation.constraint_hertz / constraint_damping_ratio: joint constraint softening parameters.
  • simulation.max_linear_speed: mapped to the Box3D world maximum linear speed. max_angular_speed is a legacy configuration compatibility field; the current Box3D API has no corresponding world-level setting.
  • simulation.max_fixed_steps_per_update: the maximum number of catch-up fixed world steps in a single tick/frame update, default 12; backlog beyond the budget is dropped, which stops one stall from causing a sustained physics spiral.
  • sleeping.enabled: whether the whole group of rigid bodies sleeps. It is recommended to turn this off when debugging collisions or running sustained airborne simulation.
  • sleeping.linear_speed / angular_speed: scaled by each shape's size into a per-rigid-body farthest-point speed threshold for Box3D. delay_seconds is a legacy configuration compatibility field; the actual sleep delay is managed by Box3D itself.
  • collision.self_collision: whether the inside of one ragdoll collides with itself. false uses a Box3D negative group index; turning it off is recommended for a humanoid main body. When it is false, Box3D filters shape pairs inside the whole ragdoll, not just adjacent joints.
  • collision.continuous: whether to enable swept collision, to avoid penetration at high speed.
  • environment: the Minecraft block collision cache refresh frequency, boundary expansion, friction, and restitution.
  • initial_state: the optional overall initial offset and root rigid body velocity, mainly for demos or spawn effects.
  • dragging.enabled: register this instance for crosshair dragging.
  • dragging.mouse_button / max_distance: the mouse button (0 is the left button) and the maximum picking distance.
  • dragging.bias_rate: mapped to the spring hertz of the Box3D drag spherical joint. The remaining legacy drag tuning fields are still read for resource pack compatibility, but no extra Java stabilizer runs.

In game, aim the crosshair at the model's main body and hold the left button to drag it; after release the rigid bodies keep the velocity they had at the moment of release. Profile humanoid picking uses the capsules generated from the bones; the profile-less compatibility mode still uses PMX spheres, boxes, and capsules. What is grabbed is a local point on the hit surface; the whole skeleton is not teleported. The whole group of rigid bodies stays awake for as long as the mouse constraint exists, so gravity, joints, and collisions do not suddenly freeze mid-drag. Dragging applies a soft constraint only at the grab point of the hit rigid body and no longer applies extra linear or angular damping to the whole group. After the mouse is released, the rigid bodies only sleep normally once they touch the static environment and meet the low-speed threshold.

docs.title: Runtime deployment and removal
docs.text:
The client main thread can create instances dynamically through MinecraftRagdollDeployments. The model package must already have been scanned and published by models/model_proxy.json; while it is not yet published, deploy returns empty and you can retry after resource loading completes:

var request = new MinecraftRagdollDeployments.Request(
        ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("kasuga_lib", "models/pmx/test3.mmd.zip"),
        "TDA Bunny Miku 2.0.pmx",
        ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("example", "ragdoll/1"),
        ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("kasuga_lib", "ragdolls/tda_bunny_miku.json"),
        new Transform().translate(x, y, z),
        true
);
RagdollDeployment deployment = MinecraftRagdollDeployments.deploy(request).orElseThrow();

For glTF, prefer a manifest request rather than passing a hardcoded configuration path:

var request = new MinecraftRagdollDeployments.Request(
        ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("example", "models/character.glb"),
        ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("example", "ragdoll/1"),
        new Transform().translate(x, y, z),
        true
);
RagdollDeployment deployment = MinecraftRagdollDeployments.deploy(request).orElseThrow();

The handle exposes both instance() and ragdoll() for applying velocity or changing parameters at runtime. The two removal forms below are equivalent and can be called repeatedly:

deployment.remove();
MinecraftRagdollDeployments.remove(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("example", "ragdoll/1"));
