try (RigidBodyWorld world = new RigidBodyWorld(
        List.of(sphere, compound), List.of(), RigidBodyWorld.DEFAULT_SUBSTEP_COUNT)) {
    world.setSimulationHertz(120f);
    world.setGravity(new Vector3f(0f, -9.80665f, 0f));
    world.addGroundPlane(0f, 0.8f, 0f);
    world.step(deltaSeconds, RigidBodyWorld.KinematicDriver.none());
}

Object and joint management:

  • add(SimBody) / remove(SimBody)
  • add(BallJoint) / remove(BallJoint) (the ball joints PMX/gltf ragdolls use)
  • add(PhysicsJoint) / remove(PhysicsJoint) (weld/distance/revolute/prismatic, see 2.2.1)
  • bodies() / joints() / physicsJoints()
  • excludePair(bodyA, bodyB)
  • close()

When a body is removed, both kinds of joint attached to it are destroyed automatically.

docs.title: 2.2.1 Generic Joint Types
docs.text:
The four common Box3D joints have been ported in full through JNI (all constraint solving happens inside native code):

// Weld: rigidly bonds two props (0 hertz = hardest), softness adjustable
WeldJoint weld = WeldJoint.atCurrentPose(blockA, blockB).build();
world.add(weld);

// Distance: rope/spring/winch, supports spring, length limits, and motor
DistanceJoint rope = DistanceJoint.between(anchor, payload)
        .length(1f)
        .spring(true, 3f, 0.9f)
        .limits(true, 0.5f, 1.5f)
        .motor(true, 1f, 50f)      // winch reeling in the rope
        .build();

// Revolute: hinge (door, lid, windmill), can carry angle limits and a motor
RevoluteJoint hinge = RevoluteJoint.between(frame, door)
        .hingeAxis(new Vector3f(0, 1, 0))
        .limits(true, -(float) Math.PI * 0.25f, (float) Math.PI * 0.25f)
        .motor(true, -6f, 40f)
        .build();

// Prismatic: slide rail (piston, drawer), can carry travel limits and a motor
PrismaticJoint piston = PrismaticJoint.between(rail, slider)
        .slideAxis(new Vector3f(1, 0, 0))
        .limits(true, -1.2f, 1.2f)
        .motor(true, 2f, 200f)
        .build();

Runtime tuning goes through each joint's setters (setLimits, setMotor, setSpring, setLength); calling a setter on a joint that is not bound to a world throws IllegalStateException.

KinematicDriver.beginStep(world) runs before every fixed step; kinematicTarget(body) returns the target position and rotation of that same step. lastFixedStepCount(), droppedSimulationTime(), and interpolationAlpha() are used to diagnose the fixed step.

Main tuning parameters:

  • setSimulationHertz(10..1000)
  • setSubstepCount(1..50)
  • setMaxFixedStepsPerUpdate(1..1000)
  • setConstraintTuning(hertz, dampingRatio)
  • setSpeedLimits(linear, angular); the current Box3D only provides a world linear speed mapping
  • setRestitutionThreshold(value)
  • setSleepingEnabled(boolean) / setSleepingThresholds(...) / wake()
  • setContinuousCollisionEnabled(boolean)
  • setCollisionsEnabled(boolean)
  • setSelfCollisionsEnabled(boolean)

setSolverIterations is a compatibility entry point for old configurations. Box3D does not expose an iteration count of the same name, so it only validates and stores the value.

docs.title: 2.3 Impulse, Force, and Body Control
docs.text:
All vectors are in world coordinates:

world.applyImpulse(body, impulse);
world.applyImpulse(body, impulse, worldPoint);
world.applyAngularImpulse(body, angularImpulse);

world.applyForce(body, force);
world.applyForce(body, force, worldPoint);
world.applyTorque(body, torque);

world.setGravityScale(body, 0.25f);
float scale = world.gravityScale(body);
world.setAwake(body, true);
boolean awake = world.awake(body);

An impulse changes velocity immediately; force/torque is integrated by the next native Box3D step. The methods return false when the body does not belong to that world, when the body is not dynamic, or when an input is not a finite number. A negative gravity scale inverts that body's gravity.

docs.title: 2.4 Collision, Contact, and Query
docs.text:
Static environment entry points:

  • addPlaneCollider(normal, offset, friction, restitution)
  • addGroundPlane(y, friction, restitution)
  • addStaticBoxCollider(minimum, maximum, friction, restitution)
  • addEnvironmentMesh(friction, restitution)
  • setCollisionEnvironment(CollisionEnvironment)

StaticEnvironmentMesh incrementally synchronizes Minecraft terrain through putCell/removeCell; Java does not do the collision solving.

Queries:

Optional<RayHit> hit = world.raycast(origin, direction, maximumDistance);
List<BodyContact> contacts = world.contacts(body);

RayHit returns the Java SimBody, the world hit point, and the distance. BodyContact fields:

Field Meaning body the body from the query's point of view other the other Java body; empty for native static terrain point world contact point normal unit normal pointing from other to body separation negative means penetration normalImpulse normal impulse of the current solver point totalNormalImpulse normal impulse including the accumulated warm start normalVelocity pre-solve normal velocity touching() the separation or the impulse shows a current contact

Summary counts are available through selfContactCount() and staticContactBodyCount().

docs.title: 2.5 Ray Drag
docs.text:
world.setDragSettings(DragSettings.DEFAULT);
world.beginDrag(hit);                 // or beginDrag(body, worldPoint)
world.updateDragTarget(target, frameSeconds);
world.endDrag();

Drag creates a kinematic anchor and a spherical joint inside native Box3D; it does not teleport the body and does not run a Java stabilizer. A world currently has only one drag target at a time.

docs.title: 3. PMX and glTF ragdoll API
docs.text:
SkeletonRagdoll ragdoll = instance.enablePhysics();
// or generate only the body capsules registered in the profile
SkeletonRagdoll profiled = instance.enablePhysics(profile);

Queries:

  • bodies() / joints()
  • body(definitionIndex): index into the generic bodies list; the MMD Reader keeps the original rigid body order, the glTF Reader keeps the node order
  • body(Bone) / body(boneName)
  • animationTarget(body): the body target after this frame's animation + IK and before physics
  • raycast(...)

SkeletonRagdoll forwards the generic impulse, force, torque, gravity, collision, drag, fixed-step, sleep, and environment controls directly. Body additionally provides position(), rotation(), shapeSize(), velocity, toWorldPoint(...), toLocalPoint(...), teleport(...), and velocity setters.

Mode semantics:

  • PMX mode 0: kinematic, follows the animated bones.
  • PMX mode 1: dynamic, full physics writeback.
  • PMX mode 2: dynamic, keeps the animated translation and writes back the physics rotation.
  • profile ragdoll: both PMX and glTF can generate capsules and semantic masses from the shared UML bone segments; internal self-collision is off by default. PMX can keep the author-made skirt/hair rigid body chains through include_secondary_bodies; these secondary-motion rigid bodies keep the PMX-internal filter relationships in an independent collision group/mask namespace and attach to the main body one-way through a kinematic proxy, so they do not inherit the main body's negative group filters and do not drag the main body back. glTF must supply an explicit profile, and does not guess human topology from bone names.

For the configuration format, profile roles, and Minecraft deployment see mmd-ragdoll.md.

MMD/glTF ragdolls use a per-instance double world anchor and origin-local float physics coordinates. The Minecraft block mesh, rays, mouse drag, and entity attachment points all subtract that anchor first; rendering also uses a double camera-relative displacement. This avoids magnifying small colliders, bone segments, and joint error to centimeters or even whole blocks anywhere from a hundred thousand blocks out to the world border.

docs.title: 4. IK API
docs.text:
SkeletonInstance supports persistent external targets:

skeleton.setIkTarget("右足ＩＫ", worldTarget, 1f);
skeleton.clearIkTarget("右足ＩＫ");
skeleton.clearIkTargets();

skeleton.setIkEnabled("右足ＩＫ", false);
skeleton.resetIkEnabled();

weight ranges over [0,1] and blends between the chain controller's position and the external world target. The name denotes a generic IK chain name, and an undefined chain returns false. For the full construction, limits, closure, and diagnostics see Skeleton Dynamics API.

setFrameIkTarget(...) and clearFrameIkTargets() are the tick loop's transient entry points. ModelTickLoop.tick clears them at the start of every evaluation; the pre-IK modules write them again, and IK and physics then consume them together within that same evaluation. Ordinary callers should usually use IkTargetModule instead of managing the lifecycle directly.

docs.title: 5. ModelTickLoop Modules
docs.text:
Every ModelInstance carries its own ModelTickLoop pipeline (instance.getTickLoop()), with four built-in modules installed by default:

Slot Module Responsibility kasuga:apply SkeletonApplyModule flushes pending transforms into the skeleton; the identity slot skips, and does not overwrite bones the animation already wrote kasuga:ik IkModule same-frame constrained animation/IK target for all motion states kasuga:physics SkeletonPhysicsModule advances the SkeletonRagdoll (Box3D) and writes back; no-op when physics is not enabled kasuga:anchor AnchorModule recomputes the anchor world transform and notifies the display children

User modules attach between the standard slots with typed helpers, and ordering is provided entirely by the pipeline:

ModelTickLoop loop = instance.getTickLoop();
loop.addPreIk("my-target", module);      // before apply, pending writes take effect in the same evaluation
loop.addPostIk("my-controller", module); // after IK, before physics
loop.addPostPhysics("my-observer", module); // after physics, before anchor
loop.module(ModelTickLoop.SLOT_ANCHOR, AnchorModule.class); // fetch a built-in module instance

When you need to write pending transforms and have the default apply consume them, use loop.getPipeline().addBefore(ModelTickLoop.SLOT_APPLY, "my-pose", module). You can also use addFirst/addLast/addBefore/addAfter/remove through loop.getPipeline() to insert anywhere. tick() clears the transient IK targets at the start, so their lifetime is exactly one tick.

docs.title: 5.1 IkTargetModule
docs.text:
IkTargetModule hand = new IkTargetModule("右手ＩＫ", new Vector3f(1f, 2f, 0f), 1f);
instance.getTickLoop().addPreIk("hand", hand);

hand.setTarget(new Vector3f(1.2f, 2f, 0f));
hand.setTarget(target, 0.6f);
hand.setEnabled(false);

It writes the transient world target only in the pre-IK stage, and does not modify authored animation data.

docs.title: 5.2 ActiveRagdollModule
docs.text:
This compatibility controller reads the target already solved by the standard IK stage. It computes bounded PD forces/torques through beforePhysicsStep on every fixed step, without another hierarchy or IK solve. Box3D handles integration, contacts and joints. Whole-skeleton tracking can use skeleton.drivePose(...) directly. Zero weight skips both body traversal and force submission. Angular drive retains the legacy ActiveRagdollModule mass scaling for parameter compatibility; it is not normalized by rotational inertia. The maximum torque remains significant for small skeletons.

Control all dynamic bodies:

ActiveRagdollModule active = new ActiveRagdollModule(
        5f,    // frequency Hz
        1f,    // damping ratio
        800f,  // maximum force
        250f   // maximum torque
);
instance.getTickLoop().addPostIk("active-ragdoll", active);

Control only the bodies of the given bones:

var upperBody = new ActiveRagdollModule(
        List.of("上半身", "首", "頭"), 6f, 1f, 600f, 180f, 0.7f);

At runtime you can use setWeight, setSettings, and setEnabled. An empty bone set means all dynamic bodies.

IkTargetModule and ActiveRagdollModule can be used together: the former modifies the targets first, Caliko solves the generic IK chains, and the latter then makes the Box3D bodies follow the post-IK pose. This is the recommended combination of animation, IK, and active physics.

docs.title: 5.3 AnchorModule and Display Children
docs.text:
Anchor in the model library (uml.structure.skeleton.Anchor) is a display-child anchor bound to a skinned bone, for example the sword a player holds. SkeletonInstance.anchorTransform(name) blends the bound bone's bind→current delta with the same rules as BDEF skinning to obtain the anchor world transform:

// hand the hand anchor's world transform to the host rendering logic every frame
instance.attachToAnchor("hand_r", worldTransform -> {
    if (worldTransform == null) { /* anchor is invalid, hide the held item */ return; }
    placeHeldItem(worldTransform.getPosition(), worldTransform.getRotation());
});
instance.detachFromAnchor("hand_r", attachment);

AnchorModule pushes these transforms in the last stage of every pipeline (kasuga:anchor), so an anchor always follows the final pose (including IK and physics). You can also call instance.anchorTransform(name) directly to query it immediately.

docs.title: 6. glTF Animation Compatibility
docs.text:
.glb and .gltf are registered as built-in resource pipelines. The parser API is in lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.typo.gltf:

GltfAsset asset = GltfLoader.load(path);                    // does not read animation tracks
GltfAsset animated = GltfLoader.load(path, Set.of("walk"));
GltfAsset all = GltfLoader.loadAllAnimations(path);
Model model = GltfModelConverter.convert(all);

GltfModelConverter merges all glTF nodes into one shared UML Skeleton and remaps every skin's JOINTS_0 to global Bones, so the existing CPU/GPU skinning and tick loop modules can be used directly. The Minecraft resource pipeline places embedded base-color images into the existing texture atlas.

ModelInstance instance = ...;
var animation = instance.getPosing();
animation.play("walk", true);

For the generic entry point see ModelPosing; the glTF sampler supports translation/rotation/scale/weights, STEP, LINEAR, and CUBIC_SPLINE. Resource-pack streaming of .gltf supports only embedded/data URIs; when you need external .bin or image URIs use the Path API, or package the asset as .glb.

In Minecraft you can place a <model>.gltf.json manifest next to the model:

{
  "model_scale": 1.3,
  "ragdoll": "example:ragdolls/character.json"
}

model_scale applies to the vertices, the bones, and the generated ragdoll at the same time; ragdoll points to a profile/simulation configuration. The deployment logic reads only the manifest and does not choose a profile by file name or model name. The generic command is:

/kasuga_ragdoll deploy example:models/character.glb

docs.title: 7. Minecraft Physics Block
docs.text:
MinecraftBlockRigidBody converts every voxel AABB of BlockState#getCollisionShape into one body-local BodyShape.Box, instead of always using the full unit cube. Slabs, fences, pillars, and combined shapes therefore keep their real collision gaps. The visual is still drawn by the vanilla block renderer.

MinecraftBlockPhysics uses one shared Box3D world:

  • physics blocks collide with each other in real native collision;
  • terrain is incrementally synchronized into static Box3D boxes by MinecraftBlockRagdollEnvironment;
  • collision groups: props sit in group 1; the local player AABB is a group 15 dynamic proxy and, through a non-collision mask, excludes group 0 (terrain and other default bodies), so the solver noise between the player and the terrain is not passed on to a ground-hugging prop through the proxy. Spectators and dead players get no proxy;
  • ground feel is synthesized from the contact writeback: the correction takes only the deepest contact's MTV (split by orientation — a top-face contact only lifts vertically and produces no horizontal drift; a side-face contact blocks walking just like a real wall), and the proxy's own solver displacement is not fed back to the player, so walking is not pushed back into "sliding" by the solver; while support holds, onGround is reset every frame and fallDistance is zeroed (vanilla clears that state every tick because no real block is underfoot), which makes ground friction, jumping, and fall-damage checks match real blocks;
  • the default cap is MAX_PROPS = 256, and a prop is released automatically when it falls out of the level or the dimension changes;
  • a block with an empty collision shape is not generated.

Debug commands:

/kasuga_physics block [1-32]
/kasuga_physics status
/kasuga_physics clear

This is a client-side playground. To the local player it shows as a pushable, standable collision prop, but it is not a server-registered Block/Entity and takes no part in server-authoritative collision, saving, chunk serialization, or multiplayer synchronization. If you need "like a normal block" semantics that include those network and save behaviors, add a server-side entity and a synchronization protocol above it; do not treat the current local collision bridge as an anti-cheat security boundary.

docs.title: 8. Current Limitations
docs.text:
• Box3D has no built-in Minecraft fluid volume/buoyancy API; the old Java buoyancy model has been deleted.
  • A PMX six-axis joint is currently mapped to a spherical joint; the rotation box is approximated as cone/twist, and the three translation axes are tightened to a fixed anchor.
  • A world currently has only one drag constraint.
  • glTF morph targets already convert POSITION / NORMAL and their weight animations; TANGENT, TEXCOORD / COLOR targets, a second set of skin weights, non-triangle primitives, and material extensions are not converted yet.
  • The glTF parser stores the metallic/roughness factor, but the current Minecraft adapter only uploads base-color directly; Kasuga's stylized PBR conversion still uses its own rules and atlas baker from pbr.md.

For the render pipeline, shader, and effect APIs see effect-rendering.md.

docs.title: Model Material Alpha Rendering Reference
docs.text:
Interfaces, configuration, and call reference. For the mechanics see render-alpha-passes.md.

Model materials are now split into three classes by the alpha contract of glTF/generic materials:

Class GPU state Fragment behavior Order OPAQUE No blending, depth write Ignores the sampled alpha, outputs 1 AFTER_ENTITIES priority 0 MASK No blending, depth write Fragments below the material alphaCutoff are discarded, the rest output 1 AFTER_ENTITIES priority 1 BLEND OIT accumulation/revealage, no depth write Drops only the near-invisible alpha <= 1/255, keeps the actual alpha AFTER_TRANSLUCENT_BLOCKS, WBOIT needs no sorting

BackendInstance creates a separate FlatModelData and vertex buffer for each non-empty pass, so a model with several materials does not draw incompatible geometry into the wrong RenderType. OPAQUE/MASK can still go into the global batch, but the batch key includes the alpha pass; BLEND does not go into the global batch, so that the two OIT geometry submissions and the ordinary batching state do not get mixed together.

Overlay models that must stay coplanar with another surface can explicitly set an instance-level depth bias; ordinary models preserve their original depth by default. Different bias policies split batches, and translucent sub-passes replay the same policy.

glTF's alphaMode and alphaCutoff are passed to the backend by GltfMaterialData. Older loaders without a transparency contract default to OPAQUE; the PMX loader infers OPAQUE/MASK/BLEND from the diffuse alpha and the texture alpha.

The non-Iris path of BLEND is a weighted-blended OIT (WBOIT) over two geometry sub-passes: the first pass adds color * alpha * weight and alpha * weight into an RGBA16F accumulation, the second multiplies 1 - alpha into an R16F revealage. Both passes use the scene depth copied from the main framebuffer, testing depth but not writing it; finally the fullscreen resolve computes color = accumulation.rgb / accumulation.a and alpha = 1 - revealage, then composites back to the main target with straight-alpha source-over. Therefore KasugaLib's BLEND geometry on this path does not depend on the far-to-near submit order.

With an Iris shader pack enabled, the same accumulation/revealage/resolve targets are used, but Iris's entities_translucent shader is kept to produce the straight-alpha color after material, PBR, lighting, and fog. Since Kasuga's depth weight cannot be injected into its fragment shader without modifying the shader pack, the Iris path uses a constant-weight WBOIT with weight 1: RGB accumulates with SRC_ALPHA, ONE, A accumulates with ONE, ONE, and revealage stays ZERO, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA. The translucent entity shader of Iris 1.8.12 carries its own 0.1 alpha test, lower than the 0.5 cutoff usually used by MASK.

Iris binds a shader pack gbuffer and can override the blend state on every ShaderInstance.apply(), so Kasuga rebinds the OIT attachment after apply and before draw, and explicitly restores the blend equation, blend factors, and color/depth mask. The scene depth is copied from Iris's after-translucent default framebuffer, and the resolve writes back to the same framebuffer; only the dedicated OIT composite shader is allowed to bypass the Iris unknown-shader guard, and the compatibility policy for other mod shaders is not relaxed.

docs.title: IrisOitCompat and CompatCapability Fallback Path
docs.text:
OitRenderer calls IrisWorldFramebuffer in the isolated modules/iris-compat module through IrisOitCompat (lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.compat.iris.IrisOitCompat) and IrisCompat. IrisWorldFramebuffer wraps its reflective probe in CompatCapability<BooleanSupplier> (lib.kasuga.core.compat.CompatCapability) to verify the exact method descriptors of Iris::getPipelineManager, PipelineManager::getPipelineNullable, IrisRenderingPipeline::bindDefault, and IrisApi.getInstance()::isRenderingShadowPass.

Whenever any of the following conditions occurs, OitRenderer / IrisWorldFramebuffer falls back safely to the far-to-near sorted translucency path (and never misreports sorted fallback as WBOIT):

  • The CompatCapability probe fails due to Iris/Sodium ABI changes (ReflectiveOperationException, InaccessibleObjectException, or LinkageError).
  • Iris is rendering a shadow pass (isRenderingShadowPass() is true), the active pipeline is absent, or the active pipeline is not an IrisRenderingPipeline.
  • Floating-point targets are unavailable, OpenGL 3.0 reports fewer than 2 color attachments or draw buffers, OitCompositeShaderInstance or OIT RenderType entries are missing after a resource reload, or a runtime framebuffer operation throws an exception.

On fallback, IrisOitCompat.reportFallback(reason, cause) emits one deduplicated warning log carrying the installed iris and sodium versions and displays a client SystemToast (kasuga_lib.oit.fallback.title / kasuga_lib.oit.fallback.iris).

WBOIT is an approximation, not an exact source-over for an arbitrary number of layers, and it does not bring vanilla water or the transparent fragments of a shader pack into the same OIT equation; the current stage is still AFTER_TRANSLUCENT_BLOCKS, so its scope is "the KasugaLib BLEND layer composited onto an already finished scene". Iris OIT resolves the main color only; a shader pack that relies on custom extra gbuffer channels to express transparent materials may still need pack-specific integration.

A material's alphaCutoff for MASK and the near-zero 1/255 working cutoff of BLEND are two independent concepts: the former decides whether depth is written, and the latter only removes OIT work items that are almost invisible.

docs.title: Visual acceptance scene (contentTesting)
docs.text:
In the development client, /ksglib debug oit enables OITVisualTestScene, fixed relative to the camera. The scene splits the screen into six regions A-F:

Region What it verifies A OPAQUE geometry and scene depth; the red BLEND behind it must not pass through the solid blocks B Artificial alpha ramp; alpha < 0.5 must discard, and the retained part must write depth C Red/blue crossing faces whose depth relation is reversed left to right; ordinary object sorting cannot be correct on both sides at once D Two transparent layers in front of and behind an irregular opaque wall, checking depth copy, depth test, and depth write=OFF E 12 colored transparent faces, whose submit order changes by a deterministic permutation F Stage/framebuffer regression for a transparent model composited onto the current scene (you can stand on vanilla water to observe)

Keybinds: F6 toggles between WBOIT and the sorted fallback, F7 toggles the normal/reverse submit order, and F8 cycles FINAL → ACCUM_RGB → ACCUM_WEIGHT → REVEALAGE → COPIED_DEPTH. The HUD shows the actual path; so with Iris, with insufficient capabilities, or when OIT fails, the sorted fallback is not mistaken for WBOIT.

Available commands:

/ksglib debug oit
/ksglib debug oit mode oit|sorted
/ksglib debug oit order auto|normal|reverse|rotate|shuffle
/ksglib debug oit buffer final|accum_rgb|accum_weight|revealage|depth

/ksglib debug oit capture saves oit_normal.png, oit_reverse.png, sorted_normal.png, and sorted_reverse.png in that order to the development client's screenshots/kasuga_oit_visual/, and computes

E_oit = mean(abs(oit_normal - oit_reverse))
E_sorted = mean(abs(sorted_normal - sorted_reverse))

The acceptance condition is E_oit < 1/255 and E_sorted greater than at least 2/255 and significantly higher than E_oit. This does not require WBOIT to equal the exact source-over ground truth; it checks its independence from submit order, and the tiny non-associativity error of floating-point addition should not be treated as a failure.

docs.title: Model render scheduling (Render Scheduling)
docs.text:
Interface, configuration, and call reference. For the principles see render-scheduling.md.

For the public scheduling and buffer/backend contracts see the UML rendering framework. The ModelRenderScheduler in this document is an MC compatibility adapter; the policy and frame marks are managed by uml.framework.schedule; VANILLA_RENDERER corresponds to the public HOST_RENDERER. Multi-camera visibility marks are cleared per view and animation sampling is deduplicated by the shared frame token; see the multi-camera and offscreen output document.

After a UML model is mounted to mc_backend, it is drawn by the phased world pipeline. This document answers "when a model should render and when it should not", and how to integrate with the scheduling mechanism of Minecraft's vanilla renderer.

docs.title: 0. Model handle: the split between the logic side and the render side
docs.text:
Upper-layer code operates on the same model in two halves, following MC's mental model:

upper logic side ────► state machine (FSM / PoseDriver)    decides "what action to perform": state, transition, animation behavior
                     │ writes bone local transforms
                     ▼
              ModelInstance ◄───────────────────── the same instance
                     ▲ writes root transform / scheduling / anchors / physics
upper render side ───► McModelHandle                  decides "where it goes, whether it is visible, which schedule to use"

McModelHandle (mc/api/McModelHandle) is the only entry point on the render side: resource-level outfit uses ofAssembly / switchAssembly, see outfit resources and switching.

// Render side: the handle can be created before resources are published; the pose is stashed and takes effect on mount
McModelHandle handle = McModelHandle.of(modelLoc, null, instanceLoc, new Vec3(x, y, z));
handle.mount();                       // returns false while resources are unpublished; retry next tick
handle.setPos(entity.position());     // vanilla-style verb
handle.scheduleVanillaRenderer();     // visibility is decided by the vanilla renderer
handle.attachToAnchor("hand_r", (name, t) -> placeItem(t));  // held item
handle.enablePhysics(UpdateMode.RENDER_FRAME);
handle.hide() / show() / markRenderedThisFrame();

A state machine is attached through the handle in three forms:

// ① Local data-driven: built from a definition id; the logic side ticks the bound object
var binding = handle.attachLocalStateMachine(Id.of("kasuga_lib", "door"));
if (binding != null) {
    binding.machine().mutableVars().set(OPEN, true);  // the logic side triggers the transition
    binding.tick();                                   // call from the BE/Entity game tick
}

// ② Local programmatic: take over an already built machine directly
var machine = StateMachine.builder(owner)...build();
handle.attachLocalStateMachine(machine);

// ③ Full host with server-authoritative sync (recommended for BE/Entity):
//    create the handle with ofFsm to align the instance identity; it hosts an FsmAnimatedModel
//    internally, the client-bound instance is adopted into the handle automatically,
//    and render scheduling still applies as usual.
McModelHandle handle = McModelHandle.ofFsm(modelLoc, null, pos.asLong(), null);
FsmAnimatedModel fsm = handle.attachSyncedStateMachine(this, pos.asLong(), fsmId);
fsm.tick(level, pos);        // forwarded from the BE ticker (server pushes sync / client drives the puppet)

If the instance was already created by an existing component (such as the FsmAnimatedModel inside an AnimationBlockEntity), the render side adopts it with McModelHandle.ofExisting(modelLoc, modelName, instanceLoc) instead of creating a second instance.

docs.title: 1. The three scheduling modes
docs.text:
ModelRenderScheduler maintains one policy per mounted instance, defaulting to ALWAYS (the historical behavior: unconditional draw every frame). To switch modes:

ModelRenderScheduler.setMode(instance, RenderScheduleMode.VANILLA_RENDERER);
Mode Decision maker Typical host ALWAYS The global pipeline draws every frame Static decoration, effect-type content MANUAL Host code: setVisible(instance, bool) or pipeline.setRendering(model, id, bool) Custom LOD/switch logic VANILLA_RENDERER Whether the vanilla renderer is called Entities (EntityRenderer), block entities (BER)

Beyond the modes there are two orthogonal gates:

  • Render distance: setMaxRenderDistance(instance, blocks) culls by squared camera distance; 0 means unlimited.
  • Frustum: for each instance the pipeline runs a Frustum.isVisible test using "the vertex bounding sphere translated to the root position" (the bounding radius is computed and cached on first use). A culled instance is not sampled for animation and does not upload vertices in that frame — consistent with "the vanilla renderer is not called once a mob is beyond its distance". Physics stepping is independent of visibility (MinecraftRagdollRuntime) and does not freeze because of culling.

Unmounting an instance (stopRendering/removeInstance) automatically cleans up its scheduling state.

docs.title: 2. Integrating with the vanilla Entity renderer
docs.text:
The vanilla flow: EntityRenderer.render is called only after EntityRenderDispatcher.shouldRender (tracking distance + frustum) passes. To make an entity model inherit this scheduling:

  1. Mount the model in VANILLA_RENDERER mode;
  2. Provide a renderer extending UmlModelEntityRenderer<T> and register it for the entity type:
public class MyEntityRenderer extends UmlModelEntityRenderer<MyEntity> {
    public MyEntityRenderer(EntityRendererProvider.Context ctx) { super(ctx); }

    @Override protected ModelInstance resolveModel(MyEntity entity) {
        return entity.getKasugaModel();   // the instance held by the host
    }

    @Override protected ResourceLocation modelTexture(MyEntity entity) {
        return null; // queried only by the vanilla UI overlay; null → white fallback
    }
}

For entities culled by tracking range or outside the frustum, the vanilla code does not call their renderer's render() → no mark → the pipeline skips sampling and drawing for that frame.

docs.title: 3. Integrating with the vanilla BlockEntity renderer
docs.text:
The vanilla flow: BlockEntityRenderDispatcher.render first checks BlockEntityRenderer.shouldRender (view distance, 64 blocks by default), then the section frustum outside it; render() is called only when both pass.

BlockEntityRenderers.register(MY_BE_TYPE,
        context -> new UmlBlockEntityRenderer<>(context,
                be -> be.getKasugaRender().getModelInstance("main")));

Mount in VANILLA_RENDERER mode here as well. getViewDistance can be adjusted at construction time.

docs.title: 4. What about "blocks that go through the chunk dispatcher"
docs.text:
Modern vanilla bakes static block geometry straight into the mesh of a whole chunk section (SectionRenderDispatcher builds in batches) and has no per-block renderer callback — a deliberate batching optimization. The conclusion splits into two cases:

  • Purely static models: they can still be baked into the chunk mesh (or use an ordinary BakedModel) and benefit from the vanilla section-level culling and batching; the price is that they can never move.
  • Dynamic/skeletal models: they cannot be baked into a section mesh (vertices change every frame), so vanilla provides no dispatcher entry point for them. There are two proper paths:
  • Promote to a BlockEntity + the BER adapter above — recommended, it fully reuses vanilla scheduling; this is also how vanilla itself handles "blocks that need to change every frame" (chest open/close animations, banners, etc. are all BEs).
  • Keep the global pipeline mount and use MANUAL mode with your own visibility logic, or rely on the pipeline's built-in frustum/render-distance culling (ALWAYS mode gets these two gates as well).

In short: the chunk baking path carries static content only; any dynamic model that needs scheduling should land in an Entity / BlockEntity renderer or under explicit MANUAL control.

docs.title: 5. Frame timing
docs.text:
vanilla pass: entities + block entities
  └─ EntityRenderer.render / BER.render
       └─ ModelRenderScheduler.markRenderedThisFrame(instance)
kasuga pipelines:
  └─ AFTER_ENTITIES (priority 0 → 1)
       ├─ OPAQUE: no blend + depth write
       └─ MASK: alpha discard + depth write
  └─ AFTER_TRANSLUCENT_BLOCKS
       └─ BLEND: low alpha discard + no depth write + weighted-blended OIT
          (Iris/unsupported-target fallback: far-to-near sort)

  The first pass calls flipFrame() to lock in this frame's marks. The sampled-instance
  cache remains alive until BLEND, so a mixed model is sampled once even
  though its three material classes are submitted independently.

The mark buffer uses a double-buffer swap: marks written by the vanilla pass are locked in at the start of the pipeline, next frame's marks go into the other buffer, and the two stages need no synchronization barrier.

docs.title: Rendering backend integration reference
docs.text: Backend integration and contract reference; for module layering, resource ownership, and synchronization principles see the explanation.

docs.title: Module dependencies
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    Host[modelling: Minecraft host adaptation] --> GL[render-opengl: OpenGL / LWJGL]
    Host --> Core[render-core: UML and rendering contracts]
    GL --> Core
    Future[future Vulkan / Metal backend] -. implements the same set of contracts .-> Core

render-core is a plain Java library. It does not apply the ModDev plugin and does not depend on Minecraft, NeoForge, LWJGL, or a specific graphics API. Before compileJava, checkGraphicsApiIsolation runs and checks source imports as well as compile and runtime dependencies, keeping these dependencies out of the core. DataFixerUpper is used for the existing data codecs; it is not Blaze3D or the Minecraft renderer. The dependencies of formula and utils disable transitive resolution and only reuse the existing Java expressions and data structures.

render-opengl likewise does not apply ModDev. It depends on the core and on LWJGL and centrally manages GL buffers, textures, shaders, VAOs, fences, FBOs, readback, and preview windows. The host that runs it is responsible for providing the current GL context, the correct thread, and the LWJGL natives for the platform.

modelling keeps Minecraft's world render events, RenderType, VertexFormat, texture atlases, lighting, Iris/Sodium compatibility, and multi-camera world rendering. These classes are host adapters for the current Minecraft + OpenGL combination and cannot serve as a general interface for other graphics APIs.

docs.title: UML and resource lifecycle
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant H as host
    participant P as ModelPipeLine / ModelInstance
    participant B as RenderBackend
    participant C as RenderContext
    participant D as concrete graphics API
    H->>P: load model, create instance, bind PoseDriver
    H->>B: add(key, adapter, instance)
    B->>C: create context and apply()
    C->>D: create backend resources
    loop every view, every render stage
        H->>B: renderAllObjects(hostContext)
        B->>P: schedule, sample pose per frame
        B->>C: beforeRender(hostContext)
        B->>D: upload data, submit draws
    end
    H->>B: remove(key) / close()
    B->>C: close()
    C->>D: release or defer recycling of resources

The core covers model loading, model structures, skeletons, morph, animation, FSM, and pose sampling and scheduling, plus the RenderBackend, RenderContext, ModelGeometryAdapter, RenderableFactory, RenderBuffer, TypedBuffer, and output routing contracts. Its resource type, host frame context, and transform metadata are all generic; it does not require GL objects or Minecraft classes.

Backend / BackendContext provide the default mount and release behavior; a concrete backend implements context creation, data packing, and drawing. A failed mount does not publish a half-built context; removing an instance releases only that mount's backend resources, while the model instance itself is managed by the model pipeline.

The core still contains the Java/JNI physics adaptation of the existing Box3D. Physics is not part of a graphics API; when used standalone, a host that enables Box3D must additionally provide the platform's native library.

docs.title: Upload and output
docs.text:
UploadRing is responsible only for slot rotation, dirty element merging, version tracking, and the resource lifecycle, and performs allocation, writes, and completion-status queries through UploadDevice. GpuUploadRing on the production path is now its OpenGL adapter, keeping the original constructors, statistics types, and FloatBuffer entry points. The macOS TBO orphan policy continues to be provided by MacTboUploadDevice in the OpenGL module.

The integer buffer token and the long completion token of UploadDevice are opaque handles internal to the backend, not cross-API native resource IDs. A new backend can map them into its own resource table. A device must guarantee that reads already submitted remain valid after the storage is replaced; completion queries must not block. A device that cannot meet this contract should use its own upload implementation and reuse the higher-level UploadBuffer / RenderBuffer.

FrameOutputRouter<T>, FrameOutputTarget<T>, OutputFrame<T>, and the camera state belong to the core. T is defined by the backend. FrameTexture is the OpenGL framebuffer/texture carrier and belongs to the OpenGL module; other APIs should provide their own output carrier and target.

docs.title: Integrating another API
docs.text:
1. Create a standalone Java backend module that depends only on render-core and the binding of the target API.
  2. Implement RenderBackend / RenderContext, or extend the default Backend / BackendContext. Model, skeleton, and pose data are read directly from the existing ModelInstance; the adapter is responsible for the target API's vertex layout, skeleton data representation, shader, synchronization, and submission.
  3. Have the host inject the corresponding backend and host frame context. ModelPipeLine.Builder already supports registering a backend; a default implementation can extend Backend, and a standalone RenderBackend implementation can also mount model instances directly.
  4. Implement FrameOutputTarget<YourFrame> and reuse the core output routing and camera lifecycle.
  5. Handle windows, resource reload, render stages, and other platform interop in the host adaptation layer.

Existing public class names are kept to preserve call and serialization name compatibility. Some GL classes therefore still use the historical uml.backend.gpu package name, and the pure math Direction also keeps the historical models.mc.util package name. Whether something belongs to the core is determined by Gradle module dependencies; the core must not import the OpenGL module.

This split did not implement a Vulkan/Metal backend, nor does it let Minecraft's Blaze3D switch APIs at runtime. Minecraft's effect pipeline description still uses its own draw state for now; replacing the whole renderer of that host would additionally require the corresponding host adaptation and shader generation path.

docs.title: Unified Resource Platform and Script Tickets
docs.text: Built on top of the existing VFS, this platform provides stable identity, immutable content capture, directory routing, generational publication, and revocable access. The Java host approves sources and Entry Points; JSON only describes routing for already-approved sources—it never mounts paths, downloads files, or registers Java implementations.

docs.title: Identity and Content
docs.text:
Concrete identities take the form ksg://<source>/roots/<root>/<path>#<child>. source and root are assigned by the host and cannot be synthesized on the fly from absolute paths, enum ordinals, or pack display names. URIs do not carry scope or generation; runtime handles bind those two separately.

Paths preserve Unicode, spaces, and case; serialization uses canonical UTF-8 percent-encoding. Absolute paths, backslashes, empty segments, . / .., control characters, queries, malformed UTF-8, and encoded separators are rejected. To reject double-decoding, raw names also cannot contain % followed immediately by two hexadecimal digits. Use ResourceUri.file(...) / .child(...) instead of hand-assembling URI strings.

For example, an original 模型/列车 A.bbmodel and its sub-resource #texture/uuid/… each have distinct identities. MinecraftNameCodec generates reversible names in the reserved kasuga_generated namespace with version prefix v1/ and hexadecimal UTF-8 encoding of the full URI. The MC adapter prepends models/ or textures/ and appends a format suffix. Existing assets/<namespace>/... and data/<namespace>/... retain their native ResourceLocation and must obey vanilla lowercase naming rules.

ResourceSourceDescriptor carries owner/source/root, an explicit rank, and an origin category. Ranks layer from low to high; equal-rank conflicts on the same logical path fail rather than relying on HashMap order. ResourceCatalog retains both all providers and the visible winner. Permissions filter providers first before choosing the winner; a winner with an incompatible type fails rather than silently falling back to a lower layer.

ResourceSources supports host-approved directories, ordinary ZIP/JAR archives, expanded mod directories, and any existing VFS. It captures actual bytes and computes SHA-256, returning a snapshot only when consecutive captures match; modifying or replacing an archive re-opens it on the next capture. Traversal, duplicate archive entries, file/directory conflicts, symbolic links, special files, encrypted or split ZIPs, and currently ZIP64 are rejected. No filename can trigger automatic network access.

InputPolicy.DEFAULT enforces 8 MiB for JSON, 256 MiB per file, 1 GiB total per source, 50,000 files, JSON depth 64, and spooling to a private temporary file above 1 MiB. Actual decompressed and derived bytes also count toward these budgets. Depth is checked by the JSON decoder; the bbmodel adapter uses the passed policy's depth. Sources with cross-file dependencies should still be published by the host via transactions or atomic replacement.

ResourceTypeDetector inspects at most 512 bytes: PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP, WAV/Ogg/FLAC/ID3-tagged MP3, GLB/PMX, and ZIP are classified first by magic number. Text formats without fixed signatures use extension hints only after UTF-8 and control-character checks pass; a JSON prefix can identify extensionless text. A descriptor's typeEvidence distinguishes MAGIC, TEXT_PREFIX, EXTENSION, DECLARED, and UNKNOWN. Signatures are discovery evidence only and never substitute for format decoding, permission checks, or script execution authorization.

docs.title: Schema and Structural Routing
docs.text:
Validatable editor schemas live in resource-routing.schema.json and resource-template.schema.json. At runtime, decoding also checks for duplicate JSON keys, unknown fields, source authorization, template cycles, duplicate IDs, and path safety. Format version is 1.

{
  "format_version": 1,
  "bindings": [
    {"id": "root", "source_id": "example", "schema_id": "minecraft_resource_schema"},
    {
      "id": "scripts", "source_id": "example", "source_prefix": "scripts",
      "outputs": [{
        "id": "blocks", "entry_point_id": "kasuga:script_blocks",
        "when": "resource_reload", "side": "server", "target_prefix": "scripts"
      }]
    }
  ]
}

source_prefix matches on full path segments. The longest-matching binding is chosen first, then its outputs' event and side are checked; if a child binding has no output for the active side, routing does not fall back to a parent binding. a/b does not match a/bc. Paths strip source_prefix and prepend target_prefix; root-level kasuga.resources.json is not passed as an ordinary consumer input.

Templates use id, a single extends, remove_outputs, and outputs. Inherited outputs are replaced whole by stable output ID; you cannot remove and re-add the same ID, and removing a non-existent ID fails. A single binding can emit explicitly to multiple consumers; duplicate emissions of the same file to the same consumer and target path fail. Maximum template inheritance depth is 32. The template registry is passed by the host to ResourceRouting.decode; JSON contains no external $ref or remote schema loading.

Events in ResourceEvent are host_bootstrap (HOST_BOOTSTRAP), client_startup, server_startup, resource_reload, and remote_connect; sides are client, server, both, and none. both is a declaration value—each actual invocation uses one concrete logical side, and server scripts on an integrated server still execute as server. none is only for consumers that do not depend on an MC context. Declarations cannot exceed the events and sides permitted by the Java EntryPointDescriptor.

docs.title: Initial MC Discovery and Models
docs.text:
Native pack projections are added during the AddPackFindersEvent / RepositorySource phase. Before initial discovery, the host calls:

ResourceSource source = ResourceSources.directory(
    new ResourceSourceDescriptor("my-mod", "example", "main", 100,
        ResourceSourceDescriptor.Origin.EXTERNAL), approvedDirectory, InputPolicy.DEFAULT);
ResourceRouting routing = ResourceRouting.decode(json, ResourceRouting.builtinTemplates(), Set.of("example"));
AutoCloseable registration = resourceSystem.getApprovedPacks().register("example", List.of(source), routing);

ResourceSystem already subscribes its finder to the mod bus. Approved directories must be supplied by the host; configuration text is read and explicitly decoded by the host. Optional ModelResourceSource wrapping should be done before registration. Each source/root is an independent MC pack layer, and Minecraft's real ResourceManager determines the winner and pack stack. The registration handle only unregisters the entry without closing the host source; opened packs and streams use their own leases.

McManagedResourceView borrows the MC manager, preserves its real pack stack, and can capture resources as MC_MANAGED sources under host-supplied stable pack provenance. It does not close the MC manager or packs. MC_MANAGED inputs are forbidden from projecting back into MC to avoid resource discovery cycles.

Non-MC .bbmodel files use ModelResourceSource: it keeps the original file, extracts embedded PNGs as derived textures with parent URIs, distinguishes same-named textures by texture UUID or explicit index, and generates an MC model copy referencing those textures. Models and textures are prepared before the same discovery pass so existing model scanning, decoding, material, and atlas pipelines receive them without a second reload round. Pixel counts are bounded by a host limit.

Input Current integration Native assets/data models and textures Retains existing loading paths and native IDs Non-MC .bbmodel + embedded PNGs Full capture, derivation, initial model/atlas load, replacement, and deletion OBJ/PMX/glTF/FMT, etc. Provides ResourceModelInput and text/json/binary Source adapters; migrating each decoder's container/external dependencies requires corresponding host adaptation .bbmodel external images, non-PNG embedded images Currently rejected; requires an explicit dependency adapter

ResourceModelInput.sibling allows only relative dependencies within the same concrete source/root; it cannot search across roots or steal dependencies from lower-priority providers. The platform does not build a separate GPU backend.

docs.title: Scopes and Publication
docs.text:
Java consumers implement ResourceEntryPoint, declaring input types, events, sides, dependencies, and reload support; prepare(ResourceBatch, InvocationContext) returns an asynchronous PreparedConsumerBatch. The entire plan is validated first, then captured, then prepared in dependency topological order, and finally published on the host's publishExecutor, replacing the coordinator's current generation atomically. A new request invalidates older unpublished preparations; preparation failures keep the already-published generation intact.

Select the appropriate owner via ResourceSystem.createClientResourceScope, createServerResourceScope(server, id), or createProcessResourceScope; stopping a server closes only scopes belonging to that server. Call coordinator.reload(sources, routing, event, side, prepareExecutor, publishExecutor) to start work. The host is responsible for subscribing to appropriate events or optional VFS watchers and coalescing reload requests; declarative config itself does not create watchers.

publishExecutor must remain alive until the last generation lease is released. ResourceGeneration.lease() retains old content; retirement immediately revokes script calls, and once the last lease closes, consumers and snapshots are closed on publishExecutor. disposal() reports the final release result. A ResourceSnapshot file/stream lease independently retains captured bytes and rejects new reads after close. Calling cancel on the future returned by reload only abandons observation; it does not skip internal cleanup or roll back an already-committed publication.

MinecraftResourceEntryPoint.Projection.openLayers() is provided for hosts that manage their own MC discovery/reload barrier. The coordinator's atomic publication guarantees a consistent platform view; vanilla MC reload and external side effects of consumer publish() still follow their own lifecycles, as the platform cannot undo side effects already performed by arbitrary Java callbacks.

docs.title: Script Blocks and Tickets
docs.text:
Data files declare only a reference and expected contract:

{
  "package": "ksg://example/roots/main/scripts/package.toml",
  "block": "increment",
  "side": "server",
  "contract": {"arguments": ["number"], "result": "number"}
}

Static decoding calls ScriptReferenceCodec.decode or data-driven's opt-in ScriptBlockReferenceDecoder, validating structure, logical side, and host visibility without executing scripts. After package startup, scripts register explicitly on the sandboxed ScriptThread:

ScriptBlocks.register("increment", '{"arguments":["number"],"result":"number"}', value => value + 1);

The host registers ManagedScriptEntryPoint(engineLookup, trustedSourcePredicate, referencePermissionPredicate) (with an optional AccessFactory overload) and routes package files. Each generation uses an independent module registry bound to scope / generation / ScriptPackage / ScriptEngine / ScriptThread. Only after package preparation completes does ScriptBlockRegistry.bind(ref, context) yield a ScriptBlockHandle; mismatched names, contracts, or generations fail. Ordinary module.exports do not automatically become externally callable blocks. Trust is determined by the host's source policy—never by self-reported fields inside the package.

ScriptTicket ticket = handle.submit(List.of(41)); // copies data and enqueues only; returns immediately
ticket.poll().ifPresent(outcome -> consume(outcome));
ticket.onComplete(callerExecutor, outcome -> consume(outcome));

This is a Java implementation of an io_uring-style submission/completion token and does not use Linux native io_uring. Each target thread has a bounded MPSC ring (default capacity 1024); ScriptThread drains on the owner thread with a batch budget of at most 64 requests / 2 ms. The budget is checked between callbacks and cannot preempt a single currently executing function. Arguments and results permit only copied bounded-depth data so engine values or host objects cannot leak out.

Ticket states are QUEUED, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED, and REJECTED; a full ring or invalid arguments reject immediately, and exceptions are returned as a failure type and message. Callers may cancel; generation retirement or scope close immediately cancels all pending tickets, and late results cannot overwrite cancellation. Tickets have no blocking get/join API; completion callbacks run on the caller's executor, and the MC main thread must never synchronously wait on scripts.

Currently, Javet's general sandbox capabilities are marked UNVERIFIED, so the new entry rejects untrusted scripts by default. Untrusted packages may be permitted only once an engine explicitly proves isolation for host classes/reflection, files, network, execution budget, memory, and cancellation; this change does not claim to have completed that sandbox. The legacy script entry remains compatible, with its reload changed to wait asynchronously for retirement rather than joining on the game thread.

An optional AccessFactory assigns ResourceAccess to a package, giving scripts a data-only Resources facade. Grants restrict owner/source/root/prefix and read/query/write/create/delete operations; reads enforce per-call and total byte budgets. Writes go only into a host-created bounded in-memory Workspace, never modifying source packs, arbitrary disk paths, or world saves. Scope retirement revokes access, and the host is responsible for closing the Workspace.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
./gradlew :modules:core:test :modules:data-driven:test :modules:scripting:test :modules:modelling:modelUnitTest
./gradlew :modules:modelling:test --tests '*ModelResourceSourceTest' :external:slp:javet:test --tests '*ResourceScriptTicketIntegrationTest'
./gradlew :modules:modelling:runClientHeadless -PkasugaClientDirectory="$PWD/build/resource-platform-client" -PkasugaTestResources=true

Client smoke verifies the initial model and GPU texture, updated pixels under the same ID, and model/sprite cleanup after deletion from the menu, writes debug/resource-platform/report.json, and exits without opening a world. FML integration tests use real packs and managers, and Javet integration tests actually register and execute JS. Pure JVM modelUnitTest does not run vanilla metadata integration scenarios tagged minecraft-resource-integration; those run under normal test.

docs.title: Aeronautics / Sable scene hosts
docs.text: Aeronautics physics structures are backed by Sable SubLevel instances whose blocks live in a separate plot coordinate space. SableSceneHosts adapts these structures to the existing SceneHost, SceneModels, and world-UI APIs through the official Sable Companion API. The code lives in the modules/create client adapter package and does not modify Sable or Aeronautics source code.

docs.title: Block anchors
docs.text:
// plotBlockPos is the block's actual storage position, e.g. BlockEntity.getBlockPos(), not its projected world position.
SableSceneHosts.block(minecraft.level, plotBlockPos).ifPresent(host -> {
    var scene = SceneModels.open(minecraft.level);
    scene.add(myDisplayScene, host);
    Constants.UI_BACKEND.addRenderable(myWorldPanel, host,
            new Matrix4f().translation(0, 2, 1).scale(.01f, -.01f, .01f));
    // Retain a reference to scene and call scene.close() when the content owner's lifecycle ends.
});

Local (0,0,0) corresponds to the lower corner of the anchor block. Model and UI offsets are in blocks, and the UI matrix maps pixels into host-local space. Scene-attached panels automatically share the model's sampled pose; standalone panels sample on the UI draw frame.

The adapter calls ClientSubLevelAccess.renderPose(partialTick), transforming the plot anchor in double precision through the rotation point, orientation, and scale into world coordinates before constructing a nearby float basis. It never converts a distant plot origin to Matrix4f first, and never draws with the uninterpolated logical physics pose.

Factories return Optional.empty() when Companion is absent, the target is outside a sublevel, or the chunk/anchor is not ready. A target known to belong to Sable should retry once ready rather than temporarily mounting at raw plot coordinates while waiting. isAvailable() only reports that the optional API is on the classpath, not that a sublevel necessarily exists at a given position.

docs.title: Ordinary Create contraptions aboard a ship
docs.text:
SableSceneHosts.contraption(entity).ifPresent(host -> {
    var source = CreateModelSources.contraptionLocal(entity);
    scene.add(new ModelDisplayTarget(source), host);
});

This entry composes the Sable parent pose followed by the Create entity's local pose, avoiding double-applied rotation. Ordinary Create contraptions outside Sable continue using CreateSceneHosts.contraption(entity). Use contraptionLocal as the model source; the existing independent preview source already includes rotation and must not be attached to the same moving host again.

docs.title: Lifecycle and responsibility boundaries
docs.text:
The adapter continuously resolves the sublevel containing the original anchor or child entity and checks original object identity and UUID. Breaking the original anchor, moving it out of its original plot on a split, having the child entity leave its original sublevel, unloading, or switching worlds permanently expires the old attachment. Reappearing identical UUIDs or storage slots never revive old panels; content layers must create a new attachment in the new object's lifecycle.

Existing SceneModels / UIBackend owners clean up model and input resources. The adapter only reads poses and creates no new physics authority, network protocol, or model JSON fields; gameplay actions triggered by buttons still require validation through the existing server-side interfaces.

docs.title: Optional dependencies and verification environment
docs.text:
Production code only has a compileOnly dependency on Companion 1.6.0, and Sable supplies that API at runtime. Ordinary Create environments without Companion installed can load the optional entry points and receive empty results. Full Sable, Aeronautics, and Rapier libraries are not bundled into KasugaLib artifacts.

The current integration target is official Sable 2.0.6, Aeronautics 1.3.2, and Companion 1.6.0. These releases require at least NeoForge 21.1.228, Create 6.0.10, and Flywheel 1.0.6. Base project versions remain unchanged; tests select the isolated run profile through explicit Gradle properties and an init script.

Place the official Sable and Aeronautics bundled JARs into an isolated game directory's mods folder and use a dedicated test world:

./gradlew :modules:create:runClientHeadless \
  -I scripts/sable-scene-smoke.init.gradle \
  -Pneo_version=21.1.228 -Pcreate_version=6.0.10-280 \
  -Pflywheel_version=1.0.6 -Pregistrate_version=MC1.21-1.3.0+67 \
  -PkasugaSableSmokeJar=/absolute/path/sable-neoforge-1.21.1-2.0.6.jar \
  -PkasugaClientDirectory=/absolute/path/to/isolated/game \
  -PkasugaQuickPlayWorld=sable-scene -PkasugaTestSableScene=true --console=plain

The full Sable API is only used by development acceptance sources compiled when kasugaSableSmokeJar is set and does not enter the default source set. The test drives real sublevels via the upstream server assembly and physics teleport APIs, including an Aeronautics levitite block and an ordinary Create bearing aboard the ship. It checks main framebuffer RGBA, clicks on scene/standalone/nested panels, structure picking, and unload cleanup. The bearing fixture uses the native ROTATE_NEVER_PLACE setting so it does not place blocks back when unpowered. Results are written to debug/sable-scene/report.json in the game directory; verify passed rather than relying on the Gradle exit code alone.

Pure JVM regressions use Companion's actual Pose3d to verify distant coordinates, rotation points, non-uniform scale, nested Create parent-child composition, identity invalidation, and class-loading paths without Companion.

On 2026-11-11, client acceptance passed on macOS arm64 with official Sable 2.0.6 / Aeronautics 1.3.2: two phases of 30 frames each, 60 accumulated clicks on each of the three panel types, ship translation/rotation, 25°/65° child bearing rotation, model picking, and host-removal cleanup all passed. The native Rapier library used the unmodified aarch64 macOS version inside the official JAR. Ordinary Create 6.0.6 and 6.0.10 windmill demos were regressed separately, and both actual curve gauge bake paths were exercised and verified. Testing did not cover dedicated servers, multiple clients, Valkyrien Skies, or all third-party shader pack combinations.

docs.title: Scripting and Javet Runtime Reference
docs.text:
:modules:scripting (package prefix lib.kasuga.scripting) provides the engine-agnostic scripting runtime, package discovery, package.toml parsing, module registries, @Api security enforcement, timers, and the animation state-machine (FSM) scripting bridge. :external:slp:javet (package prefix lib.kasuga.slp.javet, standalone NeoForge mod ID kasuga_lib_javet) provides the Javet / V8 5.0.1 JavaScript engine backend and automatic native library downloader.

For ScriptBlockRegistry, ScriptSubmissionRing, ManagedScriptEntryPoint, and the asynchronous ScriptTicket contract in the unified resource platform, see Unified Resource Platform and Script Tickets.

docs.title: Modules and Coordinates
docs.text:
Module Gradle Project Mod ID / Packaging Responsibility Core scripting runtime :modules:scripting Merged into kasuga_lib (useModProject) Engine abstraction, package scanning, threading model, module registries, timer, @Api security feature, FSM API Javet V8 backend :external:slp:javet kasuga_lib_javet (requires kasuga_lib, AFTER) JavetScriptEngine, FastJavetClassConverter, JsModuleResolver, JavetDownloader

modules/library/build.gradle bundles :modules:scripting into the primary distribution via useModProject(project(':modules:scripting')); :external:slp:javet ships as an optional companion mod (see Library Packaging and Multiversion Structure).

docs.title: ScriptEngine and ScriptEngineType
docs.text:
lib.kasuga.scripting.ScriptEngine defines the per-instance script engine lifecycle:

Method Description usePackageRegistry(PackageRegistry packages) Injects an isolated PackageRegistry before init; defaults to UnsupportedOperationException safetyCapabilities() Returns ScriptSafetyCapabilities, defaulting to ScriptSafetyCapabilities.UNVERIFIED init(ScriptConsole console) Initializes the runtime instance, console interceptor, and built-in modules setFeatures(Map<EngineFeatureType<?>, EngineFeature>) / getFeature(type) Binds and retrieves engine features (such as SecurityEngineFeature) createValue(Object object) Wraps a Java object as a ScriptValue loadModule(ResolvedScript script) / getLoadedModule(String sourcePath) Loads and caches a script module by source path, returning ScriptModuleHandle executeEntry(String entryName, InputStream source[, ResolvedPackage owner]) Executes an entry script; supplying owner scopes relative require calls on the entry's first frame to that package tick() / close() Advances the engine and active ScriptModule instances each tick, or tears down the runtime on close registerGlobal(String name, Object api) Registers an engine-global object (such as Animator, AnimatorBuilder, ScriptBlocks)

lib.kasuga.scripting.ScriptEngineType<T> encapsulates engine instantiation and metadata via ScriptEngineType.builder(Supplier<T>):

Builder Method Field / Default Description scriptType(String) scriptType Primary language identifier (e.g., "javascript") engineSupplier(Supplier<T>) engineSupplier Engine instance factory resolver(ModuleResolver) resolver Script file locator (locateScript / getExtension) multiThreadSupporting(boolean) false Multithreading capability flag priority(int) 0 Resolution priority per language name (higher wins) addFeature(EngineFeatureType<?>) featureTypes Instantiated independently per engine via featureType.build() addGlobalApi(String, Function<ScriptEngine, Object>) globalApis Creates a global API object receiving the initialized ScriptEngine addGlobalApi(String, Supplier<Object>) globalApis Convenience overload when no engine back-reference is needed

ScriptEngineType.create(ScriptConsole console[, PackageRegistry packages]) executes in strict order: instantiate engine -> usePackageRegistry (if provided) -> build and setFeatures -> init(console) -> registerGlobal in registration order. If ScriptException or RuntimeException occurs, engine.close() is invoked and any cleanup exception is attached as suppressed. isAvailable() returns true only when loadingIssues is empty.

docs.title: ScriptEngineRegistry
docs.text:
lib.kasuga.scripting.ScriptEngineRegistry (@Singleton) indexes engines by ResourceLocation and language type strings:

  • register(ResourceLocation location, List<String> types, ScriptEngineType<?> engineType, int priority): records the exact location entry and pushes (location, priority) into a max-priority queue for every declared language string in types.
  • resolve(String requiredEngine, boolean allowLoadingIssueWhenNoEnginePresent):
  • If requiredEngine parses as a registered ResourceLocation, returns it directly (or null if allowLoadingIssueWhenNoEnginePresent == false and loadingIssues is non-empty).
  • Otherwise looks up the language queue by descending priority, returning the first engine with empty loadingIssues.
  • If all candidates have loadingIssues and allowLoadingIssueWhenNoEnginePresent == true, returns the first engine carrying issues for diagnostics; otherwise returns null.

docs.title: Legacy Pack Runtime vs. Managed Resource Entry
docs.text:
Two package execution paths exist:

  • Legacy pack runtime (ScriptingSystem + ScriptRuntime): @Context singleton ScriptingApplication registers ScriptingSystem as a ScopedResourceManagerConsumer on ResourceSystem. Each ScopedResourceManager (client server == null, or server MinecraftServer) owns a ScriptRuntime. onReloaded(...) serializes shutdown of the prior ScriptThreadGroup (observing a 5-second timeout warning without blocking game threads), scans ScopedPackResources, builds the ScriptPackage tree, and starts threads. ServerTickEvent.Pre and ClientTickEvent.Pre call ScriptRuntime.tick().
  • Managed resource entry (ManagedScriptEntryPoint): registered under ID "kasuga:script_blocks", accepting RESOURCE_RELOAD, CLIENT_STARTUP, SERVER_STARTUP and CLIENT, SERVER, NONE. Prepares an isolated ScriptBlockRegistry, PackageRegistry, and ScriptThreadGroup per generation, starting packages via ScriptPackage.startManaged(...) and exposing ScriptBlockHandle / ScriptTicket (see Unified Resource Platform and Script Tickets).

docs.title: Client and Dedicated-Server Error Handling
docs.text:
• Client (ScriptingClientApplication, @BeanOnlyIn.Client): listens to ClientResourceReloadFinishEvent. When PackageSystem.getMissingEngines() is non-empty, opens ScriptEngineMissingScreen (offers "Open Mods Folder", "Download" to https://ecosystem.kycraft.cn/search?keyword=...&platform=..., "Ignore and Continue(Dangerous!)" with ConfirmScreen, and "Quit"). When PackageSystem.getEngineErrors() is non-empty, opens ScriptEngineErrorScreen displaying engine exceptions and stack traces.
  • Dedicated server (ScriptingServerApplication, @BeanOnlyIn.DedicatedServer): implements Configurable and registers server config boolean ignore_scripting_errors (default false). On ServerResourceReloadFinishEvent, missing engines log a warning when ignore_scripting_errors is true or throw RuntimeException when false; non-empty engineErrors always log and throw RuntimeException.

docs.title: package.toml Schema
docs.text:
PackageSystem.readPackageInfo(ScopedPackResources spr, String packRelativeRoot) parses <packRelativeRoot>/package.toml (UTF-8) via NightConfig TomlParser into PackageInfo:

Key Java Type Required Description name @Nullable String Recommended Unique package name (e.g., "@test/scripting-test"); duplicate names throw DuplicatePackageException into loadingErrors engine String Required for runnable packages Engine language type (e.g., "javascript") or ResourceLocation string (e.g., "kasuga_lib_javet:javet") description String No Human-readable description version String No Package version string main String No Main entry resolved by require("<packageName>") (extensionless logical path, e.g., "index") workspaces String or List<String> No Sub-package workspace patterns (e.g., ["packages/*"] or ["./packages/*"]); scanned on HierarchicalScopedPackResources by stripping trailing /* and checking subdirectories for package.toml entry.common String or List<String> No Entry scripts executed on both client and server entry.server String or List<String> No Entry scripts executed only on the server side entry.client String or List<String> No Entry scripts executed only on the client side

Example (from external/slp/javet/src/main/resources/scripts/package.toml and packages/scripting-test/package.toml):

# scripts/package.toml (workspace root)
engine = "javascript"
workspaces = ["packages/*"]

# scripts/packages/scripting-test/package.toml
name = "@test/scripting-test"
engine = "javascript"
version = "1.0.0"
main = "index"

[entry]
client = ["index"]

docs.title: Discovery and Side Filtering
docs.text:
PackageSystem.scan(ScopedPackResources) probes scripts/package.toml, resolves its engine, registers it in PackageRegistry, and scans declared workspaces. Packs without package.toml are skipped. Diagnostics accumulate in loadingErrors, engineErrors, and engineMissing.

ScriptPackage.startInternal(...) filters [entry] differently depending on mode:

  • Legacy (ScriptPackage.start(ScriptThreadGroup)): filters by physical FMLEnvironment.dist (Dist.DEDICATED_SERVER runs common + server; Dist.CLIENT runs common + client). Integrated-server scripts that must also run in a physical client belong in entry.common under the legacy path, or should use managed mode below.
  • Managed (ScriptPackage.startManaged(..., LogicalSide side, ...)): filters by concrete LogicalSide (rejects LogicalSide.BOTH): SERVER runs common + server, CLIENT runs common + client. Attaches ScriptBlockRegistry.PackageSession (ring capacity 1024) and installs global ScriptBlocks plus optional Resources (ScriptVfsFacade).

docs.title: ScriptThreadGroup and ScriptThread
docs.text:
Each runnable package creates a child ScriptThreadGroup(groupName, parent) and an owning ScriptThread named Script-<packageName>-<entryName>.

Threading and queue invariants:

  • Engine creation, module loading, callbacks, tick(), and close() execute exclusively on the owning ScriptThread (ScriptThread.owns(ScriptEngine)).
  • recordCall(Runnable) enforces a bounded task queue of 4096 tasks, throwing RejectedExecutionException when full or closed.
  • Each wakeup iteration executes one pendingTasks item, drains all ScriptSubmissionRing instances via ring.drain(64, 2_000_000) (up to 64 requests / 2 ms budget), and runs engine.tick() when a tick signal is pending; otherwise parks in wait().
  • shutdown() closes all submission rings, interrupts the thread, runs registered onTermination(Runnable) hooks (such as unpinning ScriptFunction handles), calls engine.close(), and completes shutdownFuture.

docs.title: ModuleResolver, BuiltinModuleRegistry, and PackageRegistry
docs.text:
• lib.kasuga.scripting.module.ModuleResolver: declares locateScript(ResolvedPackage pkg, List<String> relativeSegments) and getExtension(), resolving segments into ResolvedScript(filePath, pack, ModuleId, owner).
  • lib.kasuga.scripting.module.BuiltinModuleRegistry (@Context):
  • register(String moduleName, Supplier<Object> supplier): registers shared global built-in modules.
  • registerFactory(ScriptModuleFactory<M> factory): registers per-engine ScriptModule factories (init(), tick(), close()); created automatically during JavetScriptEngine.init(...).
  • lib.kasuga.scripting.module.PackageRegistry (@Context): thread-safe map of name -> ResolvedPackage; rejects duplicates with DuplicatePackageException. Managed generations keep an isolated PackageRegistry in ScriptBlockRegistry.modulePackages().

docs.title: TimerModule and KasugaTimer
docs.text:
lib.kasuga.scripting.timer.TimerModule (TimerModule.FACTORY, name "kasuga:timer", registered by KasugaLibJavet) delegates to KasugaTimer (a PriorityQueue<CallbackEntry> tick scheduler):

@Api Method Signature Semantics and Units setInterval int setInterval(ScriptValue callback, int ms) Requires callback instanceof ScriptFunction (returns -1 otherwise); clones & pins via ScriptReference, repeating every Math.max(1, ms / 50) ticks (50 ms/tick) setTimeout int setTimeout(ScriptValue callback, int ms) Fires once after Math.max(1, ms / 50) ticks clearInterval void clearInterval(@Nullable Integer id) Unregisters timer id, unpins and closes its cloned ScriptFunction clearTimeout void clearTimeout(@Nullable Integer id) Delegates to clearInterval(id)

TimerModule.close() unpins and closes all active callbacks and clears KasugaTimer.

docs.title: Script FSM API (lib.kasuga.scripting.fsm)
docs.text: FsmApiRegistration.install(ScriptEngineType.Builder) registers "Animator" (AnimatorApi) and "AnimatorBuilder" (AnimatorBuilderApi) with back-references to the owning ScriptEngine. See State Machine and Animation Clip JSON Reference for the FSM JSON schema.

docs.title: Two-Tier Error Philosophy and Auto-Tick
docs.text:
• AnimatorBuilderApi (authoring / registration, fail-fast): throws IllegalArgumentException on invalid JSON/definitions, unknown definition IDs, or missing engine binding.
  • AnimatorApi (runtime control, never throws across the boundary): unknown handles, unknown var IDs, or wrong types log a warning once per key (256-entry LRU) and return inert defaults (null, false, 0, 0.0, "", -1, or empty arrays).
  • FsmAutoTickModule (FACTORY.name() == "kasuga:fsm_autotick"): per-engine ScriptModule that ticks registered scripting handles on the owning ScriptThread, honoring the FSM single-ticker invariant.

docs.title: AnimatorBuilderApi Methods
docs.text: Method Description String[] varTypes() Lists registered StateVarType tokens ("bool", "int", "float", "string", "vec3", plus any host-registered types) String registerStateVar(String namespace, String path, String type[, Object defaultValue[, boolean ephemeral]]) Registers a typed StateVar (ephemeral = true creates a tick-scoped trigger); returns "" on unknown type, or idempotent "namespace:path" void registerCondition(String namespace, String path, ScriptFunction guard) Registers a JS guard (clones & pins callback; passes ScriptFsmContext; evaluates truthiness via ScriptValues.isTrue; degrades exceptions to false). Java callers use the Predicate<StateContext<?>> overload void registerAction(String namespace, String path, ScriptFunction action) Registers a JS action (Java callers use Consumer<StateContext<?>>) String registerDefinition(ScriptValue definition) / (String json) Decodes a JS object literal or JSON string via StateMachineDefinition.CODEC into FsmDefinitions and returns the definition ID int instantiate(String id, Object owner[, Object model]) Creates a runtime StateMachine and returns an int handle (avoiding JS BigInt). Attaches ModelInstancePoseSink when model instanceof ModelInstance; logs a warning and runs sink-less otherwise

docs.title: AnimatorApi Methods
docs.text: Group Methods Inert Return Notes Typed vars get(int handle, String varId) / has(...) / set(..., Object value) null / false / no-op Resolves full "namespace:path" first, then unambiguous short name (no : or /, matching /<shortName>) Var discovery listVars(int handle) / declaredVars(int handle) / varType(String varId) [] / [] / "" listVars returns explicitly set vars; declaredVars returns all vars declared by the definition State reads getState(int handle, String layerId) / getStateElapsed(...) / getStateDuration(...) "" / 0 / -1 Active state ID, elapsed ticks, and configured duration ticks Layer properties getLayerMode(int handle, String layerId) / getLayerWeight(...) / isLayerLocked(...) "" / 0.0 / false BlendMode#serialName() ("base", "additive", "override"), weight, lock flag Clock & version getTick(int handle) / getVersion(int handle) 0.0 / 0 getTick returns double so JS receives a plain Number Triggers & jumps trigger(int handle, String triggerVarId) / isTriggered(...) / goTo(int handle, String layerId, String stateId) no-op / false / no-op trigger requires a boolean var; goTo takes effect on the next tick Lifecycle & tick tick(int handle) / tick(int handle, double dt) / dispose(int handle) no-op dispose removes the handle from FsmAutoTickModule and releases it Auto-tick autoTick(int handle, boolean on) / onTick(int handle, ScriptFunction) / onStateChanged(int handle, ScriptFunction) no-op onTick fires after each advance; onStateChanged fires only when machine.version() changes

docs.title: ScriptFsmContext and StateValueCoercer
docs.text:
JS guard/action callbacks receive ScriptFsmContext with @Api methods:

  • owner(): returns the owner object passed to instantiate (JS objects round-trip with live V8 object identity).
  • isClientSide(), stateElapsedTicks(), stateDurationTicks(), isLayerLocked().
  • get(String varId), has(String varId), set(String varId, Object value), trigger(String triggerId), isTriggered(String triggerId) (resolved by full ID via StateVarRegistry.resolve).

StateValueCoercer marshals script values: bool requires Boolean; int accepts Integer or finite integral Double; float widens Integer/Double/Float; string requires String; vec3 accepts Vector3f, 3-element List, or {x, y, z} Map (and boxes back to 3-element List<Float>); ResourceLocation converts from/to string.

docs.title: @Api Export and Security Model
docs.text:
lib.kasuga.scripting.security enforces member-level access checks on exported Java objects:

  • @Api (RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME):
  • boolean export() default true: excludes a public member when false.
  • Parameters[] parameters() default {}: key/value metadata (@Api.Parameters(name = "...", value = "...")) passed to conditions and callbacks.
  • Class<? extends SecurityCheckCondition>[] conditions() default {}: required condition classes checked before invocation or field access.
  • SecurityEngineFeature & SecurityEngineFeatureType.INSTANCE:
  • Each engine builds its own SecurityEngineFeature.
  • Conditions are registered by class on getConditionRegistry() (SecurityConditionRegistry; built-in AlwaysAllow). Missing condition classes fail closed (false).
