  • After all declared conditions pass, an optional SecurityCheckCallback (setSecurityCheckCallback) runs. Failure throws RuntimeException("Security check denied: " + name).

Note: @Api governs individual members on exposed Java objects, whereas package-level untrusted isolation is governed by ScriptSafetyCapabilities. Because JavetScriptEngine currently reports ScriptSafetyCapabilities.UNVERIFIED, ManagedScriptEntryPoint and ScriptBlockRegistry reject untrusted packs by default (see Unified Resource Platform and Script Tickets).

docs.title: KasugaLibJavet and JavetDownloader
docs.text:
KasugaLibJavet (@Mod("kasuga_lib_javet")):

  1. Registers JavetDownloader via JavetLibLoader.setLibLoadingListener.
  2. Loads the native V8 library via V8Host.getV8Instance().loadLibrary() and evaluates "1 + 1", recording any failure into ENGINE_RUNTIME_ISSUES.
  3. Upon KasugaLibStartupEvent, registers TimerModule.FACTORY and FsmAutoTickModule.FACTORY in BuiltinModuleRegistry, builds KasugaLibJavet.ENGINE_TYPE ("javascript", JsModuleResolver, SecurityEngineFeatureType.INSTANCE, FsmApiRegistration.install, ScriptingTestApi), and registers it in ScriptEngineRegistry under kasuga_lib_javet:javet with priority 0.

JavetDownloader extracts missing V8 natives into <gamePath>/native-libraries/javet/ (up to 3 attempts, reporting ModLoadingManager / ModLoadingProgress):

  1. Alibaba Cloud Mirror: https://maven.aliyun.com/repository/public/com/caoccao/javet/javet-{0}-{1}-{2}{3}/{4}/javet-{0}-{1}-{2}{3}-{4}.jar
  2. Maven Repository: https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/caoccao/javet/com/caoccao/javet/javet-{0}-{1}-{2}{3}/{4}/javet-{0}-{1}-{2}{3}-{4}.jar

Android and unsupported OS/architectures fail fast with a message recommending GraalJS mode. external/slp/javet/build.gradle explicitly places org.apache.httpcomponents:httpclient:4.5.13 on additionalRuntimeClasspath because KasugaLibJavet eagerly instantiates JavetDownloader at mod construction.

docs.title: JavetScriptEngine and FastJavetClassConverter
docs.text:
Each JavetScriptEngine owns an isolated V8Runtime:

  • Attaches KasugaJavetConsoleInterceptor forwarding console.* to ScriptConsole.
  • Logs unhandled promise rejections (event.getCode() == 0) to console.error.
  • Calls runtime.lowMemoryNotification() every 21 ticks (gcTicks++ > 20).
  • Wraps modules and entries in CommonJS function(require, exports, module) signatures; inserts a null placeholder in loadedModules before execution to break circular requires.

FastJavetClassConverter (with ClassAccessor, NativeProxyAccessor, MethodOverrideMap, ScriptConverter, V8ScriptFunctionProxy):

  • Java -> V8 (toV8Value): unwraps/clones JavetValue, ScriptValue (via ScriptConverter), and V8Value; delegates primitives/primitive arrays/BigInteger to JavetObjectConverter; proxies arbitrary Java objects by caching prototypes of @Api(export = true) public methods/fields (plus @FunctionalInterface abstract methods), tagging V8 proxies with "KasugaLib#Address" (WeakReference map + __nGCTracker__ + setWeak()).
  • V8 -> Java (toObject): resolves "KasugaLib#Address" back to live Java instances; wraps plain JS objects via JavetValueBridge.wrap(object.toClone()) to preserve object identity across callbacks. JavetValueBridge checks V8ValueArray before V8ValueObject so JS arrays arrive as JavetValueArray rather than string-keyed objects.
  • Per-arity overload dispatch (ClassAccessor + MethodOverrideMap): parameter slots typed as ScriptValue (or ScriptFunction, ScriptObject, ScriptArray, ScriptPrimitive) clear their converterMask bit so arguments use JavetValueBridge.wrap(...) instead of provider.toObject(...), allowing JS arrow functions to match ScriptFunction overloads directly.

docs.title: JsModuleResolver and PackageAwareRequireResolver
docs.text:
JavetScriptEngine resolves require(moduleName) in three stages:

  1. Per-engine ScriptModule instances (scriptModules, e.g., require("kasuga:timer").default).
  2. Global built-in suppliers in BuiltinModuleRegistry.resolve(moduleName) wrapped with "default" export in JavetModuleHandle.
  3. PackageAwareRequireResolver:
  4. By package name: PackageRegistry.lookup(moduleName) (scoped registry when configured, otherwise global bean) -> package main.
  5. Relative (./..., ../...): normalizes segments from fromSourcePath, rejecting any .. climbing past package root (null). Searches engine.getOwningPackage(fromSourcePath) first, then falls back to scanning packageRegistry.all() (iteration order is unspecified because PackageRegistry is backed by a HashMap and returns Map.copyOf(packages)).

JsModuleResolver.locateScript(...) independently splits and normalizes segments (rejecting path traversal) and probes <basePath>.js followed by <basePath>/index.js.

docs.title: Verification Commands
docs.text:
# Pure-JVM FSM scripting API tests (no NeoForge server launcher)
./gradlew :modules:scripting:scriptUnitTest

# Full scripting suite (package discovery & runtime via EphemeralTestServerProvider)
./gradlew :modules:scripting:test

# Javet V8 engine tests (security, converter, FSM assembly, Script Ticket integration)
./gradlew :external:slp:javet:test
./gradlew :external:slp:javet:test --tests '*ResourceScriptTicketIntegrationTest'

docs.title: Java Shader DSL
docs.text:
• The DSL does not parse a Java AST and does not decompile a lambda. A builder lambda runs immediately in Java and creates typed shader IR.

  • Java conditions and loops control only IR construction. The final shader does not contain these Java structures. Use the shader builder for conditions and loops that must stay dynamic in GLSL.

  • The backend inserts an expression from a Java variable at each use location. The expression does not automatically create a GLSL local variable.

  • A let* call creates an initialized GLSL local variable. For later assignments, use a local* call that returns ShaderVariable.

  • A fullscreen program contains only a fragment module and uses the built-in fullscreen vertex stage.

  • A graphics program contains a vertex module and a fragment module. position(...) writes to gl_Position.

  • Each fragment input must have a vertex output with the same name and type. Otherwise, program construction fails.

  • A uniform or sampler with the same name in both stages must have an identical declaration. An identical declaration occurs only one time in the Minecraft shader JSON.

  • A program ID must use the lowercase namespace:path resource-ID format.

  • The current profile supports float, int, bool, vec2, vec3, vec4, mat2, mat3, mat4, and sampler2D. The profile also supports float uniform arrays and named structs. The profile supports stage inputs and outputs, local variables, structured control flow, common mathematical operations, and texture sampling.

  • The current backend generates GLSL 150 and Minecraft core-shader JSON.

  • During loading, a runtime-generated bundle has priority for its own .vsh, .fsh, and .json files. For a missing resource or import, loading uses the current client ResourceProvider.

  • The DSL checks the stage interface of a graphics program during Java construction. The caller must match the RenderShaderDescriptor vertex format to the attributes.

docs.title: GraalJS Scripting
docs.text:
The optional :modules:shader-graal module provides lib.kasuga.shader.graal.GraalShaderCompiler. It uses GraalJS Community 24.1.2 on Java 21 to call the Java DSL directly and return the same ShaderProgram type. The module declares its Graal Maven dependencies; the main library does not include it automatically.

dependencies {
    implementation project(':modules:shader-graal')
}

For example, screen-tint.js:

const tintParameter = ShaderParameter.builder(
    "Tint", "Screen tint", ShaderParameterType.COLOR_RGB
).range(0, 1).defaultValues(1, 0.5, 0.25).build();

Shader.fullscreen("example:script_tint", shader => {
    const tint = shader.exposeVec3(tintParameter);
    const source = shader.sampler2D("SceneSampler").sample(shader.texCoord());
    shader.fragmentColor(shader.vec4(source.rgb().mul(tint), source.a()));
});

The host reads a UTF-8 file or supplies a diagnostic name and source text:

import lib.kasuga.shader.ShaderProgram;
import lib.kasuga.shader.graal.GraalShaderCompiler;
import java.nio.file.Path;

GraalShaderCompiler compiler = new GraalShaderCompiler();
ShaderProgram program = compiler.compile(Path.of("shaders/screen-tint.js"));
// Or compiler.compile("screen-tint.js", scriptText)

Pass program to RenderShaderDescriptor.generated(program) for registration, or to ShaderResourceCompiler.compile(List.of(program), outputDirectory) to write .vsh, .fsh, and .json resources. The caller owns source discovery, recompilation timing, and installing the replacement program. This entry point does not scan resource packs or register a general-purpose ScriptEngine.

Script global Java type Shader lib.kasuga.shader.ShaderProgram, including fullscreen / graphics ShaderParameter Parameter factories and builder ShaderParameterType Parameter type enum ShaderStructType Named struct builder ShaderType Basic shader type enum

Builders, expressions, variables, and struct fields use their Java method names and type constraints. JavaScript arrow functions map to Consumer / Runnable, including nested callbacks for forRange, ifThenElse, whileLoop, doWhile, and switchOn. Vectors, matrices, arrays, exposed parameters, and stage linking use the existing DSL.

Scripts can insert inline GLSL with shader.rawDeclaration(...), rawStatement(...), rawFloat(...), and related methods. The host can also explicitly supply named snippets or UTF-8 files:

import java.util.Map;

ShaderProgram program = compiler.compileWithGlslFiles(
        Path.of("shaders/effect.js"), Map.of("helpers", Path.of("shaders/helpers.glsl")));
// Or compiler.compile("effect.js", scriptText, Map.of("helpers", glslText))

Shader.fullscreen("example:custom", shader => {
    shader.rawDeclaration(glsl("helpers"));
    const transform = shader.mat2(1, 0, 0, 1); // column-major
    shader.letVec2("uv", transform.transform(shader.texCoord()));
    shader.fragmentColor(shader.vec4(shader.rawVec3("customColor(uv)"), shader.f32(1)));
});

glsl(name) can only retrieve host-provided content, not read arbitrary paths. Unknown names fail at the script location, and file read failures throw IOException. Files must contain snippets appropriate to the insertion point, not complete shaders replacing generated main, #version, or resource metadata. Raw GLSL bypasses DSL validation and must be trusted. Matrices also support mat3, mat4, uniformMat*, and localMat*.

JavaScript numbers passed to float parameters use Java float rounding, so values such as 0.1, 1.35, and Math.sin(...) work directly. Values passed to int parameters must still be integers within range. Existing DSL checks for non-finite numbers remain in effect.

The final script expression must evaluate to one ShaderProgram. Top-level return, ES module import / export, and Node.js require are outside this script entry point. JavaScript if, for, and operators execute during construction. Use .add(), .mul(), .lt(), and builder control flow to generate shader arithmetic and dynamic control flow.

Each call creates and closes an independent Graal context. The returned IR has no JavaScript dependencies and remains usable for resource generation. Compiler instances can be shared between threads. Compile definitions outside per-frame drawing callbacks. File failures throw IOException; script, DSL validation, and budget failures throw ShaderScriptException, with sourceName(), line(), column(), and the original cause. Lines and columns are one-based, or zero when unavailable.

The default budget is 1,000,000 executed JavaScript statements per compilation, including a few statements that initialize the globals. Use new GraalShaderCompiler(statementLimit) to set a positive budget. Contexts expose only the listed DSL types and members, with no arbitrary host class access, reflection, file I/O, thread creation, or native access. This construction-time statement budget does not provide a wall-clock, memory, or process isolation boundary. The existing raw* GLSL methods remain available for trusted shader definitions.

The bridge uses the official Graal Java interoperability and HostAccess APIs. Verify it with:

./gradlew :modules:shader-graal:check :modules:shader-graal:assemble :modules:shader:test

The real-client regression compiles the original screen-tint.js once and installs its generated shader through the existing registry. Prepare an isolated client directory with a copy of an existing test world, then run:

./gradlew :modules:modelling:runClientHeadless \
  -PkasugaTestGraalShader=true \
  -PkasugaClientDirectory=/absolute/path/to/isolated-client \
  -PkasugaQuickPlayWorld=existing-test-world

The test dispatches real mouse click, drag, and release events through ShaderParameterScreen, adjusts RGB, and clicks reset. It checks GPU pixels from the world and a translucent probe, parameter values, uploaded uniforms, program ID, and generation. Success logs GRAAL_SHADER_CLIENT_SMOKE_PASS and exits. Check passed in debug/graal-shader/report.json: a normal client shutdown after a failed assertion can still make Gradle report success. This directory also contains the three generated resources and PNGs for the default, neutral, blue, reset, and parameter-editor states. The opt-in flag adds Graal to that development run only, without a modelling main-library dependency.

On 2026-11-04, Apple M3 Max, Java 21.0.3, Minecraft 1.21.1 / NeoForge 21.1.203, and Iris 1.8.12 + Sodium 0.6.13 with no shader pack enabled passed this test. All four parameter states had zero maximum channel error across the 1920×1080 world image and 32×16 translucent probe, unchanged alpha, and stable GPU program and generation. The run also exposed and fixed NeoForge scanning a Graal aggregator POM as a jar, and reset buttons retaining their initial enabled state after slider changes. This record does not cover active shader packs, other platforms, or other Minecraft versions.

docs.title: User-Adjustable Shader Parameters
docs.text:
For runnable source code, typed IR, GLSL/JSON outputs, and a gameplay video demo, see the Prism Scan Polyglot Example. The example executes GraalJS, Kotlin/JVM, and Python/JPype hosts and compares every generated output file.

A shader does not expose all uniforms automatically. Register each user-adjustable parameter. Each parameter has a fixed name, description, ShaderParameterType, inclusive range, and defaultValues. The parameter name is also the GLSL uniform name. The name must be a valid, non-reserved GLSL identifier.

public static final ShaderParameter EXPOSURE = ShaderParameter.floatParameter(
        "Exposure",
        "Controls the final output exposure",
        1.0f,  // default
        0.0f,  // minimum
        4.0f   // maximum
);

public static final ShaderParameter TINT = ShaderParameter.builder(
                "Tint",
                "Multiplies the output color",
                ShaderParameterType.COLOR_RGB
        )
        .range(0.0, 1.0)
        .defaultValues(1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f)
        .build();

In a generated shader, use the applicable expose* call to declare a uniform and register the parameter specification. A uniform* call keeps the uniform internal. The call does not add the uniform to the public schema.

ShaderProgram program = ShaderProgram.fullscreen("example:adjustable", shader -> {
    FloatExpr exposure = shader.exposeFloat(EXPOSURE);
    Vec3Expr tint = shader.exposeVec3(TINT);
    Vec3Expr color = shader.sampler2D("SceneSampler").sample(shader.texCoord()).rgb();
    shader.fragmentColor(shader.vec4(color.mul(tint).mul(exposure), shader.f32(1.0f)));
});

A resource shader or custom factory cannot use the DSL. Register the same specification on RenderShaderDescriptor. The resource uniform must match the parameter name and basic GLSL type. The first bind fails if the uniform is missing.

RenderShaderDescriptor descriptor = RenderShaderDescriptor.builder(id, format)
        .resource()
        .expose(EXPOSURE)
        .expose(TINT)
        .build();

RenderShaderHandle.parameters() supplies the default runtime parameter block for the registration. ShaderParameterBlock validates each change for component count, numeric type, finite values, and range. A parameter change does not regenerate or compile the shader. reset(name) uses the declared default. resetAll() restores all declared defaults.

RenderShaderHandle handle = registration.handle();
handle.parameters().setFloat(EXPOSURE, 1.35f);
handle.parameters().set(TINT, 1.0, 0.55, 0.2);

When a fullscreen method receives a handle, Kasuga uploads the default parameter block before the draw. The applicable methods are PostProcessContext.fullscreen(...) and PostProcessGraphContext.fullscreen(...). Kasuga cannot infer a registration from a direct ShaderInstance. Use .parameters(block) to bind a parameter block. Use handle.createParameterBlock() for each independent configuration of one shader.

The current ShaderParameterType values include float, integer, boolean, vec2, vec3, vec4, RGB color, and RGBA color. ShaderParameterType also includes mat2, mat3, and mat4. The range applies to all components. Boolean parameters always use [0, 1].

For floating-point parameters, values and range endpoints are compared after rounding to 32-bit shader floats, matching runtime storage. Integer and boolean ranges retain exact integer semantics.

To open the parameter panel:

  1. Enter /kasuga_effects in the client.
  2. Select Parameters.

The schema generates the parameter panel. The panel is not specific to one effect. The panel shows each shader that exposes parameters. A boolean parameter uses a switch. Other parameter types use component sliders.

Vectors, colors, and matrices use the applicable component names. A parameter change applies during the next draw. The change does not regenerate or recompile the shader.

Kasuga saves the default parameter blocks asynchronously in config/kasuga_lib/shader-parameters.json. After a client restart, Kasuga restores values by shader ID and parameter name. An independent block from createParameterBlock() contains effect-instance state. Kasuga does not store this block in the global configuration.

The configuration stores only values that override schema defaults. A reset permits a later schema default to apply. Use isDefault(name) and hasOverrides() to examine the current state.

The following client commands examine, change, and reset exposed shader parameters. Use a command when a slider cannot set a large integer accurately. Also use a command to enter a complete vector or matrix:

/kasuga_effects parameter list <shader-id>
/kasuga_effects parameter set <shader-id> <name> <value...>
/kasuga_effects parameter reset <shader-id> <name>

Spaces or commas separate vector and matrix components. The built-in black-hole example exposes LensingScale, DiskBrightness, and ChromaticScale. The screen, time, and per-effect packed uniforms stay internal.

The following example builds and registers a fullscreen shader from Java expressions:

ShaderProgram program = ShaderProgram.fullscreen("example:screen_tint", shader -> {
    var scene = shader.sampler2D("SceneSampler");
    var tint = shader.uniformVec3("Tint", 1.0f, 1.0f, 1.0f);
    var source = scene.sample(shader.texCoord());
    shader.fragmentColor(shader.vec4(source.rgb().mul(tint), source.a()));
});

ShaderRegistration shader = pipelines.shader(
        RenderShaderDescriptor.generated(program)
                .withPreload(ShaderPreloadPolicy.DEFERRED, 50)
);

shader.whenReady().thenAccept(status -> rebuildDependentResources(shader.handle()));

docs.title: Migration from GLSL to the Java Shader DSL
docs.text: A builder lambda represents the body of the GLSL main() function. The lambda does not calculate pixel results. The lambda records declarations, expressions, and statements in call order. The backend then generates GLSL 150.

docs.title: Types and Expressions
docs.text:
The Java DSL uses expression-wrapper types in place of GLSL operators. Use var for an intermediate expression when the expression type is clear. The Java compiler checks the exact type.

GLSL Java DSL float, int, bool FloatExpr, IntExpr, BoolExpr vec2, vec3, vec4 Vec2Expr, Vec3Expr, Vec4Expr mat2, mat3, mat4 Mat2Expr, Mat3Expr, Mat4Expr sampler2D Sampler2DExpr struct Material ShaderStructType, StructExpr 1.0, 1, true shader.f32(1), shader.i32(1), shader.bool(true) vec2(x, y) shader.vec2(x, y) vec4(rgb, alpha) shader.vec4(rgb, alpha) a + b, a - b a.add(b), a.sub(b) a * b, a / b a.mul(b), a.div(b) a < b, a >= b, a == b a.lt(b), a.gte(b), a.equalTo(b) a && b, a || b, !a a.and(b), a.or(b), a.not() texture(image, uv) image.sample(uv) normalize(v), length(v) v.normalize(), v.length() mix(x, y, t) x.mix(y, t) atan(y, x) y.atan2(x) matrix * vector matrix.transform(vector) left * right (matrix) left.mul(right) value.rgb, value.a value.rgb(), value.a() Values[index] values.get(index) float(integer) integer.toFloat()

Only a method from the applicable Expr type can generate code. For example, the current Vec2Expr supplies normalize(). Other vector wrappers do not always supply the same method. If an expression does not accept a Java number, use f32(), i32(), or an applicable primitive overload.

docs.title: Globals, Stage Inputs, and Stage Outputs
docs.text:
• uniformFloat, uniformInt, uniformBool, uniformVec*, and uniformMat* declare GLSL uniforms. Supplied values become defaults in the Minecraft shader JSON. A matrix overload without a default uses an identity matrix.

  • uniformFloatArray is the only current method for uniform arrays. The length must be greater than 1. Use an IntExpr to index an element.

  • sampler2D declares uniform sampler2D.

  • inputFloat, inputInt, and inputVec* declare in values for the current stage.

  • In a vertex stage, outputFloat and outputVec* declare out values. position(...) writes to gl_Position.

  • In a fragment stage, fragmentColor(...) writes to the generated fragColor.

  • A fullscreen fragment can use texCoord() to read the texture coordinates from the built-in vertex stage.

  • A graphics fragment must use a method such as inputVec2 to declare the fragment inputs. A call to texCoord() fails.

  • A vertex program must call position(...) at least one time. A fragment program must call fragmentColor(...) at least one time. Validation only confirms that the IR contains a write. The shader author must write to the required output on all runtime paths.

The two stages in a graphics program represent the .vsh and .fsh files:

ShaderProgram particle = ShaderProgram.graphics(
        "example:particle",
        vertex -> {
            var position = vertex.inputVec3("Position");
            var uv = vertex.inputVec2("UV0");
            var color = vertex.inputVec4("Color");
            var modelView = vertex.uniformMat4("ModelViewMat");
            var projection = vertex.uniformMat4("ProjMat");

            vertex.outputVec2("particleUv", uv);
            vertex.outputVec4("particleColor", color);
            vertex.position(projection.transform(modelView.transform(
                    vertex.vec4(position, vertex.f32(1))
            )));
        },
        fragment -> {
            var uv = fragment.inputVec2("particleUv");
            var color = fragment.inputVec4("particleColor");
            var radial = fragment.f32(1).sub(
                    uv.sub(fragment.vec2(0.5f, 0.5f)).length().mul(2).min(1)
            );
            fragment.fragmentColor(fragment.vec4(
                    color.rgb().mul(radial), color.a().mul(radial)
            ));
        }
);

RenderShaderDescriptor descriptor = RenderShaderDescriptor.generated(
        particle,
        DefaultVertexFormat.POSITION_TEX_COLOR
);

The Position, UV0, and Color input names and types must match the supplied Minecraft VertexFormat. The DSL checks the vertex-to-fragment interface, but it does not check the VertexFormat.

docs.title: Local Variables and Control Flow
docs.text:
A Java variable holds one IR expression. In this example, brightness does not create a GLSL local variable. The backend inserts the brightness expression at the use location:

var brightness = color.rgb().mul(intensity);
shader.fragmentColor(shader.vec4(brightness, color.a()));

letFloat/letVec*, letMat*, and letStruct create GLSL local variables that are read-only in the DSL. For later assignments, use the applicable local* method. get() reads the variable. set() writes the variable.

This GLSL:

float sum = 0.0;
for (int index = 0; index < Count; ++index) {
    if (index >= 8) break;
    if (Values[index] <= 0.0) continue;
    sum = sum + Values[index];
}
fragColor = vec4(sum, sum, sum, 1.0);

The equivalent Java DSL is:

var count = shader.uniformInt("Count", 0);
var values = shader.uniformFloatArray("Values", 8, 0.0f);
var sum = shader.localFloat("sum", shader.f32(0));

shader.forRange("index", shader.i32(0), count, index -> {
    shader.ifThen(index.gte(shader.i32(8)), shader::breakLoop);
    shader.ifThen(values.get(index).lte(shader.f32(0)), shader::continueLoop);
    sum.set(sum.get().add(values.get(index)));
});

shader.fragmentColor(shader.vec4(sum.get(), sum.get(), sum.get(), shader.f32(1)));

  • ifThen and ifThenElse generate shader branches. A Java if runs one time during IR construction.

  • forRange(name, start, end, body) generates an integer loop. The loop increments by 1 and uses < end as the end condition.

  • whileLoop(condition, body) generates while. doWhile(condition, body) generates do while.

  • breakLoop() can exit only the innermost loop. You can use continueLoop() in a loop.

  • A Java for can unroll an expression for constant values. The Java loop does not generate a GLSL loop.

  • If a shader value changes across branches or loops in a Java lambda, use ShaderVariable. Do not rebind a Java local variable to represent a shader assignment.

var cursor = shader.localInt("cursor", shader.i32(0));

shader.whileLoop(cursor.get().lt(count), () -> {
    cursor.set(cursor.get().add(1));
    shader.ifThen(cursor.get().gte(shader.i32(64)), shader::breakLoop);
});

shader.doWhile(cursor.get().gt(shader.i32(0)), () ->
        cursor.set(cursor.get().sub(shader.i32(1)))
);

docs.title: Structs
docs.text:
A struct is a named type. The ShaderStructType.Builder that creates a field owns the field key. You cannot use the field key with a different struct. This restriction applies when the other struct has a field with the same name and type.

Declare a dependency struct before you declare the struct that contains the dependency. The current DSL supports structs for typed locals, construction, field reads, and field assignments. The DSL does not support structs for uniforms, stage inputs, or stage outputs.

var materialBuilder = ShaderStructType.builder("Material");
var tint = materialBuilder.vec3Field("tint");
var roughness = materialBuilder.floatField("roughness");
var materialType = materialBuilder.build();

shader.declareStruct(materialType);
var material = shader.localStruct("material", shader.structValue(
        materialType,
        shader.vec3(1.0f, 0.8f, 0.6f),
        shader.f32(0.5f)
));

shader.setStructField(material, roughness, shader.f32(0.25f));
var finalTint = material.get().field(tint);

structValue arguments must follow the order of field declarations. The builder checks the argument count and types during Java construction.

docs.title: Switch Statements
docs.text:
switchOn accepts an IntExpr. caseOf keeps declaration order and does not insert break. Therefore, caseOf permits GLSL fallthrough. Call breakSwitch() to end a case. The generated output puts defaultCase after all cases.

shader.switchOn(mode, cases -> cases
        .caseOf(0, () -> {
            intensity.set(shader.f32(0.25f));
            shader.breakSwitch();
        })
        .caseOf(1, () -> intensity.set(shader.f32(0.75f))) // fallthrough
        .defaultCase(() -> intensity.set(shader.f32(1.0f)))
);

For breakLoop() and breakSwitch(), the applicable structure must be the innermost break target. This rule prevents an invalid bare break. A case in a loop can call breakSwitch(). The case cannot call breakLoop() directly. To exit the outer loop, set a boolean local variable. Test the variable after the switch.

docs.title: Naming and Link Rules
docs.text:
• A shader program ID must use lowercase namespace:path.

  • A shader identifier must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*. It must not start with gl_, and it must not be a reserved GLSL word.

  • Globals, locals, and loop indexes in one stage share one name set. A name cannot occur more than one time in the complete stage. Separate code blocks do not create reusable name scopes.

  • A fragment input must have a vertex output with the same name and type. A vertex can have additional outputs that the fragment does not read.

  • If both stages use a uniform or sampler with the same name, its storage, type, array length, and default value must be identical.

  • Names are case-sensitive. The final GLSL and Minecraft JSON use these names without changes.

docs.title: Runtime Uniforms and Samplers
docs.text:
F3+T replaces the current ShaderInstance. For a long-life object:

  1. Store only a RenderShaderHandle.

  2. During each render, access the current generation through the handle or pass context.

  3. On the render thread, update a uniform through currentShader.safeGetUniform(name).set(...).

  4. In a fullscreen pass, use colorSampler, depthSampler, or textureSampler to bind a sampler.

To upload a float array:

  1. Set the float[] capacity to the length in the shader declaration.

  2. Upload the complete float[].

  3. A uniform default in the DSL generates a JSON default. It does not overwrite a current value that Java uploads each frame.

context.fullscreen(PostProcessGraphTarget.main(), shaderHandle)
        .colorSampler("SceneSampler", context.read(scene))
        .uniforms(active -> active.safeGetUniform("Tint").set(red, green, blue))
        .draw(false);

docs.title: Raw GLSL Escape
docs.text:
Use a raw escape for GLSL that the typed API cannot represent. All raw entry points have @DelicateShaderApi. This annotation identifies code for additional review. The annotation does not guarantee API stability. The Java compiler does not validate raw GLSL.

@DelicateShaderApi
static ShaderProgram derivativeShader() {
    return ShaderProgram.fullscreen("example:derivative", shader -> {
        shader.rawPreamble("#extension GL_ARB_gpu_shader5 : enable");
        shader.rawDeclaration("""
                float saturate(float value) {
                    return clamp(value, 0.0, 1.0);
                }
                """);

        var edge = shader.rawFloat("dFdx(texCoord.x)");
        shader.rawStatement("if (edge < 0.0) discard;");
        shader.fragmentColor(shader.vec4(edge, edge, edge, shader.f32(1.0f)));
    });
}

  • rawPreamble inserts text after #version 150. Use it for extensions and macros.

  • rawDeclaration inserts text after globals and before main(). Use it for user functions and backend-specific declarations.

  • rawStatement copies the statement text into the current block. The method does not parse or change the text.

  • rawFloat, rawInt, rawBool, rawVec*, rawMat*, and rawStruct wrap source text in caller-declared expression types.

The raw API rejects only empty strings. The raw API does not parse source text. The raw API does not track types, identifiers, uniforms, stage interfaces, or control flow. The caller is responsible for the declared type of a raw expression. The caller is also responsible for raw-uniform JSON entries and GLSL driver support. Use the typed API when the typed API supports the required feature.

The typed API does not currently supply user functions, struct uniforms, struct stage inputs, or struct stage outputs. The typed API also excludes non-float uniform arrays, arbitrary swizzles, discard, derivatives, and advanced texture sampling. A raw escape can supply these features. A resource shader or custom factory can also supply these features. Extend the typed IR and backend for cross-backend support, link validation, or a long-life public API. Do not use a raw string as a permanent interface.

docs.title: Gradle Shader Generation
docs.text:
plugins {
    id 'builder.kasuga.shader'
}

  • The builder.kasuga.shader plugin creates the shader source set. The plugin reads src/shader/java and src/shader/resources. The plugin also adds the shader DSL dependency.

  • generateKasugaShaders runs before processResources. The task first clears the generated-output directory. The task then runs the shader providers.

  • A provider must be a non-abstract public class that implements ShaderProgramProvider. The provider must have a public no-argument constructor. The generation task fails if the provider does not meet these conditions.

  • The task sorts providers by class name before execution. The task converts each returned program to .vsh, .fsh, and .json resources.

  • If two programs generate the same path, the task fails. The task does not overwrite generated output.

  • The plugin adds the generated directory to the main resources. Therefore, the final JAR contains the generated content.

Other pages of this topic: Custom Rendering Specification and Managed Effects and Post-Processing.

docs.title: Sidedness Model
docs.text: This page documents physical side detection (Dist / @BeanOnlyIn), logical side contracts (LogicalSide / Level.isClientSide), Mixin sidedness and ABI gating, resource/script routing sides, and the subsystem sidedness matrix in KasugaLibNext.

docs.title: 1. Physical Side Detection and Micronaut Conditional Beans
1.1 Envs Utilities
docs.text:
modules/inject provides two environment helpers:

  • lib.kasuga.inject.class_loader.Envs (safe when FMLLoader.getDist() == null, suitable for plain JVM tests):
  • isDevEnvironment(): !FMLLoader.isProduction()
  • isClient(): dist != null && dist.isClient()
  • isDedicatedServer(): dist != null && dist.isDedicatedServer()
  • lib.kasuga.inject.Envs: delegates directly to FMLLoader.getDist().isClient() and isDedicatedServer() without a null check on dist.

docs.title: 1.2 @BeanOnlyIn and MinecraftDist
docs.text:
lib.kasuga.inject.class_loader.BeanOnlyIn uses Micronaut @Requires(condition = ...) to restrict bean activation:

Annotation Condition (MinecraftDist) Active When Representative Beans @BeanOnlyIn.Client MinecraftDist.IsClient Envs.isClient() KasugaLibClientApplication, ClientRenderingRegistry, DefaultClientRegisterContextDispatchers, WeatherFilterConfig, ScriptingClientApplication, ClientCreateRegistrationBridge, ClientBogeyRendererRegistry @BeanOnlyIn.DedicatedServer MinecraftDist.IsDedicatedServer Envs.isDedicatedServer() ScriptingServerApplication @BeanOnlyIn.Development MinecraftDist.IsDevelopment Envs.isDevEnvironment() Dev-only beans @BeanOnlyIn.Never MinecraftDist.Never Always false Disabled beans @CreateModBeans (lib.kasuga.create) IfCreateModLoaded ModList.get() != null && ModList.get().isLoaded("create") CreateApplication, CreateConfig, CreateRegistrationDispatcher, ClientCreateRegistrationBridge, ClientBogeyRendererRegistry

MinecraftDist.ModLoaded is an abstract Condition checking ModList.get().isLoaded(getModId()) for optional mod integrations.

docs.title: Replacing Common Fallback Beans on the Client
docs.text: DefaultRenderingRegistry (@Singleton) acts as the server-side no-op fallback (logs at DEBUG and skips renderer registration). ClientRenderingRegistry is annotated with @Singleton, @Replaces(DefaultRenderingRegistry.class), and @BeanOnlyIn.Client, so on physical clients Micronaut replaces the default bean and performs actual BlockEntityRenderer, EntityRenderer, and DocumentComponentRenderer registration.

docs.title: 2.1 RegisterContextRegistry.Side
docs.text:
lib.kasuga.registration.core.RegisterContextRegistry.Side defines two registration sides:

  • COMMON: activated by KasugaLibApplication via registry.register(modEventBus), dispatching NEW_REGISTRY, CreateRegistrationStages.PREPARE, REGISTER_EVENT, REGISTER_CAPABILITIES, PAYLOAD_REGISTRATION, and CREATIVE_TAB_CONTENT_REGISTRATION.
  • CLIENT: activated by KasugaLibClientApplication (@BeanOnlyIn.Client) via registry.registerClient(modEventBus), dispatching MENU_SCREEN_BINDING, REGISTER_CLIENT_EXTENSIONS, and BAKING_COMPLETE on the physical client only.

In the Create integration, CreateRegistrationDispatcher runs on Side.COMMON and looks up CreateClientBridge as a Registry attachment: ClientCreateRegistrationBridge installs the client implementation on Side.CLIENT (handling PartialModel, TrackModel, and BogeyStyle.SizeRenderer), whereas dedicated servers fall back to CreateClientBridge.noop().

docs.title: 2.2 Mixin Sidedness and Bytecode ABI Gating
docs.text: Mixin Config Plugin Class Sidedness & Gating Behavior kasuga_lib.mixins.json lib.kasuga.mixins.KasugaLibMixinPlugin (extends ServiceMixinPlugin) Checks for lib/kasuga/mixins/modelling/PeelShaderLoaderMixin.class: when Side != CLIENT, loads only 3 common/server modelling mixins (CameraChunkServerMixin, CameraEntityDataAccessor, ModelCollisionLevelMixin); when Side == CLIENT, loads the full client world-view, headless, and weather mixin set kasuga_lib_create.mixins.json lib.kasuga.create.compat.CreateMixinPlugin "mixins" applies on both sides; "client" applies on client only (and inspects BezierConnection.getBakedSegments bytecode to choose between BezierConnectionMixin and ModernBezierSegmentsMixin / ModernBezierGirdersMixin) kasuga_lib_iris.mixins.json ("required": false) lib.kasuga.compat.iris.IrisCameraMixinPlugin Returns an empty list unless MixinEnvironment.Side.CLIENT and all Iris + Sodium bytecode ABI checks pass (with an independent gate for WorldViewIrisCloudMixin)

docs.title: 3. Logical Side (LogicalSide), State Callbacks, and Script Entry Points
docs.text: Physical sides and logical sides (singleplayer integrated server vs. client world) differ across resource routing, block-state callbacks, and script execution:

docs.title: 3.1 LogicalSide and ResourceRouting
docs.text:
lib.kasuga.core.resource.lifecycle.LogicalSide defines CLIENT, SERVER, BOTH, and NONE:

  • ResourceRouting.route(catalog, event, side) requires a concrete invocation side (LogicalSide.BOTH throws IllegalArgumentException).
  • Output validation rejects impossible combinations: CLIENT_STARTUP cannot target SERVER or BOTH; SERVER_STARTUP cannot target CLIENT or BOTH.
  • ResourceCoordinator passes context.neutral() to LogicalSide.NONE entry points and forbids mixing NONE and game-side outputs in one entry point invocation.
  • ManagedScriptEntryPoint and ScriptBlockRegistry also reject LogicalSide.BOTH, and ScriptBlockRegistry.bind(ref, context) requires context.side() == side && ref.side() == side (client and server script blocks never cross-bind).

docs.title: 3.2 ScriptPackage.start (Legacy Physical Dist) vs. ScriptPackage.startManaged (Managed Logical Side)
docs.text:
package.toml declares server, client, and common entry arrays under [entry], filtered differently by the two startup paths:

  • Legacy ScriptPackage.start(ScriptThreadGroup) (used by ScriptRuntime): filters by physical FMLEnvironment.dist (entry.server runs only on Dist.DEDICATED_SERVER, entry.client only on Dist.CLIENT, and entry.common on both). Integrated-server logic in legacy packages must therefore be placed in entry.common.
  • Managed ScriptPackage.startManaged(...) (used by ManagedScriptEntryPoint): filters by logical LogicalSide (LogicalSide.SERVER runs common + server; LogicalSide.CLIENT runs common + client).

docs.title: 3.3 StateProperty.Side and Saved<T>
docs.text:
• lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.state.StateProperty:
  • set(ServerLevel, BlockPos, T, int) asserts level.getServer().isSameThread() and writes only on the server thread.
  • onChange(Side, Consumer<Change<T>>) supports Side.SERVER (default), Side.CLIENT, and Side.BOTH, matching level.isClientSide.
  • lib.kasuga.inject.auto_configure.Saved<T>: provided by SavedFactory, bound on ServerStartedEvent, and cleared on ServerStoppingEvent; calling get() before server start or without a server context throws IllegalStateException("The level is not loaded yet.").

docs.title: 4. Module and API Sidedness Matrix
docs.text: Category Modules / APIs Allowed Side Notes Pure JVM / Graphics-Independent modules/utils, modules/formula, modules/data-driven pipeline (DataDrivenBuildPipeline), modules/render-core (ModelInstance.forSimulation, ModelTickLoop, SkeletonRagdoll, ProxyRuntime) Both + offline tests Physics requires native Box3D (NativeBox3D.availableOrWarn()); no Minecraft or OpenGL dependency Common Registration, VFS & Networking KasugaLib, Registry / Reg, ResourceSystem, VirtualFileSystem, RpcSessionManager, DeviceRegistries, DocumentComponentRegistries Both (COMMON) Client and server maintain separate ScopedResourceManager instances Server / Dedicated-Server Only Saved / SavedFactory, ServerCollisionModels, ScriptingServerApplication Logical server / dedicated server ScriptingServerApplication is annotated @BeanOnlyIn.DedicatedServer Client-Only Rendering & Output modules/render-opengl, modules/iris-compat, Constants, PipelineRegistry, MCBackend, EffectRenderPipeline, RenderShaderRegistry, WorldRenderPipelineRegistry, PostProcessGraphRegistry, MinecraftWorldViews, MinecraftFrameOutputs, ItemModelRenderers, ModelParticleRuntime, ModelLightRuntime, ClientBlockUpdateHooks, HeadlessClient, ScriptingClientApplication, ClientBogeyRendererRegistry Physical client only (GPU calls on render thread) Loading client rendering classes on a dedicated server fails due to client/OpenGL types; HeadlessClient still runs as a full physical client

docs.title: Skeleton Dynamics API Reference
docs.text: This page covers the generic skeleton dynamics interfaces in render-core. Data conversion happens at the model construction stage; at runtime, instances are controlled by IK chain name. Algorithms and ownership are documented in the concept document. The underlying world, forces, collision, active ragdoll, and Minecraft integration are covered in Physics API; format manifest/profile are covered in MMD/glTF configuration.

docs.title: Types and Packages
Lifecycle and Units
docs.text:
1. Load the Model; the configureSkeleton(Skeleton) hook of format metadata runs during Model construction.
  2. Create a dynamics Builder from the Skeleton, append or override definitions, then attach().
  3. Create a ModelInstance; set targets, tick loop modules, and physics.
  4. Evaluate through the instance's pose pipeline; on disposal, close the ModelInstance or detach physics.

Dynamics configuration should be completed before creating instances. The collections in shared definitions are immutable, and both vector constructor arguments and vector accessor results are copied, but Bone is a structural reference, and its definition transform cannot be modified as an instance pose. Multiple instances each keep their own targets and solver corrections.

Data Unit/coordinates RigidBody.position, Joint.position, shape sizes, and translation ranges definition coordinates; the physics adaptation multiplies by Physics.unitScale RigidBody.rotation, Joint.rotation, and rotation ranges XYZ Euler, radians IK angles, maxRotationStep, Rotor, Hinge radians IK tolerance distance units in the current evaluation space; import/root scaling affects the actual corresponding scale Targets of setIkTarget, setFrameIkTarget, IkTargetModule world coordinates, Vector3f; with floating origin enabled, the double world anchor is subtracted at evaluation time SkeletonRagdoll.Body.position() and ordinary physics queries simulation-local coordinates; use the worldPosition/*World interfaces to obtain or supply world coordinates

A float external target is already precision-limited by itself; floating origin does not restore world-coordinate fractions lost when the Vector3f was constructed.

docs.title: Skeleton and SkeletonDynamics
docs.text:
SkeletonDynamics Skeleton.getDynamics();
void Skeleton.setDynamics(SkeletonDynamics dynamics);

new SkeletonDynamics(Physics physics, List<IkChain> ikChains,
                     List<DiamondConstraint> diamonds);
new SkeletonDynamics(Physics physics, List<IkChain> ikChains,
                     List<DiamondConstraint> diamonds, List<BonePoseConstraint> poseConstraints);

Skeleton uses SkeletonDynamics.EMPTY by default. It is usually mounted through a Builder after validation; direct construction and the setter do not perform all bone ownership, chain hierarchy, joint reference, and closure validation.

Accessor Returns physics() the shared physics definition poseConstraints() unmodifiable map from target Bone to inheritance/fixed-axis constraints; empty by default with the three-argument constructor ikChains() IK chain list preserving definition order diamonds() diamond closure constraint list chainsByName() read-only Map<String, IkChain>; chain names must be unique ikChainsByBone() read-only Map<Bone, List<IkChain>>; reverse mapping from a driver bone to all chains that control it

docs.title: SkeletonDynamicsBuilder
docs.text:
new SkeletonDynamicsBuilder(Skeleton skeleton);

Construction copies the definitions already mounted on the Skeleton into the Builder; it does not automatically clear the original rig.

Full method Behavior Skeleton skeleton() current target skeleton Bone bone(String name) resolves a structural reference by bone name; unknown names throw IllegalArgumentException <T> SkeletonDynamicsBuilder read(T source, SkeletonDynamicsReader<? super T> reader) runs the Reader synchronously, returns this Builder SkeletonDynamicsBuilder physics(Physics definition) replaces the whole physics definition, preserving IK/closure SkeletonDynamicsBuilder physics(List<RigidBody> bodies, List<Joint> joints) replaces bodies/joints; unit scaling, no required profile, affine writeback, radius scale 1, no bind-pose followers SkeletonDynamicsBuilder ik(IkChain chain) adds a chain; the same chain name replaces the existing chain SkeletonDynamicsBuilder diamond(DiamondConstraint diamond) adds a constraint; the same constraint name replaces the existing constraint SkeletonDynamicsBuilder pose(BonePoseConstraint constraint) adds a bone pose constraint; the same target Bone replaces the existing constraint SkeletonDynamics build() validates and returns the definition; does not mount, create a solver, or create a native world SkeletonDynamics attach() calls build() first, then writes into the Skeleton and returns the mounted definition

The structural validation performed by build()/attach() includes:

  • Non-null body bones, bind-pose followers, and IK controller/effector/link all belong to the target Skeleton.
  • A pose constraint's target and inheritance source both belong to this Skeleton; self-references and inheritance cycles are rejected.
  • A joint's two rigid body indices are valid and different; the indices refer to Physics.bodies(), not Bone.index.
  • The IK chain is non-empty, driver bones do not repeat, and each subsequent link/effector must be a descendant of the previous link; intermediate bones may be skipped.
  • A diamond closure references two existing POSITION chains; the same chain cannot belong to multiple closures.
  • Closure branches do not share driver bones, their endpoints differ, the bind positions of the branch bases are no farther apart than the closure tolerance, and one branch's driver bone cannot be an ancestor of the other base.

Illegal structures throw IllegalArgumentException. Null required arguments usually throw NullPointerException.

docs.title: Reader and Existing SkeletonBuilder
docs.text:
@FunctionalInterface
public interface SkeletonDynamicsReader<T> {
    void read(T source, SkeletonDynamicsBuilder builder);
}

The Reader only fills generic definitions into the Builder; it does not attach() by itself. External formats may use any source type:

Skeleton skeleton = model.getSkeleton();
SkeletonDynamicsReader<String> reader = (chainName, builder) -> builder.ik(
        new IkChain(chainName, builder.bone("hand-target"), builder.bone("hand"),
                List.of(new IkLink(builder.bone("upper-arm")),
                        new IkLink(builder.bone("forearm")))));

new SkeletonDynamicsBuilder(skeleton).read("left-arm", reader).attach();

The existing SkeletonBuilder provides:

SkeletonBuilder dynamics(Consumer<SkeletonDynamicsBuilder> configure);

The callback runs after the skeleton's build(...) completes Bone/Anchor/Vertex binding, and automatically validates and mounts. Repeated calls to dynamics(...) replace the configuration callback; clear() removes it as well. A custom ModelData may override void configureSkeleton(Skeleton skeleton), hooking up a Reader during Model construction. The Model construction hook of format metadata runs after the SkeletonBuilder callback and may override the physics table or same-named chains; configuration that needs to override format defaults should go after Model loading and before ModelInstance creation.

docs.title: Generic Bone Pose Constraints
docs.text:
new TransformInheritance(Bone source, float weight, boolean translation, boolean rotation);
new BonePoseConstraint(Bone bone, TransformInheritance inheritance, Vector3f fixedAxis);

Both are public records under SkeletonDynamics; they do not require a BoneData type. The inheritance weight must be finite and may be negative; at least one of translation or rotation must be enabled. The inheritance source provides the currently evaluated local pose delta, translation is multiplied by weight, and rotation is slerped from the identity quaternion by weight; it does not inherit the source's bind pose or world position. The target bone's original local pose applies inheritance first, then extracts the twist along fixedAxis, and then applies IK and physics overrides. The fixed axis is in the target bone's local coordinates; the input vector is copied and normalized, and is rejected when its squared length is less than 1e-8. The physics override takes the final simulated pose as authoritative; this axis constraint does not replace physics joint limits.

inheritance or fixedAxis may be null, but not both. fixedAxis() returns a copy; hasFixedAxis() queries whether an axis is defined, and fixedAxis(Vector3f destination) copies into the caller's scratch when an axis is defined. The Builder validates skeleton ownership and inheritance cycles by bone reference. Instances are evaluated in dependency order; cross-branch inheritance does not depend on hierarchy traversal order, and the update range is widened to cover affected vertices.

PMX/PMD bone inheritance and fixed axes are converted in MmdSkeletonDynamicsReader.read; when reading a PMX bone table alone, you can also call MmdSkeletonDynamicsReader.readBoneConstraints(builder) and readIk(builder). Index references of format files exist only in the Reader layer; MC or external formats just fill these definitions through the same Builder.

docs.title: Physics
docs.text:
new Physics(List<RigidBody> bodies, List<Joint> joints, Vector3f unitScale,
            boolean profileRequired, boolean affineWriteback,
            float profileRadiusScale, Set<Bone> bindPoseFollowers);
Parameter Contract bodies, joints copied definition lists; profile/joints reference the list indices of bodies unitScale three finite positive components; used for rigid body position/size and joint translation profileRequired when true, this table cannot be enabled directly without a profile; used for candidate tables affineWriteback when true, computes the local physics transform inversely within the full affine parent hierarchy, preserving scale/shear profileRadiusScale finite positive number; radius scale of generated profile capsules bindPoseFollowers follower bones without a direct physics body; they can follow the bind-to-current affine delta of the nearest physics ancestor

Physics.EMPTY: empty tables, unitScale=(1,1,1), profileRequired=false, affineWriteback=true, profileRadiusScale=1, empty follower set.

docs.title: RigidBody
docs.text:
new RigidBody(String name, String alias, Bone bone, int collisionGroup,
              int nonCollisionMask, int shape, Vector3f size, Vector3f position,
              Vector3f rotation, float mass, float linearDamping,
              float angularDamping, float restitution, float friction, int mode);
Parameter Contract name, alias non-null display/auxiliary names; they are not required to be bone names; alias may be an empty string bone may be null, meaning a body not bound to a bone; when non-null it must belong to the Skeleton collisionGroup integer 0..63 nonCollisionMask integer filter mask; the physics adaptation preserves exclusion layer semantics shape SPHERE=0, BOX=1, CAPSULE=2 size finite non-negative vector; spheres use the x radius, boxes use xyz half-extents, capsules use x radius / full height of the y cylinder segment position, rotation body position in definition coordinates and XYZ Euler orientation; both finite mass finite non-negative mass; 0 produces no dynamic inverse mass linearDamping, angularDamping finite non-negative damping restitution, friction finite non-negative material parameters mode the motion/writeback mode in the table below Constant Value Runtime behavior KINEMATIC 0 rigid body driven by animation targets DYNAMIC 1 physics writes back the full pose DYNAMIC_ROTATION 2 dynamic body; writes back only the bone rotation, preserving animation translation

Definition construction allows non-negative sizes; when collision shapes are actually created, sphere/capsule radii and all three box half-extents must be positive. Creating physics bodies may therefore reject degenerate shapes further.

docs.title: Joint
docs.text:
new Joint(String name, String alias, int rigidBodyA, int rigidBodyB,
          Vector3f position, Vector3f rotation, Vector3f positionMin,
          Vector3f positionMax, Vector3f rotationMin, Vector3f rotationMax,
          Vector3f positionSpring, Vector3f rotationSpring);

name/alias are non-null, and all vectors are finite and copied. rigidBodyA/B must be valid and different during Builder validation. position/rotation is the shared joint frame, *Min/*Max are the author limits, and *Spring are the author spring parameters. The current model adapter maps this set of six-axis author parameters to a Box3D spherical cone/twist; translation is tightened to a fixed anchor. Other native joints are created through the Physics API and are not selected by this record's type field.

docs.title: Physics Example Without Format Metadata
docs.text:
var builder = new SkeletonDynamicsBuilder(model.getSkeleton());
var body = new RigidBody("torso-body", "", builder.bone("torso"),
        0, 0, RigidBody.BOX, new Vector3f(0.2f, 0.3f, 0.1f),
        new Vector3f(0, 1, 0), new Vector3f(),
        2f, 0.05f, 0.1f, 0f, 0.6f, RigidBody.DYNAMIC);
builder.physics(List.of(body), List.of()).attach();

var instance = new ModelInstance(model, null, null, null, null, null);
var ragdoll = instance.enablePhysics();
if (ragdoll != null) {
    ragdoll.setGravity(new Vector3f(0, -9.80665f, 0));
    // Called once per frame by the host; instances already wired into the Minecraft runtime are advanced by that runtime.
    instance.evaluatePhysicsFrame(0f, 1f / 60f);
}
// On lifecycle end: instance.detachPhysics() or instance.close().

The high-level enablePhysics returns null when the native library is unavailable; it throws IllegalArgumentException when the library is available but bodies are empty, or when profileRequired=true and no profile is passed. Body.source() returns this generic RigidBody, and Joint.source() returns this generic Joint.

docs.title: IkLink, RotationLimit, and IkJoint
docs.text:
new IkLink(Bone bone);
new IkLink(Bone bone, RotationLimit limit);
new IkLink(Bone bone, RotationLimit limit, IkJoint joint);
new RotationLimit(Vector3f minimum, Vector3f maximum);
new Rotor(float angle);
new Hinge(Vector3f axis, Vector3f reference, float minimum, float maximum);
Type Parameters and behavior IkLink bone required; limit/joint may be null; the omitted fields of the two simplified constructors are null RotationLimit finite XYZ Euler lower/upper bounds, per-axis minimum ≤ maximum; applies to the IK local correction IkJoint sealed interface, permits Rotor and Hinge Rotor finite angle 0..π; the first segment revolves around the uncorrected pose direction, later segments are relative to the previous segment's direction Hinge axis/reference are in the driver's uncorrected local frame; non-zero, automatically normalized, orthogonality error ≤ 1e-4; angle in [-π,π] and minimum ≤ maximum

Rotor/Hinge constrain position solving in Caliko; RotationLimit projects onto the local correction. When both are given, both restrictions participate, but Euler box projection does not guarantee global convergence for complex constraints. Chains that have already reached the target do not choose another solution.

docs.title: IkChain
docs.text:
new IkChain(String name, Bone controller, Bone effector, List<IkLink> links);
new IkChain(String name, Bone controller, Bone effector, List<IkLink> links,
            int iterations, float tolerance, float maxRotationStep,
            boolean replaceAuthoredRotation, TargetMode targetMode);
Parameter Simplified-construct default Contract name required non-blank chain name; control and diagnostics address it by this name, and it is not required to equal the controller bone name controller required default target source bone effector required final effector bone links required non-empty, from base to tip; the final link points to the effector iterations 32 1..256; caps the adaptation iterations and the library's attempt count tolerance 1e-4f finite positive distance maxRotationStep π finite non-negative value, the maximum angle of each direction-alignment increment; 0 limits that increment to zero, and subsequent Euler projection can still adjust the correction replaceAuthoredRotation false true takes over the chain bones' authored local pose; the current implementation starts from the identity local transform and skips even authored translation/scale, while morph/grant/fixed-axis still participate afterwards targetMode POSITION non-null; modes below

POSITION uses the controller's current absolute position as the default target. DIRECTION determines orientation from the bind bone-segment direction and the controller's rotation difference when there is no external target, ignoring its pure translation. When a persistent or single-tick external target exists, it switches to position blending; this mode does not interpret the external Vector3f as a direction vector.

var builder = new SkeletonDynamicsBuilder(model.getSkeleton());
var elbow = new Hinge(new Vector3f(0, 0, 1), new Vector3f(1, 0, 0),
        -(float) Math.PI / 2f, 0f);
builder.ik(new IkChain("left-arm", builder.bone("hand-target"), builder.bone("hand"),
        List.of(new IkLink(builder.bone("upper-arm")),
                new IkLink(builder.bone("forearm"), null, elbow)))).attach();

This hinge example assumes the forearm's bind direction is local +X and the bend axis is +Z; real assets need to fill in their own bone frame.

docs.title: Diamond Closure
docs.text:
new DiamondConstraint(String name, String firstChain, String secondChain);
new DiamondConstraint(String name, String firstChain, String secondChain,
                      int iterations, float tolerance);

The simplified constructor uses iterations=32 and tolerance=1e-4f. The name is non-blank, the two chain names are required and different, iterations is 1..256, and tolerance is a finite positive number. Branch requirements are validated by the Builder, see its structural validation list.

var builder = new SkeletonDynamicsBuilder(model.getSkeleton());
var left = new IkChain("left-linkage", builder.bone("closure-target"), builder.bone("left-tip"),
        List.of(new IkLink(builder.bone("left-base")), new IkLink(builder.bone("left-mid"))));
var right = new IkChain("right-linkage", builder.bone("closure-target"), builder.bone("right-tip"),
        List.of(new IkLink(builder.bone("right-base")), new IkLink(builder.bone("right-mid"))));
builder.ik(left).ik(right)
        .diamond(new DiamondConstraint("linkage", left.name(), right.name()))
        .attach();

The two bases should coincide at the bind pose position and drive separate hierarchies; the two endpoints represent the same closure point. The two controllers may be the same bone or have separate targets; solving starts from the midpoint of the two targets. Disabling either chain pauses the closure; when branches belong to a closure they are not first solved as independent chains. The constraint only guarantees position closure; it does not guarantee equal endpoint orientation, equal side lengths, or native mechanical feedback.

docs.title: SkeletonInstance Runtime Control
docs.text:
var skeleton = instance.getSkeletonInstance();

In the table below, name always denotes an IK chain name. The existing parameter names boneName/controllerBone are historical.

Method signature Returns/Behavior boolean setIkEnabled(String name, boolean enabled) returns false for an undefined chain; on success requires re-evaluation boolean isIkEnabled(String name) reads the toggle, default true; not an existence check, unknown chains also return true void resetIkEnabled() clears overrides, restoring the default true boolean clearIkEnabled(String name) clears an individual chain's explicit toggle; returns true when state was removed boolean setIkTarget(String name, Vector3f worldTarget, float weight) persistent target; false for an undefined chain; copies the target and requires an update boolean clearIkTarget(String name) clears the persistent target; returns false when there is no target void clearIkTargets() clears all persistent targets boolean setFrameIkTarget(String name, Vector3f worldTarget, float weight) transient target for the current pose pipeline cycle; false for an undefined chain void clearFrameIkTargets() clears transient targets; ModelTickLoop calls it automatically at the start of a cycle void updateTransform() evaluates hierarchy, IK, and final hierarchy; manual hosts call it according to their own evaluation order void updateTransformAfterPhysics() rebuilds the hierarchy after writeback, preserving solved IK corrections without solving IK again Map<String, CalikoIkSolver.SolveResult> ikSolveResults() read-only diagnostic view of the most recent IK solve

Targets must be non-null and finite, and weight must be finite and within [0,1]; otherwise the corresponding argument exception is thrown. Blending runs from the controller's current position to the external position; weight is not "the strength of enabling IK". Transient targets take precedence over persistent targets; unknown chains return false before the target value is validated. Setting a target only marks the input as changed; it does not solve immediately. Afterwards run the instance's normal evaluation entry point.

var skeleton = instance.getSkeletonInstance();
boolean accepted = skeleton.setIkTarget("left-arm", new Vector3f(1, 2, 0), 1f);
instance.updateImmediate();
var result = skeleton.ikSolveResults().get("left-arm");

The accessors of SolveResult(float residual, boolean satisfied) are residual() and satisfied(). For an ordinary chain, residual is the distance from the actual endpoint to this target; for a closure, it is the larger of the two endpoint distance and the two base distance. Closure branch results correspond to the most recent shared target and do not mean that the branch's original controller target was necessarily reached. satisfied only expresses that the corresponding position residual is within tolerance; it is not a complete angular/dynamics acceptance. Disabled or unrun chains have no result for that solve; the Map is a live read-only view that is cleared and updated on the next solve; copy it yourself if you need to keep a snapshot.

docs.title: Per-Tick Targets: IkTargetModule
docs.text:
new IkTargetModule(String name, Vector3f worldTarget);
new IkTargetModule(String name, Vector3f worldTarget, float weight);

The two-argument constructor uses weight 1 and initial enabled true. Accessors: controllerBone() (chain name), target() (copied vector), weight(), enabled(). Control methods: void setTarget(Vector3f), void setTarget(Vector3f,float), void setEnabled(boolean). Setting the target preserves the enabled state; the one-argument setter preserves the current weight.

var target = new lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.dynamic.tick_loop.handler.IkTargetModule(
        "left-arm", new Vector3f(1, 2, 0));
instance.getTickLoop().addPreIk("hand-target-input", target);
target.setTarget(new Vector3f(1.2f, 2, 0), 0.6f);
target.setEnabled(false);

The constructor only validates that the name is non-blank and the target values; it does not verify that the chain exists. Chain names are resolved only when the module is published to an instance at runtime. addPreIk places the module before IK and after the default apply; transient targets are consumed by both IK and physics within the same cycle. When you need to write pending transforms for the default apply to consume, use the tick pipeline's addBefore(SLOT_APPLY, ...).

docs.title: Actual Default Behavior of Format Readers
docs.text:
Reader Read interface Default mapping MmdSkeletonDynamicsReader void read(MmdModelData, SkeletonDynamicsBuilder) authored rigid body order, direct Bone references, valid joints, imported unitScale; no required profile, rigid writeback, profile radius scale 1 same as above static void readIk(SkeletonDynamicsBuilder) converts only PMX IK already attached to bones; usable for skeletons without a full tail same as above static void readBoneConstraints(SkeletonDynamicsBuilder) converts PMX inheritance/fixed axes into generic constraints; the full read calls it automatically GltfSkeletonDynamicsReader void read(GltfModelData, SkeletonDynamicsBuilder) generates candidates in node order; requires an explicit profile, affine writeback, skin bone bind followers; does not guess/create IK automatically

MMD uses the controller bone name as the chain name, and reverses chains from the file's tip-to-base to base-to-tip; positive iteration counts are capped at 256, tolerance is 1e-4f, the step angle takes the absolute value of the original limit, and authored local pose takeover is enabled. Expressible single-axis Euler limits are converted to Hinge; other box limits keep RotationLimit. DIRECTION is used when there is a single link, the controller/effector bind positions coincide, and the controller has a vector tail. Chains without a valid effector/link or with a non-positive iteration count do not enter the definition. Invalid or self-connected PMX joints do not enter the simulatable table.

The external indices of glTF profiles continue to correspond to node order; MMD profiles correspond to the original rigid body order. Both sources complete conversion at the Reader boundary, so at runtime Body.source().bone() directly yields a generic bone reference.

docs.title: Solver Adaptation for Custom Hosts
docs.text:
CalikoIkSolver(Skeleton skeleton, PoseAccess pose) provides void solve() and Map<String, SolveResult> results(). It is usually managed by SkeletonInstance; when used directly, the host implements:

PoseAccess method Host responsibility Transform absolute(Bone bone) the evaluated absolute pose Transform correction(Bone bone) mutable per-instance local IK correction Vector3f target(IkChain chain) returns a new vector for this target; closures modify the returned value to solve for the shared target boolean enabled(String chain) chain toggle void refresh(Bone driver, Bone endpoint) after correction, synchronously rebuild the affected hierarchy; subsequent reads must see the latest pose

The host is responsible for animation/physics evaluation order, correction cleanup, and thread ownership. The solver has mutable state and cannot solve the same instance concurrently. The current library is the official Caliko 1.3.8 core; dependency notes and licenses are included under modules/render-core/libs.

docs.text:
The classes for this page are all in the render-core module; see the "Types and Packages" table for package paths:

  • SkeletonDynamics
  • SkeletonDynamicsBuilder
  • SkeletonDynamicsReader
