docs.title: UI model previews
docs.text:
Create machines, contraptions, schematics, vanilla structure NBT and .litematic files use GuiModelPreview(MinecraftModelSource). See Minecraft structures and Create previews for layers, exploded views, UML composition and post-processing.

GuiModelPreview displays a model published by the existing model loader. Resource locations and optional MMD entry names follow the normal registration contract. Each preview owns a local ModelInstance, material state, GPU buffers and transparent depth canvas. It does not mount its instance in the world backend or change an existing world's model pose.

var preview = new GuiModelPreview(
        ResourceLocation.parse("kasuga_lib:models/gltf/maribel.glb"), null);
preview.setView(-0.55f, 0.25f, 1f); // yaw / pitch in radians; positive zoom

render returns false while the asset is unavailable, allowing the host to draw a placeholder. It resolves the current publication on each draw and releases the old private instance when the asset changes. Default framing fits the model's bounds; zooming in can intentionally crop it. An alternative constructor accepts a Supplier<Model> that lends an asset or returns null.

Toolkit Control Ownership Vanilla ModelPreviewWidget(x, y, width, height, preview) The owning Screen calls close() from removed() LDLib2 ModelPreviewElement(preview) Removal closes the preview; supports normal ModularUI and world panels LDLib2 Compose ModelPreview(modelLocation, modelName, ...) Removal or an asset-key change releases the preview; see the Compose adapter ModernUI ModelPreviewView(context, modelLocation, modelName) Uses the public MinecraftSurfaceView renderer; detach schedules cleanup on Minecraft's render thread

Toolkit adapters live separately in external/uip/ldlib and external/uip/modernui. The shared renderer depends on neither toolkit. Give each owning control its own preview.

For custom hosts use preview.render(graphics, x, y, width, height, partialTick); an overload accepts opacity in [0,1]. Rendering, instance access and closing belong to the Minecraft render thread; setView may be called by UI input threads. currentFrame() lends a read-only color frame, valid until the next draw, resize or close; never delete its texture or framebuffer. instance() allows the caller to pose the local model. The preview does not drive world physics or global scheduling.

The native preview material path supports depth, skinning and model textures independently of Iris world passes. Verified on macOS arm64, MC 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.203, LDLib2 2.2.1 and ModernUI 3.13.0.1. Windows, Linux and Iris combinations have not been exercised.

docs.title: Development demos
docs.text:
./gradlew :external:uip:ldlib:runClientModelDemo -PkasugaModelToolkit=vanilla
./gradlew :external:uip:ldlib:runClientModelDemo -PkasugaModelToolkit=ldlib
# Place an isolated world in this module's run/model-demo/saves first.
./gradlew :external:uip:ldlib:runClientModelDemo -PkasugaModelToolkit=world -PkasugaQuickPlayWorld=YourTestWorld
./gradlew :external:uip:modernui:runClientModelDemo

Add -PkasugaModelCapture=/absolute/path/model.png to run the smoke, capture and exit. Inspect passed in the adjacent model-report.json: a failed client assertion can still yield a successful Gradle exit. Vanilla/LDLib2 check actual model pixels, rotation, repeated GUI resizing, current attachment dimensions/completeness and close cleanup. :modules:modelling:renderGlTest checks color/FBO/depth retirement immediately after resize, before later allocations can reuse their OpenGL names. A delayed glIsTexture(oldId) query cannot identify the original object. ModernUI checks its real render callback and detach cleanup. Demo classes stay out of release jars.

docs.title: UML rendering framework and backend interfaces
docs.text:
Interface, configuration, and call reference. For the principles see uml-render-framework.md.

models.uml.framework defines the public capabilities extracted from existing rendering implementations. It does not depend on Minecraft, Iris, or LWJGL; model structures and JOML math types remain public data types. uml.bridge and uml.backend handle adaptation and default implementations and are no longer the only entry point for all capabilities. MC, OpenGL, and platform upload strategies stay in concrete implementations.

docs.title: Layers and responsibilities
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Pipeline[ModelPipeLine / host render callback] --> Schedule[framework.schedule.RenderScheduler]
    Pipeline --> Backend[framework.render.RenderBackend]
    Backend --> Context[framework.render.RenderContext]
    Context --> Factory[framework.render.RenderableFactory]
    Factory --> Geometry[framework.render.ModelGeometryAdapter]
    Context --> Buffers[framework.buffer]
    MC[MCBackend / MCBridge / IVertexBuffer] -.implements or adapts.-> Backend
    MC -.implements or adapts.-> Geometry
    GL[MappedBuffer / GpuUploadRing / GL Device] -.implements.-> Buffers
Layer Interface/implementation Responsibilities framework.schedule RenderScheduler<I>, DefaultRenderScheduler<I> Per-instance visibility policy, host frame marks, render distance limit, unmount cleanup framework.schedule FrameSampleCache<I> Deduplicates identity sampling across camera views/material passes within a shared frame token framework.render ModelGeometryAdapter Vertex/mesh conversion, skeleton binding selection; does not own scheduling or drawing framework.render RenderableFactory<R> Creates render resources for one instance, receives explicitly provided backend services framework.render RenderContext<R,Q,E> Resource cache for one mount, hard visibility switch, host transform/lighting metadata, release framework.render RenderBackend<A,C,Q> Mount registry, context creation, draw submission, replacement and unmount, backend shutdown framework.buffer TypedBuffer<T> Fixed-capacity CPU element read/write, partial/full updates, borrowed byte view framework.buffer UploadBuffer, UploadDevice Full snapshot upload, dirty element ranges, in-flight read protection; device calls and state restoration framework.buffer RenderBuffer<D,S> Geometry upload, update, draw, and markSubmitted after every consumption uml.bridge Bridge<R> Combines geometry conversion with the legacy resource creation entry point, compatible with the old pipeline uml.backend Backend, BackendContext Default lifecycle implementation of registry and context mc / uml.backend.gpu MC renderer, OpenGL buffer/device Vanilla frustum/lighting, shader, VAO/VBO/TBO, Iris, and platform policies

docs.title: The boundary between Bridge and Backend
docs.text:
Bridge provides the model conversion rules. The backend owns services such as the executor, chooses the context type and passes those services explicitly to the resource factory. The current MC main path is:

MCBackend.add(key, bridge, instance)
  → MCBackend.createContext(bridge, instance)
  → MCRenderableContext(bridge, instance, factory)
  → factory: bridge.createRenderable(instance, backend.executor)

This path does not require Bridge to look up the executor from the string mc_backend. Bridge.getBackendContext, setBackends/getBackends, and the single-argument createRenderable/apply are kept as compatibility entry points for old calls; the default Backend.createContext can still call the old factory. New backends should override createContext and return a type-matching context directly. Do not let the geometry adapter close the executor, manage frame marks, or handle the draw pipeline.

Q is the host frame context, E is pre-render metadata, R is the mount resource; none of them substitutes for another. BackendContext does not allocate R at construction; the first apply creates and caches it. The default Backend.add calls apply up front, so the mount is published only after resources are prepared successfully. beforeRender(Q) reads metadata; it does not sample animation and does not create buffers. Animation sampling, version updates, morph, and upload are done by the rendering implementation and cannot be achieved by rebuilding the context over and over.

docs.title: Mount and release rules
docs.text:
• The registry matches mounts by the caller's key; key, adapter, instance, context, and resources must not be null.
  • Replacing the same key prepares the new context first. If preparation fails, the unpublished context is closed and the old mount is kept; on success the new mount is published and the old context is closed. A failure to release the old resources reports an exception, and the new mount is already in effect at that point.
  • getRenderingObjects is a read-only view; mount changes must go through add/remove.
  • remove first removes from the registry, then releases resources; release exceptions are visible and are not silently ignored.
  • A context owns only the render resources returned by the factory; it does not own the ModelInstance, the Bridge, or the shared executor. close is idempotent; after closing, apply throws, and resources of an unmounted instance cannot be reallocated.
  • On shutdown the Backend tries to release all mounts and aggregates release exceptions; after shutdown it rejects new mounts and submissions. The MC Backend then releases batching/translucent resources and stops the executor.
  • Mounts, buffer operations, and drawing are held by the render thread; the scheduler independently synchronizes tick/render access.

docs.title: Scheduling rules
docs.text:
The framework modes are ALWAYS, MANUAL, HOST_RENDERER. MC's VANILLA_RENDERER maps to HOST_RENDERER; the old static ModelRenderScheduler only forwards to ModelRenderScheduling.scheduler(). ModelPipeLine and MCBackend use the same framework scheduling domain. Other backends may create an independent DefaultRenderScheduler.

Instances are distinguished by object identity. Switching modes keeps the per-instance render distance limit; setVisible selects MANUAL. Render distance uses host world units; a non-positive value disables the distance gate, and NaN/Infinity are rejected. shouldRender answers the policy result only; the distance and frustum checks are performed by the backend in order. Culled instances are not sampled and not uploaded; physics stepping continues to be managed by the independent runtime.

The host renderer calls markRenderedThisFrame within its own visible frame. The first model pass calls flipFrame once, and later material/translucent passes share the mark; when the next flip has no new mark, the old mark expires. Marks made after a flip are also immediately visible. Removing the last mount cleans up the instance policy and both mark sets; unmounting the whole render domain can call resetAll. For MC's concrete timing see render-scheduling.md.

Multi-camera calls clearFrameMarks() before each host view pass; it clears only visibility marks and keeps the instance policy and render distance. FrameSampleCache.beginFrame(token) instead clears the sample set when the token changes; later camera views with the same token use firstSample(instance) to avoid duplicate sampling, while still being able to sample instances visible only in the new camera view. For the MC producer see the multi-camera and offscreen output document.

docs.title: Buffer rules
docs.text:
TypedBuffer counts index/offset in elements and sizeOfType/bufferCapacity in bytes. For a short array, updateAll updates only the prefix, keeping the capacity and the tail; updateRange must not go out of bounds and may write zero elements at the end of the capacity. slice keeps the packed byte order and borrows memory; it must not outlive the close point. A direct writeData in an implementation must also check the closed state and the element range. Closing is idempotent.

GpuUploadRing implements UploadBuffer, and the old GpuUploadRing.Device extends the framework's UploadDevice. Upload requires a complete direct snapshot; dirty bits are element indices, stride is in bytes, and mergeGap is in elements. An empty dirty set may reuse the current storage; each slot independently fills in the changes since its last upload. The input position/limit stay unchanged.

Every GPU consumption, including repeated draws of unchanged data and translucent replay, must mark markSubmitted. A busy slot cannot be overwritten; the device may reallocate storage; fence checks do not block. The device is responsible for API calls and bind state restoration; the ring owns the release of buffers/fences. The concrete OpenGL and macOS TBO orphan policies continue to be provided by the existing device implementations.

IVertexBuffer extends RenderBuffer<FlatModelData, ShaderInstance> and only adds access to the Minecraft VertexBuffer and the GL id. A new host integrates with the framework contract through its own data/shader types without referencing Minecraft interfaces.

docs.title: Utils Module (modules/utils)
docs.text: modules/utils provides foundational annotations, lightweight data structures, path/glob matchers, and Gson binding policies with no dependencies on other KasugaLib modules. It sets FMLModType: GAMELIBRARY and is bundled into the :modules:core and :modules:library shadow JARs.

docs.title: 1. Module Coordinates and Dependencies
docs.text:
• Gradle subproject: :modules:utils (group: lib.kasuga, Java 21)
  • Consumer dependency: implementation project(":modules:utils")
  • Gson runtime contract: modules/utils/build.gradle declares compileOnlyApi 'com.google.code.gson:gson:2.10.1'. Because Minecraft supplies Gson at runtime, :modules:core and :modules:library do not bundle a duplicate copy in their shaded JARs. Pure JVM consumers outside Minecraft (such as :modules:render-core and :modules:resource-compiler) must provide Gson on their runtime classpath.
Package Responsibility lib.kasuga.annotations Conditional Mixin and code-generation marker annotations lib.kasuga.utils.json Shared GsonBindings and JsonFieldPolicy validation rules lib.kasuga.structure Lazy cache LazyRecomputable, MapSet, and Pair lib.kasuga.utils.glob Segment-tree glob matching (GlobMatcher / GlobTreeNode) lib.kasuga.utils.path Extensible segment-filter tree and parallel matcher (PathMatcher) lib.kasuga.utils ValueInspectionUtils and VectorUtils

docs.title: 2.1 @ConditionalMixin and MixinCondition
docs.text:
@Documented
@Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME)
@Target({ElementType.TYPE})
public @interface ConditionalMixin {
    Class<? extends MixinCondition> condition();
}

@FunctionalInterface
public interface MixinCondition {
    boolean shouldEnableMixin();
}

Declares a runtime enablement predicate on a Mixin class so a host Mixin config plugin can evaluate condition() before applying the Mixin.

docs.title: 2.2 RegistryGeneration
docs.text:
public interface RegistryGeneration {
    @interface Modifier {}
    @interface Configure {}
}

Container for marker annotations (@RegistryGeneration.Modifier, @RegistryGeneration.Configure) used by registration code generation. Neither nested annotation specifies @Retention or @Target, so they retain default CLASS retention.

docs.title: 3.1 GsonBindings
docs.text:
lib.kasuga.utils.json.GsonBindings standardizes snake_case field naming (FieldNamingPolicy.LOWER_CASE_WITH_UNDERSCORES) and attaches JsonFieldPolicy across configuration and model/data-driven DTOs.

Member Signature / Type Behavior builder() public static GsonBuilder builder() Creates a GsonBuilder with LOWER_CASE_WITH_UNDERSCORES and new JsonFieldPolicy() GSON public static final Gson builder().create() for standard DTO deserialization STRICT public static final Gson Built from builder() with StringAdapter, BooleanAdapter (boolean / Boolean), and IntegerAdapter (int / Integer)

The strict adapters on GsonBindings.STRICT reject Gson's implicit scalar coercions and throw JsonParseException (with reader.getPath()) on type mismatch:

  • GsonBindings.StringAdapter: requires JsonToken.STRING (rejects numbers or booleans).
  • GsonBindings.BooleanAdapter: requires JsonToken.BOOLEAN (rejects strings such as "false").
  • GsonBindings.IntegerAdapter: requires JsonToken.NUMBER and calls new BigDecimal(reader.nextString()).intValueExact(), rejecting fractional numbers (1.5), strings ("2"), and 32-bit overflow.
private record Input(String name, boolean enabled, int[] meshIndices) {}

// GsonBindings.STRICT rejects {"name":3}, {"enabled":"false"}, {"mesh_indices":[1.5]} with JsonParseException
Input decoded = GsonBindings.STRICT.fromJson(
        "{\"name\":\"body\",\"enabled\":true,\"mesh_indices\":[0,2]}",
        Input.class
);

docs.title: 3.2 JsonFieldPolicy
docs.text:
public final class JsonFieldPolicy implements TypeAdapterFactory enforces two opt-in DTO field policies (scanning up the superclass chain before Object.class, skipping static, transient, and synthetic fields, and honoring @SerializedName primary names and alternate() aliases):

Annotation Target & Retention Behavior @JsonFieldPolicy.NonNullFields @Inherited, @Target(TYPE), @Retention(RUNTIME) Throws JsonParseException if the root element is JSON null or any declared field receives an explicit null (including null inside arrays or nested arrays); omitted fields keep constructor defaults and unknown fields stay ignored @JsonFieldPolicy.DefaultOnMismatch @Target(FIELD), @Retention(RUNTIME) When a field receives a non-matching JSON kind (String requires string, boolean/Boolean requires boolean, others require number) or explicit null, removes that key from a shallow copy of the JsonObject before delegating to Gson so the constructor default survives

JsonFieldPolicy never mutates caller-owned JsonElement trees and only allocates a shallow copy of the enclosing JsonObject when at least one mismatched field is stripped.

@JsonFieldPolicy.NonNullFields
public class ExampleDto {
    public String id = "default";

    @JsonFieldPolicy.DefaultOnMismatch
    public float scale = 1.0f;
}

docs.title: 4.1 LazyRecomputable<T>
docs.text:
Lazy evaluation and invalidatable cache (not thread-safe; tracks initialization with a dedicated isCached flag so null values are cached as well):

API Description new LazyRecomputable<>(Supplier<T> supplier) / LazyRecomputable.of(supplier) Creates a lazy cache T get() Evaluates on first access or after clear() void clear() Resets cached value so the next get() recomputes LazyRecomputable.predictable(Supplier<T> supplier, Supplier<Boolean> predict) Returns PredictableLazyRecomputable<T>; checks predict.get() on every get() and clears the cache if false

docs.title: 4.2 MapSet<K, V>
docs.text:
public class MapSet<K, V> implements Iterable<V> wraps HashMap<K, Set<V>> (backed by HashSet):

  • void put(K key, V value): inserts value into the key's set.
  • Set<V> get(K key): returns the mapped set or Collections.emptySet().
  • Iterator<V> iterator(): flattens values across all keys.

docs.title: 4.3 Pair<K, V> and Pair.Mutable<K, V>
docs.text:
Immutable pair and mutable subclass (with Lombok @Getter):

API Description Pair.of(K first, V second) Creates an immutable Pair<K, V> getFirst() / getSecond() / Object get(boolean isFirst) Reads components; get(true) returns first new Pair.Mutable<>(K first, V second) Creates a mutable pair with setFirst(K) and setSecond(V) Pair.Mutable.create(boolean first, boolean second) Shorthand for Pair.Mutable<Boolean, Boolean>

docs.title: 5. Path and Glob Matching (lib.kasuga.utils.glob, lib.kasuga.utils.path)
docs.text: For VFS logical path normalization and mount-table routing, see Virtual file systems. These two utility packages match path-segment lists against tree-structured pattern rules.

docs.title: 5.1 GlobMatcher and GlobTreeNode
docs.text:
GlobMatcher compiles segmented path patterns into a prefix tree (GlobTreeNode) supporting literal segments, single-segment "*", and recursive "**" wildcards:

  • new GlobMatcher(List<List<String>> patterns): builds the pattern tree and marks terminal nodes (setTerminator()).
  • List<List<String>> match(Function<List<String>, List<String>> listProvider, Predicate<List<String>> willNext): traverses lazily using a directory-listing callback.
  • List<List<String>> collect(Stream<List<String>> fileEntries) / boolean validate(List<String> entry, GlobTreeNode node): filters an existing stream of path-segment lists.
GlobMatcher matcher = new GlobMatcher(List.of(
        List.of("a", "b", "d"),
        List.of("a", "**", "d")
));
List<List<String>> matched = matcher.collect(Stream.of(
        List.of("a", "b", "c", "d"),
        List.of("a", "b", "e", "f")
));

docs.title: 5.2 PathMatcher, PathEntry, and PathFilter
docs.text:
lib.kasuga.utils.path provides a pluggable segment-filter tree supporting discovery-style traversal (match) and batch parallel matching (matchParallel).

Type Key Members Description PathEntry parse(path) / parse(path, sep) / parseAny(path), extend(subPath), getParent() Extends ArrayList<String>; parseAny splits on [\\/], while parse(path) splits on File.separator PathFilter Result test(String pathPart), boolean willMatchSelf(), PathFilter.INIT Result values: INITIAL, REJECT, RECURSIVE_ACCEPT, ACCEPT, RETURN PathFilter.GlobPathFilter new GlobPathFilter(String glob) Supports ** (RECURSIVE_ACCEPT, willMatchSelf() == true), * (.*), ? (.), escaping regex metacharacters PathEntryFilter ArrayList<PathFilter> Represents a single multi-segment filter rule PathEntryFilterTreeNode add(PathEntryFilter), markTerminal() / unsetTerminal(), addTerminal(PathFilter), replaceTerminal(Function) Tree node for compiled filter rules PathMatcher new PathMatcher(PathEntryFilterTreeNode root), setNoExplore(boolean), match(listFunction, initialPath), matchParallel(entries, node) Discovery and batch matching; noExplore = true stops descending after matching a terminal node 
PathEntryFilterTreeNode root = new PathEntryFilterTreeNode(PathFilter.INIT);
PathEntryFilter rule = new PathEntryFilter();
rule.add(new PathFilter.GlobPathFilter("**"));
rule.add(new PathFilter.GlobPathFilter("*.txt"));
root.add(rule);

PathMatcher matcher = new PathMatcher(root);
Collection<PathEntry> matched = matcher.matchParallel(entries, root);

docs.title: 6.1 ValueInspectionUtils
docs.text:
ValueInspectionUtils.INSTANCE throttles debug callbacks by hashCode() changes:

  • public void print(String key, Object value, Runnable debugger): computes long hashCode = value.hashCode() and runs debugger.run() only when it differs from lastLoggedHashcode.getOrDefault(key, 0L). value must be non-null; if the first value for key happens to have hashCode() == 0, that first invocation is skipped.

docs.title: 6.2 VectorUtils
docs.text: • public static String blockPosAsUnderlineFormat(BlockPos localPos): formats a Minecraft BlockPos as "<x>_<y>_<z>" (requires net.minecraft.core.BlockPos on the classpath).

docs.title: Virtual file systems
docs.text: modules/core provides VirtualFileSystem, logical VfsPath values, writable directory and memory backends, read-only ZIP/JAR access, overlay resolution, mount routing, transactions, and change subscriptions. The VFS package has no Minecraft client dependencies. VfsPackResourcesBridge exposes a VFS to Minecraft; VfsScopedPackResourcesAdapter supplies the existing scoped resource interfaces.

docs.title: Reading, writing, and metadata
docs.text:
try (DirectoryVfs files = new DirectoryVfs("authoring", authoringDirectory)) {
    VfsPath model = VfsPath.of("assets/demo/models/train.json");
    files.writeString(model, json);
    String contents = files.readString(model);
    VfsNodeStat metadata = files.stat(model);
    VfsNodeStat fingerprint = files.statWithHash(model);
}

stat() is a metadata query and may omit its optional SHA-256. Use statWithHash() when a current content digest is required. Memory files have immutable content versions, so an existing read stream remains stable across subsequent writes. readBytes() returns a defensive copy.

Directory openWrite() streams into a hidden temporary file and publishes on successful close. It checks the destination again at publication, then performs atomic replacement with a same-directory staging fallback. Memory output uses immutable chunks. Both avoid accumulating multiple full-size temporary arrays.

Logical paths use / and reject traversal segments, internal empty segments, control characters, backslashes and colons. Physical directory resolution additionally checks portable filenames and existing symlink ancestors. Archive logical paths can address Minecraft-valid names such as con.json; these names need not be valid physical Windows filenames. The legacy scoped directory adapter continues to accept safe ./ workspace paths.

docs.title: Mounts and transactions
docs.text:
try (InMemoryVfs runtime = new InMemoryVfs("runtime");
     DirectoryVfs pack = new DirectoryVfs("pack", packDirectory);
     MountTableVfs files = new MountTableVfs("assets")) {
    files.mount(VfsPath.of("runtime"), runtime);
    files.mount(VfsPath.of("packs/train"), pack);
    try (VfsWriteTransaction tx = files.beginTransaction()) {
        tx.putString(VfsPath.of("runtime/index.json"), indexJson);
        tx.putString(VfsPath.of("packs/train/model.json"), modelJson);
        tx.commit();
    }
}

Mounts resolve by longest logical prefix, including synthesized parent directories. The returned mount handle owns that specific mount entry; closing an old handle cannot remove a replacement mounted at the same path. Directory moves preserve empty descendants, including across backends. Active mounts and their ancestors are protected against deletion or replacement by a move.

Transactions stage inputs, reserve participating backends in a stable order, apply all operations, and release every reservation before invoking change listeners. A failed preparation or apply restores affected content and internal watch baselines without a successful notification. Directory recovery retains before-images, including empty directories and permissions. If the filesystem prevents recovery, the original error reports recovery failures and retains the backup location.

putStream(path, source) accepts a deferred source whose returned stream is owned and closed by the transaction. Inputs are materialized before any backend reservation; keep them readable until staging completes. Custom backends can implement stage() and reversible prepare() participants. coordinationKey() identifies a shared backend reservation; unsupported coordinated commits fail before applying any participant.

The protocol covers in-process validation and I/O failures. It does not provide power-loss recovery or isolation against external processes rewriting the same files.

docs.title: Changes and resource integration
docs.text:
watch(prefix, listener) / watchAll(listener) return closeable subscriptions. Internal writes emit INTERNAL_WRITE; directory polling emits EXTERNAL_DISK. A mount-table transaction produces one combined notification after all backend locks are released. Callbacks execute synchronously, so expensive reload work should be scheduled by the consumer.

Directory polling remains a strict full-content SHA-256 check, including same-size changes with restored timestamps. It uses streaming buffers and scans outside the state lock, then validates the internal-write version before publication. Under sustained write contention it retries and eventually reserves the original locked scan for progress. Full verification therefore remains linear in total file content; it does not become a metadata-only watcher.

VfsWatchService is optional and uses one daemon polling thread with a fixed delay after each cycle. Close it and its subscriptions with their owning lifecycle. ResourceSystem.getUnifiedVfs() exposes a process-level mount table; use mountScoped(server, ...) / registerManagedCloseable(server, ...) for per-MinecraftServer mounts and mountClientScoped(...) / registerClientManagedCloseable(...) for client-scoped mounts so stopping one server does not tear down client or other server instances' mounts. Read-only ZIP indexes are shared only between adapters for the same open ZipFile instance; a new handle builds a fresh index.

ScopedPackResources.toLogicalPath(...) strips . identity segments uniformly across directory, ZIP (ScopedVanillaFileResourcePack), and VFS (VfsScopedPackResourcesAdapter) packs as well as PackageSystem.scanWorkspace(...), while still rejecting .. traversal and empty path segments. Custom packs backed by a VFS implement VfsBackedPackResources (including VfsPackResourcesBridge and modelling's KsgPackResource), which ScopedResourceManager adapts before PathPackResources / FilePackResources. In modelling, GeneratedShaderResourceProvider serves generated shaders from InMemoryVfs via VfsPackResourcesBridge, and LiveModelSync reads .kasuga-sync.json / pack.mcmeta through DirectoryVfs and ResourceSystem.mountClientScoped(...).

docs.title: Validation and diagnostic benchmarks
docs.text:
Run the regression suites:

./gradlew :modules:core:test :modules:scripting:test :modules:modelling:modelUnitTest

The reported validation has 106 core tests and 70 scripting tests passing with no failures, errors or skips, along with the modelling unit suite (GeneratedShaderResourceProviderTest and LiveModelSyncStateTest passing with 0 failures/errors/skips; 1196 total modelUnitTest tests with 0 failures/errors and 8 pre-existing skipped environment/asset tests). An additional deterministic before/after probe compared 4,600 memory/directory operation states, including rejected transactions, trees, contents and polling results. Windows host execution and full Minecraft GUI performance have not been measured locally.

Build classes and run the checked-in diagnostic harness with the same JDK for each checkout:

./gradlew :modules:core:testClasses :modules:core:writeNeoForgeTestClasspath
python3 scripts/benchmark-vfs.py --scenario main
python3 scripts/benchmark-vfs.py --scenario extra
python3 scripts/benchmark-vfs.py --scenario zip-reuse

Available --scenario values are main, extra, contention, and zip-reuse. Select a JDK with --java /path/to/jdk-21/bin/java or VFS_PERF_JAVA. --repo /path/to/other/checkout uses that checkout's compiled classes while retaining this harness, and --output chooses a separate JSONL result. Do not rebuild the measured class directory while a benchmark is running. The pre-optimization implementation is commit 67ceefe312d52c7c32f776d69ce9e9e0587e3b7c.

The harness uses three warmup batches, nine measurement batches, G1, a 512 MiB initial/1.5 GiB maximum heap, temporary synthetic data, and warm filesystem caches. JSONL includes per-operation batch medians, ranges, CPU time and Java allocations. It is a diagnostic benchmark, not JMH or a game-FPS measurement. Allocation totals are not retained heap or physical I/O.

Representative results on an Apple M3 Max with native Java 21.0.3:

Scenario Before After One 1 KiB transaction in a 10,000-file tree 34.68 ms 0.46 ms File-type query through a mount, 64 MiB file 48.25 ms 0.026 ms Move one byte across two 10,000-file memory mounts 37.88 ms 0.035 ms Reader overlapping a full directory scan 126.87 ms 0.083 ms 64 MiB chunked directory output, allocated heap 192 MiB 0.069 MiB Re-adapt the same open 10,000-file ZIP 11.91 ms 0.0011 ms

The unchanged 250 MiB polling workload took about 122 ms before and 124 ms after; allocations fell from about 253 MiB to 1.77 MiB. Some already short writes have additional constant overhead. These results cover the same 78 original scenarios plus the same-handle ZIP scenario; they do not imply every operation becomes faster. The reader probe starts after the scan worker has consumed 5 ms of CPU, and was rerun with that same observation method against both versions.

docs.title: Sky Volumetric Clouds and Cumulonimbus Instances
docs.text:
Interfaces, configuration, and call reference. For the mechanics see volumetric-clouds.md.

Volumetric clouds are a separate optional feature, off by default. CloudEffects.setEnabled(true) automatically draws a sky cloud field spread around the observer position, and hides the vanilla block clouds in the main view and in standalone camera views at the same time. Turning it off restores the previous cloud settings; the toggle neither modifies nor saves the user's vanilla cloud options. Leaving the world turns it off automatically. Dimensions without a vanilla cloud layer do not draw the sky cloud field.

docs.title: Enabling the sky cloud field
docs.text:
import lib.kasuga.rendering.cloud.SkyCloudSettings;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.effect.builtin.cloud.CloudEffects;

CloudEffects.sky().settings(SkyCloudSettings.DEFAULT);
CloudEffects.setSkyEnabled(true);
CloudEffects.setEnabled(true);

// Coverage, seed, and quality are adjustable at runtime; a change of wind speed does not teleport existing cloud clusters.
CloudEffects.sky().settings(CloudEffects.sky().settings()
        .withQuality(SkyCloudSettings.Quality.FAST));
CloudEffects.setEnabled(false);

The cloud field stacks 1–4 independent continuous density layers. Low cumulus layers have rolling tops, dark cloud bases, and varying development heights; mid-level cloud decks spread into sheets, and high thin clouds stretch into bands. Weather regions control cloud clusters, cloud gaps, and thickness variation; cloud bodies can cross weather grid boundaries, connect, or overlap, and are no longer arranged one per cell. A small number of cumulonimbus clouds that use independent shape envelopes are kept in the low layers.

The default three cloud layers have cloud base Y values of 900, 2700, and 5400, with thicknesses of 2100, 900, and 600. These values are adjustable scene scales; cumulus and cumulonimbus can also extend to the heights of other layers. The SCATTERED, CLOUDY, and OVERCAST presets use coverage controls of .38, .80, and .98 respectively: scattered cloud keeps large areas of clear sky, cloudy weather connects the cloud clusters, and overcast forms a continuous sheet.

SkyCloudSettings parameters are the seed, weather cell size, raw cloud base, maximum cumulonimbus thickness, coverage control, maximum display distance, X/Z wind speed, quality, a layer list, and rendering controls. The nine-parameter constructor generates three default layers from the cloud base and thickness. The actual height of each layer is controlled by SkyCloudLayer, and the list can contain several layers of the same type; changing the quality, coverage, or seed keeps the layer list. Wind speed uses world units per second. coverage=0 hides the clouds completely in clear weather, and rain increases the coverage; the sun direction, day/night, and weather colors come from the world.

Each layer separately controls the type, cloud base, thickness, horizontal shape scale, coverage offset, and optical density. Coverage and density are set separately, so a single cloud still keeps a sense of solidity even under scattered cover. A density of zero hides that layer, including the cumulonimbus embedded in it. The configuration can be replaced at runtime:

import java.util.List;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.cloud.SkyCloudLayer;

CloudEffects.sky().settings(SkyCloudSettings.CLOUDY.withLayers(List.of(
        new SkyCloudLayer(SkyCloudLayer.Type.CUMULUS, 900, 2100, 5200, 0, 2),
        new SkyCloudLayer(SkyCloudLayer.Type.STRATIFORM, 2700, 900, 3400, -.08f, 1.5f),
        new SkyCloudLayer(SkyCloudLayer.Type.CIRRUS, 5400, 600, 8000, -.12f, .55f))));

Each observer position uses a 32×32 weather window. The window relocates with the observer position, and clouds in the overlapping part stay unchanged; a standalone camera view can observe its own local window at a distant position. Near the world border, the camera position is first subtracted in double, then converted to GPU coordinates. Frame.weatherCellCount() only counts the candidate occupancy of weather control cells; a continuous cloud body has no per-cloud numbering, and that statistic cannot represent the on-screen coverage either. Each layer generates its weather independently.

SkyCloudRendering controls extinction, erosion, detail frequency, forward/backward scattering, approximate multiple scattering, ambient light, sample counts, resolution, debug views, color space, and temporal accumulation. Extinction uses inverse world units; zero sampling or resolution values select the quality preset. Settings can change at runtime:

import lib.kasuga.rendering.cloud.SkyCloudRendering;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.cloud.SkyCloudTemporal;

var rendering = SkyCloudRendering.DEFAULT
        .withDensityDetail(.009f, .12f, 4)
        .withScattering(.55f, -.25f, .15f, .5f, 1)
        .withSampling(160, 4, 2, true)
        .withTemporal(SkyCloudTemporal.STABLE);
CloudEffects.sky().settings(CloudEffects.sky().settings()
        .withWind(8, 3).withRendering(rendering));

SkyCloudTemporal.STABLE defaults to weight .65, a maximum time gap of .2 seconds, camera displacement of 16 blocks, and relative depth tolerance .05; OFF disables history. withDebug(...) selects DENSITY, TRANSMITTANCE, RADIANCE, MARCH_STEPS, or HISTORY_VALIDITY; NONE restores the normal image. withColorSpace(...) selects DISPLAY_SRGB or LINEAR_HDR and should match the host target's color space.

docs.title: Creating a single cumulonimbus
docs.text:
The single-cloud API is kept; it can be used together with the sky cloud field, or with the field turned off to observe a single cloud:

import lib.kasuga.rendering.cloud.CloudPose;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.cloud.CloudSettings;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.effect.builtin.cloud.CumulonimbusCloud;

var cloud = new CumulonimbusCloud(CloudPose.at(100, 900, 1800).withYaw(20),
        CloudSettings.CUMULONIMBUS);
var handle = CloudEffects.spawn(cloud);
CloudEffects.setSkyEnabled(false);  // Observe only explicitly created instances
CloudEffects.setEnabled(true);
cloud.wind(.6, 0, .2);
cloud.moveBy(20, 0, 0);
cloud.rotateBy(30);                // Around the world Y axis, in degrees
cloud.scale(1.2f, 1, 1.2f);
cloud.settings(CloudSettings.CUMULONIMBUS.withCoverage(.75f));
handle.remove();
cloud.close();
CloudEffects.setEnabled(false);

A single cloud's position is the center of its base; the default size is 1600 wide, 1200 high, and 1200 deep. CloudSettings controls density, extinction, erosion, coverage, the anvil, seed, and quality. Direct transforms take effect immediately; wind and internal noise advance only with the client tick and stop when paused; the main view and several camera views sample the same moment and do not advance animation by render count.

docs.title: Rendering and cost
docs.text:
The cloud field uses one ray-marching pass covering the sky and one compositing draw, and does not create a fullscreen pass per cloud. It first intersects the ray with the height interval of each layer, sorts and merges overlapping intervals, and skips the gaps between layers directly. The sample budget is allocated by the square root of the interval length, so high thin clouds are not starved of budget by low layers and disappear; the densities of several layers at the same point are summed. The total number of samples per ray is limited by the budget, and the march ends early when the transmittance is very low. The weather window and the GPU textures use a cache of at most 8 entries, so travelling does not make memory grow continuously.

A shared shape texture preserves the cloud tower and anvil envelopes of the cumulonimbus; periodically generated Perlin-Worley/Worley noise provides the body, rolling, and erosion of the continuous layers. Each layer uses its own weather, noise phase, and shape scale, and thin clouds use a stretched anisotropic shape. Quadratically spaced light intervals integrate to layer exits for soft self-shadowing. Beer–Lambert extinction accumulates premultiplied radiance and transmittance; dual Henyey–Greenstein lobes control forward/backward scattering. Three approximate scattering orders progressively halve extinction and anisotropy with normalized energy. a single cumulonimbus uses a cached lighting voxel atlas, usually updated every 0.25 seconds.

For the cloud field, FAST/BALANCED/HIGH use width and height resolutions of 1/3, 1/2, and 1 of the original viewport, respectively; the total budget per ray is 112/160/256 samples, with 2/4/6 light samples. For single-cloud quality, the corresponding resolutions are 1/3, 1/2, and 1, with at most 48/80/128 fine steps. Low-resolution results are upscaled with conservative depth and depth-aware interpolation. Both paths clip at the opaque scene depth, write no depth, do not limit the sky clouds by the terrain far plane, and restore the host GL state.

RGBA16F stores radiance/opacity and RG32F stores extinction-weighted mean cloud distance plus the scene-ray endpoint. Stable view IDs enable independent ping-pong histories. Reprojection compensates camera movement and wind, rejects incompatible depth/endpoints, boundaries, time, lighting and settings, and clamps history to the current 3×3 neighborhood. Teleports, world changes, resize and lighting discontinuities reset history; at most eight views are cached. Anonymous views or historyWeight=0 keep the independent spatial path, and empty current rays never resurrect old cloud silhouettes. Resize replaces and releases old history targets; cache eviction, world changes, and renderer shutdown also release history textures.

Composition snapshots host color and evaluates Lcloud + Tcloud * Lscene in linear light. The default explicitly decodes and encodes display sRGB; linear HDR mode does not tone-map or clamp radiance. The host owns final exposure.

Distant views add atmospheric perspective and distance fade. There is currently no long-range cross-cloud shadowing, no ground cloud shadows, and no complete weather simulation; compositing with transparent objects such as water follows render stages. The extra gbuffer channels of an Iris shader pack are not yet verified, and acceptance with the shader pack disabled cannot be used to infer its compatibility.

docs.title: Examples and verification
docs.text:
Development client:

  • /ksglib debug cloud enables the whole sky cloud field.
  • /ksglib debug cloud sparse switches to a sparse, multi-layer scattered-cloud state.
  • /ksglib debug cloud dense switches to a cloudy state with connected cloud clusters.
  • /ksglib debug cloud overcast switches to a continuous sheet.
  • /ksglib debug cloud single places a cumulonimbus in front and turns the sky cloud field off.
  • /ksglib debug cloud stop turns volumetric clouds off and restores the vanilla clouds.

Standalone preview, without starting Minecraft:

./gradlew :modules:modelling:renderPreview -PkasugaRenderScene=sky \
  -PkasugaRenderWidth=1920 -PkasugaRenderHeight=1080 --offline --no-daemon

The arrow keys change the view direction, W/S fly, and Escape exits. -PkasugaRenderFrames=60 ends automatically and saves the preview image; -PkasugaRenderScene=cloud keeps the original orbit preview of a single cumulonimbus. Images and reports are in modules/modelling/build/reports/renderHarness/.

./gradlew renderingReleaseCheck :modules:modelling:renderGlTest --offline --no-daemon
./gradlew :modules:modelling:renderBench -PkasugaRenderScene=sky \
  -PkasugaRenderWidth=1280 -PkasugaRenderHeight=720 \
  -PkasugaRenderWarmup=20 -PkasugaRenderFrames=60 --offline --no-daemon

The benchmark uses GL_TIME_ELAPSED and covers the depth copy, the complete cloud field, and compositing, across ground, scattered cloud, overcast, inside the cloud layer, rain, and a distant observer position. This is GPU time for a standalone scene and cannot be converted into a full Minecraft frame FPS.

On 2026-11-09, on an Apple M3 Max using OpenGL 4.1 Metal, 1280×720, with 20 warm-up frames and 60 sampled frames:

View / state GPU P50 GPU P95 FAST ground 2.05 ms 2.35 ms BALANCED ground 5.86 ms 6.43 ms BALANCED sparse 3.67 ms 4.22 ms BALANCED inside 6.80 ms 9.01 ms BALANCED temporal 5.89 ms 6.39 ms HIGH ground 25.91 ms 29.38 ms HIGH inside 44.66 ms 50.57 ms

The HIGH setting is substantially more expensive in the dense and inside views, so BALANCED remains the practical default. The values come from a standalone run of renderBench; the report is at build/reports/renderHarness/bench/report.json, relative to the module directory.

The pure-JVM regression checks per-layer weather independence, configuration immutability, weather continuity, spatial overlap, wind and interpolation, world-border precision, and cache boundaries. The GPU regression of the production shader checks the on-screen coverage difference between scattered and overcast, the separate visibility of each layer, the budget error relative to double sampling, several directions, distant/inside/above viewpoints, occlusion, relocation continuity, state restoration, and caching, and keeps the single-cloud regression.

Client acceptance in a temporary world uses -PkasugaTestSkyCloud=true, verifying a real camera near and 40000 units away, the main frame, the shared clock, and restoration of the vanilla cloud toggle. The success log is SKY_CLOUD_SMOKE_PASS, and the reports and screenshots are in debug/sky-cloud/ under the game directory. -PkasugaTestCloud=true keeps the single-cloud acceptance. These switches are only for purpose-built temporary test worlds.

docs.title: World UI and Free-Cursor Input
docs.text: Package: lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.backend.ui. Call these APIs on the Minecraft client thread. For coordinate transforms and input ownership, see the design. For Create attachments, see Scenes and UI on moving structures.

docs.title: Integrating an Existing Screen
docs.text:
Minecraft mc = Minecraft.getInstance();
UIBackend backend = Constants.UI_BACKEND; // Available after client setup.
Screen panel = new MyPanelScreen();
panel.init(mc, 320, 180); // Panel-local dimensions, independent of the input viewport.

// Center the panel 2.5 blocks ahead of the camera, 1.92 blocks wide. Local +Y points down.
var camera = mc.gameRenderer.getMainCamera();
var center = camera.getPosition().add(
        camera.getLookVector().x * 2.5,
        camera.getLookVector().y * 2.5,
        camera.getLookVector().z * 2.5);
Matrix4f localToWorld = new Matrix4f()
        .translation((float) center.x, (float) center.y, (float) center.z)
        .rotate(camera.rotation())
        .scale(.006f, -.006f, 1)
        .translate(-160, -90, 0);
backend.addRenderable(panel, localToWorld);
backend.openPointer();

The built-in world_ui pipeline renders Constants.UI_BACKEND at AFTER_LEVEL in the main view. Call openPointer() from gameplay with a player, a world, and no other Screen active, for example from a key binding. A chat command must finish the chat Screen first, as the development demo does with mc.setScreen(null). The method returns the WorldUiInputScreen submitted to Minecraft.setScreen; other mods may still cancel screen opening.

The input Screen draws no background and does not pause the world. Minecraft's Screen lifecycle releases the mouse. Escape closes the input layer and restores mouse-look. The panel remains registered and returns to crosshair interaction. Call removeRenderable(panel) to remove it. Registrations belong to the backend and survive world changes; callers must remove world-specific panels when leaving their world.

In normal mouse-look, clicking an EditBox or MultiLineEditBox with the crosshair temporarily captures the keyboard. Characters reach the text field while gameplay movement and shortcuts are suppressed; the mouse still rotates the view. Escape clears text focus and exits without opening the pause menu. Repeats/releases from keys still held at exit are consumed; fresh presses resume gameplay. Buttons, disabled/hidden fields, and read-only fields do not start capture. World changes, window focus loss, another Screen, or target removal also end capture.

A panel with its own widget tree can implement WorldUiTextInput and report editable text focus through hasTextInputFocus(). It must clear internal focus when setFocused(false) is called, so Escape, target removal and panel changes can end editing. The shared backend remains independent of third-party widget libraries. LDLib2's LdElement.attach(backend, ui, width, height, transform) implements this contract and owns ticking, closing and world-boundary cleanup; see the LDLib2 world-UI adapter and demo.

A panel Screen can use its normal child-widget focus, keyboard, and text handling. Override the panel's own renderBackground if it should be transparent; its appearance is separate from the input layer. World rendering temporarily disables panel blur and then restores its previous value.

Widgets first render into a transparent RGBA canvas with the normal orthographic GUI depth range. The canvas is then drawn once on the world plane, preserving the small depth separation between text and shadows. Canvas density follows GUI scale, targets resize when needed, and local scissor rectangles use canvas dimensions. Premultiplied-alpha composition preserves translucent edges and does not write the panel rectangle into world depth. MIN_GUI_Z, MAX_GUI_Z, and boundary text shadows affect only canvas ordering. Composite vertices always use local Z=0, so GUI depth cannot push the panel towards the player. Canvas clipping reserves one extra unit beyond each GUI depth endpoint.

docs.title: API and Contracts
docs.text:
API Behavior addRenderable(Renderable) Centers the default panel at the world origin, using GUI height as pixels per block; duplicate registration does not duplicate drawing addRenderable(Renderable, Matrix4fc) Registers the panel and copies its pixel-local to absolute-world transform setTransform(Renderable, Matrix4fc) Sets or updates a transform; rejects non-finite, non-affine, or singular matrices removeRenderable(Renderable) Stops rendering and releases that target's captured mouse buttons and keys openPointer() Opens the input Screen; throws IllegalStateException without a player/world or while another Screen is active getInputRouter().setMaxDistance(float) Maximum hit distance from the rendered near plane, default 5 blocks; requires a finite positive value worldChanged() Clears input and GPU canvases, removes moving-host panels and retains static registrations; the global backend uses the existing world-change hook close() Clears input, canvases, and registrations; custom backend owners must call it on destruction resetInput() Clears hover, keyboard focus, and captures, balancing held mouse buttons and keys with release events isKeyboardCaptured() Whether normal-view text keyboard capture is active WorldUiTextInput.hasTextInputFocus() A third-party panel reports editable text focus in its own widget tree and clears that state on focus loss renderAllUis(GuiGraphics, float) Custom world-render entry using the current world projection and effective model-view; do not call during the HUD orthographic pass renderWorld(WorldRenderPipelineContext) World-pipeline entry for a custom backend; saves/restores projection and model-view and accepts only the main view

Screen.width/height or the position and size of a LayoutElement define the input rectangle. Objects without GuiEventListener or known dimensions only render. Plane intersection reuses RayTracingHelper.intersectRayWithPlane. The nearest rectangle receives input; ties follow registration order. Picking does not test block occlusion or texture alpha.

The transparent layer consumes incoming mouse, scroll, and keyboard events, including misses, so they do not operate the world. Keyboard input goes to the last clicked panel, whose normal child dispatch selects the widget. Escape always exits. An accepted mouse press captures its target per button. Dragging outside the rectangle continues to project onto that panel's plane, and release returns to the original target. Parallel rays or intersections behind the ray origin retain the last valid capture coordinates. Window focus loss, screen replacement, target removal, dimension changes, and disconnect cancel captures.

docs.title: Reusing an Existing Raycast
docs.text:
Use the projection component independently when the host already has a world-space hit solver:

var projection = new ScreenPointerProjection(worldProjection, guiWidth, guiHeight);
Vector3f origin = new Vector3f(), direction = new Vector3f();
if (projection.ray(mouseGuiX, mouseGuiY, origin, direction)) {
    // If viewMatrix includes camera translation, inverseView restores absolute world coordinates.
    inverseView.transformPosition(origin);
    inverseView.transformDirection(direction).normalize();
    existingRaycast(origin, direction);
}

When the view matrix contains only camera rotation, apply its inverse and then add the camera world position to origin. ray produces a unit ray starting on the near plane, supporting perspective and orthographic cameras. Coordinates are GUI logical pixels with (0,0) at the top left. Convert raw GLFW/window cursor coordinates using guiWidth / screenWidth and guiHeight / screenHeight; do not mix framebuffer dimensions with window coordinates. The constructor copies and validates the projection and viewport, throwing IllegalArgumentException for invalid values. Non-finite cursor coordinates make ray return false. Capture the rendered projection again after FOV, zoom, or viewport changes.

docs.title: Development Acceptance
docs.text:
./gradlew :modules:modelling:modelUnitTest --tests 'lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.backend.ui.*' --offline
./gradlew :modules:modelling:compileContentTestingJava --offline
./gradlew :modules:modelling:runClient

In a test world, run /ksglib debug world_ui. A panel is fixed in front of the camera at its opening pose, and the free cursor opens immediately. Click both sides, type in the text field, scroll, drag outside the panel, and release. Check the counters and local drag deltas. Press Escape, turn the camera, and check crosshair interaction. Run the command again to rebuild the panel and reopen the cursor. /ksglib debug world_ui stop removes it.

After leaving the free cursor, crosshair-click the text field and type WASD/Chinese. Text should change without moving the player, while the mouse still rotates the view. Hold W, press Escape, then release and press W again: editing exits first, and the fresh press restores movement. Buttons must not capture the keyboard. Run /ksglib debug world_ui min_z and /ksglib debug world_ui max_z to check complete glyphs/shadows and unchanged panel distance; both presets use the same world transform as the default.

Check that text, shadows, button borders, and edit-box borders have no stripes or missing fragments. Enter long ASCII and Chinese text to check clipping, then stop the demo and verify world, hand, and HUD rendering.

Window resizing, GUI scale, FOV, third-person views, and focus changes require real-client acceptance. JVM tests cover projection math and routing state; they do not replace in-game rendering or GLFW verification.

With an existing isolated test world, run the real keyboard Mixin/character and GUI-depth pixel smoke:

./gradlew :modules:modelling:runClientHeadless --offline \
  -PkasugaClientDirectory=run/world-ui-smoke -PkasugaQuickPlayWorld=TestWorld \
  -PkasugaTestWorldUiInput=true

Place TestWorld under that run directory's saves/. The test uses a hidden window and exits on completion; JSON and PNG output is in debug/world-ui-input/ under the run directory. It does not cover OS input-method candidate windows or the feel of player interaction.

docs.title: Data-Driven Registration
docs.text:
Trap: the old layout does not match the current implementation. The layout described by earlier upstream docs is data/<modid>/kasugalib/*.json (flat files, a sources field), which is deprecated. The current contract is the index directory data/<modid>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/ plus content directories (such as data/<modid>/kasuga_lib_content/ or any path declared relative to data/<modid>/).

The current tree ships two registration entry points: the v2 host-managed multi-source build pipeline (DataDrivenRegistrationProviders + ContentSourceFactory.snapshot + DataDrivenBuildPipeline) and the legacy single-mod JAR path (JsonTreeBuilder.buildForMod).

Reference pages (this directory):

Document Type Content schema.en.md Reference Index and content fields, built-in proxy_model / proxy_model_be schema, STRICT vs LEGACY behavior, D1–D6 rules, and error classification shapes.en.md Reference Shape definitions, expressions, inheritance, references, transforms, and diagnostics block-state-properties.en.md Reference Block-state declarations, vanilla properties, and custom factories api-registration.en.md Reference v2 host providers and build pipeline (DataDrivenRegistrationProviders, ContentSourceFactory, SnapshotContentSource, DataDrivenBuildPipeline, BuildOptions, BuildResult, DataDrivenBuildHooks), plus legacy JsonTreeBuilder, index API, dispatch, and conflict resolution api-extension.en.md Reference TypeHandler, HandlerCapability (including OVERLAY), DefinitionKey, RegistryClaim, ValidationContext, BuildContext, FactoryRegistry, and property parsers api-diagnostics.en.md Reference Diagnostics, /kasuga_data, BuildDiagnostic, /kasuga_proxy list, and error classification api-reload.en.md Reference ReloadOrchestrator, ReloadHandler, ManagedReloadAllowlist, the assertable pure-function surface, and call examples

docs.title: Data-Driven Diagnostics API (Diagnostics, Commands, and Error Classification)
6. The Diagnostics Facade
docs.text:
diagnostics/Diagnostics.java is the unified diagnostics facade shared by the v1 registration path and the reload domain. Errors are addressed along two dimensions that never mix:

v1/reload buckets vs. v2 BuildDiagnostic: Diagnostics backs v1 JsonTreeBuilder and ReloadOrchestrator / FsmReloadHandler (and is surfaced by /kasuga_data errors). The v2 multi-source DataDrivenBuildPipeline instead returns structured List<BuildDiagnostic> values on PreparedContent.diagnostics() and BuildResult.diagnostics() (see section 19), and does not write into Diagnostics.

docs.title: 6.1 Dimensions
docs.text:
• mod dimension: buckets keyed by mod id, which are the existing JsonTreeBuilder buckets. report(String, Throwable) and errors(String) delegate to them verbatim, keeping "assert JsonTreeBuilder.getLoadingErrors(modId) is empty" intact.
  • domain/source-key dimension: buckets keyed by (Domain, key), for failures that belong to a source rather than a mod. Reload producers already write here: the reload domain uses Domain.RELOAD_DATA keyed by namespace (ReloadOrchestrator and FsmReloadHandler). RELOAD_ASSETS and CONFIG remain reserved.

docs.title: 6.2 Method Table
docs.text:
mod dimension:

Signature Responsibility Failure behavior report(String modId, Throwable error) (:64) Records one failure into the mod bucket, equivalent to JsonTreeBuilder.addLoadingError No validation errors(String modId) (:73) Immutable snapshot for that mod Returns List.of() when empty errorsByMod() (:78) All mods, keys sorted by id, immutable Returns an empty map when empty clear(String modId) (:83) Clears that mod's bucket only Other mods and source buckets are untouched

domain/source-key dimension:

Signature Responsibility Failure behavior report(Domain domain, String key, Throwable error) (:96) Records one failure into a source bucket Throws NullPointerException if any argument is null errors(Domain domain, String key) (:107) Immutable snapshot of one source bucket Returns List.of() when empty errors(Domain domain) (:116) Aggregate across all sources of a domain, sorted by key Returns an empty list when empty clear(Domain domain) (:125) Clears all source buckets of one domain Other domains and mod buckets are untouched

Shared by both dimensions:

Signature Responsibility clearAll() (:130) Clears both dimensions summarize() (:143) One line per non-empty bucket, see 6.4

docs.title: 6.3 Domain
docs.text:
public enum Domain { REGISTRATION, RELOAD_DATA, RELOAD_ASSETS, CONFIG }   // Diagnostics.java:40
Value Meaning REGISTRATION Mod jar registration content (reserved in domain dimension) RELOAD_DATA Reload data from data packs, read from the pack stack on /reload RELOAD_ASSETS Pack-stack assets (reserved) CONFIG Files under config/ (reserved)

docs.title: 6.4 summarize Output Format
docs.text:
public static List<String> summarize()   // Diagnostics.java:143

One line per non-empty bucket: mod buckets format as <mod>: N error(s); source buckets format as <DOMAIN>[<key>]: N error(s). Mods come first sorted by id, then Domain declaration order with sources sorted by key.

docs.title: 6.5 Which Dimension Producers Use
docs.text: Reload-domain errors go to the domain/source-key dimension (Domain.RELOAD_DATA) keyed by the namespace owning the file. ReloadOrchestrator.reportError (:617-627) and handler reporters (FsmReloadHandler.java:118-130) call Diagnostics.report(Domain.RELOAD_DATA, namespace, ...). v1 registration errors go to the mod dimension. Labels come from Diagnostics.bucketLabel (:166): [<mod>] <error> vs. [RELOAD_DATA[<namespace>]] <error>. The reload dimension is cleared at the start of every runCycle (Diagnostics.clear(Domain.RELOAD_DATA), ReloadOrchestrator.java:208).

docs.title: 7. The /kasuga_data errors Command
docs.text:
DataDiagnosticsCommands.java exposes the Diagnostics facade in-game (see 19.2 for /kasuga_proxy list).

public static LiteralArgumentBuilder<CommandSourceStack> kasugaDataCommand()   // DataDiagnosticsCommands.java:45

Command syntax:

  • /kasuga_data errors (printSummary, :63): prints the per-bucket Diagnostics.summarize() summary covering both dimensions, or Kasuga data: no loading errors recorded when clean.
  • /kasuga_data errors <mod> (printMod, :81): lists both the mod dimension ([<mod>] <throwable>) and the RELOAD_DATA[<mod>] source dimension ([RELOAD_DATA[<mod>]] <throwable>), or Kasuga data: no loading errors for '<mod>'.

Constraints and registration:

  • Requires permission level 2 (requires(source -> source.hasPermission(2)), :47).
  • kasugaDataCommand() has no dispatcher or event dependency, allowing pure unit tests to verify command shape.
  • Auto-registered on COMMON via @EventBusSubscriber (:31) and onRegisterCommands (:57); returns the number of printed lines.

docs.title: 12. Error Classification (v1 Registration Buckets and Reload Domain)
docs.text:
This table covers diagnostics written to Diagnostics buckets or downgraded to logs (see section 19 for v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline structured diagnostics).

Bucketed errors (logged at ERROR and appended as Throwable — mod dimension in v1 registration, Domain.RELOAD_DATA in reload):

Case Source Index file unreadable or not JSON JsonTreeBuilder.readIndexManifest:194-204 Unknown top-level field in an index (including removed sources) JsonTreeBuilder.parseIndexManifest:231-238 Neither on_register nor on_reload declared JsonTreeBuilder.parseIndexManifest:247-253 Non-array path field or non-string array element JsonTreeBuilder.readPathArray:263-279 Same path listed in both on_register and on_reload (fail-closed) JsonTreeBuilder.resolveIndexManifests:330-345 No index declares either domain JsonTreeBuilder.resolveIndexManifests:347-352 Index directory cannot be listed JsonTreeBuilder.listIndexFiles:783-795 Illegal content path JsonTreeBuilder.parseSource:420-426 Mod file not found JsonTreeBuilder.parseSource:432-438 Content file missing JsonTreeBuilder.parseSource:447-452 Content file read / JSON exception JsonTreeBuilder.parseSource:458-461 Unknown top-level field in content (including top-level block_entities) JsonTreeBuilder.dispatchContent:496-518 Type field is not an array or element is not an object JsonTreeBuilder.dispatchContent:523-535 Embedded extraction failure JsonTreeBuilder.dispatchContent:554-560 Single-entry parse throws JsonTreeBuilder.parseAndCollect:613-620 handler.apply throws JsonTreeBuilder.applyUnchecked:733-742 Duplicate id conflict JsonTreeBuilder.resolveDuplicates:688-692 Legacy layout directory present JsonTreeBuilder.buildForMod:83 buildAll exception for a single mod JsonTreeBuilder.buildAll:177-181 Reload decode/register/validate failure ReloadOrchestrator.reportError:617-627, FsmReloadHandler.reportError:118-121 Reload attempts to load an index not permitted by ManagedReloadAllowlist ReloadOrchestrator.collectIndex:430-434 Reload wrap-up finds a dangling clip reference FsmReloadHandler.reportWarning:127-130

docs.title: 19. v2 Structured BuildDiagnostic and Proxy Diagnostics
19.1 BuildDiagnostic
docs.text:
The v2 multi-source DataDrivenBuildPipeline replaces global exception buckets with immutable pipeline/BuildDiagnostic.java:9-76 records attached to PreparedContent.diagnostics() and BuildResult.diagnostics():

public record BuildDiagnostic(
        Severity severity,
        Stage stage,
        Code code,
        @Nullable String sourceId,
        @Nullable String ownerId,
        @Nullable String logicalPath,
        @Nullable String jsonPointer,
        @Nullable String handler,
        String message,
        @Nullable String suggestion
) {
    public boolean blocking() { return severity == Severity.ERROR; }
    public enum Severity { WARNING, ERROR }
    public enum Stage { SOURCE, MANIFEST, PARSE, SELECTION, VALIDATION, CLAIMS, APPLY, FINALIZE }
    public enum Code { ... }
}

All 25 BuildDiagnostic.Code constants grouped by Stage:

Stage Code values Meaning SOURCE INVALID_SOURCE, UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY, SOURCE_FILE_MISSING, SOURCE_READ_FAILED Duplicate (sourceId, rootId) or rank, unknown dependency owner, missing content file referenced by manifest, or snapshot/I/O read error MANIFEST MANIFEST_INVALID, MANIFEST_EMPTY, INVALID_PATH Non-object manifest, D1–D6 violation (including removed sources key or dual-listed path), invalid LogicalPath, or zero declared on_register/on_reload paths PARSE CONTENT_INVALID, UNKNOWN_TYPE, PARSE_FAILED, IDENTITY_FAILED, MISSING_IDENTITY, HANDLER_NOT_STRICT_READY StrictResourceJson syntax/duplicate-key error, unknown top-level key, on_reload preflight decode error, TypeHandler.parse failure, resolveIdentity throw or null/blank return, or used handler failing strict capability checks VALIDATION INVALID_IDENTITY, UNKNOWN_FACTORY, UNKNOWN_REGISTRY_GROUP, MISSING_REFERENCE, REFERENCE_NOT_DECLARED, REFERENCE_AMBIGUOUS, GROUP_CYCLE, VALIDATION_FAILED Bare/invalid ResourceLocation, missing factory, unknown registry_group, missing or undeclared cross-definition reference, ambiguous visible matches (findAllVisible.size() > 1), parentDefinition cycle (ERROR in STRICT, WARNING in LEGACY), or strict property/param check failure CLAIMS CLAIM_CONFLICT, CLAIM_FAILED Two definitions competing for the same (registry, id), collision with reservedRegistryClaims, or TypeHandler.claims exception APPLY / FINALIZE APPLY_FAILED, FINALIZER_FAILED Runtime exception thrown by apply or BuildFinalizer.afterBuild (also transitioning BuildResult.status() to Status.FAILED)

docs.title: 19.2 /kasuga_proxy list and ProxyDebug
docs.text:
For runtime inspection of proxy-rendered hosts (including proxy_model / proxy_model_be), modules/modelling exposes:

  • In-game command /kasuga_proxy list (ProxyCommands.java:40-76, auto-registered via @EventBusSubscriber on both sides):
  • Permission level 0 (source.hasPermission(0) — usable in dev worlds without cheats).
  • Prints [proxy] instances=N live=L mounted=M, followed by up to 64 (MAX_LINES) ProxyInstance.describe() lines (ProxyInstance.java:410-420): 
    <identity|<unresolved>> side=client|server|? element=<class> stage=NEW|LIVE|FAILED|RELEASED machine=<id> model=<loc> [parts=M/T] mounted=<bool> lastTick=never|<gameTime>
  • Field interpretation: NEW = not yet ticked, FAILED = ElementProxy#configure returned null or threw, LIVE with mounted=false = client-side model publishing or loader rejection, lastTick=never = proxy is not being ticked.
  • Verbose tracing flag -Dkasuga.proxy.debug=true (ProxyDebug.java:20-49): [proxy] trace lines normally emit at DEBUG (logs/debug.log); setting ProxyDebug.PROPERTY promotes them to INFO (latest.log and console).

Other pages in the data-driven section: Registration API · Extension API · Diagnostics API · Reload API · Schema Reference · Block State Properties · Section index

}
Method Responsibility and constraints Failure behavior getTypeName() Top-level JSON field name; unique in TypeHandlerRegistry (v1), and duplicates are rejected by v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline In v1, a later registration with the same name silently overrides an earlier one; in v2 STRICT mode, emits HANDLER_NOT_STRICT_READY getPhase() Apply phase order: PHASE_GROUPS(0) → PHASE_CONTENT(1) → PHASE_EMBEDDED(2) None parse(json) Turn a JSON object into a definition object Recommended to be a pure function; v1 skips the entry into the error bucket; v2 emits PARSE_FAILED apply(definition, context) Register the definition into the registration tree or build context In v1, exceptions are caught by applyUnchecked and bucketed; in v2, exceptions abort the build with Status.FAILED capabilities() v2 capability flags for strict preflight, registry claims, and multi-source retention (see 8.8) Defaults to empty Set.of(); triggers HANDLER_NOT_STRICT_READY if used under BuildOptions.STRICT strictValidationImplemented() Explicit confirmation in v2 that strict validate logic is implemented (declaring STRICT_PREFLIGHT alone is insufficient) Defaults to false; emits HANDLER_NOT_STRICT_READY under STRICT unless overridden to return true validate(definition, context) v2 STRICT preflight run only during prepare; must have no registration side effects Reports BuildDiagnostic entries via ValidationContext.error/warning claims(definition, context) v2 declaration of all Minecraft registry ResourceLocation keys this definition will occupy (see 8.8) Produces CLAIM_CONFLICT or CLAIM_FAILED under BuildOptions.STRICT parentDefinition(definition) v2 parent DefinitionKey used for GROUP_CYCLE detection and topological ordering in stableApplyOrder Defaults to null (no explicit parent edge) getParentTypeName() Non-null indicates an embedded type; value is the parent top-level field name null means a top-level type getEmbeddedKeyName() Key name of the embedded type inside a parent entry, for diagnostic hints null omits that key hint from diagnostics extractEmbedded(parentJson) Extract embedded JSON objects from a parent entry Returning null yields no embedded items; never participates in top-level dispatch resolveIdentity(modId, definition) Identity string used for deduplication / selection Default null opts out of deduplication resolveIdentity(modId, definition, strict) Mode-aware identity resolution (RegTypeHandler uses EffectiveId.of when strict=true vs ofLegacy) Defaults to calling the 2-arg overload

public static Collection<TypeHandler<?>> all();                     // :19
public static TypeHandler<?> findByParent(String parentType);       // :23
  • Global static LinkedHashMap shared by all mods in v1 (JsonTreeBuilder), with no namespace isolation. all() returns an immutable registration-order view, and findByParent returns only the first match.
  • v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline does not read TypeHandlerRegistry implicitly; the host explicitly passes a Collection<? extends TypeHandler<?>> (for example after calling JsonTreeBuilder.ensureHandlersRegistered() and reading TypeHandlerRegistry.all()).

docs.title: 8.3 Top-level vs embedded
docs.text: A top-level type occupies one top-level JSON field (such as blocks, items, registry_groups). An embedded type occupies no top-level field and enters only via extractEmbedded. BlockEntityTypeHandler (getParentTypeName() = "blocks", getEmbeddedKeyName() = "block_entity", BlockEntityTypeHandler.java:48-51) copies the parent block's id into _parent_block (:54-67) and retrieves the parent BlockReg via context.getBlockReg(...) during apply (:137-170). Writing block_entities as a top-level field causes both v1 (dispatchContent) and v2 (DataDrivenBuildPipeline) to report it as an unknown top-level field and suggest moving it under blocks[].block_entity, while remaining valid fields continue dispatching.

docs.title: 8.4 RegTypeHandler
docs.text:
handler/RegTypeHandler.java is the abstract base class shared by blocks and items, encapsulating identity normalization, strict preflight, registry claims, and apply logic:

protected abstract String resolveRawId(T definition);                                    // :26
protected abstract Reg<?, ?> createRegistration(T definition, String path);              // :28
protected String resolveType(T definition) { return getTypeName(); }                     // :35
protected void configureTypeSpecific(T definition, Reg<?, ?> reg) {}                     // :37
protected String resolveRegistryGroup(T definition) { return null; }                     // :39
protected JsonObject resolveItemProperties(T definition) { return null; }                // :41
protected ResourceLocation resolveCreativeTab(T definition) { return null; }             // :43
protected FactoryRegistry.FactoryType factoryType() { ... }                              // :45
protected String claimRegistry(T definition) { ... }                                       // :49
protected String resolveNamespace(String rawId)                                          // :57
protected String resolvePath(String rawId)                                               // :62
public String resolveIdentity(String modId, T definition)                                // :77
public String resolveIdentity(String modId, T definition, boolean strict)                // :82
public Set<HandlerCapability> capabilities()                                             // :89
public boolean strictValidationImplemented()                                             // :97
public void validate(T definition, ValidationContext context)                            // :102
public List<RegistryClaim> claims(T definition, ValidationContext context)               // :144
public void apply(T definition, BuildContext baseContext)                                // :155
  • Capabilities: returns {HandlerCapability.STRICT_PREFLIGHT, HandlerCapability.REGISTRY_CLAIMS} (:89-93) and strictValidationImplemented() == true (:97-99).
  • Identity split: resolveIdentity(modId, def) uses EffectiveId.ofLegacy (:77-79), while resolveIdentity(modId, def, strict) uses EffectiveId.of when strict == true to preserve explicit minecraft: namespaces (:82-86).
  • Strict validate (:102-141): verifies non-blank rawId, presence of an explicit namespace (rawId.indexOf(':') > 0, rejecting bare IDs in STRICT), valid ResourceLocation, context.factoryAvailable(factoryType(), resolveType(def)), and, when registry_group is set, calls context.requireDefinition(new DefinitionKey("registry_groups", groupId), "/registry_group") (producing MISSING_REFERENCE, REFERENCE_NOT_DECLARED, or REFERENCE_AMBIGUOUS).
  • Strict claims (:144-151): emits a RegistryClaim for claimRegistry(definition) under the resolved ResourceLocation (subclasses may add auxiliary claims such as minecraft:item).
  • Fixed apply flow (:155-202):
  • Splits rawId into namespace and path; if the factory is missing, throws IllegalStateException when context.isStrict() or logs WARN and skips otherwise (:161-166).
  • Attaches a ResourceLocation namespace rewrite whenever rawId.indexOf(':') >= 0 && (context.isStrict() || !namespace.equals("minecraft")) (:168-174), enabling explicit minecraft: targeting under v2 STRICT while preserving v1/legacy behavior.
  • Attaches the registry group (falling back to root if absent), resolves the creative tab (definition overrides group), invokes configureTypeSpecific, and stores the Reg into context.putReg(getTypeName(), ...) (:175-191).
  • Re-throws exceptions when context.isStrict() (failing the pipeline with Status.FAILED), or logs WARN and returns in non-strict mode (:192-201).
  • Unused hook: resolveItemProperties (:41) remains uncalled; BlockTypeHandler and ItemTypeHandler parse item properties inside their own configureTypeSpecific.

docs.text:
