Per-handler specifics:

  • RegistryGroupHandler: resolveIdentity returns the raw id unchanged (:66-68); parentDefinition returns registry_groups:<parent> for GROUP_CYCLE checks and topological apply ordering (:101-106); validate runs JsonPropertyParser.validateStrict, JsonItemParser.validateStrict, and requireDefinition on parent (:71-98).
  • BlockTypeHandler: validate (:70-105) additionally validates properties and item_properties via validateStrict and checks ValidationContext.factorySupports(..., StatefulBlockFactory.class) when state_properties is declared; claims (:108-123) emits both minecraft:block and minecraft:item when FactoryRegistry.createsBlockItem(def.type()) is true; apply throws if stateProperties != null and the resolved factory is not a StatefulBlockFactory (:39-44).
  • ItemTypeHandler: validate (:59-71) runs JsonItemParser.validateStrict.
  • BlockEntityTypeHandler: validate (:99-121) validates parentBlockId, factoryAvailable(BLOCK_ENTITY, def.beType()), and requireDefinition(blocks:<parent>); claims (:124-134) claims minecraft:block_entity_type at <ns>:<path>_be; apply rethrows missing-parent or factory errors when context.isStrict() (:141-166).

docs.title: 8.6 Adding a new type (v1 and v2)
docs.text:
1. Implement TypeHandler<T> (or extend RegTypeHandler<T> when registering into Minecraft registries).
  2. To participate in v2 BuildOptions.STRICT:
  3. Declare HandlerCapability.STRICT_PREFLIGHT plus either REGISTRY_CLAIMS or NON_REGISTRATION (and optionally OVERLAY);
  4. Override strictValidationImplemented() to return true;
  5. Implement side-effect-free validate(def, ValidationContext) and, for registration handlers, claims(def, ValidationContext);
  6. Implement resolveIdentity(modId, def, strict) (and parentDefinition if hierarchical).
  7. Register any backing factories with FactoryRegistry (see section 10).
  8. Wire the handler:
  9. v1: call TypeHandlerRegistry.register(handler) so JsonTreeBuilder discovers it.
  10. v2: pass the handler collection explicitly to DataDrivenBuildPipeline(...) (optionally after registering into TypeHandlerRegistry and passing TypeHandlerRegistry.all()).

Reference example: TestGenericFactory.java shows a minimal custom handler paired with FactoryRegistry.registerGeneric.

docs.title: 8.7 ContentStructure (shared structure layer)
docs.text:
structure/ContentStructure.java:30. Pure structural validator shared by v1 JsonTreeBuilder and the reload domain (ReloadOrchestrator and decoders), depending only on Gson and java.util.

public final class ContentStructure {
    public enum Kind { BODY_NOT_OBJECT, UNKNOWN_KEY, MISSING_KEY, VALUE_NOT_ARRAY, ELEMENT_NOT_OBJECT }  // :33

    public record Issue(Kind kind, String key, int index, JsonElement actual) {}   // :55
    public record Field(List<Element> elements, List<Issue> issues) {}             // :65
    public record Element(int fileIndex, JsonObject body) {}                       // :76

    public static Issue body(JsonElement raw);                                     // :84
    public static List<Issue> unknownKeys(JsonElement body, Set<String> knownKeys); // :98
    public static Field field(JsonElement body, String typeKey);                   // :123
    public static String joinWithOr(List<String> items);                           // :162
    public static String describe(JsonElement json);                               // :177
}
  • body: requires a JSON object (null is treated as non-object); returns null when valid.
  • unknownKeys: produces one UNKNOWN_KEY per key not in knownKeys; returns empty list if body is not an object.
  • field: splits a single array field; missing key / non-array value emits one issue and zero elements, while non-object array elements emit issues with surviving siblings kept.
  • describe: shared JSON type formatter (e.g. "an array", "a primitive (5)").

ContentStructure makes structural decisions without user-facing templates so registration and reload can preserve separate message templates and opposite D9 hints. v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline uses StrictResourceJson paired with structured BuildDiagnostic emission.

docs.title: 8.8 HandlerCapability, DefinitionKey, and RegistryClaim
docs.text: Located in lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.pipeline, these types define v2 capability checks, selection, and cross-source registry claims:

docs.title: HandlerCapability (pipeline/HandlerCapability.java:6-26)
docs.text:
public enum HandlerCapability {
    STRICT_PREFLIGHT,   // Implements side-effect-free validate(...) for BuildOptions.STRICT
    NON_REGISTRATION,   // Apply mutates build metadata only (e.g. registry_groups); emits no MC registry claims
    REGISTRY_CLAIMS,    // Emits explicit RegistryClaim keys from claims(...)
    OVERLAY             // Retains every source candidate sharing a DefinitionKey instead of collapsing by last-wins
}

DataDrivenBuildPipeline enforces two invariants on capabilities:

  1. Strict readiness (checkStrictCapabilities, DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:1101-1147): in BuildOptions.STRICT, every used handler (and duplicate typeName entry in handlers) must declare STRICT_PREFLIGHT, return strictValidationImplemented() == true, and satisfy NON_REGISTRATION ^ REGISTRY_CLAIMS (exactly one of the two); failures emit Stage.PARSE / Code.HANDLER_NOT_STRICT_READY.
  2. Candidate retention (selectDefinitions, DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:1149-1183): when multiple candidates share a DefinitionKey, all candidates are retained whenever capabilities.contains(HandlerCapability.OVERLAY) || (options.isStrict() && capabilities.contains(HandlerCapability.REGISTRY_CLAIMS) && !capabilities.contains(HandlerCapability.NON_REGISTRATION)); otherwise only the last-wins maximum by (sourceOrder, declarationOrder) survives. Consequently, strict registration handlers retain duplicate/conflicting entries into validate and claims so conflicts surface instead of disappearing silently.

docs.title: DefinitionKey (pipeline/DefinitionKey.java:11-30)
docs.text:
public record DefinitionKey(String typeDomain, String id) implements Comparable<DefinitionKey>

Pairs the handler's getTypeName() (typeDomain) with the resolved id.

docs.title: RegistryClaim and RegistryKey (pipeline/RegistryClaim.java:20-56)
docs.text:
public record RegistryClaim(
        String registry,
        ResourceLocation id,
        SourceDescriptor source,
        int sourceOrder,
        DefinitionKey definitionKey,
        LogicalPath logicalPath,
        String jsonPointer
) {
    public RegistryKey registryKey() { return new RegistryKey(registry, id); }
    public record RegistryKey(String registry, ResourceLocation id) {}
}

Every RegistryClaim links a (registry, id) key back to its originating source, logical path, and JSON Pointer; collisions against another candidate or against reservedRegistryClaims produce Stage.CLAIMS / Code.CLAIM_CONFLICT.

docs.title: RegistryClaimSnapshot (pipeline/RegistryClaimSnapshot.java:15-39)
docs.text:

Runs BFS across an existing host Reg tree (skipping subtrees with !group.isDispatchEnabled()), collecting MinecraftDeferRegistryReg keys as reservedRegistryClaims so code-registered entries cannot be overwritten silently by JSON definitions.

docs.text:
validation/ValidationContext.java:18-112 (implemented by pipeline/PipelineValidationContext.java:20-273), passed to TypeHandler.validate (VALIDATION stage) and TypeHandler.claims (CLAIMS stage) during DataDrivenBuildPipeline.prepare:

enum ResourceDomain { ASSETS, DATA }                                               // :101
enum FactoryType { BLOCK, ITEM, BLOCK_ENTITY, GENERIC }                            // :106

Key behavioral contracts:

  • Visibility and ambiguity:
  • findAllVisible(key) returns definitions matching key whose ownerId is either the current definition's ownerId or in directDependencies() (non-transitive), in session declaration order (PipelineValidationContext.java:88-95).
  • find(key) returns Optional.of(visible.getFirst()) only when findAllVisible(key).size() == 1; both 0 matches and > 1 matches return Optional.empty() (:82-85).
  • requireDefinition(key, relPtr) (:115-155) returns true when there is a single visible match; otherwise it returns false and records MISSING_REFERENCE when absent globally (findAll(key) empty), REFERENCE_NOT_DECLARED when present only in an undeclared owner, or REFERENCE_AMBIGUOUS when visible.size() > 1.
  • findAll(String typeDomain) (ValidationContext.java:60-63, PipelineValidationContext.java:103-107) returns every parsed definition across all IDs and sources matching typeDomain in session declaration order; the default interface method throws UnsupportedOperationException.
  • Resource lookup: resourceExists(domain, id) (:158-184) checks the current owner and directDependencies() under assets/<ns>/... or data/<ns>/..., plus sharedAssetOwners when domain == ResourceDomain.ASSETS.
  • Constructing RegistryClaim values: PipelineValidationContext.claim(registry, id) and claimAt(registry, id, relPtr) (:218-240) construct and return a RegistryClaim (with JSON pointer resolved via JsonPointers.append) for TypeHandler.claims(...) to return to the pipeline; calling them inside validate(...) does not record claims as a side effect.

docs.title: 11.3 Property inheritance and override
docs.text:
Properties apply in Reg-tree parent-to-child order so later stages override earlier ones: root-group properties, parent group, child group, then block level (highest priority). Item properties follow the same order (item_properties on groups before item_properties on blocks). Overrides replace whole keys rather than deep-merging objects.

docs.title: Data-driven registration-phase API (JsonTreeBuilder, index, and content dispatch)
docs.text: This page is a reference (for looking things up). Its subject is the KasugaLibNext data-driven Java API: classes, methods, signatures, call timing, and failure behavior. Applies to: Minecraft 1.21.1 / NeoForge 21.1.203 / Parchment 2024.11.17 / Java 21. Signatures and line numbers refer to the current working tree (modules/data-driven, modules/core, and modules/modelling), covering both the v2 multi-source build pipeline (DataDrivenRegistrationProviders, ContentSourceFactory.snapshot, DataDrivenBuildPipeline) and the legacy single-mod entry point (JsonTreeBuilder). Boundary: which key a JSON field is written under, what type it has, and whether it is required all belong to schema.md; the getting-started tutorial belongs to intro.md, and the steps for content authors and extension authors belong to guide-content.md / guide-extension.md. Terminology: a domain is one of the two arrays in the index manifest, on_register (registration domain) and on_reload (reload domain); a bucket holds legacy registration diagnostics (mod dimension, keyed by mod id) or reload diagnostics (RELOAD_DATA[<namespace>]), whereas the v2 multi-source pipeline produces structured BuildDiagnostic values instead of writing to Diagnostics.

docs.title: 2. Legacy registration-phase entry point: JsonTreeBuilder
docs.text: builder/JsonTreeBuilder.java is the legacy single-mod JAR entry point (and also hosts pure-JVM index/content parsing helpers). All methods are static, and the class cannot be instantiated (:882). Multi-source builds, external packs, owner dependency isolation, strict preflight, and claim checking should use the v2 DataDrivenRegistrationProvider + DataDrivenBuildPipeline APIs in sections 16–18.

docs.title: 2.1 buildForMod
docs.text:
public static JsonRegistryGroup buildForMod(String modId)   // JsonTreeBuilder.java:67

Responsibility: load one mod JAR's on_register content, and build and return its root registry group <modId>:json_root.

Parameter constraint: modId must have a corresponding mod file in FML's ModList (internally via findModFile, :744). When not found, null is returned and no error is reported.

Execution order (one call):

  1. ensureHandlersRegistered() (:57), idempotent, registers DataDrivenBlockFactory and the four built-in TypeHandlers once.
  2. clearLoadingErrors(modId) (:69), clears only that mod's bucket.
  3. Locate the index directory data/<modId>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/ (findIndexDir, :797).
  4. Read the index manifests one by one (listIndexFiles scans the directory, readIndexManifest parses), then aggregate them (resolveIndexManifests).
  5. Parse only the content files on_register points at; on_reload is recognized and validated here, but not parsed (:106-117).
  6. Resolve duplicate ids before any apply side effect (:125).
  7. Apply each handler in ascending getPhase() order; registry_groups gets an extra topological sort before apply (:128-152).
  8. Return rootGroup (:154).

Cases that return null:

Case Location Error recorded? The index directory does not exist, and the old-layout directory data/<mod>/kasugalib/ does not exist either :82-85 No, only a DEBUG record The index directory does not exist, but the old-layout directory does :73-81 Yes, WARN + bucket entry, hinting at migration to on_register The index directory exists, but no manifest declares either domain (an empty directory included) :103-105 Yes; aggregation records "declares neither ... in any index file"

Note: a mod that declares only on_reload does not count as nothingDeclared(), so it returns a non-null empty root group (:106-109 records only INFO), not null.

docs.title: 2.2 buildAll
docs.text:
public static Map<String, JsonRegistryGroup> buildAll()   // JsonTreeBuilder.java:157

Responsibility: walk every mod file in ModList, call buildForMod for each mod, and collect non-null results keyed by mod id in LinkedHashMap order. The same mod file path is processed only once (visitedRoots, :168). When a single mod throws, the catch logs an ERROR and wraps the failure as an IllegalStateException in that mod's bucket (:177-181) before continuing. Production wiring currently routes through JsonTreeIntegration per mod rather than buildAll().

docs.title: 2.3 When JsonTreeIntegration is wired up
docs.text:
JsonTreeIntegration (JsonTreeIntegration.java:13) is a Micronaut @Context bean. @PostConstruct (:21) registers a COMMON-side callback with RegisterContextRegistry (:24-42):

  1. First checks DataDrivenRegistrationProviders.find(modRegistry.getModId()).orElse(null) (:25-26):
  2. If a provider is installed: calls provider.build(modRegistry.getModId()); if non-null, attaches it as a child of modRegistry; if null, returns immediately without falling back to JsonTreeBuilder; exceptions thrown by a provider are not swallowed here (hosts manage their own diagnostics).
  3. If no provider is installed: falls back to JsonTreeBuilder.buildForMod(modRegistry.getModId()) inside a try/catch, attaching any non-null root (:34-41).

The callback fires lazily on the first registration-event dispatch for that mod, guaranteeing that @Context factory registrations and early provider installations run before JSON parsing.

docs.title: 2.4 Phase semantics
docs.text:
Constant Value Handler that uses it Reason TypeHandler.PHASE_GROUPS 0 registry_groups Groups must exist before content TypeHandler.PHASE_CONTENT 1 blocks, items Regular content TypeHandler.PHASE_EMBEDDED 2 block_entities A BE has to attach to an already existing block Reg

Within the same phase in JsonTreeBuilder, order follows TypeHandlerRegistry registration order (LinkedHashMap); in v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline, sorting additionally considers handler list index, sourceOrder, logicalPath, jsonPointer, declarationOrder, and parentDefinition topological edges (see section 18). JsonTreeBuilder topologically sorts registry_groups via topoSortGroupDefs (:890), logging a WARN on cycles and falling back to the root group for missing parents (whereas v2 STRICT reports GROUP_CYCLE as a blocking error).

docs.title: 3. Index API
docs.text: Index directory: data/<modId>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/. Every .json under it is a manifest, and a manifest declares only content-file paths, never types.

// JsonTreeBuilder.java:386

The result of aggregating all of one mod's manifests and removing cross-domain conflicts. nothingDeclared() is the D4 test: when true, no manifest declared either domain.

docs.title: 3.3 parseIndexManifest
docs.text:
public static IndexManifest parseIndexManifest(String modId, String label, JsonObject root)
// JsonTreeBuilder.java:228

Responsibility: parse one in-memory manifest with no NeoForge dependency, callable from plain JVM tests. A null root is treated as an empty file. Only on_register and on_reload are recognized; unknown fields are recorded in the modId bucket without throwing and without aborting sibling fields (D3).

docs.title: 3.4 resolveIndexManifests
docs.text:
public static ResolvedIndex resolveIndexManifests(String modId, List<IndexManifest> manifests)
// JsonTreeBuilder.java:318

Responsibility: aggregate all manifests of one mod, apply cross-domain fail-closed filtering (D6: a path appearing in both domains is reported and removed from both lists), and emit the aggregate D4 warning/error when neither domain was declared.

docs.title: 3.5 listIndexFiles
docs.text:
public static List<Path> listIndexFiles(Path indexDir, String modId)   // JsonTreeBuilder.java:783

Responsibility: list .json files in indexDir, sorted by path string; records an ERROR in the mod bucket and returns an empty list if listing fails.

docs.title: 3.6 How D1 to D6 show up at the API layer
docs.text:
Rule Meaning Where it lands D1 Both fields are individually optional; when neither appears an error is reported and nothing is consumed JsonTreeBuilder.parseIndexManifest:247-253 D2 An empty array is legal and counts as "declared" parseIndexManifest:244, resolveIndexManifests:347 branch D3 An unknown top-level field or non-array field does not abort sibling fields parseIndexManifest:231-238, readPathArray:263-279 D4 The aggregate warning branches on "which field was declared" resolveIndexManifests:347-352 D5 sources is not an alias; reported as an unknown field parseIndexManifest:231-238 D6 A path listed in both arrays fails closed and neither domain consumes it resolveIndexManifests:330-345

v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline (readManifest:513-588, resolveNamespace:635-710) enforces the same D1–D6 rules with MANIFEST_INVALID and MANIFEST_EMPTY diagnostics.

docs.title: 3.7 The deprecated field
docs.text: sources is no longer a legal index field (D5); writing it produces an unsupported-field error / MANIFEST_INVALID and declares no domain. Only on_register and on_reload are valid.

docs.title: 3.8 Path contract
docs.text:
public static String validateSourcePath(String path)              // JsonTreeBuilder.java:407
public static String[] indexDirectorySegments(String modId)       // JsonTreeBuilder.java:766

validateSourcePath: returns null when legal (non-empty, relative without leading /, ends in .json, no empty segment, no . or ..), otherwise a reason string. Pure JVM function.

docs.title: 4.1 parseSource (private)
docs.text: parseSource (JsonTreeBuilder.java:419) validates via validateSourcePath, deduplicates via parsedSources, reads data/<modId>/<sourcePath> from findModFile, and hands the object to dispatchContent.

docs.title: 4.2 dispatchContent (private)
docs.text: dispatchContent (JsonTreeBuilder.java:485) dispatches top-level fields (getParentTypeName() == null), reports unknown top-level fields (including embedded types written at the top level and D9 reload-domain hints via reloadDomainHint:580-591), checks arrays/objects via ContentStructure.field, and extracts embedded definitions via extractEmbedded (:544-569).

docs.title: 4.3 parseContentBody
docs.text:
public static Map<String, List<Object>> parseContentBody(String modId, String contentLabel, JsonObject root)
// JsonTreeBuilder.java:641

In-memory half of the legacy content pipeline with no NeoForge dependency: parses and groups definitions by handler typeName without registering or applying; malformed input goes into the mod's error bucket rather than throwing.

docs.text:
public static void applyUnchecked(TypeHandler handler, Object definition, BuildContext context, String modId)
// JsonTreeBuilder.java:733

Runs handler.apply and records any thrown exception as a Failed to apply '<type>' handler for mod '<mod>' ERROR (IllegalStateException) in the mod bucket.

docs.title: 5. Conflict resolution
docs.text: Duplicate ids are resolved before any apply side effect so MappedRegistry never sees a duplicate key.

docs.title: 5.1 DuplicateIdResolver
docs.text:
dedup/DuplicateIdResolver.java, pure function with no Minecraft types.

public record Candidate(String typeName, String identity, String sourcePath, Object payload)  // :39

docs.title: 5.4 last-wins order (legacy loader)
docs.text: resolveDuplicates (JsonTreeBuilder.java:673) builds candidates in load order: ascending index filename → on_register array order → content array order (with embedded BEs following their host blocks). Losers never enter apply, and each conflict emits a WARN log plus a mod-bucket IllegalStateException. For v2 multi-source selection, OVERLAY, and REGISTRY_CLAIMS checks, see section 18 and api-extension.md §8.8.

docs.text:
DataDrivenRegistrationProvider.java:8-11:

@FunctionalInterface
public interface DataDrivenRegistrationProvider {
    JsonRegistryGroup build(String hostModId);
}

Replaces legacy mod-JAR scanning (JsonTreeBuilder.buildForMod) for a host mod. Returning null indicates that the host took over and no JSON root group should be attached for this run.

docs.title: 16.2 DataDrivenRegistrationProviders
docs.text:
DataDrivenRegistrationProviders.java:11-55:

public static Attachment install(String hostModId, DataDrivenRegistrationProvider provider)  // :14
public static Optional<DataDrivenRegistrationProvider> find(String hostModId)                // :25

public static final class Attachment implements AutoCloseable {
    @Override public void close()                                                            // :51
}
  • Process-wide map: backed by ConcurrentHashMap<String, Attachment>.
  • Uniqueness: installing a second provider for the same hostModId throws IllegalStateException (:18-21); null or blank hostModId throws IllegalArgumentException (:31-36).
  • Exact removal: Attachment.close() calls PROVIDERS.remove(hostModId, this) so tests or explicit teardowns only remove their own attachment (:51-53).

docs.title: 17.1 Two-layer capture vs registration view
docs.text:
v2 production wiring separates physical capture from registration-time reading across modules/core and modules/data-driven:

  1. Platform capture layer (modules/core, lib.kasuga.core.resource.source):
  2. ResourceSourceDescriptor(String ownerId, String sourceId, String rootId, int rank, Origin origin) (ResourceSourceDescriptor.java:6-16): unique platform identity; IDs forbid colons (ResourcePaths.id), rank >= 0, origin is EXTERNAL, MC_MANAGED, or DERIVED.
  3. ResourceSource (ResourceSource.java:5-9): constructed via ResourceSources.mod, directory, readOnlyDirectory, archive, or vfs. ResourceSources.fixed(descriptor, source, policy) (ResourceSources.java:94-118) immediately captures an immutable baseline snapshot and closes the underlying live source, returning a FixedResourceSource whose subsequent capture() calls emit independent ResourceSnapshots.
  4. ResourceSnapshot (ResourceSnapshot.java:17-187): immutable captured bytes (stored in memory up to InputPolicy.memoryThresholdBytes, or spooled to private temp files above that); reference-counted open() / lease() lets in-flight streams finish after snapshot.close() while rejecting new leases (STALE_REFERENCE).
  5. InputPolicy.DEFAULT (InputPolicy.java:6): 8 MiB max JSON file, 256 MiB max regular file, 1 GiB max total per snapshot, 50,000 max files, max JSON depth 64, 1 MiB memory threshold.
  6. Registration view layer (modules/data-driven, lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.source): ContentSource exposes a single captured root to DataDrivenBuildPipeline.

docs.title: 17.2 ContentSource and supporting value types
docs.text:
ContentSource.java:16-66:

public interface ContentSource extends AutoCloseable {
    SourceDescriptor descriptor();                                // :17
    Optional<InputStream> open(LogicalPath path) throws IOException;  // :24
    boolean exists(LogicalPath path);                             // :26
    List<LocatedFile> files();                                    // :31 immutable, path-sorted
    default List<LocatedFile> indexes()                           // :37 data/<ns>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/*.json
    default InputStream requireOpen(LogicalPath path) throws IOException; // :44 throws NOT_FOUND if absent
    @Override default void close() throws IOException
}

Supporting types:

  • SourceDescriptor (SourceDescriptor.java:20-112):
  • Platform factory: SourceDescriptor.of(ResourceSourceDescriptor resource, Collection<String> namespaces, String diagnosticLabel) (:78-84), preserving rootId(), rank(), origin(), and resource().
  • Legacy adapter factory: SourceDescriptor.of(String sourceId, String ownerId, Collection<String> namespaces) (:74-76), with resource() == null and rank() == 0.
  • namespaces must be non-empty, sorted, and match [a-z0-9_.-]+.
  • LogicalPath (LogicalPath.java:15-83): relative slash-separated literal path; rejects blank, leading /, \, Windows drive prefixes, empty segments, . / .., NUL, and ISO control characters.
  • LocatedFile (LocatedFile.java:11-47): carries source, path, size, plus snapshot uri (ResourceUri), SHA-256 revision, and tags.
  • SourceLimits (SourceLimits.java:6-36): byte/file limits for legacy adapters (DEFAULT matches InputPolicy.DEFAULT).
  • SourceAccessException (SourceAccessException.java:9-90): typed IOException carrying Reason (NOT_FOUND, ACCESS_DENIED, OUT_OF_BOUNDS, SYMLINK_REJECTED, DUPLICATE_ENTRY, INVALID_ENTRY, LIMIT_EXCEEDED, CORRUPT_ARCHIVE, SOURCE_CLOSED, IO_ERROR).

docs.title: 17.3 ContentSourceFactory
docs.text:
ContentSourceFactory.java:21-140:

Method Behavior Intended use snapshot(ResourceSnapshot, ResourceSourceDescriptor, Collection<String> namespaces, String diagnosticLabel) (:52) Wraps a captured snapshot as SnapshotContentSource (default index scan) v2 production path snapshot(snapshot, resource, namespaces, diagnosticLabel, Collection<String> declaredIndexes) (:61) Same, restricting indexes() to host-declared logical paths (Scene indexing) v2 production path (e.g. parcel roots) directory(Path, SourceDescriptor[, SourceLimits]) (:25,29) Opens a filesystem directory (rejects symlinks / special files) Legacy / plain-JVM tests zip(Path, SourceDescriptor[, SourceLimits]) (:34,38) Opens a ZIP/JAR archive Legacy / tooling modJar(IModFile, SourceDescriptor[, SourceLimits]) (:43,47) Opens a NeoForge IModFile without closing shared secure-JAR FS Legacy open(Path, SourceDescriptor[, SourceLimits]) (:80,84) Auto-selects directory or zip from physical path Legacy / CLI

docs.title: 17.4 SnapshotContentSource
docs.text:
SnapshotContentSource.java:23-145:

  • Factory SnapshotContentSource.open(...) (delegated to by ContentSourceFactory.snapshot(...)).
  • Construction checks:
  • every file in snapshot must match the supplied ownerId, sourceId, and rootId, otherwise IllegalArgumentException (:52-57);
  • duplicate logicalPath values are rejected (:43-47);
  • files are sorted by path and retain uri, revision, tags, and size.
  • declaredIndexes semantics (:40, 121-129):
  • null: falls back to ContentSource.super.indexes(), discovering data/<declared-ns>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/*.json;
  • non-null collection: filters indexes() to files whose path is in declaredIndexes (an empty collection explicitly yields zero manifests for pure asset/data roots). Does not prune files() or open(), and does not validate that declared paths exist.
  • Ownership & close semantics: SnapshotContentSource owns the supplied ResourceSnapshot and calls snapshot.close() on close() (:132-137). Calling open, exists, or files after close throws IllegalStateException (:139-144). Never pass the same ResourceSnapshot to two owners; capture separate snapshots from a FixedResourceSource when sharing bytes across consumers.

docs.title: 18. v2 Multi-Source Build Pipeline: DataDrivenBuildPipeline and Hooks
docs.text: pipeline/DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:54-1644 orchestrates discovery, strict JSON decoding, definition selection, cross-source validation, registry claim checks, apply, and finalizers across a prepare / build boundary.

docs.title: 18.1 Construction and options
docs.text:
public DataDrivenBuildPipeline(
        String hostModId,
        Collection<? extends TypeHandler<?>> handlers,
        Collection<? extends BuildFinalizer> finalizers)   // :64

public DataDrivenBuildPipeline(
        String hostModId,
        Collection<? extends TypeHandler<?>> handlers,
        Collection<? extends BuildFinalizer> finalizers,
        RegistrationTarget registrationTarget,
        Collection<String> reservedSymbols)                // :72

public DataDrivenBuildPipeline(
        String hostModId,
        Collection<? extends TypeHandler<?>> handlers,
        Collection<? extends BuildFinalizer> finalizers,
        RegistrationTarget registrationTarget,
        Collection<String> reservedSymbols,
        Collection<RegistryClaim.RegistryKey> reservedRegistryClaims)  // :89
  • The pipeline does not automatically read TypeHandlerRegistry or DataDrivenBuildHooks: hosts must pass explicit handlers and finalizers (for example, calling JsonTreeBuilder.ensureHandlersRegistered() then passing TypeHandlerRegistry.all(), plus DataDrivenBuildHooks.finalizersFor(hostModId)).
  • Handler list order breaks ties within the same getPhase(); in STRICT mode, duplicate getTypeName() entries raise HANDLER_NOT_STRICT_READY.
  • BuildOptions (BuildOptions.java:6-20):
  • BuildOptions.LEGACY: Gson tolerant parsing, EffectiveId.ofLegacy, skips strict capabilities and validate, does not reject build on hasBlockingDiagnostics();
  • BuildOptions.STRICT (isStrict() == true): StrictResourceJson, EffectiveId.of, strict capability checks, full validate and claim conflict detection, and REJECTED before apply when any Severity.ERROR diagnostic exists.

docs.title: 18.2 prepare stage and PreparedContent
docs.text:
public PreparedContent prepare(Collection<? extends ContentSource> sources, BuildOptions options)
public PreparedContent prepare(Collection<? extends ContentSource> sources, BuildOptions options,
                               Map<String, ? extends Collection<String>> dependencies)
public PreparedContent prepare(Collection<? extends ContentSource> sources, BuildOptions options,
                               Map<String, ? extends Collection<String>> dependencies,
                               Collection<String> sharedAssetOwners)  // :111-143

Parameters:

  • sources: content sources. Platform sources (descriptor.resource() != null) are ordered by their explicit non-negative rank as sourceOrder; only legacy 4-arg SourceDescriptor instances (resource() == null) derive order from collection iteration index.
  • dependencies: direct owner-to-owners dependency map (not transitive). Unknown dependency owners emit UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY (ERROR in STRICT, WARNING in LEGACY, :411-461).
  • sharedAssetOwners: owners whose ASSETS domain files are visible to every source in ValidationContext.resourceExists(ResourceDomain.ASSETS, ...) without exposing their DATA files or definitions (:158-164).

Execution order of prepare (never calls TypeHandler.apply):

  1. Check (sourceId, rootId) uniqueness and global rank uniqueness (INVALID_SOURCE on duplicates, :368-409).
  2. Normalize and validate dependencies (:411-461).
  3. Per source, read indexes(), aggregate manifests per namespace (D1–D6), parse on_register files (parse + resolveIdentity(hostModId, parsed, options.isStrict())), and collect on_reload paths (:463-511, 764-917). Unexpected per-source RuntimeExceptions are isolated as SOURCE_READ_FAILED (:173-185).
  4. Preflight-decode on_reload files using ReloadHandlerRegistry.get(field) (validateReloadContentFile, :919-1025) without calling clearBucket() or register().
  5. In STRICT mode, verify every used handler declares STRICT_PREFLIGHT, returns true from strictValidationImplemented(), and declares XOR of NON_REGISTRATION / REGISTRY_CLAIMS (:1101-1147).
  6. Select definitions (selectDefinitions, :1149-1183): OVERLAY or STRICT && REGISTRY_CLAIMS keep every candidate per DefinitionKey; all others keep the highest (sourceOrder, declarationOrder) winner.
  7. In STRICT mode, run validate(definition, PipelineValidationContext) in deterministic order (:1185-1226).
  8. Detect parentDefinition cycles (GROUP_CYCLE: ERROR in STRICT, WARNING in LEGACY, :1233-1297).
  9. Collect claims from REGISTRY_CLAIMS handlers and check collisions against reservedRegistryClaims and other claims (CLAIM_CONFLICT / CLAIM_FAILED, :1304-1401).

Output PreparedContent (PreparedContent.java:14-81):

public record PreparedContent(
        String hostModId,
        BuildOptions options,
        List<SourceDescriptor> sources,
        List<LocatedDefinition<?>> definitions,
        List<LocatedDefinition<?>> allDefinitions,
        List<LocatedContentPath> registerFiles,
        List<LocatedContentPath> reloadFiles,
        List<LocatedIndexPath> indexFiles,
        List<RegistryClaim> claims,
        List<BuildDiagnostic> diagnostics,
        Map<String, Set<String>> dependencies,
        Set<String> reservedSymbols
) {
    public boolean hasBlockingDiagnostics()  // true when any diagnostic has Severity.ERROR
}

Each definition is wrapped in LocatedDefinition<T> (LocatedDefinition.java:22-45), carrying key (DefinitionKey), handler, definition, source (SourceDescriptor), sourceOrder, logicalPath, jsonPointer, and declarationOrder.

docs.title: 18.3 build stage, BuildResult, BuildFinalizer, and RegistrationTarget
docs.text:
public BuildResult build(PreparedContent prepared)                             // :231
public BuildResult build(PreparedContent prepared, RegistrationTarget target)  // :241
  • Verifies prepared.hostModId() matches hostModId.
  • If prepared.options().isStrict() && prepared.hasBlockingDiagnostics(), returns Status.REJECTED immediately (rootGroup == null, zero apply/finalizer side effects).
  • Creates JsonRegistryGroup(hostModId + ":json_root") with default namespace rewrite to hostModId, then creates RegBuildContext via target.createContext(hostModId, root, prepared.options()) (:260-266).
  • Applies each selected definition inside context.withCurrentDefinition(definition, ...) in stableApplyOrder (:1411-1477):
  • TypeHandler.getPhase() ascending;
  • first index of handler in handlers;
  • sourceOrder ascending;
  • logicalPath lexicographically;
  • jsonPointer lexicographically;
  • declarationOrder ascending;
  • topological parent-before-child ordering from parentDefinition.
  • Runs finalizers in order (BuildFinalizer.afterBuild(BuildContext, PreparedContent), BuildFinalizer.java:9-11), collecting their return values.
  • Any RuntimeException thrown during context creation, ordering, apply, or a finalizer stops execution and returns Status.FAILED (carrying the possibly partially populated rootGroup and cause, with no automatic rollback).

BuildResult (BuildResult.java:12-50):

public record BuildResult(
        String hostModId,
        Status status,
        @Nullable JsonRegistryGroup rootGroup,
        List<BuildDiagnostic> diagnostics,
        List<Object> finalizerResults,
        @Nullable Throwable cause
) {
    public enum Status { REJECTED, APPLIED, FAILED }
    public boolean successful() { return status == Status.APPLIED; }
    public boolean applied()    { return status == Status.APPLIED; }
}

Note: both BuildResult.successful() and BuildResult.applied() return true only when status == Status.APPLIED (both return false on FAILED, even if earlier apply calls already mutated the context; pinned by BuildResultTest.onlyAppliedStatusCountsAsApplied).

RegistrationTarget (RegistrationTarget.java:10-17): RegistrationTarget.standard() constructs new RegBuildContext(hostModId, rootGroup, options.isStrict()); hosts can supply custom subclasses.

RegistryClaimSnapshot (RegistryClaimSnapshot.java:15-39):

public static Set<RegistryClaim.RegistryKey> collect(Reg<?, ?> root)  // :19

Runs BFS from root, skipping any RegistryGroup (and its subtree) where isDispatchEnabled() is false, and collects MinecraftDeferRegistryReg entries as RegistryKeys for passing into reservedRegistryClaims.

docs.title: 18.4 Process-wide hooks: DataDrivenBuildHooks
docs.text:
DataDrivenBuildHooks.java:12-36:

public static void registerFinalizer(String hostModId, BuildFinalizer finalizer)  // :16
public static List<BuildFinalizer> finalizersFor(String hostModId)                // :23

Registers session-end BuildFinalizers keyed by hostModId (ConcurrentHashMap + CopyOnWriteArrayList). There is no unregister API, so callers must guard against duplicate registration, and host providers must explicitly pass DataDrivenBuildHooks.finalizersFor(hostModId) when constructing DataDrivenBuildPipeline.

docs.title: Data-Driven Reload API (Including the Assertable Pure-Function Surface and Call Examples)
13. Reload API
docs.text: The reload domain is orchestrated by data-driven's ReloadOrchestrator, using ReloadHandler as its extension point (symmetric with TypeHandler at registration time). The orchestrator hardcodes no type names — it iterates ReloadHandlerRegistry and accepts each handler's typeName() as a valid top-level key.

docs.title: 13.1 ReloadHandler (Extension Point)
docs.text:
reload/ReloadHandler.java:41. Each handler owns decode, register, and post-reload validation for one reload type.

public interface ReloadHandler<T> {
    String typeName();                                              // :50 top-level key and dedup collision space
    default String describeFile() { return "reload-domain file"; }  // :60 noun in decode diagnostics
    default Set<String> globDirectories() { return Set.of(); }      // :72 empty = index-only
    void clearBucket();                                             // :85 once per cycle before discovery
    Decoded<T> decode(JsonObject root);                             // :97 pure decode; no file I/O
    void register(T payload);                                       // :107 registers last-wins winners
    default void afterReload(List<Reloaded<T>> registered) {}       // :117 cross-type validation
}
Method Responsibility and constraints Failure behavior typeName() Claimed top-level JSON key (e.g. "state_machines"); unique key and dedup space Re-registering the same name replaces in place describeFile() Noun inserted into decode error messages (e.g. "state machine file") Defaults to "reload-domain file" globDirectories() Directories under data/<ns>/ scanned via glob; empty default = index-only Return an ordered set to keep discovery order clearBucket() Runs once per cycle before discovery; must clear only reload entries (keep SCRIPT) Exceptions are isolated by runClear (:250-258) under Domain.RELOAD_DATA decode(root) root is guaranteed to be a JSON object; do no file I/O and return errors in Decoded.errors() Exceptions are isolated per file and recorded register(payload) Called only for last-wins winners after discovery completes Throw on failure so orchestrator attributes to namespace afterReload(registered) Called after every handler finishes register, only for entries registered this cycle Exceptions attribute to KasugaLib.MODID without blocking later handlers

docs.title: 13.2 ReloadHandlerRegistry
docs.text:
reload/ReloadHandlerRegistry.java:27. Static LinkedHashMap keyed by typeName(), preserving registration order.

public static void register(ReloadHandler<?> handler);       // :37
public static ReloadHandler<?> get(String typeName);         // :45
public static Collection<ReloadHandler<?>> all();            // :50 immutable view in registration order
public static void clearForTest();                           // :58 tests only
  • Order matters: dispatch and registration order follow all().
  • Idempotent replacement: re-registering an existing typeName replaces in place at the original position.

docs.title: 13.3 Decoded / Entry
docs.text:
reload/Decoded.java:19:

public record Decoded<T>(List<Entry<T>> entries, List<String> errors) {   // :19
    public record Entry<T>(String id, T payload) {}                        // :28
    public static <T> Decoded<T> empty();                                  // :36
}
  • Entry.id is the deduplication key within the handler type; rejected files produce empty entries and non-empty errors.

docs.text:
reload/Reloaded.java:14:

Pairs a surviving registered payload with its source namespace modId for afterReload attribution.

docs.title: 13.5 ReloadOrchestrator
docs.text:
reload/ReloadOrchestrator.java:121. Implements ScopedResourceManagerConsumer and ScopedResourcePackListener.

public ReloadOrchestrator()                                      // :133 DI entry point, registered via init():155
public ReloadOrchestrator(ReloadHandler<?>... handlers)          // :145 registers handlers, then runs
public void reload(ResourceManager resourceManager)              // :186
public static String indexResourcePath(String modId)             // :290 -> "kasuga_lib/data_driven"
  • Legal top-level keys come dynamically from knownTypeNames() (:528) via ReloadHandlerRegistry.all(), while D9 registration-type examples come from registrationFieldsExample() (:543) via TypeHandlerRegistry.all().
  • reload(ResourceManager) includes a final safety catch (:188-193) attributing escaped exceptions to KasugaLib.MODID.
  • Cycle stages (runCycle, :198):
  • Clear Diagnostics.clear(Domain.RELOAD_DATA) (:208) and create HandlerCycle (:633) per handler;
  • Call runClear → clearBucket() per handler (:250-258);
  • Collect unique globDirectories() across handlers;
  • Per-namespace discovery (collectNamespace, :266): readReloadPaths (:307) reads on_reload manifests → collectGlob (:365) scans globs skipping indexed paths (enforcing ManagedReloadAllowlist when managed) → collectIndex (:392) reads explicit indexed files with allowlist validation;
  • Dispatch and decode (dispatch, :484; readAndDispatch, :460): unknown top-level keys report with D9 hint (:494-501), matching handlers run decode;
  • Deduplicate (resolveAndReport, :602) and call register (:562) with glob candidates first, index candidates second (last-wins; losers never reach handler.register);
  • Run runAfterReload (:585).

docs.title: 13.7 StateMachineDefinitionLoader
docs.text:
Pure file decoder (modules/modelling/.../dynamic/fsm/StateMachineDefinitionLoader.java:36-103):

public static final String PATH = "state_machines";                                        // :39
public static final String FIELD_STATE_MACHINES = "state_machines";                        // :42
public record DecodedFile(List<StateMachineDefinition> definitions, List<String> errors) {}// :55
public static DecodedFile decodeFile(JsonElement json);                                    // :67

Expects {"state_machines": [...]}. Non-object roots, missing keys, or non-array values reject the whole file; extra top-level keys are ignored by the decoder (unknown keys are reported by the orchestrator); malformed array entries are skipped individually.

docs.title: 13.8 AnimationClipLoader
docs.text:
Pure file decoder (modules/modelling/.../dynamic/fsm/AnimationClipLoader.java:44-135):

public static final String FIELD_ANIMATION_CLIPS = "animation_clips";                      // :47
public record DecodedFile(List<AnimationClip> clips, List<String> errors) {}               // :59
public static DecodedFile decodeFile(JsonElement json);                                    // :71
public static void register(FsmAnimationClips clips, AnimationClip clip);                  // :127
  • Removed-key rejection (:100-108): elements containing removed keys "functions" or "formula_parts" are explicitly rejected with "animation_clips[i] uses removed key '<legacyKey>'; replace it with 'formula_transforms'; element skipped", skipping only that element.
  • Registration & discovery: AnimationClip.CODEC reads id from each clip object; register writes to clips.registerResource (preserving script-wins). Clips are index-only (on_reload), with no glob directory.

docs.title: 13.11 ManagedReloadAllowlist
docs.text:
reload/ManagedReloadAllowlist.java:22-163 enforces a process-wide allowlist for resources projected from ApprovedResourcePacks, leaving legacy mod and data packs unchanged:

public static synchronized void install(
        String hostModId,
        List<LocatedIndexPath> indexes,
        List<LocatedContentPath> reloadFiles)                                                // :28
public static synchronized void install(
        String hostModId,
        List<SourceDescriptor> sources,
        List<LocatedIndexPath> indexes,
        List<LocatedContentPath> reloadFiles)                                                // :36
public static synchronized void install(
        String hostModId,
        List<SourceDescriptor> sources,
        Map<String, String> projectedSourcePackIds,
        List<LocatedIndexPath> indexes,
        List<LocatedContentPath> reloadFiles)                                                // :45
public static synchronized boolean isManaged(String sourcePackId)                            // :96
public static synchronized boolean allowsIndex(String sourcePackId, ResourceLocation loc)    // :101
public static synchronized boolean allowsContent(String sourcePackId, ResourceLocation loc)  // :109
public static synchronized int priority(String sourcePackId)                                 // :117
public static synchronized void clearForTests()                                              // :126

ReloadOrchestrator applies the allowlist at three points: - readReloadPaths (:317-332): when a stack contains managed entries matching ManagedReloadAllowlist.isManaged(sourcePackId(resource)), filters to allowsIndex(sourcePackId, loc) and orders them by priority(sourcePackId) (skipping if none are allowed); - collectGlob (:375-380): filters !ManagedReloadAllowlist.isManaged(sourcePackId(resource)) so managed packs never leak into directory globs; - collectIndex (:419-437): filters managed stack entries via allowsContent(sourcePackId, loc) ordered by priority(sourcePackId), blocking unapproved managed paths with a Domain.RELOAD_DATA diagnostic.

docs.title: 13.12 v2 Startup on_reload Preflight
docs.text:
DataDrivenBuildPipeline (DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:919-1025, validateReloadContentFile) runs read-only preflight on all files listed under on_reload during registration-phase prepare:

  • Checks each top-level key against ReloadHandlerRegistry.get(field), emitting UNKNOWN_TYPE (ERROR under STRICT, WARNING under LEGACY) for unregistered fields.
  • Calls handler.decode(root) and converts Decoded.errors() or thrown exceptions into BuildDiagnostic entries (Stage.PARSE, Code.CONTENT_INVALID).
  • Performs zero bucket mutations: clearBucket(), register(...), and afterReload(...) are never called during startup preflight.

docs.title: 15.1 v2 Multi-Source Pipeline prepare + build (Pure JVM SnapshotContentSource)
docs.text:
import java.util.List;
import lib.kasuga.core.resource.source.InputPolicy;
import lib.kasuga.core.resource.source.ResourceSourceDescriptor;
import lib.kasuga.core.resource.source.ResourceSources;
import lib.kasuga.core.vfs.VfsPath;
import lib.kasuga.core.vfs.backend.InMemoryVfs;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.TypeHandlerRegistry;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.builder.JsonTreeBuilder;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.pipeline.BuildOptions;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.pipeline.BuildResult;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.pipeline.DataDrivenBuildPipeline;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.pipeline.PreparedContent;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.source.ContentSource;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.source.ContentSourceFactory;

JsonTreeBuilder.ensureHandlersRegistered();

ResourceSourceDescriptor resDesc = new ResourceSourceDescriptor(
        "kuayue", "kuayue_main", "root_0", 0, ResourceSourceDescriptor.Origin.EXTERNAL);

try (var vfs = new InMemoryVfs("kuayue_main")) {
    vfs.writeString(VfsPath.of("data/kuayue/kasuga_lib/data_driven/index.json"),
            "{\"on_register\": [\"blocks/demo.json\"]}");
    vfs.writeString(VfsPath.of("data/kuayue/blocks/demo.json"),
            "{\"blocks\": [{\"id\": \"kuayue:demo_block\", \"type\": \"data_driven_block\"}]}");

    try (var snapshot = ResourceSources.fixed(
                    resDesc,
                    ResourceSources.vfs(resDesc, vfs, false, "", "", InputPolicy.DEFAULT),
                    InputPolicy.DEFAULT).capture();
         ContentSource source = ContentSourceFactory.snapshot(snapshot, resDesc, List.of("kuayue"), "main")) {

        DataDrivenBuildPipeline pipeline = new DataDrivenBuildPipeline(
                "kuayue",
                TypeHandlerRegistry.all(),
                List.of());
        PreparedContent prepared = pipeline.prepare(List.of(source), BuildOptions.STRICT);
        if (!prepared.hasBlockingDiagnostics()) {
            BuildResult result = pipeline.build(prepared);
            boolean ok = result.applied(); // true only for Status.APPLIED
        }
    }
}
