docs.title: Reference Usage Notes
docs.text:
• v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline with in-memory SnapshotContentSource runs prepare preflight directly in pure JVM JUnit tests; running build/apply for Minecraft Block/Item registrations or ReloadOrchestrator.reload requires NeoForge registries / ResourceManager.
  • v1 pure helpers (parseContentBody, parseIndexManifest, resolveIndexManifests, DuplicateIdResolver, EffectiveId, Diagnostics) can likewise be asserted without NeoForge runtime bootstrap.

Other pages in the data-driven section: Registration API · Extension API · Diagnostics API · Reload API · Schema Reference · Block State Properties · Section index

docs.title: Data-driven block-state properties
docs.text:
A blocks entry can declare real Minecraft BlockState properties in state_properties. This is separate from properties, which controls hardness, friction, and other block behaviour. List the content file in the index's on_register array.

{
  "blocks": [{
    "id": "mymod:control_panel",
    "type": "data_driven_block",
    "state_properties": {
      "open": { "type": "vanilla", "property": "OPEN", "default": false },
      "active": { "type": "boolean", "default": false },
      "level": { "type": "integer", "min": 0, "max": 3, "default": 1 },
      "mode": { "type": "enum", "values": ["idle", "working", "paused"], "default": "idle" },
      "facing": { "type": "vanilla", "property": "HORIZONTAL_FACING", "default": "north" }
    }
  }]
}

data_driven_block is a built-in plain block factory with a default block item (note: a v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline host that does not call JsonTreeBuilder.ensureHandlersRegistered() must call DataDrivenBlockFactory.registerIfAbsent() explicitly to register it). For state-driven proxy rendering, modules/modelling also ships proxy_model, which implements StatefulBlockFactory and handles HORIZONTAL_FACING / DOOR_HINGE placement, rotation, and mirroring automatically.

type Fields Property Default when omitted boolean default: JSON boolean New BooleanProperty false integer min, max, optional default: integers New IntegerProperty min enum values: strings, optional default: one of them StringStateProperty; values are strings, not a Java enum First value vanilla property: uppercase BlockStateProperties field; optional default The original vanilla Property instance First possible value; specify a default explicitly for stability

Names and string values must match [a-z0-9_]+; enum values must be unique. Integer ranges are non-negative, with max > min and max < 2147483647. Each property has 2–64 values, and JSON-declared properties may produce at most 4096 combinations. Native properties on custom block classes multiply the total further.

For vanilla, the JSON key must equal the property's actual name: HORIZONTAL_FACING uses facing. Referencing OPEN this way allows state.getValue(BlockStateProperties.OPEN). A newly created boolean named open is a different instance; retrieve it from that block's getStateDefinition().getProperty("open"). Do not assume properties from different blocks are interchangeable.

Invalid JSON declarations are reported in registration diagnostics and that block is skipped (under v2 STRICT mode, a parse exception records PARSE_FAILED and rejects the whole build). Existing factories without state_properties retain their old behaviour; a block declaring them requires an opted-in factory (StatefulBlockFactory, otherwise STRICT reports UNKNOWN_FACTORY during validate). The plain block does not implement door, redstone, or other interaction logic. Change states on the server through Minecraft's world APIs, and provide blockstate models, item models, loot and localization separately.

Definitions are fixed during registration and cannot be changed by /reload. Client and server need identical definitions. Block IDs, property names and values are part of world saves; changing them can discard or reset existing values. No automatic migration is provided, so back up worlds before upgrades or downgrades.

docs.title: Opt a custom factory in
docs.text:
Minecraft builds the state definition inside the Block superclass constructor. Implement StatefulBlockFactory and scope construction with StatePropertyContext.construct:

FactoryRegistry.register("mymod:custom_block", (StatefulBlockFactory) (id, params, states) ->
    blockWithItem(id, properties -> StatePropertyContext.construct(states,
        () -> new MyBlock(properties))), true);

blockWithItem is the helper from the factory extension guide. The block must add properties during definition creation and apply the JSON defaults after super returns:

public class MyBlock extends Block {
    public MyBlock(Properties properties) {
        super(properties);
        registerDefaultState(StatePropertyContext.applyDefaults(defaultBlockState()));
    }

    @Override
    protected void createBlockStateDefinition(StateDefinition.Builder<Block, BlockState> builder) {
        super.createBlockStateDefinition(builder);
        // Add any native properties first.
        StatePropertyContext.addTo(builder);
    }
}

Preserve defaults set by the superclass before applying JSON defaults. A JSON property must not duplicate a property already added by the block or its superclass; Minecraft rejects duplicates during construction, and a conflict between a custom factory and its block class can abort registration. Both block hooks are required. See StatefulTestBlock and DataDrivenTestFactories in the data-driven contentTesting source set for a working example.

docs.title: Creating and accessing properties from Java
docs.text:
Java code can build a property set with the same validation as JSON. Pass it to StatePropertyContext.construct while the block is constructed during registration:

StatePropertySet properties = StatePropertySet.builder()
    .booleanProperty("charging", false)
    .integerProperty("stage", 0, 3, 0)
    .stringProperty("mode", List.of("idle", "running"), "idle")
    .add(BlockStateProperties.OPEN, false)
    .build();

BlockReg.of("machine", blockProperties ->
    StatePropertyContext.construct(properties, () -> new DataDrivenBlock(blockProperties)));

build() returns an independent immutable snapshot. add(Property<T>, T) retains the supplied instance, also accepts Java enum properties, and checks that every serialized value can be read back. The normal registration flow still configures block items, namespaces and creative tabs as needed.

After registration, resolve a typed reference to the block's actual property:

StateProperty<Boolean> charging = StateProperty.of(machineBlock, "charging", Boolean.class);
boolean current = charging.get(serverLevel, pos);
boolean changed = charging.set(serverLevel, pos, true);
BlockState other = charging.with(state, false); // no world mutation or event
Property<Boolean> minecraftProperty = charging.property();

set requires the server thread and defaults to Minecraft update flags 3 (Block.UPDATE_ALL); an overload accepts explicit flags. It returns false for an unchanged value or rejected update. A true return follows Level#setBlock semantics: later neighbour reactions can still change the state. Wrong block, property name, type or value causes an exception.

docs.title: onChange
docs.text:
StateProperty.Subscription subscription = charging.onChange(change -> {
    LOGGER.info("{}: {} -> {}", change.pos(), change.oldValue(), change.newValue());
});

// Close when the owner no longer needs the listener.
subscription.close();

Subscriptions are scoped to one block and property. The default is the logical server; onChange(StateProperty.Side.CLIENT, callback) and BOTH select other sides. The event provides level() as a LevelReader, an immutable pos(), the old and new states, and oldValue() / newValue(). Closing is idempotent. A listener's runtime exception is logged without preventing other listeners from running.

Only an actual value change on the same block triggers a callback. Placement, removal, unchanged values and changes to other properties do not. Java set, commands and ordinary Level#setBlock use the same hook. Uncommitted NeoForge block snapshots are not reported and rollback is suppressed; loading an entire chunk is not a sequence of block-change events.

The callback runs synchronously inside NeoForge's onBlockStateChange, where world mutation is prohibited. StateProperty.set rejects writes from inside the callback; do not bypass that restriction with Level#setBlock. Schedule world mutations for a later safe server tick. with is safe because it only returns an immutable state.

DataDrivenBlock (as well as ProxyModelBlock) forwards the hook. A custom block must forward it once as well; do not repeat the call if a superclass already does so:

@Override
public void onBlockStateChange(LevelReader level, BlockPos pos,
                               BlockState oldState, BlockState newState) {
    super.onBlockStateChange(level, pos, oldState, newState);
    StateProperty.notifyChanges(level, pos, oldState, newState);
}

docs.title: Client synchronization smoke
docs.text:
An opt-in single-player client smoke places and updates a fixture near the player, so use an isolated client directory and test world:

./gradlew :modules:data-driven:runClient \
  -PkasugaStatePropertyClientDirectory=/absolute/path/to/isolated-client \
  -PkasugaStatePropertyQuickPlayWorld=test-world \
  -PkasugaStatePropertyClientSmoke=true

test-world must already exist under that directory's saves/. Success logs STATE_PROPERTY_CLIENT_SMOKE_PASS server=1 client=1 and then exits; failure logs STATE_PROPERTY_CLIENT_SMOKE_FAIL. This covers one client with an integrated server, not a multiplayer dedicated server.

docs.title: Data-driven JSON format specification (schema)
docs.text: Type: Reference (information-oriented, for looking things up). Applies to: Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.203, Parchment 2024.11.17, Java 21. The format described on this page holds only within this version range. Authoritative source: rules on this page are verified against the current modules/data-driven, modules/core, and modules/modelling source code and tests, covering both the v2 multi-source build pipeline (DataDrivenBuildPipeline in STRICT / LEGACY mode) and the legacy single-mod entry point (JsonTreeBuilder). The old sources layout has been migrated to the index manifest; each rule cites the class, line number, or test name so you can check it directly.

docs.title: 0.1 Three concepts you must keep apart
docs.text:
• registration phase: the phase before mod construction / registry events finish, where object intents are written into Reg trees and then into Minecraft registries (such as BuiltInRegistries.BLOCK). It completes once and cannot hot reload on /reload. On the v2 path (DataDrivenRegistrationProvider + DataDrivenBuildPipeline), input comes from host-captured immutable ResourceSnapshot / ContentSource instances (e.g. SnapshotContentSource); when no provider is installed, JsonTreeBuilder.buildForMod falls back to reading the mod JAR.
  • reload phase: the resource re-read triggered on initial ResourceManager attachment and on /reload; the source it reads is the active Minecraft pack stack, so data packs can override it (managed ApprovedResourcePacks sources are additionally filtered by ManagedReloadAllowlist).
  • index file (index manifest): a .json under data/<namespace>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/ that declares only which content files belong to which domain; it contains no registration objects of its own.

A mod or source's index files can declare only the registration domain, only the reload domain, or both.

docs.title: 0.2 What this page covers
docs.text:
Covered: the index file format; the registration-phase content file format (registry_groups / shapes / blocks / items / embedded block_entity); built-in proxy_model / proxy_model_be params schema; duplicate id, OVERLAY, and REGISTRY_CLAIMS rules; the wrapper format of reload-phase content files; STRICT vs LEGACY decoding and validation differences; and error classification and outlets. Shape expressions and the reference graph are specified in shapes.en.md.

Not covered: the concrete gameplay effect of each properties key in the registry (see ../../guides/data-driven/guide-content.md); the complete codec fields inside state machine definitions and animation clip elements (see ../fsm.md and the codecs under uml/); Java-side TypeHandler extensions in depth (see api-extension.md and ../../guides/data-driven/guide-extension.md).

docs.title: 1.1 Location and discovery rules
docs.text:
The index directory is fixed at a 4-segment path:

data/<namespace>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/
  • Pinned by JsonTreeBuilder.indexDirectorySegments(modId), which returns {"data", modId, "kasuga_lib", "data_driven"} (JsonTreeBuilder.java:766-768).
  • Note that kasuga_lib is a fixed spelling and data_driven uses an underscore. Writing kasuga-lib, or dropping the kasuga_lib level, leads to silently loading 0 entries; that risk is pinned by JsonTreeBuilderIndexPathTest.indexDirectorySegmentsMatchCanonicalLayout() with assertArrayEquals.
  • By default, every direct child .json file in the directory is treated as an index and read in ascending path/filename order (JsonTreeBuilder.listIndexFiles, :783-795; ContentSource.indexes(), ContentSource.java:37-65). Subdirectories are not scanned recursively. There is no filename convention; index.json is only a habit.
  • In v2 SnapshotContentSource, a host can pass declaredIndexes to limit which manifest paths are exposed for the current registration scene (for example a parcel root exposing only parcel.json.indexes); null restores default directory discovery, and an empty collection represents a pure asset/data root with zero manifests. See api-registration.md §17.
  • In the legacy entry point, a missing directory only logs DEBUG and does not count as an error (JsonTreeBuilder.java:83); in the v2 pipeline, a source with no manifests yields zero definitions and succeeds when there are no blocking errors.
  • The reload side reuses the same path segments when it reads the same directory (ReloadOrchestrator.indexResourcePath, ReloadOrchestrator.java:290-297).

docs.title: 1.2 Top-level fields
docs.text:
An index file has only two top-level fields, each a string array:

Field Type Domain Meaning on_register string[] registration phase Lists the content files parsed during registration build and written into Reg / MC registries on_reload string[] reload phase Lists the content files parsed on /reload and written into reload buckets (also preflight-decoded by DataDrivenBuildPipeline in STRICT mode)

Both are optional, but at least one must appear (D1/D2). The legacy field constants are in JsonTreeBuilder.java:45,47 and parsing in parseIndexManifest (:228-257); v2 pipeline parsing is in DataDrivenBuildPipeline.readManifest (DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:513-588).

A legal index declaring both domains:

{
  "on_register": [
    "kasuga_lib_content/blocks.json",
    "kasuga_lib_content/groups.json"
  ],
  "on_reload": [
    "state_machines/panel.json",
    "animation_clips/wheel.json"
  ]
}

docs.title: 1.3 sources is removed (breaking change)
docs.text:
sources is now an illegal field. It is no longer recognized and has no alias; it goes down the "unknown top-level field" path: an error is logged plus a diagnostic (MANIFEST_INVALID in v2), and the file thereby "declares nothing" (which logs another "neither is declared" error / MANIFEST_EMPTY).

{
  "sources": ["kasuga_lib_content/blocks.json"]
}

The example above produces two errors: (1) contains unsupported field 'sources' (or Unsupported index field 'sources' in v2); (2) declares neither 'on_register' nor 'on_reload'. See JsonTreeBuilder.parseIndexManifest (:231-238 unknown field, :247-253 neither declared) and DataDrivenBuildPipeline.readManifest (:553-581); pinned by JsonTreeBuilderIndexSchemaTest.legacySourcesFieldIsReportedAsUnknown().

The old sources field and the old flat layout data/<namespace>/kasugalib/ were both removed by a hard migration, with no compatibility window. If the old directory exists on disk and there is no new index directory, the legacy loader logs one WARN plus a bucket entry hinting at migration to on_register (JsonTreeBuilder.java:73-86).

docs.title: 1.4 Field-level rules D1–D6
docs.text:
The executable version of these rules is JsonTreeBuilderIndexSchemaTest (see section 6). The rules are implemented in parseIndexManifest / resolveIndexManifests and mirrored in DataDrivenBuildPipeline.readManifest / resolveNamespace:

  • D1 Declare at least one field: neither field appears (an empty file, or a file with unknown fields only) → error + diagnostic, and the file contributes no paths. An empty file (parsed as null) is reported too (JsonTreeBuilder.java:247-253; DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:538-550,570-581).
  • D2 An empty array is legal: {"on_register": []} is legal and counts as declared (JsonTreeBuilder.java:244; DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:570).
  • D3 A failure in one field does not implicate its sibling: when on_register is not an array only that field is reported and on_reload is still read, and vice versa (readPathArray, :263-279; readPathField, DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:590-633). A non-string element in the array is reported and skipped, and the remaining elements are kept (:272-277; :617-629).
  • D4 The aggregate warning branches on "was anything ever declared": a pure reload mod that declares only on_reload does not raise "registration domain not declared"; only when no file declares either field does the aggregation stage record a warning/diagnostic (resolveIndexManifests, :347-352; resolveNamespace, DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:642-653). When every file fails its single-file declaration, the aggregate error is still raised.
  • D5 sources is an unknown field, not an alias (:231-238).
  • D6 A path listed in both arrays fails closed: the same path (within one file or across files) appearing in both arrays → error + diagnostic, and that path is consumed by neither domain (removed from both lists). The check spans all index files of that mod or source namespace (resolveIndexManifests, :330-345; resolveNamespace, DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:661-678).

docs.title: 1.5 Path entry rules
docs.text:
Array elements are paths relative to data/<namespace>/ and must carry the .json suffix. Validation is in JsonTreeBuilder.validateSourcePath (:407-416), reused by both the reload side (ReloadOrchestrator.collectIndex, :395) and the v2 pipeline (DataDrivenBuildPipeline.locateContent, :712-762); v2 additionally constructs a LogicalPath. Violating any rule → error + diagnostic, and that entry is skipped:

Rule Message fragment / constraint when violated Non-empty path is empty Does not start with / (must be relative) path must be relative Ends with .json path must include the '.json' suffix No empty segment (//) path contains an empty segment No . or .. segment path must not contain '.' or '..' LogicalPath character constraints (v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline) Forbids \, Windows drive prefixes (e.g. C:), NUL, and ISO control characters (LogicalPath.java:18-47)

Also:

  • The fact that a path cannot cross namespaces is structural: parseSource always joins the path under data/<modId>/ (JsonTreeBuilder.java:441-446), and DataDrivenBuildPipeline.locateContent joins under data/<namespace>/ (DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:724). An entry pointing at assets/ can never take effect.
  • The same path listed in several places within the same mod / source namespace and domain → silently deduplicated during registration (parsedSources in JsonTreeBuilder.parseSource, :427; seenRegister / seenReload in DataDrivenBuildPipeline.resolveNamespace, :680-709). Runtime ReloadOrchestrator.collectIndex does not additionally deduplicate repeated entries within a single on_reload list, so keep each path listed once.
  • The reload side additionally requires the path to form a legal ResourceLocation (only [a-z0-9/._-] is allowed); illegal characters such as uppercase are reported separately (ReloadOrchestrator.java:401-412). Note that DataDrivenBuildPipeline preflight on on_reload checks LogicalPath and source existence without constructing ResourceLocation ahead of time.
  • An illegal path, a missing file, and an unreadable JSON file all produce errors (parseSource, :419-462; locateContent / parseContentFile, DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:712-800).

docs.title: 1.6 Merging multiple manifests and strict JSON
docs.text:
All index files of the same mod or ContentSource are fully read in first and then consumed together:

  • Legacy JsonTreeBuilder: paths are concatenated by "ascending index filename → array writing order within the file" (JsonTreeBuilder.java:97-117,318-356).
  • v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline: sources are processed in ascending global rank; within each source, manifests are aggregated per namespace, cross-listed paths are rejected and same-domain duplicates removed, and on_register / on_reload paths are sorted lexicographically by logicalPath before parsing (DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:463-511).
  • STRICT JSON decoding (StrictResourceJson): when DataDrivenBuildPipeline runs with BuildOptions.STRICT, manifests, registration content files, and on_reload preflight files all pass through strict UTF-8 decoding (rejecting malformed byte sequences) and StrictResourceJson.parse (DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:1559-1574, StrictResourceJson.java:14-51):
  • reader.setLenient(false): rejects comments, single quotes, trailing commas, and other non-standard JSON;
  • requires the entire file to be exactly one JSON object with no trailing documents;
  • rejects duplicate keys inside any JSON object immediately rather than silently keeping the last value;
  • enforces a maximum text length of 8 MiB, default max depth of 64, and max 100,000 nodes.
  • LEGACY mode and JsonTreeBuilder use Gson's tolerant parsing, and in LEGACY a MANIFEST_INVALID diagnostic does not block build apply on its own.

docs.title: 2.1 File top-level structure
docs.text:
In a content file the top-level field name is the top-level registration type, and the value must be an array of objects. There are 4 built-in top-level types and 1 embedded type:

Top-level field handler phase Effect registry_groups RegistryGroupHandler 0 Establish property groups (parent/child) shapes ShapeTypeHandler -1 Precompile geometry definitions and cross-shape output references blocks BlockTypeHandler 1 Register blocks items ItemTypeHandler 1 Register standalone items block_entities (embedded) BlockEntityTypeHandler 2 Embedded inside blocks[].block_entity; invalid as a top-level field

One content file can contain several top-level fields at once (for example one registry_groups set and one blocks set), dispatched one by one by dispatchContent (JsonTreeBuilder.java:485) or DataDrivenBuildPipeline.parseContentFile (DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:764-917).

{
  "registry_groups": [
    { "id": "mymod:panels", "properties": { "no_occlusion": true } }
  ],
  "blocks": [
    {
      "id": "mymod:panel",
      "type": "data_driven_block",
      "registry_group": "mymod:panels",
      "properties": { "destroy_time": 2.0 },
      "item_properties": { "tab": "mymod:main" }
    }
  ]
}

Validation of top-level fields:

  • Unknown top-level field → ERROR (UNKNOWN_TYPE) in JsonTreeBuilder and STRICT, WARNING in LEGACY; JsonTreeBuilder and LEGACY keep dispatching the remaining fields in the same file (partial apply), whereas STRICT records a blocking diagnostic and rejects the whole batch before apply (REJECTED).
  • A known field whose value is not an array → ERROR (CONTENT_INVALID), remaining fields proceed.
  • An array element that is not a JSON object → ERROR (CONTENT_INVALID), that element is skipped, remaining elements proceed.

docs.title: 2.2 registry_groups entries
docs.text:
Parsing is in RegistryGroupHandler.parse (RegistryGroupHandler.java:45-49), application in store (:108-141), and strict validation in validate (:71-98).

Field Type Required Default Meaning id string yes — Group id. Matched by the raw string, with no namespace normalization parent string no null → attached to the root group Parent group id; in the legacy loader an absent parent falls back to the root group (:111-116); v2 STRICT verifies the parent exists and is visible properties object no — Block properties passed down to child content (see section 2.6) item_properties object no — Item properties passed down to child content; tab is singled out as this group's creative tab (:126-127)
  • A group has no type field.
  • Blocks and items look their group up through registry_group using the raw string; therefore id is not normalized and mymod:panels and panels are two different groups (RegistryGroupHandler.resolveIdentity, :66-68).
  • Before applying, a topological sort is done by parent: parents before children; in the legacy loader and LEGACY mode a cycle only gets a WARN / warning diagnostic and falls back to the original order (JsonTreeBuilder.topoSortGroupDefs, :890), while in v2 STRICT it records a GROUP_CYCLE blocking error and rejects the build (DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:1233-1297).
  • In v2 STRICT, JsonPropertyParser.validateStrict and JsonItemParser.validateStrict validate properties and item_properties on groups, emitting CONTENT_INVALID errors for unknown keys or invalid values.

docs.title: 2.3 blocks entries
docs.text:
Parsing is in BlockTypeHandler.parse (BlockTypeHandler.java:31-36), generic application in RegTypeHandler.apply (RegTypeHandler.java:155-205), and strict validation in RegTypeHandler.validate (:102-141) and BlockTypeHandler.validate (:70-105).

Field Type Required Default Meaning id string yes — Block id; STRICT requires explicit namespace:path, legacy/LEGACY allow bare paths type string yes — Factory name, looked up in FactoryRegistry.BlockFactory (BlockTypeHandler.createRegistration, :126-133) registry_group string no null → attached to the root group Owning group id (raw-string match) properties object no — Block properties, see section 2.6 state_properties object no — Minecraft block-state properties; see block-state-properties.md item_properties object no — Item properties for the block's item; tab decides the creative tab (BlockTypeHandler.resolveCreativeTab, :64-67) params object no null Passed to the factory verbatim by create(path, params) (StatefulBlockFactory also receives state_properties) state_machine JSON primitive no — Forwarded into the BE params.state_machine only when the entry contains a block_entity (see section 2.5) block_entity object no — Embedded block entity definition (see section 2.5)
  • When id or type is missing, parse throws (Objects.requireNonNull); in the legacy loader only that entry is lost while siblings proceed, while in STRICT it records PARSE_FAILED and rejects the whole build.
  • Missing factory type: in the legacy loader without state_properties, only a WARN is logged and the entry is skipped (RegTypeHandler.java:162-166). In v2 STRICT, any missing factory records UNKNOWN_FACTORY, and declaring state_properties for a factory that does not implement StatefulBlockFactory also records UNKNOWN_FACTORY (BlockTypeHandler.java:92-104).
  • Unknown keys on the block entry itself are silently ignored during Gson deserialization, but in STRICT mode keys inside properties, item_properties, and state_properties are strictly validated.
  • Built-in stateful block factories are data_driven_block and proxy_model (see section 2.9).

docs.title: 2.4 items entries
docs.text:
Parsing is in ItemTypeHandler.parse (ItemTypeHandler.java:30-35), strict validation in :59-71.

Field Type Required Default Meaning id string yes — Item id; STRICT requires explicit namespace:path type string yes — Factory name, looked up in FactoryRegistry.ItemFactory (:74-78) registry_group string no attached to the root group Owning group id properties object no — Item properties, see section 2.6; tab decides the creative tab (:53-56) params object no null Passed to the factory

docs.title: 2.5 block_entities (embedded type)
docs.text:
A block entity has no id of its own; it is carried by its host block, and the way to write one is to put a block_entity object inside that block's entry:

{
  "blocks": [
    {
      "id": "mymod:be_block",
      "type": "be_block",
      "block_entity": {
        "type": "test_be",
        "params": { "tick_interval": 4 }
      }
    }
  ]
}
  • The top-level field name is block_entities, but the embedded key name is block_entity (BlockEntityTypeHandler.getTypeName :29, getParentTypeName :48, getEmbeddedKeyName :51).
  • Extraction logic: BlockEntityTypeHandler.extractEmbedded (:54-66) injects the host block's id into the embedded object's _parent_block; if the host block has a top-level state_machine of JSON primitive type (string / number / boolean), it is forwarded into the embedded object's params.state_machine (:59-64). The test is isJsonPrimitive(), so number and boolean pass too, converted to text by getAsString() before being stored in params; objects, arrays, and null are ignored.

Fields of the embedded block_entity object:

Field Type Required Default Meaning type string yes — Block entity factory name, looked up in FactoryRegistry.BlockEntityFactory (for example built-in proxy_model_be / fsm_be) params object no null Passed to the factory; concrete keys are interpreted by the factory (see section 2.9 for proxy_model_be) _parent_block string — injected Do not write this by hand; it is injected by extractEmbedded
  • Duplicate detection: two BE entries attached to the same host block count as duplicates (resolveIdentity, :87-96, using the host block's effective id).
  • Registry claim: in v2 it emits minecraft:block_entity_type / <block_ns>:<block_path>_be (claims, :124-134).
  • Host block not found / unknown BE factory: the legacy loader logs a WARN (BlockEntityTypeHandler.apply, :141-152); v2 STRICT validates host block visibility and BE factory availability (MISSING_REFERENCE / REFERENCE_NOT_DECLARED / UNKNOWN_FACTORY), and apply propagates runtime exceptions in strict contexts (:163).

docs.title: 2.6 Inner keys of properties / item_properties
docs.text:
A top-level field's properties and item_properties are claimed by two parsers. Mode difference: the legacy loader and LEGACY pipeline log a WARN for unknown keys or most malformed values and ignore that modifier; v2 STRICT invokes JsonPropertyParser.validateStrict / JsonItemParser.validateStrict and turns unknown keys or out-of-range/wrong-type values into CONTENT_INVALID blocking errors (BlockTypeHandler.java:72-91, ItemTypeHandler.java:61-70, RegistryGroupHandler.java:78-97).

Block properties properties (JsonPropertyParser.buildCompilers, JsonPropertyParser.java:248-274; strict validation :45-109):

Key Value type Key Value type no_occlusion bool light_emission int (STRICT requires 0..15) no_collision / no_collission (spelling alias) bool friction float (finite) requires_correct_tool bool speed_factor float (finite) replaceable bool jump_factor float (finite) dynamic_shape bool destroy_time float (finite) random_ticks bool explosion_resistance float (finite) no_loot_table bool strength float or a [destroy, resist] two-finite-number array ignited_by_lava bool map_color DyeColor name (lowercase) liquid bool sound_type sound type name (see below) force_solid_on bool air bool no_terrain_particles bool
  • The legal values of sound_type come from JsonPropertyParser.buildSoundTypeMap (:197-246), such as stone / wood / metal / glass.
  • map_color uses MC DyeColor names.

Item properties item_properties (block entries) / properties (item entries) (JsonItemParser, JsonItemParser.java:23-40; strict validation :57-123):

Key Value type Meaning stacks_to int Maximum stack size (STRICT requires 1..99) rarity string COMMON / UNCOMMON / RARE / EPIC (case-insensitive) fire_resistant bool Fire resistance durability int Durability (STRICT requires >= 1) no_repair bool Cannot be repaired tab string Creative tab ResourceLocation; consumed separately (STRICT requires valid namespace:path)

Properties are inherited along the parent chain, and a child entry overrides its parent (RegTypeHandler.apply sets registry_group as the parent, Reg.applyProperties applies parents before children).

docs.title: 2.7 Unknown keys inside an object vs unknown top-level file keys
docs.text:
• An unknown top-level file field → ERROR (UNKNOWN_TYPE) in JsonTreeBuilder and STRICT, WARNING in LEGACY (JsonTreeBuilder.java:496-518, DataDrivenBuildPipeline.java:807-823). A misspelled blokcs is caught.
  • An unknown key inside an entry object → ignored by Gson deserialization in each handler's parse, except inside state_properties (which always rejects unknown fields via StatePropertySet.requireKeys) and inside properties / item_properties in STRICT mode (which reject unknown keys via validateStrict).

docs.title: 2.8 An embedded type written as a top-level field by mistake
docs.text:
Writing block_entities as a top-level field (instead of putting it in the block_entity key of a blocks entry) goes down the "unknown top-level field" path:

  • In legacy JsonTreeBuilder: ERROR + bucket entry naming the block_entity key of a blocks entry as where it belongs, and the rest of the file's blocks dispatch as usual (JsonTreeBuilder.java:496-518).
  • In v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline: reported as UNKNOWN_TYPE (ERROR blocking the build in STRICT, WARNING in LEGACY).
{
  "block_entities": [ { "type": "test_be" } ],
  "blocks": [ { "id": "mymod:ok", "type": "simple_block" } ]
}

Legacy partial-dispatch behavior is pinned by JsonTreeBuilderEmbeddedTypeDispatchTest.topLevelEmbeddedTypeIsReportedAndTheRestOfTheFileStillDispatches(). When an embedded object itself fails to parse from a missing field, the legacy loader discards only that embedded element while siblings proceed, whereas STRICT records PARSE_FAILED and rejects the batch.

docs.title: 2.9 Built-in proxy_model / proxy_model_be schema
docs.text:
modules/modelling provides a built-in generic proxy-model block/BE pair (ProxyModelBlockFactories.java, registered automatically at startup by its @Context bean or explicitly via ProxyModelBlockFactories.registerBuiltin()):

  • Block factory type: "proxy_model" (ProxyModelBlockFactories.BLOCK_TYPE): implements StatefulBlockFactory and registers createsBlockItem = true, producing ProxyModelBlock plus a default same-id block item.
  • Composes with normal state_properties: if vanilla facing (HORIZONTAL_FACING) or hinge (DOOR_HINGE) is declared, ProxyModelBlock automatically wires placement, rotation, and mirroring (ProxyModelBlock.java:71-113).
  • Always uses RenderShape.ENTITYBLOCK_ANIMATED so a missing baked block model does not show the purple/black missing texture.
  • Rejects block-level params: ProxyModelBlockFactories.validateBlockParams (:77-84) throws IllegalArgumentException if blocks[].params is non-empty (implement custom block interactions in a dedicated block subclass and factory).
  • Embedded block entity block_entity.type: "proxy_model_be" (ProxyModelBlockFactories.BLOCK_ENTITY_TYPE): creates ProxyModelBlockEntity.

Supported fields of proxy_model_be's block_entity.params (ProxyModelBlockFactories.java:155-401):

Field Type Required Default Meaning and validation rules model string (ResourceLocation) either model or model_groups — Single-model shorthand: builds a CompiledModelGroup with id "default" and one part (id "body"). Throws if neither model nor model_groups is provided model_name string no null Sub-model name inside the file (MMD .pmx only), applied with params.model default_model string no see right Group id in model_groups used when no model_by_state rule matches. When omitted, uses "default" if params.model was provided, or the first entry in model_groups otherwise. Throws if unknown yaw_offset number (float) no 0.0 Extra horizontal yaw offset in degrees added on top of the blockstate facing yaw facing_yaw object (string -> float) no {} Explicit yaw overrides in degrees keyed by HORIZONTAL_FACING serialized name ("north", "east", "south", "west"); overrides facingYaw(state) + yaw_offset when present lighting_mode string no null "pbr" (ModelLightingMode.PBR) or "vanilla_block" (ModelLightingMode.BLOCK); omitting preserves the model asset's default; any non-string or unknown value throws IllegalArgumentException at registration model_groups object (<group_id> -> group) no (required if model omitted) — Named multi-part compiled model groups; <group_id> must match [a-z0-9_.:/-]+ model_by_state object (<prop> -> {<val>: <target>}) no {} Ordered blockstate selector rules evaluated in JSON key order; the first matching rule wins animation — forbidden — Explicitly rejected (IllegalArgumentException); state-driven playback belongs in a Java ProxyModelBlock.createProxyComposition override

model_groups.<group_id> object schema:

Field Type Required Default Meaning y_offset number (float) no 0.0 Finite vertical offset applied to the proxy root when this group is active parts object[] yes — Non-empty ordered array of part objects (CompiledModelPart)

parts[] element schema:

Field Type Required Default Meaning id string yes — Non-blank part identifier, must match [a-z0-9_.-]+ and be unique within the group model string (ResourceLocation) yes — Model resource location model_name string no null Sub-model name inside the file (.pmx only) local object[] no [] Ordered array of local Transform operations relative to the proxy root; each object must contain exactly one of translate, rotate, or scale as a 3-element finite number array (rotate is in degrees)

Key invariants (ProxyModelSelection.java:40-47, 80-98):

  • Every group must share the exact same ordered part.id list: all groups in a proxy_model_be (including "default" from params.model and any implicit single-part "body" groups synthesized by model_by_state) must declare identical ordered part.id lists, or registration fails with IllegalArgumentException.
  • model_by_state resolution and registration-time validation: <target> is resolved first by group id against model_groups; if not found there, it is parsed as a ResourceLocation and wrapped as a single-part ("body") group ("legacy_<ns>_<path>"). At onRegistered time, ProxyModelSelection.validate(block.defaultBlockState()) verifies that every referenced property name and state value exists on the host block's BlockState.

Minimal single-model example:

{
  "blocks": [
    {
      "id": "example:sign_post",
      "type": "proxy_model",
      "state_properties": {
        "facing": { "type": "vanilla", "property": "HORIZONTAL_FACING", "default": "north" }
      },
      "block_entity": {
        "type": "proxy_model_be",
        "params": {
          "model": "example:models/block/sign_post.bbmodel",
          "yaw_offset": 180.0,
          "lighting_mode": "vanilla_block"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

Multi-part model_groups + model_by_state + facing_yaw example:

{
  "blocks": [
    {
      "id": "example:sliding_gate",
      "type": "proxy_model",
      "state_properties": {
        "facing": { "type": "vanilla", "property": "HORIZONTAL_FACING", "default": "north" },
        "open": { "type": "vanilla", "property": "OPEN", "default": false }
      },
      "block_entity": {
        "type": "proxy_model_be",
        "params": {
          "default_model": "closed",
          "facing_yaw": { "north": 0, "east": 90, "south": 180, "west": 270 },
          "lighting_mode": "pbr",
          "model_groups": {
            "closed": {
              "y_offset": 0.0,
              "parts": [
                { "id": "frame", "model": "example:models/block/gate_frame.bbmodel" },
                {
                  "id": "leaf",
                  "model": "example:models/block/gate_leaf.bbmodel",
                  "local": [ { "translate": [0, 0, 0] } ]
                }
              ]
            },
            "opened": {
              "y_offset": 0.05,
              "parts": [
                { "id": "frame", "model": "example:models/block/gate_frame.bbmodel" },
                {
                  "id": "leaf",
                  "model": "example:models/block/gate_leaf.bbmodel",
                  "local": [
                    { "translate": [0.75, 0, 0] },
                    { "rotate": [0, 15, 0] }
                  ]
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          "model_by_state": {
            "open": {
              "false": "closed",
              "true": "opened"
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

At runtime, use /kasuga_proxy list (ProxyCommands.java) to inspect live ProxyInstance stage, model, parts, and mounted status.

docs.title: 3. Duplicate ids, OVERLAY, and claim checks
3.1 Legacy JsonTreeBuilder deduplication (last-wins)
docs.text:
In legacy JsonTreeBuilder, deduplication happens before any registration side effect: once parsing has finished, conflicts are resolved first and losers never reach apply (JsonTreeBuilder.resolveDuplicates, :673), because MC's MappedRegistry.register does not reject duplicate keys (DuplicateIdResolver.java:11-14).

The conflict space is (typeName, identity):

Type identity (legacy / LEGACY) identity (v2 STRICT) blocks / items EffectiveId.ofLegacy(modId, id): no namespace or minecraft: → <modId>:path; other namespaces verbatim EffectiveId.of(modId, id): bare id resolves to <modId>:path (though validate rejects bare ids with INVALID_IDENTITY); explicit minecraft: stays minecraft:path block_entities host block's EffectiveId.ofLegacy host block's EffectiveId.of registry_groups raw id string (not normalized) raw id string (not normalized)

In JsonTreeBuilder, "last" in last-wins is the position in the load sequence:

  1. Between index files: ascending filename order;
  2. Within one index file: the writing order of on_register;
  3. Within one content file: array order;
  4. Embedded BEs: follow their host blocks entry.

Each conflict records a WARN log line plus one loading-error bucket entry (JsonTreeBuilder.java:688-696).

docs.title: 3.2 v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline selection and claims checks
docs.text:
The v2 pipeline branches by TypeHandler.capabilities() and BuildOptions (DataDrivenBuildPipeline.selectDefinitions, :1149-1183):

  • Configuration types (NON_REGISTRATION without OVERLAY) and LEGACY ordinary types: picks the winner with highest (sourceOrder, declarationOrder) (last-wins), where sourceOrder comes from the platform ResourceSourceDescriptor.rank() (or input position for legacy SourceDescriptor). All parsed candidates remain in PreparedContent.allDefinitions().
  • Overlay types (HandlerCapability.OVERLAY): in both STRICT and LEGACY, all candidates sharing a DefinitionKey stay selected so the handler can merge or overlay them.
  • Strict registration types (STRICT with REGISTRY_CLAIMS and without NON_REGISTRATION): retains all candidates sharing a DefinitionKey, validates each one, and collects all RegistryClaim entries before apply (collectClaims, :1304-1401):
  • collision with host reservedRegistryClaims (e.g. from RegistryClaimSnapshot.collect) → CLAIM_CONFLICT (ERROR in both modes);
  • two definitions claiming the same (registry, id) → CLAIM_CONFLICT (ERROR + batch REJECTED in STRICT, WARNING in LEGACY).

docs.title: 4.1 The two content types and how they are discovered
docs.text:
ReloadOrchestrator is the only orchestrator in the reload domain (ReloadOrchestrator.java:121), and it knows no type name itself: the typeName() of every registered ReloadHandler is a legal top-level key. The two handlers registered by modelling are state_machines and animation_clips (FsmReloadHandler / FsmClipsReloadHandler, see section 4.6).

Content Top-level key Discovery State machine definitions state_machines directory glob data/<ns>/state_machines/*.json + listed in on_reload Animation clips animation_clips only listed in on_reload
  • state_machines/ has a directory glob: FsmReloadHandler.globDirectories() (FsmReloadHandler.java:69-71) declares StateMachineDefinitionLoader.PATH (StateMachineDefinitionLoader.java:39), enumerated by ReloadOrchestrator.collectGlob (ReloadOrchestrator.java:365-385) using ResourceManager.listResourceStacks. Unmanaged mod/datapack files under state_machines/*.json are read even if no index lists them.
  • Managed packs (ManagedReloadAllowlist): packs projected by ApprovedResourcePacks are filtered by ManagedReloadAllowlist (ReloadOrchestrator.java:317-332,375-380,419-437): managed sources only load approved index and on_reload content paths at their prepared priority and do not participate in unmanaged directory glob discovery.
  • animation_clips/ has no directory glob. A clip file not listed by an index is never read (AnimationClipLoader.java:31-32; FsmClipsReloadHandler.globDirectories keeps the default empty set).
  • state_machines/ files listed by an index are skipped by the glob pass to avoid reading them twice (ReloadOrchestrator.collectGlob, :372-374).
  • Application order: glob-discovered first, index-listed second; on the same id the latter wins (class javadoc :82-94; register, :562-577).
  • Startup preflight: DataDrivenBuildPipeline.prepare also reads on_reload files declared in source manifests, parses them under StrictResourceJson in STRICT mode, and runs matching ReloadHandler.decode from ReloadHandlerRegistry without calling clearBucket() or register() (DataDrivenBuildPipeline.validateReloadContentFile, :919-1025).

docs.title: 4.2 state_machines wrapper
docs.text:
Each file is a wrapper object carrying the state_machines top-level key, whose value must be an array of definitions (extra top-level keys no longer reject the file, see section 4.4):

{
  "state_machines": [
    {
      "id": "mymod:panel",
      "layers": [
        {
          "id": "base",
          "initial_state": "idle",
          "states": [
            { "id": "idle", "duration_ticks": 20 }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
  • One file can hold several definitions, and the array order is the in-file last-wins order (StateMachineDefinitionLoader.java:26-28).
  • The element schema is decided by StateMachineDefinition.CODEC; this page specifies only the wrapper, and element fields are in ../fsm.md and the corresponding codec.

docs.title: 4.3 animation_clips wrapper
docs.text:
Likewise a wrapper object carrying the animation_clips top-level key:

{
  "animation_clips": [
    {
      "id": "mymod:wheel_spin",
      "duration_seconds": 2.5,
      "bones": [
        {
          "bone": "wheel_r",
          "keyframes": [
            { "time": 0.0, "transform": { "rotate": [0, 0, 0] } }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
  • The element carries its own id (the very id states[].clip references), and the loader does not extract an id separately (AnimationClipLoader.java:23-26).
  • Keys in the element that the codec does not name are ignored, and can serve as comments or editor metadata (:26-27). Removed legacy keys functions and formula_parts are explicitly rejected by decodeFile with a hint to use formula_transforms (AnimationClipLoader.java:100-108).
  • The file takes effect only in on_reload and registers into the reload bucket; a SCRIPT clip of the same name is not overridden by the file (AnimationClipLoader.register, :127-132).

docs.title: 4.4 File-level strictness, element-level tolerance
docs.text:
The two decoders isolate failures identically (StateMachineDefinitionLoader.decodeFile :67-100; AnimationClipLoader.decodeFile :71-116):

  • File level: a non-object body, a missing top-level key, or a non-array value → the whole file is rejected, with one error. {"state_machines": {}} is rejected as a whole (StateMachineDefinitionLoaderTest.nonArrayValueRejectsWholeFile).
  • File level (genuinely unknown key): a top-level key claimed by no reload type → one unsupported top-level field 'extra' (or UNKNOWN_TYPE in DataDrivenBuildPipeline), while at runtime known keys still contribute as usual (StateMachineDefinitionLoaderTest.extraTopLevelKeyDoesNotAffectThisType(); AnimationClipLoaderTest.ignoresAnExtraTopLevelKey()).
  • Multiple top-level keys are legal: one file can carry both state_machines and animation_clips, and the two decoders each read their own key and contribute their own entries (AnimationClipReloadTest.mixedTopLevelKeysAreConsumedByBothHandlers).
  • Element level: an array element that is not an object, fails to decode, or uses removed functions/formula_parts keys → only that element is skipped, its siblings proceed as usual, and each failure is reported.
  • An empty array is legal (AnimationClipLoaderTest.emptyClipArrayIsValid()).

docs.title: 4.5 Reload domain routing and the reverse D9 hint
docs.text:
• The domain is decided by the index array, and the content type by the top-level key.
  • An unknown top-level key in a reload file → error + RELOAD_DATA bucket entry, with a reverse hint attached: if these fields are registration content (such as blocks/items/registry_groups), list the file under on_register instead (ReloadOrchestrator.java:494-501).
  • One file can carry both content types at once: each handler claims its own top-level key and contributes its own entries (ReloadOrchestrator.dispatch, :484-525).
  • The reload wrap-up re-checks the clips referenced by state machines; a dangling reference records a WARN + RELOAD_DATA entry, without affecting registration (FsmReloadHandler.afterReload, :95-115).

docs.title: 4.6 Extending to a new reload type
docs.text: Reload types are not hardcoded: implement ReloadHandler<T> and register it via ReloadHandlerRegistry.register(handler) from a @Context bean's @PostConstruct. typeName() is the top-level key this type claims and doubles as the deduplication collision space. See guide-extension.md §6 and api-reload.md §13.

docs.title: 5.1 Errors (error log + diagnostic entry)
docs.text:
• Legacy registration loader & reload domain (lands in JsonTreeBuilder mod buckets or Diagnostics.Domain.RELOAD_DATA):
Case Source Unknown index field / field not an array / element not a string JsonTreeBuilder.java:231-277 A single file declares neither domain; every file declares neither :247-253 (error) / :347-352 (WARN + bucket) The same path listed in both arrays :330-345 Failure reading an index file or directory :194-204, :783-795 Unknown top-level field in a content file, field not an array, element not an object :496-535 Illegal content file path / missing file / parse exception :419-462 handler apply throws :733-742 Duplicate id conflict :688-692 (WARN log + bucket entry) Reload side: manifest read failure, illegal path, missing file, unauthorized managed source, wrapper shape violation, unknown top-level key ReloadOrchestrator.java:341-447,484-525 Duplicate id on the reload side :602-610 (WARN log + bucket entry) Dangling clip reference at reload wrap-up FsmReloadHandler.java:105-113 (WARN log + bucket entry)
  • v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline: produces structured BuildDiagnostic entries (with Severity.ERROR/WARNING, Stage, Code, sourceId, ownerId, logicalPath, jsonPointer, handler, message, suggestion) stored in PreparedContent.diagnostics() and BuildResult.diagnostics(). They do not write into Diagnostics or /kasuga_data errors automatically; see api-diagnostics.md §19.

docs.title: 5.2 Warnings (warn, no legacy bucket entry / mode-dependent)
docs.text:
In the legacy loader the cases below only log a WARN without entering the error bucket, whereas v2 STRICT promotes most of them to ERROR blocking diagnostics:

  • Without state_properties, an unknown factory type skips the entry with a WARN (RegTypeHandler.java:162-166). Missing/incompatible factories with state_properties, or any missing factory in v2 STRICT, report UNKNOWN_FACTORY.
  • Unknown properties / item_properties keys or invalid values → legacy logs WARN and ignores (JsonPropertyParser.java:152-159, JsonItemParser.java:147); v2 STRICT validates via validateStrict and emits CONTENT_INVALID errors.
  • BE host block not found / unknown BE factory → legacy logs WARN (BlockEntityTypeHandler.java:141-152); v2 STRICT emits MISSING_REFERENCE / REFERENCE_NOT_DECLARED / UNKNOWN_FACTORY.
  • Group reference cycle → legacy logs WARN (JsonTreeBuilder.java:907-909); v2 LEGACY emits WARNING, STRICT emits ERROR (GROUP_CYCLE).

docs.title: 5.3 Reading diagnostics
docs.text:
• Legacy registration & reload domain:
  • JsonTreeBuilder.getLoadingErrors(modId) / getLoadingErrorsByMod() / getLoadingErrors() (JsonTreeBuilder.java:827-859).
  • Diagnostics: Diagnostics.errors(modId), Diagnostics.errors(Domain, key), Diagnostics.summarize() (Diagnostics.java:64-168).
  • In-game commands: /kasuga_data errors [mod] (DataDiagnosticsCommands.java) and /kasuga_proxy list (ProxyCommands.java).
  • v2 DataDrivenBuildPipeline: inspect prepared.diagnostics() / result.diagnostics() and prepared.hasBlockingDiagnostics(); hosts export or log them directly.

docs.title: 5.4 D9 hint text (content listed under the wrong domain)
docs.text:
Conditional hints in both directions (part of the diagnostic contract for JsonTreeBuilder and ReloadOrchestrator):

  • Registration side: on_register lists a reload-domain file → goes down the unknown-field path and ends with "list this file under 'on_reload' instead", enumerating registered reload type names from ReloadHandlerRegistry at runtime (JsonTreeBuilder.java:580-591; test JsonTreeBuilderReloadHintTest.reloadDomainContentUnderOnRegisterIsReportedWithOnReloadHint()).
  • Reload side: on_reload lists a registration-domain file → ends with "list the file under 'on_register' instead", enumerating top-level registration types from TypeHandlerRegistry (ReloadOrchestrator.java:494-501,543-554).

Partial-apply guarantee: in JsonTreeBuilder and ReloadOrchestrator, listing one wrong-domain field still leaves valid sibling fields in the same file processed (JsonTreeBuilderReloadHintTest.halfApplyStillDispatchesSiblingRegistrationFields()).

docs.title: 7. Boundaries with other documents
docs.text:
• This page (schema.md): the authoritative reference for the JSON format, covering fields, types, built-in proxy_model parameters, requiredness, path rules, STRICT/LEGACY differences, and error classification.
  • intro.md: an introductory tutorial answering "what is this, and why use it".
  • guide-content.md: a task-oriented guide answering "how do I build my first content file".
  • guide-extension.md: Java-side extensions (custom TypeHandler / factories / property compilers / ReloadHandler).
  • api-registration.md / api-extension.md / api-diagnostics.md / api-reload.md: Java API references (covering both the v2 multi-source pipeline and legacy entry points).
  • block-state-properties.md: full state_properties constraints and the Java StateProperty API.
  • fsm.md: codec fields inside state machine definition and animation clip elements.
  • Data-Driven System Explanations: v2 fixed snapshots, multi-source rank ordering, host wiring, and migration.

docs.title: Appendix A: Not covered / to be confirmed
docs.text:
• The complete field table and defaults of state_machines / animation_clips elements: this page specifies only the wrapper. For the element schema, treat StateMachineDefinition.CODEC, AnimationClip.CODEC, and fsm.md as the authority.
  • The runtime behavior when tab points at a creative tab that does not exist: format validation only checks that tab parses as a valid ResourceLocation (JsonItemParser.validateStrict / RegTypeHandler.resolveCreativeTab) and does not check whether that tab is registered at runtime.
  • World-save compatibility policy across restarts: DataDrivenBuildPipeline supplies PreparedContent.claims() and BuildResult, while comparing historical pack sets/claims and refusing incompatible worlds belongs to the host layer.

docs.title: Data-Driven Shapes
docs.text:
The top-level shapes field is an array of definitions. One prepare pass selects and validates the complete domain, then compiles it into an immutable ShapeCatalog for apply. Clients never interpret the JSON DSL during ticks or rendering.

The formal JSON Schema is modules/data-driven/src/main/resources/schema/kasuga-data-driven-shapes.schema.json. A content file may also contain registry_groups, blocks, and items. Shape entries do not use a format_version field.

docs.title: Definitions
docs.text:
Each definition accepts only id, optional parent, nodes, and output. A root definition requires both nodes and output; with a parent, each may be omitted and inherited separately. id and parent are complete namespace:path resource locations. output is a non-empty node name; it never contains an id, array, operation, or ShapeRef.

{
  "shapes": [
    {
      "id": "example:frame",
      "nodes": {
        "outer": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 32.0, 32.0, 4.0],
        "opening": [8.0, 0.0, 0.0, 24.0, 30.0, 4.0],
        "result": {"op": "difference", "args": ["outer", "opening"]}
      },
      "output": "result"
    }
  ]
}

A child replaces a parent node by name; arrays and operation arguments are never appended. A child that omits output inherits the parent's selected name, while an explicit value replaces it. To use a parent's final geometry, write {"ref":"parent:id"}. A local string with the same name as a parent node resolves in the child's merged graph and can therefore create a local cycle.

docs.title: Expressions
docs.text:
A node value has one of five forms:

Expression Form Contract Box6 six JSON numbers Pixel coordinates validated before and after binary32 narrowing Empty [] A valid empty result, distinct from a missing member Local name non-empty string Resolves only in the current definition's merged nodes; forward references work ShapeRef {"ref":"namespace:path","transform":{...}} Compiles the target's output in the target's own graph Operation {"op":"union|intersection|difference","args":[...]} 2–64 recursively validated expressions

union, intersection, difference, op, args, and ref are ordinary node-name strings. Only the op member of an Operation object is an operator. The retired ["union", ...] array syntax is rejected; an expression array is either empty or exactly six numbers.

difference subtracts each later operand from the first. Face, edge, and point contacts do not create volume under the geometry module's regularized solid rules. Compilation uses its depth, work, and result fragment budgets.

docs.title: ShapeRef and transforms
docs.text:
A ShapeRef exposes only the target definition's selected output. The target compiles in its own scope; caller node names never merge into it. Each reference applies its own transform after the target result is compiled:

{
  "ref": "example:frame",
  "transform": {
    "scale": [1.0, 1.0, 1.0],
    "rotate_y": 90,
    "pivot": [8.0, 0.0, 8.0],
    "translate": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
  }
}

The order is positive per-axis scale, a Y-axis quarter turn (0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees), then translation. Pivot and translation use pixels; the default pivot is [8,0,8]. Compiled results are already in block units and must not be divided by 16 again. An explicitly empty target is a valid operand.

docs.title: Diagnostics and dependencies
docs.text:
Strict prepare checks every node, parent edge, and ShapeRef before apply, including references that are unreachable from the selected output. Diagnostics point at the failing JSON member, such as /shapes/0/nodes/result/op, /args/2, or /output. Definition ids follow the directory's ordered selection rules. A cross-owner reference requires a direct dependency. Missing or invisible targets, ambiguous ids, parent/local/external or mixed cycles, binary32 narrowing, unit-conversion overflow, and geometry budget failures all block apply.

Each target compiles once per prepare pass. ShapeRef operands share that immutable result and apply only their own transform. Failed shapes never fall back to a parent, another source, or a native block shape. P2 supplies definitions and the compiled catalog only; block slots, collision, rendering, and native fallback belong to host adapters.

docs.title: Formula Module
docs.text:
modules/formula is KasugaLib's general-purpose expression engine: arithmetic (compute) plus boolean logic (logic), with namespace-scoped variable and function registration. It is a pure JVM library with zero Minecraft dependencies — it does not touch the game, so it can be consumed by modelling, core, scripting, or any other module.

The engine was migrated from the 1.0 Forge external artifact Mixed-Arithmetic-Logic-Interpreter and is the expression layer behind Blockbench data_points (e.g. "time * 360", "math.sin(time * 180) * 30", query.anim_time * 45) and future FSM conditions.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Java 21 (the module's Gradle toolchain is pinned to Java 21).
  • No Minecraft/NeoForge runtime is required. Unit tests run on plain JUnit 5.
  • The module is registered through settings.gradle (include ':modules:formula'). Consumers add implementation project(":modules:formula").

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import lib.kasuga.formula.Code;
import lib.kasuga.formula.compute.data.Namespace;
import lib.kasuga.formula.compute.infrastructure.Formula;

// A fresh namespace inherits every built-in function and constant from the root.
Namespace ns = new Namespace(Code.ROOT_NAMESPACE);

Formula f = Code.decodeFormula("sin(rad(time * 180)) * 30", ns);
ns.assign("time", 0.5f);          // variables are auto-registered on first use (initial 0)
float result = f.getResult();     // sin(90°) * 30

Logical expressions decode the same way:

var cond = Code.decodeLogical("a > 3 and b <= 10", ns);
ns.assign("a", 5f);
ns.assign("b", 9f);
boolean ok = cond.getResult();    // true

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Operator Meaning Precedence ^ power (Math.pow) highest * / % multiply, divide, modulo — same level, left-associative middle + - add, subtract — same level, left-associative lowest

Modulo shares the precedence of * and /: 10 % 3 * 5 evaluates as (10 % 3) * 5 = 5, not 10 % 15.

** is accepted as an alias for ^ (Python style): 2 ** 3 == 8.

Unary minus is supported in all forms: -5, -(2 + 3), 2 * -3, 3 - -2. Parentheses nest arbitrarily deep.

docs.title: Built-in Functions
docs.text:
Registered on the root namespace by Code:

Arity Functions 1 cos sin tan asin acos atan log lg exp round sqrt rad deg floor ceil 2 pow max min 3 none by default — register with namespace.register3Param(...)

Trigonometric functions take radians. rad/deg convert between degrees and radians. Arguments are separated by commas: pow(2, 10), max(3, 7).

docs.title: Static Constants
docs.text: pi and e are registered as read-only static variables (they live in STATIC_VARS, so assign on them is a no-op).

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
• Names start with a lowercase letter: [a-z][a-z1-9]*, optionally containing _.
  • Dotted names separate variable scopes: query.anim_time is a single variable whose codec contains a ..
  • A variable used in an expression is auto-registered on the instance map with initial value 0; every getResult() reads the latest value written by namespace.assign("x", v).

docs.title: Comparison Operators
docs.text: >, <, >=, <=, ==, !=, and <> (alias for !=). Symbol operators do not require surrounding spaces: a>b, a>=5, and a+1==6 all parse correctly.

docs.title: Boolean Operators
docs.text: and, or, not (word operators). Because they are words, they require surrounding spaces so they cannot collide with variable names: nota is a variable, while not a is a negation. Literal booleans are spelled True / False (capitalized). Numeric values are truthy when non-zero.

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text: Highest to lowest: ==, !=, > <, >= <=, not, and, or. Use parentheses to override: not (a > 3).

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Chained comparisons are not supported: a > b > c throws FormulaSyntaxError (the intermediate result is a boolean, not a numeric). Write a > b and b > c instead.
  • Mixed relational operators in one expression (e.g. a == b > c) are not supported for the same reason.

docs.title: Namespaces And Registration
docs.text:
Namespace is the symbol table. A child namespace copies the parent's functions, static variables, and instance variables at construction; later registrations stay local.

API Behavior register(codec, function) register a function instance register1Param/2Param/3Param(codec, computer) register a function from a lambda register(codec, value) register a static (read-only) variable registerInstance(codec, assignable) register a runtime variable (auto-created when an expression uses an unknown name) assign(codec, value) write a runtime variable containsInstance(codec) / getInstance(codec) inspect the instance map clone() shallow copy — the maps are copied, the parent link is preserved

Code is the static facade over the root namespace: Code.decodeFormula, Code.encodeFormula, Code.decodeLogical, Code.encodeLogical, Code.root().

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
All exceptions extend RuntimeException:

Exception Meaning FormulaSyntaxError malformed expression (unbalanced brackets, bad operator sequence, non-numeric operand in a comparison, ...). Carries an optional message and a (formula, position) hint. FormulaParseError a token could not be parsed into any formula element; wraps the underlying FormulaSyntaxError plus the offending input string. FormulaOperationError an operator received an operator as an operand (e.g. two operators in a row).

docs.title: Development And Debugging
docs.text:
Run from the repository root:

.\gradlew.bat :modules:formula:test
.\gradlew.bat :modules:formula:compileJava

To run one test class:

.\gradlew.bat :modules:formula:test --tests lib.kasuga.formula.FormulaComputeTest

The unit tests cover operator precedence (including % sharing * / precedence), ** power, unary minus, function nesting, variable assignment/reassignment, dotted names, no-space symbol operators, word-operator spacing, and the chained-comparison error.
